swe.summary: Master one language and the command line, grind DSA until problems feel routine, then build and ship real backend services and learn to design them at scale.

phases.title: Programming foundations

steps.what: Shell navigation, file permissions, pipes and redirection, grep/sed/awk, processes, environment variables, SSH, writing small bash scripts
Syntax, types, control flow, functions, OOP (classes, interfaces, inheritance), collections, exceptions, file I/O, modules/packages, basic concurrency
Commits, branches, merge vs rebase, resolving conflicts, pull requests, .gitignore, writing clear commit messages, forking and contributing on GitHub

phases.build: A command-line log analyzer that parses multi-GB server logs, reports top error codes and latency percentiles, and supports filters by time window — versioned on GitHub with clean commits and a README.

phases.title: Problem solving & code quality

steps.what: Big-O, arrays, hashing, two pointers, sliding window, stacks/queues, linked lists, trees, heaps, graphs (BFS/DFS, Dijkstra), recursion, DP, greedy, binary search
Test structure (arrange-act-assert), edge cases, parametrized tests, mocks and stubs, test coverage, TDD basics, keeping tests fast and deterministic

phases.build: A tested library of 30+ data structures and algorithms (LRU cache, trie, union-find, segment tree, Dijkstra) with unit tests and complexity notes, plus a tracked log of 150 solved interview problems.

phases.title: Data and APIs

steps.what: Relational modeling, normalization, joins, aggregates, indexes and query plans, transactions and isolation levels, migrations, when to use NoSQL
HTTP methods and status codes, resource design, request validation, pagination, authentication (sessions, JWT), error handling, API documentation

phases.build: A campus placement-tracker REST API (students, companies, drive rounds, offers) on PostgreSQL with indexed queries, pagination, JWT auth, and integration tests against a real test database.

phases.title: Design, cloud and delivery

steps.what: Load balancing, caching, database replication and sharding, queues, consistency vs availability, rate limiting, capacity estimation, writing a design doc
Compute (EC2/Cloud Run), managed databases, object storage, IAM basics, VPC and security groups, environment config and secrets, cost awareness
Pipelines that lint, test and build on every PR, Docker image builds, environment promotion, automated deploys, rollback strategy

phases.build: Deploy the placement-tracker API to AWS behind a load balancer with Redis caching and a GitHub Actions pipeline that tests every PR, plus a design doc explaining how it would scale to 1M students.

backend.summary: Get fluent in one backend language and HTTP, master data modeling and API design, then add caching, queues and services until you can design and deploy a system that survives load.

phases.title: Language & environment

steps.what: Shell basics, file permissions, processes and signals, pipes, grep/awk, SSH into servers, reading logs, simple bash scripts
Branching, merging and rebasing, resolving conflicts, pull-request workflow, tagging releases
Request/response cycle, methods, headers, status codes, cookies, TLS basics, DNS, how a browser request reaches a server
Core syntax, OOP or Go interfaces, collections, error handling, modules, concurrency (threads/goroutines/asyncio), dependency management

phases.build: A concurrent web crawler in Go or Java that respects robots.txt, deduplicates URLs, rate-limits per domain and stores page metadata, with tests and a GitHub README showing throughput numbers.

phases.title: Data modeling & API design

steps.what: Schema design, normalization, joins, indexes and EXPLAIN, transactions and isolation, locking, document stores vs relational, migrations
Resource modeling, idempotency, pagination, error model, versioning, auth with JWT, protobuf contracts and gRPC services, OpenAPI docs

phases.build: An event-ticketing backend with PostgreSQL transactions that prevent double-booking, MongoDB for event listings, REST endpoints for clients and a gRPC service for seat allocation, all documented.

phases.title: Performance & async processing

steps.what: Cache-aside and write-through patterns, TTLs and eviction, cache invalidation, distributed locks, Redis data structures, avoiding cache stampedes
Producers and consumers, topics and partitions, consumer groups, delivery guarantees, retries and dead-letter queues, idempotent consumers

phases.build: Add Redis seat-hold locks with TTLs and a Kafka pipeline emitting booking events to notification and analytics consumers; load-test with k6 and publish p95 latency before and after caching.

phases.title: System design & services

steps.what: Load balancers, replication and sharding, CAP trade-offs, rate limiting, back-pressure, capacity estimation, failure modes, writing design docs
Service boundaries, sync vs async communication, API gateway, service discovery, sagas for distributed transactions, circuit breakers

phases.build: Split the ticketing backend into booking, payment and notification services with a saga for checkout, and write a design doc covering failure scenarios and scaling to a flash sale of 100k users.

phases.title: Containers & cloud

steps.what: Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, Compose, Kubernetes pods, deployments, services, config maps and secrets, health probes, scaling
Managed compute and databases, object storage, IAM, VPC networking, managed Kafka/Redis, logging and cost basics

phases.build: Containerize all ticketing services and deploy them to a managed Kubernetes cluster (EKS/GKE free tier) with managed Postgres and Redis, autoscaling, and health checks.

frontend.summary: Start with semantic HTML and modern CSS, get fluent in TypeScript and React, then level up with state management, testing, performance and accessibility.

phases.title: Web foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, resolving conflicts, deploying static sites from a repo
Semantic HTML, forms, box model, specificity, Flexbox, Grid, positioning, CSS variables, transitions, BEM or utility-first CSS
Mobile-first layouts, media and container queries, fluid typography with clamp(), responsive images, viewport units, testing across devices

phases.build: A pixel-accurate, responsive recreation of a real product landing page (e.g. Razorpay or Notion) from a Figma file, using semantic HTML, Grid/Flexbox and fluid type, deployed on GitHub Pages.

phases.title: JavaScript, TypeScript & React

steps.what: Closures, scope, prototypes, ES modules, DOM events, fetch and promises, async/await, event loop; TS types, generics, unions, narrowing
Components and props, useState/useEffect, custom hooks, lists and keys, forms, context, React Router, data fetching with TanStack Query

phases.build: A GitHub repository explorer in React + TypeScript: search users, paginate repos, render READMEs and language charts via the GitHub API, with loading/error states and URL-synced filters.

phases.title: Real app architecture

steps.what: Local vs global vs server state, Redux Toolkit slices, selectors, Zustand stores, optimistic updates, persisting state, avoiding unnecessary re-renders
Unit tests for logic, component tests with Testing Library, mocking APIs with MSW, end-to-end flows in Cypress, running tests in CI

phases.build: A group expense-splitting app (Splitwise-style) with a Redux Toolkit or Zustand store, optimistic updates and settle-up logic, covered by Jest component tests and Cypress end-to-end tests in CI.

phases.title: Production polish

steps.what: Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), code-splitting and lazy loading, memoization, image optimization, bundle analysis, caching headers
WCAG basics, semantic landmarks, ARIA roles, keyboard navigation and focus management, color contrast, screen reader testing
Dev server and HMR, bundling and tree-shaking, environment variables, aliases, plugins, production builds, ESLint and Prettier setup

phases.build: Audit and optimize the expense app: code-split routes, lazy-load images, tune the Vite build, fix keyboard and screen-reader issues, and document Lighthouse performance and a11y scores rising above 90.

fullstack.summary: Learn the web platform and TypeScript, build UIs in React and servers in Node.js, connect them to a real database, then containerize and deploy whole features end to end.

phases.title: Web & language foundations

steps.what: Branching, pull requests, merge conflicts, commit hygiene, GitHub issues and project boards
Semantic HTML, forms, box model, Flexbox and Grid, responsive layouts with media queries, CSS variables
Closures, scope, ES modules, DOM, promises and async/await, event loop, fetch; TS types, interfaces, generics, narrowing, strict mode

phases.build: A vanilla TypeScript single-page app that pulls live data from a public API (e.g. data.gov.in air quality), renders sortable tables and charts, and is deployed on Netlify.

phases.title: React frontends & Node servers

steps.what: Components, props and state, hooks, custom hooks, forms, routing, context, server-state fetching and caching, component composition
Event loop, npm and modules, file system and streams, Express routing and middleware, env config, WebSockets, error handling

phases.build: A real-time classroom polling app: React frontend and a Node.js Socket.IO server that broadcasts votes live across rooms, with shareable join codes and results charts.

phases.title: Data & APIs

steps.what: Relational schema design, joins, indexes, transactions, migrations, ORMs, document modeling in MongoDB and when to choose it
REST resource design, validation, pagination, JWT/session auth, GraphQL schemas, resolvers, N+1 and DataLoader, API docs

phases.build: A full-stack internship-application tracker: React UI, Node REST + GraphQL API, PostgreSQL with migrations, JWT auth, resume file uploads, and role-based access for students and mentors.

phases.title: Design, ship & scale

steps.what: Client-server architecture, caching, background jobs, load balancing, database scaling, rate limiting, trade-offs written up as design docs
Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, images vs containers, volumes, networking, Docker Compose for app + database
Deploying frontend and API, managed Postgres, environment variables and secrets, custom domains and HTTPS, CI deploys

phases.build: Containerize the tracker, deploy it with managed Postgres and a CI pipeline, add Redis caching and background email reminders, and write a one-page design doc on scaling to 100k users.

web-developer.summary: Build sites by hand with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, make them responsive, add a light server side, then deliver CMS-powered, SEO-ready sites that work in every browser.

phases.title: Markup, layout & responsiveness

steps.what: Navigating folders, creating and moving files, running npm and local dev servers, basic terminal shortcuts
Commits, branches, pull requests, resolving conflicts, publishing sites with GitHub Pages
Semantic HTML, forms, box model, specificity, Flexbox, Grid, positioning, CSS variables, transitions and simple animations
Mobile-first layouts, breakpoints and media queries, fluid typography, responsive images with srcset, testing on real devices

phases.build: A responsive multi-page website for a real local business (clinic, coaching centre or restaurant) built from scratch with semantic HTML and Grid/Flexbox, hosted on GitHub Pages with a custom domain.

phases.title: Interactivity & server side

steps.what: Variables, functions, arrays and objects, DOM manipulation, events, form validation, fetch and async/await, ES modules, localStorage
Handling form submissions, routing, server-side templating, connecting to MySQL, sending email, sessions, basic input sanitization

phases.build: Add an appointment-booking form with client-side validation and a filterable gallery to the business site, backed by a PHP or Node.js server that stores bookings in MySQL and emails the owner.

phases.title: CMS, SEO & launch

steps.what: Themes and child themes, custom post types and fields, page builders, plugins, Webflow CMS collections, user roles, backups and updates
Title and meta tags, heading structure, sitemaps and robots.txt, structured data, page speed, Search Console, local SEO basics
Vendor differences, feature detection, CSS fallbacks, autoprefixing, testing on Safari, Firefox and mobile browsers, fixing layout bugs

phases.build: A WordPress custom-theme or Webflow CMS site for a college fest or club with editable events and sponsors, contact forms, sitemap and structured data, tested across browsers with Lighthouse SEO above 90.

api-engineer.summary: Get solid in a backend language and HTTP, learn to design spec-first REST APIs, then add GraphQL, gRPC, auth, gateways and versioning that make APIs safe and pleasant to integrate.

phases.title: Backend foundations

steps.what: Branching, pull requests, conflict resolution, semantic versioning tags and changelogs
HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2, methods, headers, status codes, caching headers, CORS, TLS, DNS, TCP basics
Tables and keys, joins, aggregates, indexes, transactions, designing schemas behind API resources
Core syntax, structs/classes, interfaces, error handling, JSON serialization, concurrency, HTTP server and client libraries, testing

phases.build: A minimal HTTP server built on raw sockets in Go or Python that parses requests, routes paths and serves JSON, then the same service rewritten on a framework, with a write-up comparing the two.

phases.title: Designing REST contracts

steps.what: Resource modeling, naming, idempotency, pagination and filtering, consistent error model, HATEOAS trade-offs, bulk operations, webhooks
Writing OpenAPI 3 specs, schemas and components, spec-first workflow, generating server stubs and client SDKs, linting specs, contract tests

phases.build: A spec-first REST API for a college event-registration platform: OpenAPI 3 spec written before code, generated server stubs and a client SDK, consistent errors, pagination, and hosted Swagger UI docs.

phases.title: Beyond REST

steps.what: Schema design, queries, mutations, subscriptions, resolvers, N+1 problem and DataLoader, query complexity limits, schema evolution
Protocol Buffers, unary and streaming RPCs, code generation, deadlines and cancellation, error codes, backward-compatible proto changes

phases.build: Expose the event platform through a GraphQL endpoint with DataLoader batching and an internal gRPC seat-allocation service, with a benchmark comparing latency and payload size against REST.

phases.title: Securing & operating APIs

steps.what: OAuth 2.0 flows (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials), OIDC, JWT structure and validation, scopes, API keys, token rotation
Routing, request transformation, auth offloading, TLS termination, logging and analytics, developer portals, plugins
Token bucket and sliding window algorithms, per-client quotas, 429 handling, URI vs header versioning, deprecation and sunset policies

phases.build: Put the APIs behind Kong or AWS API Gateway with Google OAuth login and JWT validation, Redis-backed per-client rate limits, and a v1-to-v2 migration with deprecation headers and a changelog.

platform-engineer.summary: Get comfortable with Linux, networking and containers, then provision cloud infrastructure as code, run workloads on Kubernetes with automated pipelines, and finally build the self-serve tooling other engineers use.

phases.title: Systems foundations

steps.what: Filesystem, permissions, processes, systemd, package managers, networking commands, log inspection, bash scripting with loops and conditionals
Branching strategies, pull requests, rebasing, tags, monorepo vs polyrepo basics
IP addressing and subnets, DNS, TCP vs UDP, HTTP, load balancers, NAT, firewalls, TLS certificates
Images and layers, Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, volumes, networks, Docker Compose, image size and security scanning

phases.build: Containerize a three-tier app (frontend, API, Postgres) with multi-stage Dockerfiles and Compose, plus bash scripts for setup, health checks and log rotation on a Linux VM.

phases.title: Cloud & infrastructure as code

steps.what: IAM and least privilege, VPCs and subnets, compute (EC2/GCE), managed databases, object storage, load balancers, billing alerts
Providers, resources, variables and outputs, modules, remote state and locking, workspaces, plan/apply workflow, drift detection

phases.build: Provision a VPC, subnets, managed Postgres and an autoscaling group on AWS entirely with Terraform modules, with S3 remote state and locking and separate dev/prod environments rebuilt in one command.

phases.title: Orchestration & delivery

steps.what: Pods, deployments, services, ingress, config maps and secrets, resource limits, probes, HPA, namespaces and RBAC, Helm charts
Build, test and scan stages, artifact and image registries, environment promotion, GitOps, canary and blue-green deploys, rollbacks

phases.build: A GitHub Actions pipeline that tests, builds and scans images, pushes them to a registry, and deploys to Kubernetes via Helm and Argo CD with automatic rollback on failed health checks.

phases.title: Building the platform

steps.what: Writing CLIs, calling cloud and Kubernetes APIs, config parsing (YAML/JSON), concurrency basics, testing, packaging and releasing binaries
Metrics, logs and traces, Prometheus queries, Grafana dashboards, alerting rules, SLIs/SLOs, OpenTelemetry instrumentation
Service templates and scaffolding, local dev environments, pre-commit hooks, linting standards, documenting golden paths
Platform-as-product thinking, service catalogs, self-serve provisioning, scorecards, measuring developer experience

phases.build: A mini internal developer platform: a Go CLI that scaffolds a new service with Dockerfile, Helm chart and pipeline in one command, registers it in Backstage, and auto-provisions its Grafana dashboard and alerts.

software-architect.summary: Build strong engineering fundamentals first, then learn to design at the code and system level, scale out to distributed cloud architectures, and practise documenting and defending trade-offs.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: Classes, interfaces, encapsulation, inheritance vs composition, SOLID principles, exceptions, collections, in Java or Python
Complexity analysis, arrays, hash maps, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting and searching, recursion, basic dynamic programming
Branching, pull requests, code review etiquette, rebasing, release tags
Schema design, joins, indexes, transactions and isolation levels, normalization vs denormalization
Processes and threads, memory, I/O, TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, TLS, latency numbers every engineer should know

phases.build: A layered order-management service in Java with PostgreSQL persistence, unit tests and clean Git history — the baseline system you will redesign and scale in later phases.

phases.title: Design at code and system level

steps.what: Requirements and NFRs, capacity estimation, load balancing, caching, replication, sharding, queues, CAP, design-doc writing and diagrams
Factory, Strategy, Observer, Adapter, Decorator, Repository, dependency injection, hexagonal/clean architecture, recognising anti-patterns
REST resource modeling, idempotency, versioning, pagination, error contracts, async APIs and events, OpenAPI specs

phases.build: Refactor the order service into a hexagonal architecture using Strategy, Observer and Repository patterns, define its API in OpenAPI, and write a design doc for scaling it to 10k orders per minute.

phases.title: Distributed & cloud architecture

steps.what: Replication, partitioning, consistency models, consensus basics, clocks and ordering, idempotency, retries, failure detection
Well-Architected pillars, multi-AZ design, managed services vs self-hosted, serverless, cost modeling, disaster recovery (RPO/RTO)
Domain-driven service boundaries, sync vs async communication, sagas, API gateway, service mesh basics, data ownership per service

phases.build: Split the order system into order, inventory and payment services communicating over Kafka with a checkout saga, deployed on AWS (ECS or EKS, RDS, SQS) and documented with C4 diagrams.

phases.title: Security & communicating decisions

steps.what: Threat modeling (STRIDE), authN/authZ design, OAuth/OIDC, secrets management, encryption at rest and in transit, zero trust, OWASP Top 10
Writing ADRs and RFCs, explaining trade-offs to non-engineers, running design reviews, presenting options with cost and risk

phases.build: An architecture decision package for the order system: STRIDE threat model, least-privilege IAM and auth design, five ADRs on key trade-offs, and a recorded 10-minute design review presentation.

staff-engineer.summary: Staff is a senior destination, so the student path builds exceptional engineering depth first, then systems thinking, then practises leadership, review and influence on real team and open-source projects.

phases.title: Engineering depth

steps.what: Language fluency, idiomatic code, OOP or Go interfaces, error handling, concurrency, profiling, writing readable, well-tested modules
Complexity analysis, hashing, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting, binary search, dynamic programming, choosing structures for real workloads
Branching strategies, interactive history cleanup, bisect, pull-request workflow, release tagging
Schema design, indexes and query plans, transactions and isolation, migrations, when to choose NoSQL

phases.build: A job-scheduling service in Go or Java with a PostgreSQL-backed queue, retries with exponential backoff, cron-style schedules, 80%+ test coverage and CI — your reference codebase for later phases.

phases.title: Systems thinking

steps.what: Capacity estimation, load balancing, caching, sharding, queues, rate limiting, CAP trade-offs, writing and reviewing design docs
Replication, partitioning, consistency models, leader election, idempotency, exactly-once myths, failure detection, clocks

phases.build: Evolve the scheduler into a distributed job system: leader election via etcd, sharded workers, at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys, and a design doc analysing failure scenarios and capacity.

phases.title: Leading technical work

steps.what: Writing RFCs, breaking ambiguous problems into milestones, making and documenting decisions, unblocking others, owning outcomes
Reviewing for correctness, design and readability, giving actionable kind feedback, review checklists, keeping PRs small
Pair programming, onboarding guides, teaching through questions, giving feedback, helping juniors land first contributions

phases.build: Tech-lead a 3-4 person hackathon or club project: write the RFC, split work into issues, review every PR against written guidelines, onboard a first-year contributor, and publish a retrospective.

phases.title: Architecture & influence

steps.what: Architectural styles (layered, event-driven, hexagonal), C4 diagrams, ADRs, evaluating trade-offs, evolutionary architecture, tech debt
Building consensus without authority, writing persuasive proposals, handling disagreement, aligning stakeholders with different goals
Defining problem and non-goals, estimating, cutting scope into milestones, identifying risks and dependencies early

phases.build: Propose and land a significant change in an open-source project: write a design proposal, gather maintainer feedback, scope it into milestones, and ship the first milestone with docs and tests.

principal-engineer.summary: Principal is a long-horizon goal, so students build deep systems expertise first, then practise architecture, technical strategy and org-wide leadership on ambitious real projects.

phases.title: Deep engineering foundations

steps.what: Idiomatic code, memory and performance behavior, concurrency, profiling and benchmarking, testing, reading large codebases
Complexity, hashing, balanced trees, B-trees and LSM trees, heaps, graphs, dynamic programming, probabilistic structures (Bloom filters)
Branching models, bisect, history rewriting on private branches, large-repo workflows, release management
Query planning, indexing internals, transactions and MVCC, isolation anomalies, storage engines

phases.build: A key-value store in Go or Java with a write-ahead log, LSM-style compaction, Bloom filters and a benchmark suite — demonstrating depth well beyond CRUD apps.

phases.title: Systems & architecture

steps.what: Replication, partitioning, consensus (Raft), consistency models, clocks and ordering, failure detection, fault injection testing
Architectural styles, C4 modeling, NFRs (scalability, availability, cost), ADRs, evolutionary design, migration strategies

phases.build: Replicate your key-value store across 3 nodes with Raft, test it under network partitions with fault injection, and publish an architecture document with C4 diagrams and ADRs.

phases.title: Technical strategy

steps.what: Diagnosing current state, defining guiding principles, build vs buy, tech-debt economics, aligning technology bets with business goals
Sequencing initiatives, milestones and dependencies, now/next/later roadmaps, measuring progress, communicating changes
Structured evaluation criteria, proof-of-concept design, maturity and ecosystem assessment, risk and adoption cost write-ups

phases.build: A technical strategy doc for a real open-source project or college platform: current-state assessment, 12-month roadmap with milestones, and an evaluation of one emerging technology backed by a working prototype.

phases.title: Leading across the organization

steps.what: Writing proposals that win adoption, building coalitions, running RFC processes, setting standards without authority, handling dissent
Working with product, design and ops, translating technical risk into business terms, running cross-team planning
Pairing, structured feedback, growth plans, teaching design thinking, sponsoring juniors' work

phases.build: Drive a cross-club engineering initiative: propose a shared standard (e.g. a common auth service or coding guidelines) adopted by 2+ student teams, mentor 3 juniors to merged PRs, and document the outcomes.

tech-lead.summary: Become a strong hands-on engineer first, add system design and disciplined code review, then practise planning, mentoring and stakeholder communication by leading real team projects.

phases.title: Hands-on engineering

steps.what: Branching strategies, pull requests, resolving conflicts, protected branches, release tags
Fluency in Java, Python or Go: OOP, collections, error handling, modules, concurrency basics, testing, writing readable code
Complexity analysis, arrays, hashing, trees, graphs, sorting and searching, recursion, basic dynamic programming

phases.build: A well-tested REST backend for a college club's events and memberships with clean module boundaries, CI and documentation — the codebase your team will extend in later phases.

phases.title: Design & review

steps.what: Schema design, joins, indexes, transactions, migrations, reading query plans
Requirements and trade-offs, caching, queues, load balancing, database scaling, API design, writing short design docs
Reviewing for correctness, design and tests, giving specific respectful feedback, review checklists, keeping PRs small

phases.build: A design doc and implementation adding notifications and a waitlist to the club platform, delivered through small PRs reviewed against a written checklist covering correctness, tests and readability.

phases.title: Leading the team

steps.what: Breaking features into tasks, making and recording technical decisions, unblocking teammates, owning delivery and quality
Estimation, milestones, dependency mapping, risk tracking, adjusting scope to deadlines
Pair programming, onboarding docs, constructive feedback, helping juniors land their first PRs

phases.build: Lead a 4-person team building a feature for a hackathon or open-source project: break it into estimated issues, mentor a junior contributor through their first PRs, and ship on schedule.

phases.title: Working with stakeholders

steps.what: Status updates, explaining trade-offs to non-engineers, managing expectations, running demos, writing clear summaries
Sprints, backlog grooming, user stories and acceptance criteria, standups, sprint reviews and retrospectives, velocity

phases.build: Run a two-sprint student project in Jira with planning, standups, a demo to a real stakeholder (club head or faculty), weekly status reports, and a retrospective documenting what changed.

distributed-systems-engineer.summary: Go deep on one systems language, operating systems and concurrency, then learn distributed systems theory by implementing it — consensus, replication and streaming — with real observability.

phases.title: Systems programming foundations

steps.what: Processes, signals, file descriptors, permissions, strace and lsof, networking commands, bash scripting
Branching, pull requests, bisect for finding regressions, clean commit history
Language fluency, memory model basics, structs/classes, interfaces, error handling, networking libraries, testing and benchmarking
Hash tables, trees, heaps, graphs, consistent hashing, skip lists, complexity analysis

phases.build: An in-memory key-value server in Go with a custom TCP protocol (GET/SET/DEL, TTLs), a client library and a benchmarking tool reporting ops/sec and latency percentiles.

phases.title: Concurrency & the machine

steps.what: Processes vs threads, scheduling, virtual memory, system calls, file systems, I/O models (blocking, epoll), page cache
Threads and goroutines, mutexes, condition variables, channels, atomics, memory ordering, deadlocks and races, lock-free basics
TCP internals, connection handling, timeouts, RPC frameworks, serialization, head-of-line blocking, network partitions

phases.build: Scale the key-value server to 10k concurrent clients: worker pools, lock striping vs a lock-free map, race-detector-clean tests, and a benchmark report of throughput vs core count.

phases.title: Distributed systems core

steps.what: Failure models, replication, partitioning and consistent hashing, consistency models, logical clocks, quorums, idempotency
Capacity estimation, sharding strategies, caching, load balancing, back-pressure, designing for failure, writing design docs

phases.build: A fault-tolerant MapReduce framework with a coordinator and crash-tolerant workers, plus a design doc for sharding your KV store across nodes with consistent hashing and replication trade-offs.

phases.title: Consensus, streaming & observability

steps.what: Leader election, log replication, safety and liveness, snapshots and log compaction, membership changes, Paxos vs Raft
Partitioned logs, replication and ISR, consumer groups and offsets, delivery semantics, exactly-once processing, compaction
Metrics, structured logs, distributed tracing, Prometheus and Grafana, SLOs, debugging with traces across nodes

phases.build: Implement Raft to replicate your KV store across 5 nodes, inject partitions and crashes to prove safety, stream change events to Kafka, and expose Prometheus metrics with a Grafana dashboard.

java-developer.summary: Master core Java and DSA, build REST services on Spring Boot with JPA persistence and solid tests, then move to event-driven microservices with Kafka.

phases.title: Core Java

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, resolving conflicts, .gitignore for Java projects
OOP, interfaces, generics, Collections framework, exceptions, Streams and lambdas, Optional, multithreading and ExecutorService, JVM basics
Complexity, arrays, hashing, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, sorting, binary search, basic dynamic programming in Java

phases.build: A multithreaded file-deduplication tool in Java that hashes files across directories with ExecutorService, reports duplicates and space saved, with clean OOP design and Javadoc.

phases.title: Spring Boot & REST

steps.what: Project structure, dependencies and scopes, build lifecycle, plugins, multi-module projects, running tests from the build
Dependency injection, auto-configuration, controllers, services, profiles and config, validation, exception handling, Spring Security basics, Actuator
Resource design, HTTP methods and status codes, DTOs, pagination, error responses, JWT auth, documenting with OpenAPI

phases.build: A Spring Boot REST API for a hospital outpatient queue: patient registration, token assignment and doctor schedules, with validation, global exception handling, JWT auth and Swagger docs, built with Maven.

phases.title: Persistence & testing

steps.what: SQL joins and indexes, entity mapping, relationships, fetch types and N+1, JPQL, Spring Data repositories, transactions, Flyway migrations
JUnit 5, assertions, parameterized tests, Mockito mocks, @WebMvcTest and @DataJpaTest slices, integration tests with Testcontainers

phases.build: Persist the queue system in PostgreSQL with Spring Data JPA, entity relationships, Flyway migrations and transactional booking; reach 80%+ coverage with JUnit, Mockito and Testcontainers tests in CI.

phases.title: Microservices & events

steps.what: Service boundaries, Spring Cloud Gateway, service discovery, inter-service calls with resilience (Resilience4j), config server, Docker Compose
Topics, partitions, producers and consumers, consumer groups, Spring Kafka, retries and dead-letter topics, idempotent processing

phases.build: Split the hospital system into patient, appointment and notification services behind Spring Cloud Gateway, publishing appointment events to Kafka for an SMS/email notifier, all run with Docker Compose.

python-developer.summary: Get fluent in Python and its tooling, build web services with FastAPI or Django, add databases and tests, then round out with async, Pandas and Docker.

phases.title: Python foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, resolving conflicts, .gitignore and virtualenv hygiene
Shell navigation, permissions, pipes, environment variables, running scripts and cron jobs, SSH
Data types, comprehensions, functions, OOP and dataclasses, exceptions, modules and packaging, virtual environments, type hints, generators
Complexity, lists, dicts and sets internals, stacks, queues, heaps, trees, graphs, sorting, binary search, recursion

phases.build: A CLI that scrapes internship listings from three public career pages with requests and BeautifulSoup, normalizes and deduplicates them, and exports CSV/JSON — packaged with pyproject.toml.

phases.title: Web frameworks & APIs

steps.what: Routing, request validation with Pydantic, dependency injection, Django models, views, admin and auth, middleware, settings per environment

streaming-data-engineer.summary: Learn a JVM language and stream-processing theory first, then Kafka and Flink, then the hard parts: schemas, state and exactly-once delivery, finishing on managed cloud streaming.

data-warehouse-engineer.summary: Master SQL and relational design, then dimensional modeling, then build and load a cloud warehouse, finishing on query tuning and cost control.

big-data-engineer.summary: Build programming and SQL fluency, learn distributed computing on the Hadoop stack, then Spark and open table formats, finishing with cloud clusters and job tuning at scale.

steps.what: Workspaces, clusters vs serverless, notebooks and Repos, Jobs and Workflows, Databricks SQL warehouses and dashboards, Auto Loader, Delta Live Tables
Transaction log, ACID writes, MERGE upserts, schema enforcement and evolution, time travel, OPTIMIZE and Z-ordering, VACUUM, change data feed

phases.build: A medallion pipeline on Databricks: Auto Loader ingests raw files to bronze, Delta MERGE builds deduplicated silver tables, gold aggregates feed a Databricks SQL dashboard, scheduled as a Workflow.

phases.title: Cloud, governance and ML

steps.what: Object storage for the lake, IAM roles and service principals, networking basics, how Databricks deploys into a cloud account, cost tags
Metastore, catalogs/schemas/tables, grants and privileges, row filters and column masks, lineage, external locations and storage credentials
Experiment tracking, logging params and metrics, model registry, batch inference on Delta tables

phases.build: Add Unity Catalog governance to the medallion project (analyst vs engineer grants, PII column masks, lineage view), and a gold-layer demand forecast model tracked and registered in MLflow.

data-integration-engineer.summary: Get comfortable with Python, SQL and HTTP, master API integration and schema mapping, then ELT and iPaaS tools, finishing with change data capture and cloud messaging.

phases.title: Programming and data foundations

steps.what: Functions, classes, requests and httpx, JSON handling, error handling and retries, logging, pytest
Joins, aggregations, upserts with MERGE/ON CONFLICT, reconciliation queries comparing source and target counts and sums
Branches, pull requests, code review, keeping secrets out of repos
HTTP methods and status codes, headers, content types, JSON and XML structure, pagination styles, rate limits

phases.build: A Python sync tool that pulls a public REST API (e.g. GitHub issues for a large repo) into Postgres with pagination, retries and an upsert, plus a SQL reconciliation report against the source counts.

phases.title: APIs and schema mapping

steps.what: OAuth 2.0 and API keys, cursor vs offset pagination, rate-limit backoff, webhooks, GraphQL queries and pagination, idempotency keys, incremental sync by updated_at
Field-level mapping specs, type coercion, flattening nested JSON, handling schema drift, canonical data models, transformation documentation

phases.build: A connector syncing two SaaS-style APIs (one REST with OAuth, one GraphQL) into a canonical customer model, with a pydantic mapping layer that flags schema drift instead of failing silently.

phases.title: ELT and iPaaS platforms

steps.what: Source and destination connectors, sync modes (full refresh, incremental, dedup), normalization, building a custom connector, scheduling and monitoring syncs
MuleSoft flows and DataWeave transformations, Boomi processes, Fivetran connector setup, error handling and retries in iPaaS, API-led connectivity

phases.build: Package the API connector as a custom Airbyte source, run it alongside a stock Postgres connector into a warehouse, and rebuild one flow in MuleSoft to compare effort, error handling and observability.

phases.title: Real-time integration and cloud

steps.what: Database logs (Postgres WAL, MySQL binlog), Debezium CDC, Kafka topics and consumers, outbox pattern, ordering and replay
Managed queues and event buses, serverless functions for webhooks, secrets management, object storage landing zones

phases.build: A CDC pipeline streaming inserts and updates from a Postgres app database through Debezium and Kafka into a warehouse within seconds, plus a Lambda webhook receiver, with a reconciliation check proving no rows are lost.

data-quality-engineer.summary: Build SQL, Python and statistics basics, learn testing and quality frameworks, then dbt tests and orchestration, finishing with observability and profiling that catch bad data early.

phases.title: Data and statistics foundations

steps.what: Joins, aggregations, window functions, finding duplicates, orphan keys and gaps, comparing datasets with EXCEPT, NULL semantics
Functions, classes, pandas, reading files and databases, virtual environments, logging
Branches, pull requests, code review, versioning test suites
Distributions, mean/median/percentiles, standard deviation and z-scores, IQR outliers, seasonality, basic hypothesis tests

phases.build: An audit of a messy public dataset (e.g. a city's open 311 complaints data) using SQL and pandas, producing a written report of duplicates, invalid values, missing keys and outliers with counts.

phases.title: Testing and quality frameworks

steps.what: pytest fixtures and parametrization, unit tests for transforms, schema validation, contract tests between producers and consumers, test data generation
Expectation suites, checkpoints, data docs, Soda checks in SodaCL, thresholds and severity levels, running checks in pipelines

phases.build: A validation layer for the 311 dataset: pandera-tested transforms plus a Great Expectations suite and Soda checks that block bad batches and publish data docs showing pass/fail history.

phases.title: Tests inside the pipeline

steps.what: Generic tests (unique, not_null, relationships, accepted_values), singular tests, dbt-expectations, custom generic tests, severity and warn thresholds, unit tests
DAGs or assets, scheduling, asset checks, failing runs on test failures, retries and alert hooks

phases.build: A dbt project over the 311 data with 40+ tests including custom generic tests, orchestrated by Dagster so that failing asset checks halt downstream models and post an alert.

phases.title: Observability and profiling

steps.what: Freshness, volume, schema-change and distribution monitors, anomaly detection on metrics, lineage for impact analysis, incident triage and root-cause write-ups
Column statistics, cardinality and null rates, pattern and format discovery, distribution drift between batches, using profiles to set thresholds

phases.build: An observability dashboard that profiles each daily batch, flags volume and distribution anomalies with z-score thresholds, and includes a mock incident post-mortem tracing a bad upstream change via lineage.

kafka-platform-engineer.summary: Learn a JVM or Go language with Linux and networking, then distributed systems and Kafka internals, then Connect and schema registry, finishing with Kafka on Kubernetes with observability and IaC.

phases.title: Systems foundations

steps.what: Java collections, concurrency and executors, JVM memory and garbage collection basics, Maven/Gradle; Go basics for tooling and CLIs
Processes, file descriptors, disk and page cache, systemd, ulimits, iostat/vmstat/sar, shell scripting
Branches, pull requests, reviewing config changes, tagging releases
TCP/IP, DNS, load balancers, TLS and certificates, listeners and advertised addresses, firewall basics
Images, containers, volumes, networks, Docker Compose for multi-node local clusters

phases.build: A Java load-generator CLI with configurable message size, rate and concurrency that reports p50/p99 latency, packaged as a Docker image and used throughout the next phases.

phases.title: Kafka and distributed systems

steps.what: Replicated logs, leader election, quorum and ISR, consistency vs availability, partitioning, failure modes and split brain, KRaft consensus
Brokers, KRaft controllers, partitions and replication, acks and min.insync.replicas, idempotent producers, consumer groups, retention and compaction, reassignment, ACLs and TLS

phases.build: A 3-broker KRaft cluster with TLS and ACLs in Docker Compose, benchmarked with your load generator; document throughput and latency for different acks and replication settings, and a broker-failure test.

phases.title: Connect and schemas

steps.what: Connect workers in distributed mode, source and sink connectors, SMTs, dead-letter queues, offset management, Confluent Platform components overview
Subjects and versions, compatibility modes, Avro and Protobuf serializers, schema evolution rules, enforcing schemas per topic

phases.build: A self-serve ingestion setup: Debezium streams Postgres changes into Avro topics governed by Schema Registry, a sink connector writes to S3/MinIO, and a DLQ captures bad records, all driven by JSON configs.

phases.title: Running Kafka as a platform

steps.what: StatefulSets, persistent volumes, operators and CRDs, rolling upgrades, pod disruption budgets, rack awareness, running Kafka with Strimzi
JMX metrics, under-replicated partitions, request latency, consumer lag, disk usage, alerting rules and runbooks
Modules, state, managing topics, ACLs and users as code, environment promotion via pull requests

phases.build: Kafka plus Connect on Kubernetes via Strimzi, with topics and ACLs managed by Terraform, Grafana dashboards for lag and under-replicated partitions, and a recorded zero-downtime rolling upgrade.

spark-engineer.summary: Start with Python, SQL and Linux, learn distributed computing and Spark deeply, then lake formats and performance tuning, finishing on managed cloud Spark and Structured Streaming.

phases.title: Programming and data foundations

steps.what: Core syntax, functions, classes, generators, pandas, virtual environments, pytest
Joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs, reading query plans, join strategies at a conceptual level
Shell commands, processes, memory and disk inspection, SSH, environment variables, scripting job launches
Branches, pull requests, conflict resolution, versioning job code

phases.build: A pandas and DuckDB analysis of a multi-GB public dataset (e.g. NYC taxi trips) with a short note on where memory and single-core limits appear, setting up the case for Spark.

phases.title: Spark in depth

steps.what: Data parallelism, partitioning, shuffles, data locality, fault tolerance via lineage, stragglers, cluster managers (YARN, Kubernetes, standalone)
Driver/executors, jobs, stages and tasks, DAG scheduler, Catalyst optimizer and physical plans, Tungsten, AQE, caching, Spark UI and event logs
PySpark DataFrame and SQL APIs, built-in functions vs UDFs vs pandas UDFs, Scala Datasets basics, testing Spark code, spark-submit configs

phases.build: A tested PySpark job computing daily trip metrics over the full taxi dataset, with a write-up that reads its physical plan (explain) and maps each stage and shuffle to the code that caused it.

phases.title: Lake formats and performance

steps.what: Parquet row groups and pushdown, partitioning schemes, small-file problems, Iceberg and Delta transaction logs, MERGE, compaction, time travel
Diagnosing skew and salting, broadcast vs sort-merge joins, shuffle partition sizing, spill and memory tuning, caching, file compaction, avoiding Python UDFs

phases.build: A tuning case study: take a deliberately slow skewed join over Iceberg tables and document each fix (salting, broadcast, AQE, partition sizing, compaction) with Spark UI evidence and runtime cut.

phases.title: Cloud Spark and streaming

steps.what: Managed cluster setup, autoscaling and spot nodes, object storage connectors, job scheduling, serverless Spark options, cost per job
Micro-batch model, sources and sinks, triggers, watermarks and event-time windows, stateful aggregations, checkpointing, foreachBatch

phases.build: Run the tuned batch job on Databricks or EMR with a cost-per-run report, and add a Structured Streaming job that reads trip events from Kafka and maintains windowed zone metrics in a Delta table.

data-modeler.summary: Start from relational databases and SQL, master normalization and dimensional modeling, then learn warehouse methodologies, modeling tools and dbt to design schemas analysts can trust.

phases.title: Relational foundations

steps.what: Tables, primary and foreign keys, constraints, indexes, transactions and ACID, how the planner uses indexes, running a local Postgres instance
Commits, branches, pull requests, versioning DDL scripts and model files in a shared repository
All join types, GROUP BY/HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, DDL with constraints, reading EXPLAIN plans

phases.build: A Postgres schema for a college placement cell (students, companies, drives, offers) with full constraints, seed data and 15 documented analytical SQL queries in a GitHub repo.

phases.title: Normalized and ER design

steps.what: Functional dependencies, 1NF through BCNF, update/insert/delete anomalies, surrogate vs natural keys, when and why to denormalize
Conceptual, logical and physical models, crow's-foot notation, cardinality and optionality, forward and reverse engineering DDL from a model

phases.build: Reverse-engineer an open-source app's database (e.g. an Odoo or Moodle dump) into a logical ER model, flag its normalization violations and publish a corrected 3NF model with generated DDL.

phases.title: Dimensional modeling and warehouses

steps.what: Facts and dimensions, declaring the grain, star vs snowflake, conformed dimensions, SCD types 1/2/3, factless facts, junk dimensions, the bus matrix
OLTP vs OLAP, columnar storage, staging/ODS/mart layering, partitioning and clustering, ELT loading patterns, query cost

phases.build: A star-schema sales warehouse built from the Olist e-commerce dataset in BigQuery or DuckDB, with an SCD2 customer dimension, a bus matrix and queries for monthly revenue and cohort retention.

phases.title: Enterprise methodologies and modern tooling

steps.what: Kimball bottom-up marts vs Inmon corporate information factory, Data Vault 2.0 hubs/links/satellites, hash keys, raw vs business vault, choosing a method
Models, refs and sources, schema and data tests, snapshots for SCD2, incremental models, docs site and lineage graph
Data dictionaries, naming standards, lineage, data ownership, PII classification, business glossary

phases.build: Model the same e-commerce source as a Data Vault raw layer feeding Kimball marts in dbt, with tests, snapshots, a generated docs site and a naming-standards and glossary document.

data-pipeline-engineer.summary: Get solid in Linux, Python and SQL, then learn orchestration and load patterns, ingestion and cloud warehouses, and finish with Docker and Spark to run pipelines end to end.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: Shell navigation, pipes, permissions, environment variables, cron, ssh, processes and logs
Commits, branches, pull requests, code review flow, .gitignore for secrets
Data structures, functions, modules, virtualenvs, requests, pandas, logging, exception handling, pytest
Joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs, MERGE/upsert, DDL, indexes, reading query plans

phases.build: A tested Python loader that pulls daily readings from a public API (e.g. OpenAQ or data.gov.in), validates them and upserts into Postgres, scheduled with cron and logging every run.

phases.title: Orchestration and load patterns

steps.what: DAGs, tasks and operators, schedules, retries, sensors, backfills, XComs vs Dagster assets, connections and secrets, failure alerting
Full vs incremental loads, idempotency, merge/upsert, backfills, staging layers, schema drift, data quality gates

phases.build: Port the loader into an Airflow DAG with retries, a 90-day idempotent backfill, a data-quality task that fails the run on bad rows, and failure alerts to Slack or email.

phases.title: Ingestion and the cloud warehouse

steps.what: REST pagination, rate limits, OAuth, incremental cursors, webhooks; change data capture from Postgres WAL with Debezium into Kafka
Columnar storage, staged loads with COPY, partitioning and clustering, cost control, BigQuery and Snowflake SQL dialects, dbt models on top

phases.build: A CDC pipeline streaming changes from a Postgres orders database via Debezium into BigQuery or Snowflake, with dbt building daily marts and row-count reconciliation checks.

phases.title: Packaging and scale

steps.what: Dockerfiles, images and layers, volumes, networks, docker-compose stacks for Airflow plus Postgres, environment config
DataFrames, lazy evaluation, partitions, joins and shuffles, reading and writing Parquet, PySpark jobs triggered from an orchestrator

phases.build: Containerize the whole stack with docker-compose and add a PySpark job processing multi-GB NYC Taxi Parquet files, orchestrated by the same DAG with run metrics logged.

real-time-analytics-engineer.summary: Build programming and SQL basics, learn Kafka/Flink streaming into real-time OLAP stores, then master low-latency modeling, materialized views, and production cloud and observability.

phases.title: Programming and SQL foundations

steps.what: Shell, processes, ports and networking basics, logs, environment variables
Images, containers, volumes, docker-compose for running Kafka, ClickHouse and Grafana locally
Python for producers, consumers and scripting; Java basics (classes, generics, lambdas, Maven) needed for Flink and Kafka APIs
Joins, aggregations, window functions, time bucketing, percentiles, approximate distinct counts, reading query plans

phases.build: A Python clickstream simulator generating realistic sessions, page views and purchases at configurable rates, with SQL funnel and retention analytics over a sample loaded into DuckDB.

phases.title: Streaming into real-time OLAP

steps.what: Kafka topics, partitions, consumer groups, offsets, Avro schemas; Flink event time, watermarks, windows, keyed state, exactly-once sinks
Columnar engines, MergeTree family, Kafka ingestion engines, Druid/Pinot segments and real-time tables, indexes, query tuning

phases.build: Stream the simulated clickstream through Kafka, sessionize it in Flink with event-time windows, and sink into ClickHouse powering a live Grafana dashboard with sub-second queries.

phases.title: Low-latency modeling

steps.what: Denormalized wide tables, sort and primary keys, time partitioning, pre-aggregation and rollups, star-tree indexes, dedup and upserts
ClickHouse materialized views, AggregatingMergeTree states, incremental view maintenance in Materialize or RisingWave, late-data handling

phases.build: Redesign the tables for a 100M-row synthetic dataset and publish a benchmark write-up comparing p50/p95 query latency before and after sort keys, rollups and materialized views.

phases.title: Running it in production

steps.what: Managed Kafka and ClickHouse options, VMs vs Kubernetes, storage tiers, Terraform basics, cost estimation
Consumer lag, throughput, end-to-end freshness and query latency metrics, Prometheus exporters, alert rules

phases.build: Deploy the pipeline on a cloud free tier with Terraform and add Prometheus/Grafana dashboards for consumer lag, freshness and query p99, with alerts that fire when data goes stale.

head-of-data-engineering.summary: Earn hands-on data engineering credibility first, then learn platform architecture, and build the leadership, stakeholder, cost and roadmapping skills a data engineering leader runs on.

phases.title: Hands-on data engineering

steps.what: Joins, window functions, CTEs, data modeling basics, query plans and performance
Scripting, pandas, APIs with requests, packaging, testing with pytest
ETL vs ELT, batch vs streaming, orchestration with Airflow, dbt transformations, data quality checks, SLAs

phases.build: An end-to-end pipeline ingesting OpenAQ or Indian Railways open data into a warehouse with Airflow and dbt, with tests and freshness SLAs: the hands-on baseline a data leader needs.

phases.title: Platforms and architecture

steps.what: Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Delta and Iceberg tables, object storage, compute/storage separation, managed vs self-hosted
Warehouse vs lake vs lakehouse vs mesh trade-offs, build vs buy, reference architectures, ADRs, reliability SLAs, scaling plans

phases.build: An architecture decision pack comparing Snowflake, BigQuery and a Databricks lakehouse for a mid-size Indian fintech, with C4 diagrams, a migration path, risks and a recommendation.

phases.title: Leading people and stakeholders

steps.what: Running standups and retros, delegation, giving feedback, 1:1s, resolving conflict, team OKRs, healthy on-call practices
Requirement elicitation, stakeholder mapping, one-pagers, negotiating scope and SLAs with analytics and product, saying no with data
Role scorecards, structured interviews, take-home design, onboarding plans, mentoring juniors, career ladders

phases.build: Lead a 4-5 person college data project end to end and keep the evidence: stakeholder map, PRD, sprint board, retro notes, an interview scorecard and an onboarding guide for new members.

phases.title: Strategy, cost and governance

steps.what: Cloud pricing models, warehouse credit usage, FinOps basics, cost per pipeline, tagging and chargeback, cost-cutting levers
Quarterly roadmaps, RICE prioritization, dependency mapping, communicating trade-offs to leadership
Data ownership, catalogs, access control, lineage, data contracts, DPDP Act and GDPR basics

phases.build: A one-year data platform strategy for a startup: monthly cloud cost model, RICE-prioritized quarterly roadmap, governance and access policy, and a hiring plan, presented as a 10-slide deck.

data-sci.summary: Learn Python and SQL for data work, build a strong statistics and experimentation core, then add visualization, machine learning, stakeholder communication and Spark/cloud.

phases.title: Programming and data foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, keeping notebooks and code in version control
Data structures, functions, NumPy arrays, pandas indexing, groupby, merges, reshaping, datetime handling, Jupyter workflow
Joins, aggregations, CTEs, window functions, date logic, funnel and cohort queries

phases.build: An exploratory analysis of the Zomato Bangalore restaurants dataset: SQL extraction from a Postgres load plus a pandas notebook answering five concrete business questions.

phases.title: Statistics and experimentation

steps.what: Descriptive stats, probability distributions, sampling, CLT, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, linear and logistic regression, p-value pitfalls
Metric choice, power and sample size, randomization units, t and proportion tests, peeking, novelty effects, interpreting results

phases.build: Analyze a public landing-page A/B test dataset with a power analysis, significance tests, confidence intervals and a written ship or no-ship recommendation.

phases.title: Visualization and machine learning

steps.what: Choosing chart types, matplotlib and seaborn, interactive Plotly, dashboard layout, honest axes, one takeaway per chart
Regression, classification, trees, gradient boosting, cross-validation, feature engineering, leakage, AUC/RMSE, SHAP interpretation

phases.build: A churn model on the Telco Customer Churn dataset with XGBoost and SHAP, plus charts showing which customer segments to target and the estimated revenue saved.

phases.title: Communicating and scaling

steps.what: Framing business questions, pyramid-style memos, executive summaries, presenting uncertainty, handling pushback
PySpark DataFrames, partitioned Parquet, running notebooks on Databricks, querying BigQuery, basic cloud storage and compute

phases.build: A Streamlit dashboard and a two-page decision memo for a business stakeholder, with the churn feature pipeline rewritten in PySpark on Databricks Community Edition.

applied-scientist.summary: Build the math, Python and statistics base, master ML and deep learning, learn to turn papers into experiments, and finish by shipping and writing up a production-grade model.

phases.title: Math, Python and statistics

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, reproducible project structure
Vectors, matrices, eigendecomposition, SVD, gradients and chain rule, convexity, gradient descent
NumPy vectorization, pandas, OOP, typing, testing, profiling, writing clean reusable modules
Estimation, hypothesis tests, bootstrap, Bayesian basics, confidence intervals for model metrics

phases.build: Linear regression, logistic regression and a small MLP implemented from scratch in NumPy with gradient checks, verified against scikit-learn and with bootstrap CIs on accuracy.

phases.title: Core ML and deep learning

steps.what: Bias-variance, regularization, trees and boosting, SVMs, clustering, cross-validation, feature engineering, metrics, error analysis
Backprop, CNNs, RNNs, transformers and attention, optimizers, normalization, regularization, transfer learning and fine-tuning

phases.build: A review classifier for Indian-language product reviews comparing a TF-IDF plus logistic regression baseline to a fine-tuned multilingual transformer, with a full error analysis.

phases.title: From papers to experiments

steps.what: Custom Dataset/DataLoader, training loops, mixed precision, checkpointing, PyTorch Lightning, Keras functional API, experiment tracking
Reading papers efficiently, reproducing results, strong baselines, ablations, framing a product problem as an ML research question

phases.build: Reproduce a recent paper's key result (e.g. LoRA fine-tuning) on a smaller dataset, with ablations and a W&B report comparing your numbers to the paper's.

phases.title: Shipping and publishing

steps.what: Serving APIs, batching and latency, ONNX export, drift monitoring, offline vs online evaluation, feature stores, CI for models
ML paper structure, related work, LaTeX figures and tables, workshop submissions, responding to reviewers, technical blogging

phases.build: Serve the improved model behind a Dockerized FastAPI endpoint with latency benchmarks and drift monitoring, and write it up as a 4-page workshop-style paper.

research-scientist.summary: Go deep on mathematics and research-grade Python, master deep learning and its frameworks, then practise rigorous research methodology, scientific writing and distributed training.

phases.title: Mathematical foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, tagging experiment versions, publishing research code
Linear algebra (SVD, eigenvalues), multivariable calculus, probability theory, convex optimization, information theory basics
NumPy vectorization, OOP, clean research code structure, configs, Jupyter, profiling

phases.build: A NumPy-only autodiff engine for scalar and tensor ops that trains a small MLP, with each gradient derived by hand in an accompanying LaTeX note.

phases.title: Deep learning

steps.what: Backprop, CNNs, RNNs, transformers and attention, normalization, initialization, optimizers, generalization, VAEs and diffusion models
Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, custom training loops, JAX jit/vmap/grad, Flax, profiling GPU code

phases.build: A small GPT-style transformer written from scratch in PyTorch and trained on an Indian-language text corpus, then ported to JAX to compare speed and loss curves.

phases.title: Research practice

steps.what: MLE and MAP, Bayesian inference, hypothesis tests, confidence intervals across seeds, multiple comparisons, effect sizes
Finding open problems, literature reviews, hypotheses, strong baselines, ablations, controlled experiments, reproducibility

phases.build: A small original study (e.g. how a normalization or data-ordering choice affects small-transformer training) with a stated hypothesis, 5-seed ablations and significance tests, logged in W&B.

phases.title: Writing and scaling

steps.what: Paper structure, abstracts, related work, clear figures and tables, LaTeX, arXiv preprints, rebuttals
Data parallelism, DDP and FSDP, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, checkpointing, multi-GPU runs on cloud or Kaggle

phases.build: Scale the study to a larger model with DDP across two GPUs and write it up as a 4-page workshop paper with arXiv-ready LaTeX source and public code.

ml-scientist.summary: Lay the math, Python and statistics base, master classical ML with feature engineering, then deep learning in PyTorch, and finish with rigorous model evaluation and MLOps.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, reproducible project layout
Linear algebra, gradients and chain rule, probability distributions, optimization and gradient descent
NumPy, pandas, OOP, typing, testing, writing reusable training and evaluation modules
Estimation, hypothesis tests, bootstrap, confidence intervals, regression, multiple comparisons

phases.build: A statistical analysis of NFHS-5 or census microdata in pandas with bootstrap confidence intervals and hypothesis tests, packaged as a reusable, tested Python module.

phases.title: Classical machine learning

steps.what: Linear models, regularization, trees, random forests, gradient boosting, SVMs, clustering, cross-validation, hyperparameter search
Categorical and target encoding, scaling, missing values, interaction and time-based features, leakage prevention, feature selection

phases.build: A loan-default model on the Home Credit dataset with a leakage-safe scikit-learn feature pipeline, comparing logistic regression, random forest and LightGBM.

phases.title: Deep learning

steps.what: Backprop, CNNs, RNNs, transformers and attention, optimizers, normalization, regularization, transfer learning
Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoader, training loops, mixed precision, checkpointing, Lightning, torchvision models

phases.build: A PlantVillage plant-disease classifier comparing a CNN trained from scratch with a fine-tuned pretrained ViT, with training curves and confusion matrices.

phases.title: Evaluation and operations

steps.what: Metric choice, calibration, PR vs ROC, slice-based error analysis, offline-online gaps, significance of improvements, fairness checks
Experiment tracking, model registry, data versioning, reproducible pipelines, Dockerized serving, drift monitoring

phases.build: An evaluation report card for the image model: calibration plots, per-class and lighting-condition slice errors, significance tests vs baseline, tracked in MLflow with a Dockerized inference API.

statistician.summary: Start with the math and R, build rigorous inference and hypothesis testing, learn experimental design and sampling, then add SAS/SPSS, visualization and Python for industry work.

phases.title: Mathematics and R

steps.what: Calculus, matrix algebra for regression, probability axioms, random variables, expectation, common distributions
Vectors and data frames, tidyverse (dplyr, tidyr), writing functions, packages, reproducible reports in R Markdown or Quarto

phases.build: A reproducible Quarto report in R analysing a government dataset (e.g. PLFS or NFHS-5) with tidy cleaning code, summary tables and clearly stated findings.

phases.title: Statistical inference

steps.what: Estimation and MLE, linear and generalized linear models, ANOVA, residual diagnostics, nonparametric methods, Bayesian basics
Test statistics, p-values, power, t/chi-square/F tests, multiple testing corrections, effect sizes and their reporting

phases.build: A regression study in R on a public health dataset (e.g. determinants of birth weight) with model diagnostics, hypothesis tests, effect sizes and a written interpretation.

phases.title: Designing studies

steps.what: Randomization, blocking, factorial and fractional factorial designs, Latin squares, response surfaces, power and sample size
Simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling, survey weights, design effects, nonresponse adjustment

phases.build: Design and analyse a campus survey with stratified sampling by year and branch plus a randomized factorial experiment on study techniques, reporting weighted estimates with standard errors.

phases.title: Industry tools and communication

steps.what: SAS DATA step, PROC MEANS/FREQ/REG/GLM, SPSS menus and syntax, reproducing R analyses in both
ggplot2 grammar, faceting, showing uncertainty, publication-quality figures
pandas, scipy.stats and statsmodels for teams that work outside R

phases.build: Replicate the survey analysis in SAS and Python statsmodels, reconcile estimates against R, and publish a polished ggplot2 figure set with a methods appendix.

biostatistician.summary: Build statistics and SAS skills, then biostatistical methods in SAS and R, clinical trial design and survival analysis, and finally the regulatory and SAP-writing practice pharma expects.

phases.title: Statistics and SAS

steps.what: Probability, distributions, estimation, hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, linear and logistic regression
DATA step, PROC SQL, PROC FREQ/MEANS/TTEST/LOGISTIC, macros, ODS output, CDISC SDTM and ADaM dataset basics

phases.build: SAS programs that produce a demographics table and an adverse-event summary in standard TLF format from a public clinical dataset such as NHANES or Project Data Sphere.

phases.title: Biostatistical methods

steps.what: Binary and count outcomes, odds and risk ratios, logistic and Poisson regression, mixed models for repeated measures, missing data and multiple imputation
tidyverse, R Markdown, survival and lme4 packages, reproducing SAS outputs in R

phases.build: A longitudinal clinical analysis using mixed models for repeated measures and multiple imputation, with matching results in SAS and R and a reconciliation note.

phases.title: Trial design and survival

steps.what: Phases I-IV, randomization, blinding, endpoints, superiority and non-inferiority, sample size, interim analyses, adaptive designs, ICH E9
Censoring, Kaplan-Meier, log-rank test, Cox proportional hazards, assumption checks, competing risks

phases.build: Design a hypothetical Phase III non-inferiority trial (sample size, randomization, interim plan), then run Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses on a public trial dataset such as the veteran lung cancer data.

phases.title: Regulatory practice

steps.what: ICH E6/E9/E9(R1) estimands, 21 CFR Part 11, CDISC submission standards, FDA, EMA and CDSCO statistical guidance
SAP structure, analysis populations, endpoint definitions, missing-data handling, sensitivity analyses, mock TLF shells
Cohort and case-control designs, incidence and prevalence, confounding, bias, standardization

phases.build: A complete Statistical Analysis Plan with mock TLF shells for your designed trial, aligned to ICH E9(R1) estimands, with a short epidemiological background on the disease.

econometrician.summary: Ground yourself in economics, math and statistics, master econometrics in R or Stata, add causal inference and time series, then Python and structural models for industry work.

phases.title: Economics, math and statistics

steps.what: Calculus, constrained optimization with Lagrangians, matrix algebra
Consumer and producer theory, elasticity, market structure, macro basics (GDP, inflation, monetary policy), reading economics papers
Probability, distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, OLS intuition, sampling distributions

phases.build: A two-page policy brief on how a GST rate change affected a product category, using MOSPI or RBI data, supply-demand reasoning and summary statistics.

phases.title: Econometrics

steps.what: Data cleaning, regressions, robust and clustered standard errors, panel commands (xtreg, fixest), reproducible do-files and scripts
OLS assumptions, heteroskedasticity, endogeneity, IV and 2SLS, panel fixed and random effects, limited dependent variables, GMM basics

phases.build: Estimate returns to education in India from PLFS or IHDS microdata using OLS, IV and panel fixed effects, with robust standard errors in a publication-style regression table.

phases.title: Causal inference and time series

steps.what: Potential outcomes, DAGs, RCTs, difference-in-differences incl. staggered adoption, regression discontinuity, synthetic control, matching
Stationarity, unit-root tests, ARIMA, VAR, cointegration, structural breaks, forecast evaluation

phases.build: A difference-in-differences or synthetic-control evaluation of a real Indian policy (e.g. a state liquor ban) plus a VAR inflation forecast, in a fully replicable repo.

phases.title: Industry tooling and structural models

steps.what: pandas, statsmodels, linearmodels, DoWhy and EconML for causal ML, SQL data pulls
Discrete choice (logit, nested logit), BLP demand estimation basics, simulation-based estimation, counterfactual analysis

phases.build: Estimate a logit demand model for a smartphone or ride-hailing market with PyBLP on public or simulated data, and simulate price and market-share effects of a merger.

quant-analyst.summary: Build math, probability and Python, learn markets and stochastic calculus, master derivatives pricing and numerical methods, then production C++ and risk modeling.

phases.title: Math, probability and Python

steps.what: Multivariable calculus, Taylor series, ODE and PDE basics, matrix algebra, eigenvalues
Random variables, conditional expectation, distributions, moment generating functions, limit theorems, martingale intuition, brainteasers
NumPy vectorization, pandas time series, SciPy, OOP for pricing libraries, unit testing

phases.build: A NumPy Monte Carlo toolkit that simulates random walks and checks classic results (gambler's ruin, CLT, option-like payoffs) against closed-form answers, with unit tests.

phases.title: Markets and stochastic calculus

steps.what: Equities, bonds, FX, futures, options and swaps, market conventions, yield curves, how NSE derivatives trade
Brownian motion, Ito integral, Ito's lemma, SDEs, geometric Brownian motion, Girsanov, risk-neutral measure, Feynman-Kac

phases.build: Simulate GBM and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, verify Ito's lemma numerically, and fit GBM to NIFTY 50 daily data with a note on where the model breaks.

phases.title: Pricing and numerics

steps.what: Black-Scholes derivation and Greeks, binomial trees, put-call parity, implied volatility, volatility smile, exotics, intro to rate models
Finite-difference PDE schemes, Monte Carlo variance reduction, root finding, interpolation, optimization, numerical stability

phases.build: An option pricing library for European, American and barrier options via Black-Scholes, binomial trees, Crank-Nicolson and Monte Carlo, calibrating an implied vol surface from NIFTY option chains.

phases.title: Production C++ and risk

steps.what: Modern C++17/20, classes, templates, STL, smart pointers, memory and performance, CMake builds, pybind11 bindings
VaR and expected shortfall (historical, parametric, Monte Carlo), Greeks hedging, stress testing, VaR backtesting, FRTB overview

phases.build: Rewrite the pricing core in C++ with pybind11 bindings and benchmark it, then compute 1-day 99% VaR and ES for an options portfolio with Greeks hedging and a VaR backtest.

quant-researcher.summary: Build math, probability and Python, master statistical modeling and time series, then research and backtest signals honestly, adding ML and C++ for an edge.

phases.title: Math, probability and Python

steps.what: Linear algebra, calculus, optimization, eigenvectors and PCA intuition
Conditional probability, expectation, distributions, Bayes, Markov chains, martingales, interview-style puzzles
NumPy, pandas time-series ops, multi-index data, vectorization, Parquet storage, clean research code

phases.build: A cleaned NIFTY 500 daily price database in Parquet with corporate-action adjustments and delisted names kept, plus a notebook of Monte Carlo solutions to classic probability puzzles.

phases.title: Statistical modeling and time series

steps.what: Linear regression, ridge and lasso, robust regression, factor models, PCA, cross-sectional regressions, overfitting and multiple testing
Stationarity, autocorrelation, ARMA and GARCH, cointegration, regime changes, volatility modeling

phases.build: A GARCH volatility forecaster and a cointegration-based pairs screener for NIFTY stocks, with out-of-sample diagnostics and a factor-model decomposition of returns.

phases.title: Signals and backtesting

steps.what: Momentum, reversal, value and carry ideas, signal construction and normalization, information coefficient, decay, turnover, combining signals
Vectorized vs event-driven backtests, costs and slippage, look-ahead and survivorship bias, walk-forward testing, Sharpe, drawdown, deflated Sharpe

phases.build: A cross-sectional momentum plus short-term reversal strategy on NIFTY 500 with IC analysis, Indian costs (STT, brokerage, slippage), walk-forward backtest and a deflated Sharpe ratio.

phases.title: Machine learning and performance

steps.what: Gradient boosting for return prediction, purged k-fold CV, feature importance, regularization against noise, labeling methods
Modern C++, STL, profiling, cache-friendly data layout, writing a fast backtest or order-book kernel

phases.build: A LightGBM signal combiner with purged cross-validation compared against the linear blend, with the backtest's inner loop reimplemented in C++ and the speedup reported.

quant-trader.summary: Get sharp at probability and Python, learn statistics and market microstructure, then design, risk-manage and paper-trade real strategies while drilling mental math.

phases.title: Probability and Python

steps.what: Combinatorics, conditional probability, expected value, Bayes, distributions, Markov chains, betting games, Kelly criterion, brainteasers
pandas, NumPy, plotting, market-data APIs, writing clean simulation and analysis code

phases.build: A Python simulator of market-making and betting games (dice and card markets) measuring expected value and Kelly-optimal sizing against naive strategies over many runs.

phases.title: Statistics and microstructure

steps.what: Regression, correlation vs causation, hypothesis tests, volatility estimation, fat tails, time-series basics, overfitting
Order books, order types, bid-ask spread, market makers, latency, price impact, auctions, tick sizes, NSE/BSE mechanics

phases.build: An order-book replayer for LOBSTER or crypto exchange data that reconstructs the book, measures spread and depth over the day, and estimates price impact of market orders.

phases.title: Strategies, risk and speed

steps.what: Trend following, mean reversion, stat arb, market making, options strategies, signal to position, backtesting with costs, paper trading
Position sizing, stop rules, VaR, drawdown limits, Greeks exposure, correlation risk, P&L attribution
Fast arithmetic, fractions and percentages, quick EV estimates under time pressure, market-making games, daily timed drills

phases.build: A mean-reversion or market-making strategy paper-traded for four weeks on a broker sandbox or crypto testnet, with risk limits, daily P&L attribution and a written post-mortem.

experimentation-scientist.summary: Learn Python and SQL for product data, build deep statistics and experimental design, master A/B testing and causal inference, then variance reduction and metrics design.

phases.title: Product data tools

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, versioning analysis code
pandas, NumPy, functions and modules, simulation with random generators, plotting, Jupyter workflow
Joins, window functions, event-log queries, funnels, retention cohorts, assignment and exposure tables

phases.build: A SQL plus pandas analysis of the Google Analytics sample dataset on BigQuery computing funnels, retention cohorts and daily active users, with reusable query templates.

phases.title: Statistics and design

steps.what: Distributions, CLT, confidence intervals, t and z tests, power, bootstrap, delta method, multiple comparisons, Bayesian basics
Randomization units, stratification, factorial designs, interference and network effects, switchback and cluster designs, sample size

phases.build: A small Python package for power and sample size covering proportions, means and ratio metrics via the delta method, validated by simulation and documented with examples.

phases.title: A/B testing and causal inference

steps.what: Hypotheses, guardrail metrics, SRM checks, peeking and sequential testing, novelty effects, heterogeneous effects, reporting results
Potential outcomes, DAGs, difference-in-differences, propensity scores, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, synthetic control

phases.build: Analyze a public experiment end to end with SRM checks, sequential testing and segment effects, then re-estimate the effect observationally with propensity matching and compare.

phases.title: Platform-grade methods

steps.what: CUPED and CUPAC, stratification and post-stratification, regression adjustment, outlier capping, ratio-metric variance
