North-star vs guardrail metrics, sensitivity and directionality, metric decomposition, proxy metrics, overall evaluation criterion

phases.build: A mini experimentation platform in Streamlit that ingests assignment and metric tables, runs SRM, CUPED-adjusted and sequential tests, and reports the variance reduction achieved.

decision-scientist.summary: Start with SQL and a scripting language, build real statistical depth, then learn to frame business problems, reason causally and turn analysis into clear recommendations leaders act on.

phases.title: Data Toolkit

steps.what: Pivot tables, XLOOKUP and INDEX-MATCH, conditional aggregation, charts, scenario tables and Goal Seek for quick what-if analysis
SELECT/WHERE, joins, GROUP BY and HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LAG, running totals), date handling, cohort queries
pandas or dplyr for cleaning and reshaping, groupby aggregations, merging datasets, matplotlib or ggplot2 plots, Jupyter or RMarkdown notebooks

phases.build: A cohort retention analysis of a public e-commerce dataset (e.g. Olist on Kaggle): SQL queries for monthly cohorts and repeat-purchase rates, plus a notebook explaining which customer segments churn fastest and why.

phases.title: Statistical Reasoning and Business Context

steps.what: Distributions, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, power, linear and logistic regression, interpreting coefficients, multiple comparisons
Unit economics (CAC, LTV, contribution margin), P&L basics, pricing, funnels, market sizing, reading annual reports, framing a vague question as a decision

phases.build: A pricing memo for a real Indian D2C or quick-commerce company: estimate unit economics from public filings, regress demand on price using a public dataset, and recommend a price change with confidence intervals.

phases.title: Causal Thinking and Decisions

steps.what: Counterfactuals, confounding, DAGs, randomized experiments, difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity, propensity score matching, instrumental variables
Expected value, decision trees, sensitivity and tornado analysis, Monte Carlo simulation of uncertain inputs, value of information, cost-benefit framing

phases.build: A difference-in-differences study of a real policy or product launch (e.g. a state fuel-tax change) on public data, paired with a decision tree and Monte Carlo model quantifying the payoff of acting on the finding.

phases.title: Communicating Recommendations

steps.what: Pyramid principle, one-page executive memos, choosing the right chart, annotating insights, stating uncertainty plainly, structuring a 10-minute recommendation deck
KPI selection, data modeling for BI, filters and drill-downs, calculated fields, refresh schedules, designing each view around one decision

phases.build: A decision brief for a case-competition style problem: a one-page memo, a six-slide recommendation deck, and a live Tableau or Power BI dashboard tracking the KPIs the recommendation is expected to move.

actuary.summary: Build probability and financial-math foundations, learn life and general insurance models, model risk in Excel and R, and start clearing actuarial exams while learning the regulatory frame.

phases.title: Mathematical Foundations

steps.what: Differentiation and integration, series, partial derivatives, matrices and eigenvalues, numerical methods used in pricing and reserving
Random variables, discrete and continuous distributions (Poisson, gamma, Pareto), moments, conditional expectation, joint distributions, compound loss models
Advanced formulas, named ranges, data tables, Goal Seek and Solver, array functions, structured model layout with clear inputs, calculations and outputs

phases.build: An Excel-and-R workbook simulating aggregate annual claims for a motor insurance portfolio using Poisson frequency and gamma severity, with percentile tables showing the claims a reserve must cover.

phases.title: Interest Theory and Actuarial Models

steps.what: Time value of money, annuities, loan amortization, bond pricing, yield curves, duration and convexity, cash-flow matching, NPV and IRR
Life tables, survival models, assurance and annuity present values, premiums and reserves, multiple-decrement models, intro to general insurance pricing

phases.build: A term-life and endowment pricing tool using the Indian Assured Lives Mortality (2012-14) table: net premiums and policy-value reserves by age and term, with a sensitivity sheet on interest and mortality.

phases.title: Risk Modeling in Code

steps.what: Data frames, vectorized calculations, fitting distributions, simulation, plotting, reproducible scripts, tidyverse or pandas for claims data
Loss distributions, GLMs for frequency and severity, chain-ladder and Bornhuetter-Ferguson reserving, VaR and TVaR, credibility theory, stress scenarios

phases.build: A claims reserving project on a public loss triangle (e.g. CAS Schedule P data): chain-ladder and Bornhuetter-Ferguson reserves, bootstrapped reserve uncertainty, and a GLM pricing model for claim frequency.

phases.title: Regulation and the Exam Track

steps.what: IRDAI framework, solvency margins, the Appointed Actuary role, IFRS 17 basics, Solvency II and risk-based capital, product filing and policyholder protection
ACET entrance, then IAI CS1 (statistics) and CM1 (financial and actuarial maths), or SOA Exam P and FM; timed past-paper practice and exam-style R/Excel work

phases.build: A solvency report for a hypothetical Indian life insurer: reserves from your pricing model, an IRDAI-style solvency ratio under stressed mortality and interest, and a two-page board note, backed by an ACET or CS1 pass.

nlp-scientist.summary: Get fluent in Python and the maths of ML, master deep learning in PyTorch, then move from classic NLP to transformers, fine-tuning, retrieval and rigorous evaluation of language models.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Linear algebra (vectors, matrix products, SVD), calculus and gradients, probability, softmax and cross-entropy, basic information theory
Commits, branches, pull requests, .gitignore, cloning and running research repos
Data structures, functions, classes, comprehensions, NumPy arrays, file I/O, virtual environments, writing clean scripts and notebooks

phases.build: A from-scratch NumPy implementation of a bigram language model and a logistic-regression text classifier with gradient checks, published on GitHub with a clear README and results table.

phases.title: Deep Learning

steps.what: Backpropagation, MLPs, optimizers (SGD, Adam), regularization, batch and layer norm, CNNs, RNNs and LSTMs, attention, training diagnostics
Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, Dataset and DataLoader, training loops, GPU usage, checkpointing, mixed precision, experiment logging

phases.build: A character-level LSTM and a small attention model trained in PyTorch on an Indian-language corpus (e.g. Hindi Wikipedia), with loss curves, sample generations and an ablation table logged in Weights & Biases.

phases.title: Core NLP and Language

steps.what: Tokenization (BPE, WordPiece), word embeddings, text classification, NER, sequence labeling, seq2seq, language modeling and perplexity
Morphology, syntax and dependency parsing, semantics, code-mixing and script issues in Indian languages, why tokenizers struggle on agglutinative text

phases.build: A named-entity recognizer for Hindi or Tamil trained on AI4Bharat's Naamapadam data, comparing a CRF baseline with a BiLSTM, with an error analysis of code-mixed and morphologically rich cases.

phases.title: Transformers, Adaptation and Evaluation

steps.what: Self-attention, positional encodings, encoder vs decoder models, pretraining objectives, scaling laws, decoding strategies, implementing a small GPT from scratch
Full fine-tuning vs LoRA and QLoRA, instruction tuning, embeddings, chunking, vector search, retrieval-augmented generation, reranking
Benchmarks and held-out splits, BLEU, ROUGE and F1, LLM-as-judge pitfalls, data contamination, significance testing, human evaluation design

phases.build: LoRA-fine-tune a small open LLM for question answering over Indian government documents, add a RAG pipeline, and publish an evaluation report comparing base, fine-tuned and RAG variants with significance tests.

cv-scientist.summary: Build Python and math foundations, learn image processing and deep learning in PyTorch, then go deep on detection, segmentation and 3D vision before optimizing models for real-time GPU deployment.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Vectors, matrices, geometric transformations, SVD, eigenvectors, gradients and the chain rule, probability basics for ML
Commits, branches, pull requests, cloning and running research repos
Data structures, OOP, NumPy broadcasting and slicing, reading images as arrays, plotting with matplotlib, writing reusable modules

phases.build: An image toolkit written in pure NumPy: convolution, Gaussian blur, Sobel edges and affine warps implemented from scratch and benchmarked for correctness and speed against OpenCV on sample photos.

phases.title: Images and Deep Learning

steps.what: Color spaces, filtering, histograms, morphology, edge and corner detection, feature descriptors (SIFT, ORB), homographies, sensor noise
Backpropagation, CNN architectures (ResNet, EfficientNet), vision transformers, augmentation, transfer learning, regularization, debugging training runs
Tensors, autograd, custom Datasets and DataLoaders, training loops, mixed precision, torchvision models, checkpointing and logging

phases.build: A panorama stitcher using ORB features and RANSAC homographies, plus a transfer-learned ResNet classifier for crop-disease leaf images with Grad-CAM maps showing what the model attends to.

phases.title: Computer Vision Depth

steps.what: Object detection (YOLO, DETR), semantic and instance segmentation (U-Net, Mask R-CNN), tracking, self-supervised learning, mAP and IoU evaluation
Pinhole camera model, intrinsics and extrinsics, epipolar geometry, stereo depth, triangulation, point clouds, intro to NeRF and Gaussian splatting

phases.build: A pothole and road-hazard detector trained on the India Driving Dataset (IDD) with per-class mAP reported, plus a stereo depth module that estimates the distance to each detected hazard.

phases.title: Optimization and GPU Deployment

steps.what: Post-training and quantization-aware quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation, ONNX export, TensorRT engines, profiling latency vs accuracy
GPU memory hierarchy, kernels, threads and blocks, profiling with Nsight, writing a simple custom CUDA or Triton kernel, batching for throughput

phases.build: Compress your road detector to INT8 with TensorRT, report the accuracy-latency tradeoff, and run it in real time on a Jetson Nano or laptop GPU with a custom CUDA preprocessing kernel.

product-data-scientist.summary: Learn SQL and Python for product data, ground yourself in statistics and product analytics, then master metric design, A/B testing and communicating results that shape a product roadmap.

phases.title: Querying and Wrangling Product Data

steps.what: Pivot tables, lookups, conditional formulas, quick charts, sanity-checking numbers before they reach a deck
Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs, window functions, funnel and retention queries, sessionization of event logs, date bucketing, query performance basics
pandas for event data, groupby and pivots, merging, plotting with seaborn, writing reusable analysis notebooks

phases.build: A funnel and retention analysis of the Google Analytics sample dataset in BigQuery: SQL for sessionized funnels and weekly retention cohorts, with a notebook pinpointing the biggest drop-off step.

phases.title: Statistics and Product Analytics

steps.what: Sampling distributions, confidence intervals, t-tests and proportion tests, regression, variance of ratio metrics, heavy-tailed data, bootstrapping
AARRR funnels, retention curves, cohorts, engagement (DAU/MAU), segmentation, opportunity sizing, root-causing metric drops

phases.build: A metric-drop investigation on a public app-event dataset: decompose a simulated 8% DAU drop by platform, region and cohort, size each driver with confidence intervals, and write up the likely root cause.

phases.title: Metrics and Experiments

steps.what: North-star and input metrics, guardrails, metric trees, ratio vs count metrics, sensitivity and gaming risks, defining metrics precisely in SQL
Hypotheses, randomization units, power and sample size, CUPED variance reduction, novelty effects, sample ratio mismatch, peeking and sequential tests

phases.build: An experiment toolkit in Python (power calculator, SRM check, CUPED adjustment, readout generator) demonstrated on the Cookie Cats A/B dataset, with a metric tree for the feature being tested.

phases.title: Influence and Reporting

steps.what: Writing experiment readouts, framing tradeoffs for PMs, pushing back on over-reading data, running metric reviews, product-sense case interviews
Product health dashboards, self-serve exploration, filters and drill-downs, metric definitions in the BI layer, anomaly alerts

phases.build: A product-health dashboard in Metabase or Looker Studio for a public app dataset, plus a one-page product review memo recommending one roadmap change, written as if presented to a PM.

marketing-scientist.summary: Get strong in SQL, Python/R and statistics, learn how marketing funnels are measured, then progress to attribution, causal lift measurement, media-mix models and forecasts that move budgets.

phases.title: Data Foundations

steps.what: Pivot tables, lookups, campaign performance sheets, ROAS and CPA calculations, basic charts
Joins across campaign, click and order tables, CTEs, window functions, first-touch and last-touch lookups, cohort revenue queries
pandas or dplyr wrangling, time-series handling, visualization, regression with statsmodels or lm, notebook workflows

phases.build: A channel performance mart on the Google Merchandise Store BigQuery sample with simulated spend: SQL models for spend, sessions and revenue by channel, and a notebook comparing CAC and ROAS across channels.

phases.title: Statistics and Marketing Measurement

steps.what: Distributions, hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, linear and logistic regression, multicollinearity, time-series basics, bootstrapping
Funnel metrics, CAC, LTV, ROAS, RFM segmentation, churn and retention, campaign reporting, channel mix in Indian D2C and e-commerce

phases.build: An LTV and churn model on the UCI Online Retail II dataset: RFM segments, a logistic churn model, BG/NBD lifetime value estimates, and a recommendation on which segment deserves retention budget.

phases.title: Attribution and Causal Lift

steps.what: Last-click vs multi-touch, position-based and data-driven models, Markov-chain removal effects, Shapley attribution, limits under privacy changes
Randomized holdouts, geo experiments, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, propensity matching, incrementality vs correlation

phases.build: A Markov-chain attribution model on a public customer-journey dataset compared against last-click, plus a synthetic-control analysis estimating the incremental lift of a simulated city-level campaign.

phases.title: Media Mix and Forecasting

steps.what: Adstock and saturation curves, Bayesian regression MMM, priors, calibrating with lift experiments, response curves, budget optimization
Trend and seasonality, festive-season and sale-event effects, ARIMA, Prophet, backtesting, forecast error metrics (MAPE, WAPE)

phases.build: A media-mix model built with PyMC-Marketing or Robyn on a public MMM dataset, with per-channel response curves, an optimized budget split, and a 12-week sales forecast that accounts for festive-season peaks.

or-scientist.summary: Start with the maths and Python, learn to turn messy operational problems into models, master linear and integer optimization with real solvers, then add simulation and classic OR applications.

phases.title: Math and Programming Foundations

steps.what: Matrices, systems of equations, convexity, gradients, Lagrange multipliers, basic graph theory (shortest paths, network flows)
Data structures, functions, classes, NumPy, pandas, loading problem data from CSV, writing clean modular scripts

phases.build: A Python routing helper that loads a real road network for an Indian city with OSMnx and computes shortest paths and travel-time matrices between a set of delivery points.

phases.title: Modeling and Linear Programming

steps.what: Decision variables, objectives, constraints, translating word problems into formulations, binary logic and big-M constraints, validating assumptions
Simplex method, duality and shadow prices, sensitivity analysis, transportation and assignment problems, network flow formulations

phases.build: A production-planning LP for a hypothetical FMCG plant with multiple products, capacity and demand constraints, solved in PuLP, with a shadow-price report explaining which constraint is worth relaxing.

phases.title: Optimization at Scale

steps.what: Integer and mixed-integer programming, branch and bound, cutting planes, heuristics and metaheuristics, column generation, convex and nonlinear basics
Gurobi and CPLEX Python APIs, solver parameters, MIP gaps, warm starts, callbacks, reading solver logs, academic licenses vs open-source HiGHS and CBC

phases.build: A last-mile vehicle-routing solver with time windows on real city coordinates, formulated as a MIP in Gurobi and compared against an OR-Tools heuristic on cost, runtime and optimality gap.

phases.title: Operations Research in Practice

steps.what: Queueing theory, inventory models (EOQ, newsvendor), scheduling, facility location, crew rostering, Markov decision processes, airline and logistics cases
Probability distributions, fitting demand and arrival data, goodness-of-fit, confidence intervals, regression for forecasting optimization inputs
Discrete-event simulation, Monte Carlo, random variate generation, warm-up and replications, output analysis, stress-testing optimized plans

phases.build: A warehouse or hospital-OPD capacity study: fit arrival distributions from data, simulate queues in SimPy, then optimize staffing with an integer program and show wait times before and after.

bioinformatics-scientist.summary: Learn Python/R, Linux and the molecular biology an engineer usually lacks, add statistics and genomics, then build reproducible sequencing pipelines and apply machine learning to biological data.

phases.title: Computing Foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, versioning analysis code and pipelines, sharing reproducible work on GitHub
Python with pandas and Biopython for sequence files, R with tidyverse and Bioconductor basics, plotting, reusable functions and scripts
Shell navigation, grep/awk/sed on FASTA and VCF files, pipes, conda environments, SSH, SLURM job scripts, managing large files on clusters

phases.build: A command-line toolkit that parses FASTA/FASTQ files and reports GC content, read-length and quality summaries, runnable as a SLURM batch job, with Biopython code and a README on GitHub.

phases.title: Biology and Statistics

steps.what: DNA, RNA and protein, the central dogma, gene structure, transcription and regulation, mutations and variants, PCR, how sequencing experiments are designed
Hypothesis testing, multiple testing correction (FDR), linear models, count distributions (Poisson, negative binomial), PCA and clustering

phases.build: A gene-expression analysis of a public GEO dataset: normalize, test for differential expression with FDR control, run PCA, and annotate the top genes with their biological function.

phases.title: Genomics and Core Bioinformatics

steps.what: Genome assemblies and annotation, sequencing technologies (Illumina, Nanopore), SNPs and indels, population genetics basics, GWAS, reference resources
Sequence alignment (Smith-Waterman, BLAST), read mapping, variant calling, RNA-seq quantification, DESeq2, phylogenetics, SAM/BAM/VCF formats

phases.build: An end-to-end RNA-seq differential expression study on a public SRA dataset: quantify with Salmon, run DESeq2, and produce volcano plots and pathway enrichment with a written interpretation.

phases.title: Pipelines and Machine Learning

steps.what: Workflow managers, modular pipeline steps, containerized tools, QC with FastQC and MultiQC, resuming runs, nf-core pipelines, reproducible configs
Classification and clustering on omics data, feature selection in high dimensions, cross-validation, random forests, intro to single-cell analysis

phases.build: A Nextflow or Snakemake variant-calling pipeline (FastQC, BWA, GATK) run on public 1000 Genomes samples with a MultiQC report, plus a classifier predicting population ancestry from the called variants.

causal-inference-scientist.summary: Build probability and Python/R foundations, get rigorous in statistics and experimental design, then master econometrics and modern causal methods before extending to uplift and Bayesian approaches.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Random variables, expectation, conditional probability, matrix algebra for regression, OLS in matrix form
pandas or tidyverse, simulation, regression with statsmodels or lm, plotting, reproducible notebooks or Quarto reports

phases.build: A simulation notebook showing how confounding biases a naive regression: generate data from a known causal model, compare naive and adjusted estimates, and plot the bias as confounding strength grows.

phases.title: Statistics and Experiments

steps.what: Estimation, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, linear and logistic regression, robust and clustered standard errors, bootstrap, multiple testing
Randomization, blocking and stratification, power analysis, cluster randomization, interference, CUPED, pre-registration, analyzing RCTs

phases.build: A design report for a proposed field experiment (e.g. SMS reminders to improve loan repayment in India): stratified randomization plan, power curves, and a simulated pre-registered analysis.

phases.title: Econometrics and Causal Methods

steps.what: OLS assumptions, endogeneity, instrumental variables and 2SLS, panel data with fixed effects, heteroskedasticity, time-series basics
Potential outcomes, DAGs and the backdoor criterion, matching and weighting, staggered difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity, synthetic control, double ML

phases.build: A replication and extension of a published natural-experiment study (e.g. on NREGA or minimum wages) using its public data, with difference-in-differences and IV estimates, robustness checks and a written critique.

phases.title: Heterogeneous Effects and Extensions

steps.what: Conditional average treatment effects, T-, S- and X-learners, causal forests, Qini and uplift curves, targeting treatment to persuadable users
Priors and posteriors, MCMC, hierarchical models, Bayesian A/B tests, Bayesian structural time series for impact estimation
Joins, aggregations, window functions, building treatment and outcome tables from event logs for causal analysis

phases.build: An uplift model on the Hillstrom email-marketing dataset ranking customers by treatment effect, with Qini curves, a targeting policy that beats treat-everyone, and a Bayesian estimate of overall campaign lift.

risk-quant.summary: Learn Python and probability, build strong statistics and financial maths, then model credit and market risk and practise validating models the way regulators expect.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Lookups, pivot tables, data tables, Solver, structuring a model with clear inputs, calculations and outputs
Distributions, expectation and variance, covariance matrices, correlation, matrix operations used in portfolio risk
pandas for financial time series, NumPy vectorization, plotting, functions and classes, writing testable model code

phases.build: A Python notebook that pulls NSE index data with yfinance, computes returns, volatility and correlation matrices, and compares historical and parametric volatility through the 2020 COVID crash.

phases.title: Statistics and Financial Maths

steps.what: Linear and logistic regression, maximum likelihood, time series (ARIMA, GARCH), goodness-of-fit tests, backtesting statistics, bootstrap
Time value of money, bond pricing and duration, yield curves, options and Black-Scholes, Greeks, stochastic processes and Monte Carlo pricing

phases.build: A pricing and volatility toolkit: bond pricer with duration and convexity, Black-Scholes and Monte Carlo option pricer with Greeks, and a GARCH volatility forecast for Nifty 50 returns.

phases.title: Risk Models

steps.what: VaR (historical, parametric, Monte Carlo), Expected Shortfall, stress testing, scenario design, PD/LGD/EAD models, expected credit loss
Credit scorecards with WoE and IV, rating migration, IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109 ECL, market risk factors and sensitivities, counterparty risk basics

phases.build: A credit-risk model on the Home Credit dataset: a WoE-based logistic PD scorecard, LGD assumptions and an expected-credit-loss calculation, plus 99% VaR and Expected Shortfall for a sample equity portfolio.

phases.title: Validation and Governance

steps.what: Conceptual soundness reviews, discrimination (Gini, KS, AUC), calibration, stability (PSI), VaR backtesting (Kupiec), benchmarking, documentation
Basel III capital and RWA, IRB approach, FRTB basics, CCAR/DFAST stress tests, SR 11-7 model risk guidance, RBI expectations on model risk
Joins, aggregations and window functions to build loan-level and portfolio datasets, data lineage checks on model inputs

phases.build: An independent validation report on your own PD scorecard in SR 11-7 style: Gini and KS, calibration by decile, PSI on a later cohort, a VaR backtest, identified weaknesses and a remediation plan.

survey-statistician.summary: Build statistics and R skills, learn how surveys and samples are designed, then master weighting and estimation, data cleaning and the SAS/SPSS tools used in official statistics and market research.

phases.title: Statistics Foundations

steps.what: Data entry checks, pivot tables, frequency tables, cross-tabulations, simple charts
Probability, sampling distributions, estimation, standard errors, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, regression, categorical data analysis
tidyverse wrangling, factors and labelled data, ggplot2, writing functions, reproducible reports in Quarto or RMarkdown

phases.build: A Quarto report analyzing public NFHS-5 state factsheet data: cross-tabs, confidence intervals and a regression on a child-health indicator, fully reproducible from the raw files.

phases.title: Survey and Sampling Design

steps.what: Total survey error, questionnaire design, wording and order effects, modes (CAPI, CATI, web), pretesting, non-response and coverage error
Simple random, stratified, cluster and multistage sampling, PPS selection, design effects, sample size calculation, sampling frames such as census villages

phases.build: A full design for a district-level household survey: stratified multistage PPS sample from census village frames, sample size and design-effect calculations, and a pretested KoboToolbox questionnaire.

phases.title: Weighting and Estimation

steps.what: Design weights, non-response adjustment, post-stratification, raking, calibration, variance estimation (linearization, jackknife, bootstrap), small-area basics
Consistency and range checks, skip-pattern validation, outlier review, imputation for item non-response, codebooks and audit trails

phases.build: Weighted estimates from public PLFS unit-level data: clean the file, apply the published multipliers, compute state unemployment rates with design-based standard errors, and reconcile them with the official report.

phases.title: Industry Tools

steps.what: SAS DATA steps and PROC SURVEYMEANS/SURVEYFREQ, SPSS syntax and the Complex Samples module, reading and writing labelled datasets
pandas for survey microdata, weighted statistics, design-based estimation with samplics, automating tables and charts

phases.build: Reproduce your PLFS estimates in SAS PROC SURVEY procedures and in Python with samplics, document any differences, and package an automated script that outputs publication-ready tables.

ml-eng.summary: Get solid in Python, Git and ML maths, learn modeling and a deep learning framework, then build the data, serving, MLOps and cloud skills needed to run models in production.

phases.title: Engineering and Math Foundations

steps.what: Git branches and pull requests, Linux shell, permissions, processes, SSH, environment variables, small Bash scripts
Linear algebra, gradients and the chain rule, probability, distributions, loss functions and optimization intuition
OOP, type hints, packaging, virtual environments, NumPy and pandas, pytest, logging, writing clean modules instead of only notebooks

phases.build: A pip-installable Python package that loads, validates and splits a tabular dataset, with type hints, pytest coverage and a GitHub Actions CI badge.

phases.title: Modeling

steps.what: Bias-variance, train/val/test splits, cross-validation, linear models, trees and gradient boosting, metrics (AUC, F1, RMSE), class imbalance, error analysis
Tensors and autograd, building models, custom training loops, DataLoaders, GPU training, transfer learning, saving and exporting models

phases.build: A loan-default model with LightGBM and a PyTorch tabular baseline on the Home Credit dataset, compared rigorously with cross-validation and error analysis, with every experiment reproducible from config.

phases.title: Data and Features

steps.what: Joins, window functions, CTEs, point-in-time correct joins for training data, aggregations over event tables
Encoding categoricals, scaling, time-based and aggregate features, leakage prevention, text and embedding features, scikit-learn pipelines

phases.build: A leakage-safe feature pipeline that builds point-in-time features in SQL from raw event tables for a fraud or recommendation task, with a test proving no future data leaks into training.

phases.title: Serving Models

steps.what: REST APIs with FastAPI, request validation, batching, latency and throughput, ONNX export, model servers, load testing
Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, images and registries, Compose, Kubernetes pods, deployments, services, autoscaling basics

phases.build: A containerized FastAPI service serving your model with input validation and batching, load-tested with Locust to report p95 latency, and deployed on a local Kubernetes cluster with autoscaling.

phases.title: MLOps and Cloud

steps.what: Experiment tracking, model registry, data and model versioning, automated retraining, CI tests for models, drift monitoring, GitHub Actions pipelines
Object storage, compute instances, managed ML services (SageMaker, Vertex AI), IAM basics, cost control, deploying a container to a managed service

phases.build: An end-to-end ML system on AWS or GCP free tier: MLflow-tracked training, DVC-versioned data, a GitHub Actions pipeline that retrains and redeploys on new data, and a scheduled Evidently drift report.

ai-eng.summary: Become a strong Python developer, learn to call and prompt LLMs well, then build retrieval, agents, evals and a production backend before touching fine-tuning and cloud deployment.

phases.title: Programming Foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, environment files and keeping API keys out of repositories
HTTP methods, JSON, REST conventions, auth headers, rate limits, retries with backoff, streaming responses (SSE)
Data structures, OOP, type hints, async/await, httpx, Pydantic models, error handling, pytest, packaging a small project

phases.build: An async Python CLI that calls several public REST APIs concurrently with retries and rate limiting, validates every response with Pydantic, and ships with pytest coverage.

phases.title: Working with LLMs

steps.what: Chat/messages APIs, system prompts, streaming, tool calling, structured JSON output, context limits, cost and latency, local open-weight models
Clear instructions, few-shot examples, reasoning vs direct answers, output schemas, prompt templates and versioning, defending against prompt injection

phases.build: A structured-extraction service that turns messy invoices or resumes into validated JSON using tool calling, with versioned prompts and a comparison of two models on accuracy, latency and cost.

phases.title: Retrieval and Agents

steps.what: Embeddings, chunking strategies, vector indexes (HNSW), hybrid search with BM25, reranking, metadata filtering, citing sources
Tool-use loops, planning, memory, multi-step workflows as state machines, human-in-the-loop, MCP servers, failure handling and timeouts

phases.build: A RAG assistant over a university's syllabus, regulations and past papers with hybrid search, reranking and cited answers, extended into an agent that can also look up timetables through a tool.

phases.title: Shipping Reliable AI Products

steps.what: TypeScript basics, Node or FastAPI backends, REST endpoints, streaming to a frontend, auth, Postgres, background jobs, deploying a web app
Golden datasets, LLM-as-judge with rubrics, retrieval metrics, regression tests in CI, input and output filtering, PII redaction, hallucination checks

phases.build: Ship your RAG assistant as a deployed web app with a Next.js streaming UI and a FastAPI backend, plus an eval suite of 100+ graded questions that runs in CI and blocks releases when answer quality drops.

phases.title: Customizing and Deploying Models

steps.what: When to fine-tune vs prompt or RAG, dataset preparation, LoRA and QLoRA, supervised fine-tuning, evaluating against the base model, serving adapters
Containers, serverless functions, managed databases, secrets management, GPU instances, monitoring usage and spend

phases.build: LoRA-fine-tune a small open model to classify Hinglish support tickets, compare it with a prompted frontier model on your eval set, and deploy the winner behind an API with cost and latency dashboards.

mlops-eng.summary: Start with Linux, Git, Python and ML basics, then containers and Kubernetes, then model lifecycle tooling and CI/CD, cloud infrastructure as code, and finally monitoring and feature stores.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Shell, file system, permissions, processes, systemd, networking basics (ports, DNS), SSH, Bash scripting with loops and error handling
Branching strategies, pull requests, rebasing, tags and releases, monorepo vs polyrepo basics
Training vs inference, train/test splits, metrics, overfitting, scikit-learn and PyTorch training loops, model artifacts and serialization
OOP, packaging, virtual environments, CLI tools, logging, pytest, YAML and JSON configs, calling REST APIs

phases.build: A Python CLI that trains a scikit-learn model from a YAML config, saves versioned artifacts with metadata, is tested with pytest, and runs end to end from one Bash script on a fresh Linux VM.

phases.title: Containers and Orchestration

steps.what: Dockerfiles, layers and caching, multi-stage builds, slim images for ML, GPU containers, Compose, registries
Pods, deployments, services, ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, resource limits, GPU scheduling, Jobs, Helm charts, autoscaling, kubectl debugging

phases.build: Containerize a model-serving API and deploy it on a kind or minikube cluster with a Helm chart, health checks, resource limits and a horizontal pod autoscaler demonstrated under load.

phases.title: Model Lifecycle and Automation

steps.what: Experiment tracking, model registry and stages, pipeline components, Kubeflow Pipelines, hyperparameter runs, reproducible training with DVC
GitHub Actions workflows, testing data and model code, building and pushing images, staged rollouts, canary and shadow deployments, GitOps

phases.build: An MLflow or Kubeflow training pipeline whose GitHub Actions workflow retrains on new data, registers the model only if it beats the current champion, and rolls it out to the cluster via Argo CD.

phases.title: Cloud and Infrastructure as Code

steps.what: IAM, VPCs, object storage, managed Kubernetes (EKS, GKE), SageMaker or Vertex AI, GPU instances, cost monitoring and budgets
Providers, resources, variables, modules, remote state, plan/apply workflow, provisioning clusters and buckets, detecting drift

phases.build: Terraform modules that provision a small EKS or GKE cluster, an artifact bucket and an MLflow tracking server, with remote state and a teardown script that keeps the bill within free-tier credits.

phases.title: Production ML Operations

steps.what: Data and prediction drift, data quality checks, latency and error metrics, alerting, dashboards, delayed ground truth, triggering retraining
Offline vs online stores, point-in-time joins, feature definitions, materialization, preventing training-serving skew

phases.build: A monitoring stack for your deployed model: Prometheus and Grafana dashboards for latency and errors, scheduled Evidently drift reports, and a Feast feature store serving identical features online and offline.

ml-platform-eng.summary: Learn Linux, Git, Python and containers, then Kubernetes and distributed systems, then Go and API design for platform services, and finally orchestration, cloud, feature stores and Spark.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Shell, processes, permissions, networking basics, SSH, systemd, Bash scripting
Branching, pull requests, code review etiquette, tags and releases
Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, layer caching, registries, Compose, GPU-enabled images
How data scientists train, track and deploy models: notebooks, training loops, hyperparameter sweeps, model artifacts, batch vs online inference
OOP, type hints, async, packaging, building CLIs and SDKs, pytest, designing libraries other engineers import

phases.build: A pip-installable Python SDK and CLI that lets a data scientist package a training script into a Docker image and run it locally with one command, with tests and usage docs.

phases.title: Kubernetes and Distributed Systems

steps.what: Workloads, services, ingress, RBAC, namespaces and quotas, GPU scheduling, Jobs, operators and CRDs, Helm, debugging
Replication and consistency, consensus (Raft), partitioning, queues, failures and retries, data and model parallel training, Ray clusters

phases.build: Extend your SDK to submit training jobs to Kubernetes with per-team namespaces and GPU quotas, and run a distributed Ray training job that recovers when a worker pod is killed mid-run.

phases.title: Platform Services

steps.what: Syntax, structs and interfaces, goroutines and channels, error handling, net/http, testing, building Kubernetes controllers with client-go
REST and gRPC, resource modeling, versioning, pagination, idempotency, auth, OpenAPI specs, designing for internal users

phases.build: A Go service with a gRPC/REST API and a Kubebuilder operator managing a custom TrainingJob resource: create, track status, retry on failure, and clean up finished jobs.

phases.title: Pipelines and Cloud

steps.what: DAGs, scheduling, retries, backfills, parameterized pipelines, Argo Workflows on Kubernetes, artifact passing, Airflow operators
IAM, VPC networking, managed Kubernetes (EKS, GKE), object storage, GPU instance types and quotas, cost attribution per team

phases.build: A self-serve pipeline template: an Argo Workflows DAG for data prep, training and evaluation on a GKE or EKS cluster, triggered from your SDK, with per-team cost tags on every cloud resource.

phases.title: Data Layer for ML

steps.what: Offline and online stores, feature registries, point-in-time joins, materialization jobs, training-serving consistency
DataFrames, partitions and shuffles, Spark SQL, PySpark feature jobs, Spark on Kubernetes, performance tuning basics

phases.build: A feature platform slice: PySpark jobs compute features from a public event dataset, Feast registers and materializes them to Redis, and your pipeline template trains offline and serves online.

ml-infra-eng.summary: From Linux and Python to writing CUDA kernels, scaling PyTorch training across GPUs, and running the Kubernetes and Slurm clusters that keep expensive accelerators busy.

phases.title: Systems foundations

steps.what: Shell, processes, file systems, systemd, SSH, environment modules, reading nvidia-smi/top/htop, bash scripting for job automation
Branching, rebasing, pull requests, tagging releases, working in a shared repo with code review
Packaging and virtualenvs, typing, multiprocessing vs threading, asyncio basics, profiling with cProfile, writing CLI tools and tests
Tensors, autograd, training loops, optimizers, mixed precision, checkpointing; train ResNet and GPT-2 small end to end
Images, layers, multi-stage builds, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, GPU-enabled containers, pushing to a registry

phases.build: A containerized training repo that trains ResNet-50 on an ImageNet subset with one command, logging GPU utilization, memory and samples/sec per epoch, with tests and CI on GitHub.

phases.title: GPU programming

steps.what: Pointers, memory layout, RAII, templates, STL, CMake builds, writing a PyTorch C++ extension with pybind11
GPU architecture (SMs, warps, memory hierarchy), kernels, shared-memory tiling, coalescing, streams, occupancy, Nsight profiling, Triton kernels

phases.build: A small GPU kernel library (tiled matmul, softmax, layernorm) in CUDA and Triton, exposed to PyTorch as custom ops, with a benchmark report against cuBLAS and Nsight profiles explaining each speedup.

phases.title: Distributed training

steps.what: DDP, FSDP/ZeRO sharding, tensor and pipeline parallelism, gradient accumulation, activation checkpointing, torchrun, fault-tolerant checkpoints
Collectives (all-reduce, all-gather), ring vs tree algorithms, NVLink, InfiniBand/RoCE basics, nccl-tests, NCCL env tuning, debugging hangs
Dispatcher, autograd engine, CUDA caching allocator, memory snapshots, torch.compile and Inductor, reading PyTorch Profiler traces

phases.build: Scale GPT-2 small training from 1 to 4+ GPUs (cloud or Kaggle 2xT4) with DDP then FSDP, publishing scaling efficiency, all-reduce bandwidth from nccl-tests, and a profiler trace diagnosing the main bottleneck.

phases.title: Clusters and scheduling

steps.what: Pods, deployments, jobs, Helm, NVIDIA GPU Operator and device plugin, Kubeflow PyTorchJob, resource quotas and node affinity for GPUs
GPU instance types (A100/H100/L4), spot vs reserved, cluster topology, DCGM monitoring, Prometheus/Grafana, utilization and cost tracking
sbatch and srun, partitions, job arrays, multi-node launches with torchrun, accounting, and when HPC schedulers beat Kubernetes

phases.build: A mini GPU training platform: a Kubernetes cluster with the GPU device plugin running queued PyTorchJob runs, DCGM + Grafana utilization dashboards, and an equivalent Slurm sbatch setup compared in a write-up.

cv-eng.summary: From Python and the math of images, through classical OpenCV and CNN-based detection and segmentation, to optimized real-time models running in C++ on edge devices.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, .gitignore for large data, versioning datasets with Git LFS or DVC
Vectors, matrices, geometric transformations, eigenvalues, derivatives and the chain rule, convolution as an operation, basic probability
NumPy array ops and broadcasting, Matplotlib, OOP, reading images and video files, virtualenvs, writing clean scripts and tests

phases.build: Implement image convolution, Sobel edge detection, histogram equalization and resizing from scratch in NumPy, verified against library outputs, in a tested GitHub repo with a visual comparison notebook.

phases.title: Classical computer vision

steps.what: Color spaces, filtering, thresholding, morphology, contours, Hough transforms, ORB/SIFT features, homography, video capture and object tracking
Collecting images, labeling boxes, masks and keypoints, COCO/YOLO formats, label QA, class balance, leakage-free train/val/test splits

phases.build: A number-plate reader for Indian dashcam footage using contours, morphology and perspective warps, plus a 500-image plate dataset you labeled in CVAT and exported in COCO and YOLO formats.

phases.title: Deep learning for vision

steps.what: Tensors, autograd, Dataset/DataLoader, augmentation with torchvision and Albumentations, training loops, mixed precision, checkpointing
Backprop, conv and pooling, ResNet, transfer learning, detection (YOLO, Faster R-CNN), segmentation (U-Net, Mask R-CNN), mAP and IoU

phases.build: Train a YOLO detector and a U-Net segmenter on your own annotated dataset, report mAP and IoU with an error analysis of failure cases, and compare accuracy and speed against your classical OpenCV pipeline.

phases.title: Deployment and speed

steps.what: ONNX export, post-training and quantization-aware INT8, pruning, TensorRT and OpenVINO, batching, measuring latency and throughput vs accuracy
Modern C++ (RAII, smart pointers, STL), CMake, the OpenCV C++ API, running ONNX Runtime or TensorRT inference from C++

phases.build: Run your INT8-quantized detector in a C++ app on a webcam stream or a Jetson/Raspberry Pi at real-time FPS, with a table of latency, model size and mAP before and after optimization.

phases.title: Going deeper

steps.what: Pinhole camera model, intrinsics and extrinsics, calibration, epipolar geometry, stereo depth, triangulation, point clouds
GPU architecture basics, writing kernels, memory coalescing, CUDA streams, accelerating image preprocessing

phases.build: Calibrate a phone camera and build a stereo-depth or monocular visual-odometry demo with Open3D point clouds, plus a CUDA resize-and-normalize kernel benchmarked against the CPU OpenCV path.

nlp-eng.summary: From Python and ML basics through classical text pipelines and transformers to fine-tuning LLMs and building retrieval, with careful evaluation at every step.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, code review, keeping experiments and data versions alongside code
Vectors, matrix multiplication, softmax, probability distributions, Bayes rule, entropy and cross-entropy, gradients
Strings and Unicode, regex, comprehensions, generators for streaming large text files, NumPy, pandas, writing tested modules

phases.build: A text-statistics CLI that streams a large Hindi + English Wikipedia dump, handles Unicode normalization, and reports vocabulary growth, Zipf curves and n-gram counts per language.

phases.title: ML and PyTorch

steps.what: Train/val/test splits, bag-of-words and TF-IDF, logistic regression, naive Bayes, precision/recall/F1, cross-validation
Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoader, training loops, embedding layers, RNN/LSTM, GPU training on Colab or Kaggle

phases.build: A product-review sentiment classifier built twice, TF-IDF + logistic regression and a PyTorch LSTM, with a shared evaluation script, per-class F1 and an error analysis of sarcasm and code-mixed text.

phases.title: Classical NLP pipelines

steps.what: Tokenization, normalization, stemming vs lemmatization, stopwords, emojis and HTML, code-mixed Hinglish, subword tokenizers (BPE, WordPiece)
Pipelines, POS tagging, dependency parsing, rule-based Matcher, training a custom NER component, config files and spaCy projects

phases.build: A spaCy pipeline that extracts company, role, skills and salary from 2,000 scraped job posts using rule-based matchers plus a custom-trained NER model, scored with precision and recall per entity.

phases.title: Transformers

steps.what: Word embeddings, attention, the transformer architecture, BERT vs GPT objectives, fine-tuning for classification, NER and QA, seq2seq, metrics
Transformers, Datasets and Tokenizers libraries, Trainer API, pipelines, Accelerate, pushing models and model cards to the Hub

phases.build: Implement a mini transformer encoder in PyTorch, then fine-tune DistilBERT or IndicBERT on your job-post NER task with the HF Trainer, compare F1 against spaCy and publish the model with a model card.

phases.title: LLMs and retrieval

steps.what: Instruction tuning, LoRA/QLoRA, chat templates, dataset formatting, overfitting checks, evaluating generations vs zero-shot prompting
Inverted indexes, BM25, dense retrieval with sentence embeddings, vector indexes, hybrid search, MRR and nDCG
Morphology, syntax, semantics, ambiguity, Indian-language features (agglutination, scripts, transliteration) and why they break models

phases.build: LoRA-fine-tune a small open LLM to turn job posts into structured JSON, add BM25 + dense search over the corpus, and report extraction accuracy vs prompting with failures traced to linguistic causes.

dl-eng.summary: From Python and the math behind gradients to designing, training and scaling neural networks in PyTorch, reading training curves like a diagnostic tool.

phases.title: Math and code foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, tagging experiment versions, keeping configs and code reproducible
NumPy vectorization and broadcasting, OOP, dataclasses, Matplotlib, profiling slow loops, writing tested modules
Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, chain rule, probability, MLE, convexity, gradient descent, momentum, Adam, learning-rate schedules

phases.build: Implement linear and logistic regression and a 2-layer MLP from scratch in NumPy with gradient checking, and plot how SGD, momentum and Adam converge on the same loss surface.

phases.title: Deep learning core

steps.what: Bias-variance, overfitting, regularization, train/val/test splits, cross-validation, evaluation metrics
Backprop, initialization, activations, normalization, dropout, residual connections, attention, generalization, vanishing and exploding gradients
Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoader, custom training loops, mixed precision, checkpointing; Keras equivalents for reading TF code

phases.build: A micrograd-style autograd engine, then a CIFAR-10 CNN in PyTorch with a written diagnosis of initialization, normalization and learning-rate experiments backed by loss curves.

phases.title: Architectures and experiments

steps.what: CNNs (ResNet, EfficientNet), RNNs, transformers, ViT, encoder-decoder models, loss design, ablations, implementing architecture papers
Logging metrics, configs and artifacts, hyperparameter sweeps, comparing runs, reproducible seeds

phases.build: Implement ResNet, a ViT and a small GPT from their papers, run tracked ablations on depth, normalization and attention heads, and publish a report comparing accuracy, loss curves and compute cost.

phases.title: Scaling up

steps.what: GPU memory hierarchy, kernels, profiling with PyTorch Profiler and Nsight, torch.compile, writing fused kernels in Triton
DDP, FSDP/ZeRO, gradient accumulation, activation checkpointing, torchrun, debugging multi-GPU runs

phases.build: Profile your small-GPT training, add bf16, torch.compile and a fused Triton kernel, then run DDP on a 2-GPU cloud or Kaggle box, documenting throughput gains at each step.

recsys-eng.summary: From Python, SQL and statistics through collaborative filtering and two-stage retrieval-plus-ranking to Spark pipelines, low-latency serving and A/B tests.

phases.title: Data foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, code review, keeping notebooks and pipelines in version control
Distributions, hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, vectors, dot products, cosine similarity, matrix factorization intuition (SVD)
pandas, NumPy, sparse matrices with SciPy, OOP, writing tested data pipelines and CLIs
Joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs, sessionizing event logs, query plans and indexes

phases.build: Load MovieLens 1M or an e-commerce event log into PostgreSQL and analyze sparsity, the popularity long tail, session lengths and user activity using SQL window functions and pandas.

phases.title: Classic recommenders

steps.what: Supervised learning, regularization, gradient boosting, cross-validation, classification metrics and calibration
Popularity baselines, item/user kNN, matrix factorization (ALS, BPR), implicit feedback, cold start, time-based splits, Recall@K, NDCG, coverage

phases.build: Popularity, item-kNN and ALS matrix-factorization recommenders on MovieLens, evaluated offline on a time-based split with Recall@K, NDCG@10, catalog coverage and a cold-start breakdown.

phases.title: Retrieval, ranking and features

steps.what: Two-tower models, item2vec, negative sampling, ANN search (FAISS, HNSW), pointwise/pairwise/listwise ranking losses, multi-stage pipelines
User, item and context features, recency and frequency aggregates, target encoding, sequence features, point-in-time joins to avoid leakage

phases.build: A two-stage recommender: two-tower embeddings with FAISS for candidate retrieval, then a LightGBM LambdaRank ranker on user, item and context features, beating the ALS baseline on NDCG@10.

phases.title: Production at scale

steps.what: DataFrames, Spark SQL, partitioning, joins at scale, feature aggregation over large logs, Parquet, Spark MLlib ALS
Low-latency APIs, feature stores, embedding caches, serving ANN indexes, batching, p99 latency budgets, model versioning
Experiment design, randomization units, power analysis, CTR and engagement metrics, novelty effects, interleaving
Keras functional API, TensorFlow Recommenders two-tower models, tf.data pipelines, SavedModel export and TF Serving

phases.build: Compute features over a large interaction log with PySpark, serve top-10 recommendations from a FastAPI + Redis service under 50ms p99, and analyze a simulated A/B test with power and significance.

search-ranking-eng.summary: From Python and data structures through classic IR and relevance metrics to learning-to-rank, Elasticsearch and hybrid vector search.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, code review, keeping relevance experiments reproducible in version control
Strings, regex, collections, generators for large corpora, NumPy and pandas, packaging and tests
Hash maps, tries, heaps for top-k, sorting, binary search, edit distance, complexity analysis

phases.build: A typo-tolerant autocomplete over 100k product titles using a trie, heap-based top-k and edit-distance spelling correction, with unit tests and latency measurements.

phases.title: Information retrieval

steps.what: Tokenization and analyzers, inverted indexes, boolean retrieval, TF-IDF, BM25, query processing, phrase and fuzzy matching, index compression
Relevance judgments (qrels), precision@k, recall, MRR, nDCG, inter-annotator agreement, offline vs online evaluation, click metrics

phases.build: A from-scratch search engine over Wikipedia abstracts with an inverted index and BM25, evaluated on a BEIR or MS MARCO subset with nDCG@10 and MRR against Pyserini as a reference.

phases.title: Learning to rank

steps.what: Supervised learning, gradient boosting, overfitting, cross-validation, classification and regression metrics
Query-document features (per-field BM25, term proximity), document quality and popularity signals, query features, normalization, leakage
Pointwise, pairwise and listwise losses, RankNet, LambdaMART, click models and position bias, building training data from clicks

phases.build: A LambdaMART ranker trained on BM25, field-match and popularity features for MSLR-WEB10K or your own labeled queries, showing nDCG lift over BM25 with a feature-importance analysis.

phases.title: Production and semantic search

steps.what: Mappings, analyzers, synonyms, query DSL, function_score, the learning-to-rank plugin, shards and replicas, relevance tuning
Sentence embeddings, bi- vs cross-encoders, ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF), hybrid search, reciprocal rank fusion, re-ranking
Core Java, collections, Maven/Gradle, reading Lucene source, writing a custom Lucene similarity or Elasticsearch plugin

phases.build: Hybrid product search: Elasticsearch BM25 with synonyms, dense retrieval via HNSW, rank fusion and a cross-encoder re-ranker, with an offline eval harness comparing every stage on nDCG@10.

ml-research-eng.summary: From Python and the math of learning to reproducing papers in PyTorch, running disciplined experiments, and scaling them with CUDA and distributed training.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, code review, tagging the exact commit behind every experiment
Shell, SSH into remote GPU boxes, tmux, environment management, nvidia-smi, bash scripts to launch runs
NumPy vectorization, OOP, dataclasses, typing, config management, profiling, writing tested research code
Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, probability, statistics, information theory basics, optimization (SGD, Adam, convexity)

phases.build: A NumPy autodiff library supporting vector ops with gradient checks, used to train an MLP on MNIST, in a reproducible repo with tests and a one-command run script.

phases.title: Deep learning in PyTorch

steps.what: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoader, custom training loops, mixed precision, hooks for inspecting activations and gradients
Backprop, initialization, normalization, residual nets, attention and transformers, generalization, regularization, training dynamics

phases.build: Reproduce a ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 baseline to within 1% of published accuracy and train a char-level GPT from scratch, with seeded configs and a reproducibility checklist in the README.

phases.title: Research workflow

steps.what: Reading papers in three passes, translating equations to code, matching reported hyperparameters, unit-testing components, debugging silent failures
Baselines, ablations, multiple seeds, confidence intervals, hyperparameter sweeps, experiment logging and honest reporting

research-scientist-ml.summary: From strong Python and math through deep learning theory to running original, rigorous experiments and writing them up as a workshop-style paper, the portfolio research internships look for.
