phases.title: Reliability and memory

steps.what: Task success suites, trajectory evaluation, LLM-as-judge, tracing tool calls, latency and cost dashboards, regression checks
Short-term context management, summarisation, long-term vector memory, user profiles, forgetting and privacy

phases.build: A 50-task eval suite with traced runs for the research agent, then add long-term memory and report task success rate, cost and latency before and after.

fde.summary: Build strong Python and data skills, learn to ship LLM apps fast, then practise scoping and delivering solutions with real users.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, readable history, working in someone else's repo
Joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs, indexes, schema design, cleaning data in SQL
Core language, pandas, typing, scripts vs modules, HTTP clients, error handling, pytest

phases.build: A Python + SQL pipeline that loads messy data.gov.in CSVs into Postgres, cleans them, and answers ten business questions with documented, tested queries.

phases.title: LLM apps, fast

steps.what: LLM APIs, structured extraction, RAG basics, tool calling, document and image inputs, evaluating outputs on sample sets
Time-boxed builds, picking the simplest stack, demo-first UIs, hard-coding vs generalising, knowing when to stop

phases.build: A weekend-built Streamlit app that extracts fields from scanned GST invoices with a vision LLM, with a field-level accuracy table on 50 real samples.

phases.title: Connecting to real systems

steps.what: REST, OAuth, webhooks, pagination, rate limits, connecting SaaS tools (Google Sheets, Slack, CRMs) and building small APIs
Ingestion, scheduling, incremental loads, idempotency, data validation, failure alerts

phases.build: A scheduled pipeline that pulls records from a Google Sheet and a CRM API into a warehouse nightly, summarises changes with an LLM and posts a digest to Slack.

phases.title: Delivering for a customer

steps.what: Discovery calls, turning vague asks into requirements, managing scope, demos, handling feedback, handover and support
Problem framing, architecture options and trade-offs, build vs buy, security and data access constraints, success metrics
Writing crisp updates and design docs, explaining AI limits to non-technical people, presenting demos, expectation setting

phases.build: Treat a real local business or college office as a client: run discovery, write a scoping and design doc, deliver a working AI tool they use, and hand over with a runbook.

ai-product-eng.summary: Learn full-stack web development, add LLM features, then build the product sense to decide what to ship and measure whether it works.

phases.title: Full-stack foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, preview deployments from branches
ES modules, async/await, types and interfaces, DOM basics, npm, debugging in the browser
React and Next.js, server actions and API routes, Postgres and an ORM, auth, file uploads, deployment

phases.build: A campus lost-and-found marketplace with Next.js, Postgres, sign-in and photo uploads, deployed publicly and used by at least a few classmates.

phases.title: Adding LLM features

steps.what: Model APIs, streaming UIs, structured outputs, vision inputs, tool calling, latency and cost budgets, fallbacks when the model fails
System prompts, few-shot examples, schemas, prompt versioning, testing prompts on fixed inputs

phases.build: Add AI to the marketplace: auto-tag and describe items from photos with a vision model and natural-language search over listings, with streamed responses.

phases.title: Product thinking and UX

steps.what: User interviews, jobs-to-be-done, problem prioritisation, writing a one-page PRD, defining success metrics, saying no
Layout and typography, accessible components, loading and error states for AI, designing for wrong answers, responsive design
Paper and Figma prototypes, throwaway code spikes, quick usability tests, iterating within a day

phases.build: Interview 8 users, write a one-page PRD for a new AI feature, prototype two variants, test both with users, and ship the winner with a short decision write-up.

phases.title: Measuring what you shipped

steps.what: Building test sets from real usage, rubric scoring, LLM-as-judge, comparing prompt or model versions before release
Event tracking, funnels, retention, feature flags, simple A/B tests and reading their results

phases.build: An offline eval set and judge for your AI feature plus PostHog funnels and an A/B test, summarised in a one-page impact report with numbers.

ai-safety-eng.summary: Get comfortable with Python and LLM behaviour, then build guardrails, attack them, and measure safety with rigorous evals.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, versioning datasets and prompts alongside code
Classification metrics, transformers at a high level, tokenisation, sampling, pretraining vs fine-tuning, why models hallucinate
Core language, pandas, async API calls, Hugging Face pipelines, writing reusable evaluation scripts

phases.build: A Python toolkit that runs a local open-weight LLM, logs generations under different prompts and sampling settings, and visualises refusal rates and token probabilities.

phases.title: Building guardrails

steps.what: Input/output filtering, safety classifiers, system-prompt hardening, PII redaction, prompt-injection defences, layered defence design
Harm taxonomies, moderation APIs, multilingual and code-mixed (Hinglish) toxicity, thresholds, false positive vs false negative costs

phases.build: A guardrail layer for a chatbot with input/output classifiers, PII redaction and Hinglish toxicity handling, reporting block rate and false-positive rate on a labelled set.

phases.title: Attacking your own system

steps.what: Attack planning, harm categories, manual jailbreaks, multi-turn attacks, prompt injection, documenting reproducible findings
Automated attack generation, fuzzing prompts, encoding and translation attacks, adversarial suffixes, attack success rate metrics

phases.build: An automated red-team harness that attacks your guardrailed chatbot with generated jailbreaks and injections, with a findings report ranked by severity and the fixes you made.

phases.title: Measuring and aligning

steps.what: Refusal and over-refusal benchmarks, bias evals, toxicity scoring, confidence intervals, comparing model versions
Writing usage policies, model specs and constitutions, mapping policy to classifiers and evals, regulation basics (EU AI Act, India DPDP)
Preference data, reward models, PPO vs DPO, safety fine-tuning trade-offs with helpfulness

phases.build: A safety eval suite (harmful compliance, over-refusal, bias) plus a written usage policy, then DPO-fine-tune a small model on safety preferences and compare before and after.

ai-alignment-researcher.summary: Build maths, Python and PyTorch depth, learn to do and write up real ML research, then work on RLHF, interpretability and evals.

phases.title: Technical foundations

steps.what: Core language, NumPy, plotting, clean experiment scripts, configs, reproducible seeds
Linear algebra (SVD, eigen), multivariable calculus, probability and statistics, optimisation, KL divergence
Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, training loops, hooks for reading activations, mixed precision, GPU usage

phases.build: A GPT-style transformer implemented from scratch in PyTorch and trained on a small corpus, with training curves, sample outputs and hooks that dump attention patterns.

phases.title: Research craft

steps.what: Reading papers critically, forming hypotheses, baselines and ablations, seeds and error bars, avoiding fooling yourself, research taste
Structuring a paper, clear figures, related work, stating limitations, LaTeX, writing for workshops and blog posts

phases.build: Reproduce a known result (e.g. grokking on modular arithmetic) with ablations over seeds and weight decay, written up as a 4-page workshop-style paper in LaTeX.

phases.title: Learning from human and AI feedback

steps.what: MDPs, policy gradients, advantage estimation, PPO, KL penalties, reward hacking
SFT, reward modelling from preferences, PPO and DPO, constitutional AI and AI-generated feedback, reward overoptimisation

phases.build: An RLHF pipeline on a small model: SFT, a reward model on Anthropic HH data, then DPO, plus an RLAIF variant using constitution-generated preferences, compared by judged win rate.

phases.title: Alignment research directions

steps.what: Outer vs inner alignment, specification gaming, goal misgeneralisation, deceptive alignment, threat models from key papers
Probing, activation patching, circuits, logit lens, sparse autoencoders and feature analysis
Behavioural evals for sycophancy, deception and dangerous capabilities, controls, contamination, statistical power
Debate, recursive reward modelling, weak-to-strong generalisation, AI-assisted evaluation

phases.build: A 300-prompt sycophancy eval with controls run on three open models, plus an activation-patching study locating where one model represents the user's opinion, published as a write-up.

llm-eval-eng.summary: Learn Python, statistics and annotation, then design evals, calibrate LLM judges, benchmark models and wire it all into CI.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, versioning datasets and eval configs with code
Core language, pandas, async API calls, data classes, SQLite, pytest, writing reusable CLIs
Chat completions, sampling parameters, structured outputs, batching, rate limits, cost and latency tracking

phases.build: An async batch runner that sends 1,000 prompts to several hosted and local models and stores outputs, latency and cost in SQLite for later analysis.

phases.title: Designing evals

steps.what: Defining what good means, task taxonomies, rubrics, test-set coverage and difficulty, contamination, avoiding Goodhart
Accuracy, F1, BLEU/ROUGE limits, pass@k, bootstrap confidence intervals, significance tests, sample size
Annotation guidelines, label schemas, inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa), adjudication, quality control

phases.build: A 300-item eval set for a domain like Indian GST Q&A, with annotation guidelines, double-labelled items, Cohen's kappa, and model scores with bootstrap confidence intervals.

phases.title: Judges and benchmarks

steps.what: Pointwise vs pairwise judging, rubric prompts, position and length bias, calibrating against human labels, judge ensembles
Standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval), harness configs, few-shot settings, reproducibility, leaderboard pitfalls

phases.build: An LLM judge calibrated against your human labels (agreement and bias tests), plus a reproducible benchmark run of four open models published as a leaderboard with configs.

phases.title: Evals in production

steps.what: Tracing LLM calls, logging inputs/outputs, sampling production traffic into eval sets, dashboards for quality and latency
Golden sets, score thresholds, flaky output handling, gating prompt and model changes in CI

phases.build: A GitHub Actions pipeline that blocks prompt or model changes that regress eval scores, fed by Langfuse traces sampled from a running demo app.

ai-red-teamer.summary: Learn Python, LLM internals and security basics, then master jailbreaks and LLM attacks and report findings professionally.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Tokenisation, system vs user prompts, sampling, safety training basics, context windows, how tools and RAG extend models
OWASP Top 10, injection classes, XSS, SSRF, auth flaws, HTTP interception, responsible disclosure norms
Scripting, HTTP clients, async calls to model APIs, regex, pandas for logging results, building small CLIs

phases.build: A Python harness that sends prompt variants to local and hosted models, logs every response, and auto-flags refusals vs compliance with a regex plus classifier check.

phases.title: Breaking models

steps.what: Role-play, persona and hypothetical framing, obfuscation and encoding, multilingual and low-resource language attacks, multi-turn escalation
Many-shot jailbreaking, GCG adversarial suffixes, automated attackers (PAIR, TAP), transferability, reading attack papers

phases.build: A catalogued jailbreak library (role-play, encoding, many-shot, Hindi and Tamil attacks) with attack success rates measured across three open models.

phases.title: Attacking LLM applications

steps.what: Direct and indirect prompt injection, data exfiltration, tool and agent abuse, insecure output handling, OWASP LLM Top 10, defences
Assets, trust boundaries, data flow diagrams, STRIDE, attacker goals, ranking risks by likelihood and impact

phases.build: A deliberately vulnerable RAG + agent app where you demonstrate indirect injection, data exfiltration and tool abuse, with a STRIDE threat model and fixes mapped to OWASP LLM Top 10.

phases.title: Policy and professional reporting

steps.what: Harm taxonomies, provider usage policies, severity tiers, grey areas, how policy defines what counts as a failure
Reproducible findings, severity scoring, impact statements, remediation advice, executive summaries, disclosure etiquette
Pretexting, authority and urgency cues, trust exploitation, how these tactics transfer to manipulating models

phases.build: A full red-team report on an open model or AI app: scope, harm taxonomy, reproducible findings with severity, and remediations, submitted to a public bug bounty or AI red-teaming challenge.

llmops-eng.summary: Start with Python, Linux and Docker, then serve, version, deploy, monitor and cost-optimise LLM systems in production.

phases.title: Ops foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, tags and releases, trunk-based workflow
Shell, processes, systemd, networking basics, SSH, permissions, reading logs, GPU drivers and nvidia-smi
Images, layers, multi-stage builds, volumes, networking, Compose, GPU containers
Core language, async, FastAPI, config management, structured logging, testing

phases.build: A containerised FastAPI gateway in front of an LLM API with health checks, config via env vars, structured JSON logs and retries, run with Docker Compose.

phases.title: Serving and managing models

steps.what: Self-hosted inference servers, continuous batching, quantised models, OpenAI-compatible APIs, routing and fallbacks across providers
Model and prompt registries, versioning, experiment tracking, eval gates, canary and shadow releases, rollback

phases.build: Serve an open model with vLLM behind a LiteLLM router, with prompts and model versions tracked in a registry and a canary switch that can roll back a bad release.

phases.title: Platform and automation

steps.what: Pods, deployments, services, Helm, GPU node pools, autoscaling, managed Kubernetes on a cloud, secrets
Pipelines for build, test and deploy, image scanning, eval-gated releases, environment promotion

phases.build: Deploy the serving stack to Kubernetes with Helm and autoscaling, driven by a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs an eval suite and only promotes builds that pass.

phases.title: Observe and optimise

steps.what: Metrics (TTFT, tokens/sec, error rate), traces, LLM-specific logging, alerts, quality drift monitoring
Token budgeting, prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing to smaller models, batching, quantisation trade-offs
Running a vector DB in production, index tuning, backups, scaling, using it as a semantic cache

phases.build: A Grafana dashboard for latency, throughput, errors and cost per 1k requests, then add semantic caching and small-model routing and report p95 latency and cost before and after.

genai-solutions-arch.summary: Build cloud and LLM platform fluency, then practise designing secure, integrated, costed GenAI architectures and pitching them.

phases.title: Cloud and engineering foundations

steps.what: Core language, calling cloud SDKs and REST APIs, scripting, small FastAPI services
DNS, HTTP/TLS, IP and subnets, load balancers, firewalls, VPNs and private connectivity
Compute, storage, managed databases, VPCs, IAM, serverless, infrastructure as code, a cloud associate-level syllabus

phases.build: A three-tier web app on AWS (VPC, load balancer, containers, managed Postgres) provisioned with Terraform, with an architecture diagram and a teardown script.

phases.title: LLM platforms and retrieval

steps.what: Managed model services, model catalogues, provisioned vs on-demand throughput, fine-tuning options, open vs closed model trade-offs
Ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, permission-aware retrieval, retrieval evaluation

phases.build: The same document Q&A built on two managed platforms (e.g. Bedrock Knowledge Bases vs Azure OpenAI + AI Search), compared on answer quality, latency, features and lock-in.

phases.title: Designing enterprise solutions

steps.what: Requirements to architecture, non-functional requirements, reference patterns, trade-off analysis, architecture decision records, C4 diagrams
REST, events and queues, webhooks, SSO, connecting to ERPs/CRMs, API gateways, idempotency
IAM and RBAC, data residency, PII handling, prompt-injection risks, audit logging, India DPDP Act and EU AI Act basics

phases.build: A reference architecture and working slice of an enterprise HR assistant: SSO, role-aware retrieval, PII redaction, audit logs and integration with a mock HRMS, with ADRs for key choices.

phases.title: Selling the design

steps.what: Discovery questions, tailoring to CTO vs business audiences, proposals, objection handling, demo storytelling
Token cost estimation, infra vs API cost, usage scenarios, TCO comparisons, pricing calculators

phases.build: A cost model for 10,000 users across three model options plus a 10-slide proposal and recorded demo pitching the HR assistant architecture to a mock CTO.

applied-ai-research-eng.summary: Build maths and PyTorch depth, learn to implement papers and run clean experiments, then fine-tune and evaluate LLMs at scale.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, tagging experiment code, keeping data and checkpoints out of the repo
Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, probability, optimisation (SGD, Adam), information theory basics
Core language, NumPy, plotting, OOP, typing, configs, writing clean modular research code

phases.build: Logistic regression and an MLP with hand-written backprop in NumPy, gradient-checked, trained on a real tabular dataset and compared against scikit-learn.

phases.title: Deep learning in practice

steps.what: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoader, mixed precision, checkpointing, custom training loops, hooks
CNNs, transformers, scaling laws, reading papers critically, baselines, ablations, identifying open problems

phases.build: A config-driven training codebase that trains ResNet and ViT on CIFAR-100, with ablations on augmentation and LR schedule tracked in W&B.

phases.title: From paper to code

steps.what: Translating equations to code, matching reported hyperparameters, unit-testing components, debugging silent training bugs
Hypothesis-driven runs, seeds and variance, sweeps, controlled comparisons, experiment logs, negative results

phases.build: Re-implement a recent paper (e.g. LoRA, or RoPE vs ALiBi) from scratch, reproduce its main result within tolerance across seeds, and publish code and a results report.

phases.title: LLM training at scale

steps.what: Tokenisers, pretraining objectives, SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, data mixing, catastrophic forgetting, learning-rate schedules
DDP, FSDP, ZeRO stages, gradient checkpointing, multi-GPU launch, cost-aware use of cloud GPUs
Benchmark harnesses, held-out task design, LLM-as-judge, human evaluation samples, contamination checks

phases.build: SFT then DPO fine-tune a 1-2B open model on Hindi instruction data with FSDP across two cloud GPUs, evaluated with lm-evaluation-harness and a blind human-rated sample.

fine-tuning-eng.summary: Go from Python and ML basics to PyTorch, then learn to curate training data, run LoRA and full fine-tunes, and prove with evals that the tuned model beats the base.

phases.title: Python and ML foundations

steps.what: Data structures, functions, classes, virtual envs, NumPy arrays and broadcasting, pandas for tabular data, writing small reusable modules
Train/val/test splits, loss functions, gradient descent, overfitting and regularization, cross-entropy, linear algebra for vectors and matrices
Commits, branches, pull requests, .gitignore for checkpoints and data, tagging experiment versions

phases.build: A scikit-learn baseline classifier for Indian news headlines by category, with a clean train/val/test split, a reproducible notebook and a short write-up of where it overfits.

phases.title: Deep learning with PyTorch

steps.what: Tensors and autograd, nn.Module, Dataset/DataLoader, training loops, optimizers and schedulers, mixed precision, saving and loading checkpoints
Tokenization, embeddings, self-attention, causal masking, positional encodings, decoder-only models, reading a model config and state dict

phases.build: A small GPT-style character model written from scratch in PyTorch and trained on a public-domain text corpus, with loss curves and generated samples logged per epoch.

phases.title: Fine-tuning and training mechanics

steps.what: Instruction and chat formats, deduplication, quality filtering, PII removal, synthetic data generation, train/eval contamination checks, dataset cards
LoRA and QLoRA, rank and alpha, target modules, 4-bit loading, SFT with chat templates, merging adapters, comparing against full fine-tuning
Learning-rate schedules, warmup, gradient accumulation, packing, catastrophic forgetting, continued pretraining vs SFT, reading loss curves
Held-out task metrics, LLM-as-judge, base-vs-tuned comparisons, benchmark harnesses, regression checks for general ability after tuning

phases.build: A QLoRA fine-tune of a 7B open model on your curated dataset, with a W&B report showing base vs tuned scores on a held-out set and a general benchmark to check nothing regressed.

phases.title: Scaling and alignment

steps.what: GPU memory budgeting, gradient checkpointing, data parallel vs FSDP vs DeepSpeed ZeRO, multi-GPU launch, cloud GPU rental workflows
Preference data, reward models, DPO vs PPO, KL penalties, when preference tuning helps beyond SFT

phases.build: A multi-GPU DPO run on top of your SFT model using Accelerate or DeepSpeed, with a write-up of memory, throughput and win-rate against the SFT-only checkpoint.

genai-pm.summary: Build product fundamentals and real hands-on fluency with LLMs, then learn to scope AI features, define evals and guardrails, and drive a roadmap with stakeholders.

phases.title: Product and AI foundations

steps.what: Problem discovery, user personas, jobs-to-be-done, writing PRDs, prioritization frameworks like RICE, product lifecycle
Supervised vs generative models, training vs inference, tokens and context windows, embeddings, what fine-tuning and RAG mean

phases.build: A PRD for an AI study assistant for Indian engineering students, covering user research from 10 interviews, problem statement, success metrics and scope.

phases.title: Strategy and model fluency

steps.what: Hallucination, reasoning limits, context length, latency and cost per token, model families, tool use, RAG vs fine-tuning tradeoffs, safety risks
Market sizing, competitive analysis, positioning, build vs buy vs partner for models, AI moats, defining a north-star metric
System prompts, few-shot examples, structured JSON output, chain-of-thought, prompt iteration, comparing outputs across models

phases.build: A strategy memo for a GenAI feature in an existing Indian app (e.g. vernacular support bot), with competitor teardown, model choice tradeoffs and a working prompt prototype.

phases.title: Evals, guardrails and UX

steps.what: Golden datasets, rubric-based grading, LLM-as-judge, offline vs online metrics, guardrail metrics, defining launch quality bars
Designing for uncertainty, streaming responses, citations, feedback loops, error and refusal states, wireframing AI interactions

phases.build: An eval suite of 50+ graded test cases for your feature plus Figma wireframes showing how the UI handles low-confidence answers, refusals and user feedback.

phases.title: Roadmaps and stakeholders

steps.what: Now/next/later roadmaps, sequencing by risk and dependency, milestone planning, model upgrade cycles, communicating tradeoffs
Aligning engineering, design, legal and leadership, writing launch reviews, handling AI risk concerns, running decision meetings
SQL basics, funnel and retention metrics, A/B test reading, cost-per-query analysis, building simple dashboards

phases.build: A two-quarter roadmap and launch review deck for your GenAI feature, backed by a dashboard mock of adoption, quality and cost-per-query metrics.

rlhf-eng.summary: Start with Python, ML and PyTorch, learn supervised fine-tuning, then build preference-data pipelines, reward models and RLHF/RLAIF training loops with solid evaluation.

phases.title: Python and ML foundations

steps.what: Data structures, classes, NumPy, pandas, typing, writing modular scripts and CLIs, virtual environments
Loss functions, gradient descent, overfitting, probability and KL divergence, linear algebra essentials, train/eval splits
Branching, pull requests, versioning configs and experiment code

phases.build: A from-scratch logistic regression and small MLP in NumPy with manual gradients, checked against scikit-learn, and a notebook explaining cross-entropy and KL divergence.

phases.title: Deep learning, RL and SFT

steps.what: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoaders, training loops, mixed precision, checkpointing, debugging NaNs
MDPs, returns, policy gradients, REINFORCE, advantage estimation, PPO clipping, value functions
Supervised fine-tuning of small LLMs, chat templates, LoRA, loss masking on prompts, evaluating SFT checkpoints

phases.build: A PPO agent you implemented yourself solving a Gymnasium control task, plus an SFT checkpoint of a small open LLM tuned to follow instructions in a fixed format.

phases.title: Preference data and reward models

steps.what: Bradley-Terry pairwise loss, reward heads on LMs, calibration, reward hacking, overoptimization, accuracy on held-out preference pairs
Collecting pairwise comparisons, rating guidelines, inter-annotator agreement, data versioning, filtering noisy labels, AI-generated feedback

phases.build: A preference dataset of 2k+ comparisons collected through a Label Studio setup with written rater guidelines, and a reward model trained on it reporting held-out pairwise accuracy.

phases.title: RL alignment and evaluation

steps.what: PPO with KL penalty against a reference model, DPO and variants, constitutional AI-style AI feedback, rollout generation, training stability
Win-rate vs baseline, LLM-as-judge, helpfulness and harmlessness evals, reward-vs-quality divergence, red-teaming prompts
Rater onboarding, gold questions, quality audits, throughput and cost tracking, managing vendor or crowd annotators

phases.build: An end-to-end alignment run: SFT model, your reward model, then PPO and DPO variants, with a report comparing win-rates, KL drift and examples of reward hacking you caught.

llm-inference-eng.summary: Get strong in Python and C++ plus systems basics, then learn GPU performance, serving stacks, quantization and distributed inference to make LLMs fast and cheap.

phases.title: Systems and language foundations

steps.what: Python profiling and asyncio, modern C++ (RAII, templates, move semantics), building Python extensions, CMake basics
Shell, processes, memory and file systems, ssh, monitoring with top/htop, nvidia-smi, environment and driver setup
Memory hierarchy, caches, bandwidth vs compute bound, SIMD, arithmetic intensity and the roofline model
Attention, KV cache, prefill vs decode, FLOPs and memory per token, sampling methods, running models with PyTorch

phases.build: A minimal LLM inference script in PyTorch with a hand-written KV cache, benchmarked against no-cache generation, with a roofline-style explanation of prefill vs decode cost.

phases.title: GPU performance

steps.what: GPU architecture (SMs, warps, HBM), kernel fusion, memory coalescing, occupancy, profiling with Nsight, torch.compile and CUDA graphs
CUDA thread/block model, shared memory, tiled matmul, reductions, softmax kernels, writing kernels in Triton, FlashAttention ideas

phases.build: A fused softmax and tiled matmul written in both CUDA and Triton, benchmarked against PyTorch on your GPU with Nsight profiles showing where the speedup comes from.

phases.title: Serving stacks and compression

steps.what: Continuous batching, PagedAttention, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, TensorRT-LLM engine builds, Triton Inference Server, streaming responses
INT8/INT4/FP8 formats, GPTQ, AWQ, weight-only vs activation quantization, KV cache quantization, measuring accuracy loss
TTFT vs inter-token latency, batch size tradeoffs, speculative decoding, prefix caching, load testing and percentile latency

phases.build: A benchmark report serving one 7B model with HF baseline, vLLM and a quantized AWQ variant, plotting tokens/sec, TTFT and p95 latency across batch sizes with accuracy deltas.

phases.title: Scaling out

steps.what: Tensor and pipeline parallelism, NCCL communication, multi-GPU serving, disaggregated prefill/decode, routing across replicas
GPU-enabled images, CUDA base images, multi-stage builds, NVIDIA container toolkit
Deployments, services, GPU node pools, autoscaling on queue depth, health checks for model servers

phases.build: A containerized vLLM deployment with tensor parallelism across 2 GPUs on a rented cloud box, autoscaled on Kubernetes, with a load-test dashboard showing cost per million tokens.

multimodal-ai-eng.summary: Learn Python, PyTorch and image/audio processing, then integrate and adapt vision-language models and embeddings into search, understanding and generation systems.

phases.title: Python and ML foundations

steps.what: Data structures, classes, NumPy, pandas, file and media I/O, virtual environments, writing small CLIs
Loss functions, gradient descent, overfitting, classification metrics, linear algebra for vectors and similarity
Branches, pull requests, handling large files and model weights outside the repo

phases.build: A scikit-learn classifier on hand-crafted features from a small Indian street-sign image set, with a confusion matrix and error analysis in a reproducible notebook.

phases.title: Deep learning on images and audio

steps.what: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoaders, CNNs, transfer learning, mixed precision, checkpointing
Image transforms and augmentation, resizing and normalization, spectrograms and MFCCs, resampling, speech-to-text with Whisper, video frame sampling

phases.build: A pipeline that takes lecture videos, samples key frames, transcribes audio with Whisper and aligns slides to transcript timestamps, packaged as a reusable Python module.

phases.title: Vision-language models and integration

steps.what: CLIP contrastive training, vision encoders and projectors, LLaVA/Qwen-VL style architectures, image captioning, VQA, OCR-free document understanding
Calling multimodal APIs with images and audio, structured outputs, tool calling, streaming, cost and latency budgeting, serving behind an API
Image, text and audio embeddings in a shared space, cosine similarity, vector indexes, cross-modal retrieval evaluation with recall@k

phases.build: A text-to-image and image-to-image search engine over 10k product photos using CLIP embeddings in Qdrant, plus a VLM endpoint that answers questions about a selected image.

phases.title: Adapting and grounding models

steps.what: LoRA fine-tuning of a small VLM, preparing image-text instruction data, evaluating before vs after, avoiding overfitting on small sets
Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation over PDFs with figures and tables, chunking by page and image, citing sources in answers

phases.build: A LoRA-tuned VLM that reads Indian invoices or textbook diagrams, plus a multimodal RAG app over scanned PDFs that answers questions with page and figure citations.

ai-automation-eng.summary: Learn Python and API plumbing, master workflow automation on code and no-code platforms, then wire LLMs and agents into reliable business pipelines.

phases.title: Python and API plumbing

steps.what: Data types, functions, error handling, requests, JSON, reading and writing CSV/Excel, environment variables and secrets, scheduling scripts
Commits, branches, pull requests, keeping secrets out of repos
REST and HTTP methods, auth with API keys and OAuth, pagination, rate limits, receiving and verifying webhooks, retries and idempotency

phases.build: A FastAPI service that receives Razorpay or GitHub webhooks, verifies signatures, and syncs events into a Google Sheet with retries and idempotency keys.

phases.title: Workflow automation

steps.what: Mapping a manual process into triggers, steps and branches, error handling, human-in-the-loop approvals, scheduling, logging and alerting
Triggers and actions, data mapping, conditional paths, self-hosting n8n, custom code nodes, when to switch from no-code to Python
Syncing CRMs, sheets and databases, schema mapping, deduplication, incremental syncs, basic SQL for lookups

web-analyst.summary: Learn how web pages and tracking work, implement GA4 and GTM end to end, then analyze conversion with SQL and run tests and attribution.

phases.title: Web Fundamentals

steps.what: HTML structure, the DOM, CSS selectors, JS events, arrays and objects for the dataLayer, cookies, browser DevTools network tab
Pivot tables, lookups, percentages and rates, charts for traffic and conversion trends

phases.build: A multi-page demo store (static HTML/JS on GitHub Pages) with product, cart and checkout pages and a hand-written dataLayer, used as your tracking testbed in later phases.

phases.title: Measurement Implementation

steps.what: Tags, triggers, variables, dataLayer events, GA4 event tags, preview and debug mode, consent mode v2, server-side GTM overview
Event-based data model, e-commerce events, key events, custom dimensions, explorations, audiences, BigQuery export, consent and privacy settings

phases.build: A full GA4 + GTM implementation on your demo store: e-commerce events from view_item to purchase, consent mode, custom dimensions, a measurement plan and a debug-verified tracking spec.

phases.title: Conversion Analysis

steps.what: Funnel and path analysis, landing page and channel performance, segmentation, engagement metrics, CRO hypotheses, heatmaps and session recordings
BigQuery SQL on the GA4 export schema, UNNEST of event_params, sessionization, funnel and cohort queries, window functions
Chart choice for funnels and trends, scorecards, filters and date controls, clean dashboard layouts for marketing teams

phases.build: A conversion analysis of the public GA4 Google Merchandise Store BigQuery dataset: SQL funnels by channel and device, a Looker Studio dashboard and a CRO memo with three prioritized test hypotheses.

phases.title: Testing & Attribution

steps.what: Hypotheses, sample size and power, randomization, significance and confidence intervals, guardrail metrics, peeking, sample ratio mismatch checks
Last-click vs data-driven attribution, UTM governance, linear, time-decay and position-based models, Markov chain basics, cookieless measurement and MMM overview

phases.build: An experiment analysis kit (notebook that sizes tests, checks sample ratio mismatch and reports lift with confidence intervals) plus a last-click vs linear vs Markov attribution comparison on GA4 sample data.

operations-analyst.summary: Master spreadsheets and SQL on operational data, learn process mapping and statistics to find bottlenecks, then report and automate with BI and Python.

phases.title: Operational Data Foundations

steps.what: Lookups, SUMIFS, pivot tables, Power Query cleaning, what-if scenarios, Solver, capacity and staffing models
Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs, window functions, date and time arithmetic for cycle times and SLA breaches, building summary tables

phases.build: An order-fulfilment analysis on a public logistics dataset (e.g. DataCo Supply Chain or Olist): SQL for on-time delivery and SLA breach rates by region, plus an Excel staffing model with peak-season scenarios.

phases.title: Process & Statistical Analysis

steps.what: SIPOC, swimlane and BPMN maps, value-stream mapping, cycle time and bottlenecks, Little's Law, Lean wastes, 5 Whys and fishbone root cause
Distributions, variance, control charts (SPC), hypothesis tests, regression basics, moving-average demand forecasting

phases.build: A process improvement case study on a real campus process (canteen queue, library desk): BPMN map, timed observations, control chart and Little's Law bottleneck analysis with a quantified fix proposal.

phases.title: Reporting & Automation

steps.what: Chart choice for throughput, backlog and SLA trends, control-chart visuals, clear labeling, layouts for ops reviews
Connecting to SQL, data models, measures, filters, drill-through, publishing and scheduled refresh
pandas cleaning and merging, groupby, time-series resampling, simple queue simulation, automating recurring Excel outputs

phases.build: An operations SLA dashboard in Power BI or Tableau (throughput, backlog, SLA %, cost per order) fed by a pandas pipeline that cleans raw event logs and refreshes the data automatically.

insights-analyst.summary: Build data and statistics basics, learn survey and market research methods, then turn mixed data into insight narratives stakeholders act on.

phases.title: Data & Statistics Foundations

steps.what: Pivot tables, lookups, cross-tabs, charts, cleaning survey exports
Joins, aggregations, CTEs, window functions, customer segmentation and behavioral cohort queries
Sampling, confidence intervals, t-tests and chi-square, correlation, regression basics, significance vs practical importance

phases.build: A customer behavior analysis of a public dataset (e.g. Instacart or Olist): SQL segmentation by purchase frequency and basket, with significance tests on segment differences, summarized in an Excel pack.

phases.title: Research Methods & Visualization

steps.what: Research objectives, questionnaire design, Likert scales, bias, sampling and weighting, cross-tabs, NPS, interview guides, qualitative coding, market sizing
Charts for survey and segment data, diverging bars for Likert scales, small multiples, clean annotated slides

phases.build: A real survey with 150+ responses on a student topic (e.g. food-delivery app habits): questionnaire, sampling plan, weighted cross-tabs, NPS, 8 coded follow-up interviews and a visual findings summary.

phases.title: Insight to Influence

steps.what: Insight vs observation, so-what framing, pyramid principle, narrative arcs, executive summaries, persona and journey-map synthesis
Research briefs and kick-offs, scoping questions with stakeholders, presenting to non-technical audiences, handling pushback, follow-up action plans

phases.build: An insights deck combining your survey and behavioral data into 3-5 actionable recommendations, presented to a real stakeholder (club, startup or faculty) with a one-page brief and their feedback captured.

devops.summary: Start with Linux, networking, Git and scripting, then containers and CI/CD, cloud with Terraform, and finally Kubernetes with monitoring.

phases.title: Linux, Networking & Scripting

steps.what: Filesystem, permissions, processes, systemd, package managers, SSH, cron, logs and journalctl, shell navigation
TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS and TLS, subnets and CIDR, ports, load balancers, firewalls, curl, dig and ss
Commits, branches, merging vs rebasing, pull requests, tags, resolving conflicts, branch protection
Bash variables, loops, exit codes, text processing (grep, sed, awk); Python for files, subprocess, HTTP APIs and JSON/YAML

phases.build: A server bootstrap toolkit: Bash and Python scripts that harden a fresh Ubuntu VM (users, SSH keys, firewall), rotate logs and report disk/CPU health, versioned in Git with branches and PR reviews.

phases.title: Containers & CI/CD

steps.what: Images, Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, layer caching, volumes, networks, Docker Compose, registries, image size and security
Stages, triggers, build/test/lint jobs, caching, secrets, artifact and image publishing, environments, blue-green and canary deployments

phases.build: Containerize a multi-service app (API + Postgres + Redis) with Compose and a GitHub Actions pipeline that tests, scans, builds and pushes images, then deploys to a staging VM on every merge.

phases.title: Cloud & Infrastructure as Code

steps.what: IAM, VPCs and subnets, compute (EC2), storage (S3), managed databases, load balancers, managed Kubernetes, free tier and cost control
HCL, providers, resources, variables and outputs, state and remote backends, modules, plan/apply workflow, drift detection
Inventories, playbooks, roles, idempotency, Jinja2 templates, handlers, Ansible Vault for secrets

phases.build: Terraform modules provisioning a VPC, subnets, load-balanced compute and RDS on the AWS free tier with remote state in S3, plus Ansible playbooks configuring the hosts, destroyed and recreated from scratch.

phases.title: Kubernetes & Monitoring

steps.what: Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, probes, resource limits, HPA, Helm charts, kubectl debugging
Metrics, logs and traces, Prometheus scraping, Grafana dashboards, alert rules, Alertmanager routing, SLO-based alerts, on-call basics

phases.build: Deploy your app to Kubernetes (kind locally, then EKS or GKE) via Helm from your CI pipeline, with Prometheus and Grafana dashboards and an alert that fires and notifies on a simulated outage.

sre.summary: Build Linux, networking and coding foundations, run services on Kubernetes, then learn observability, SLOs, incident response and distributed-systems reliability.

phases.title: Systems & Coding Foundations

steps.what: Processes, signals, systemd, filesystems, memory and CPU tools (top, vmstat, strace), permissions, logs, SSH
TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP and TLS, load balancing, latency vs bandwidth, connection debugging with curl, dig, ss and tcpdump
Branches, pull requests, rebasing, resolving conflicts, tags, code review etiquette
Go or Python basics, concurrency (goroutines or asyncio), HTTP clients and servers, CLI tools, testing, writing automation to remove toil

phases.build: A Go or Python CLI health-checker that probes HTTP/TCP endpoints concurrently, records p50/p95/p99 latency and exposes results as JSON, with tests and a clean PR-based Git history.

phases.title: Containers, Kubernetes & IaC

steps.what: Images, Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, container networking and volumes, Docker Compose
Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, probes, resource requests and limits, HPA, PodDisruptionBudgets, rollouts, kubectl debugging, Helm
HCL, providers, resources, modules, variables, remote state, plan/apply workflow, provisioning clusters reproducibly

phases.build: A Terraform-provisioned Kubernetes cluster (kind locally, GKE or EKS on free credits) running a multi-service demo app such as Google's Online Boutique with probes, resource limits and autoscaling.

phases.title: Observability & SLOs

steps.what: Metric types, Prometheus scraping and PromQL, Grafana dashboards, RED and USE methods, logs with Loki, traces with OpenTelemetry, alert rules
Choosing availability and latency SLIs, setting SLO targets, error budgets, multi-window burn-rate alerts, SLO documents, error budget policies

phases.build: SLOs for the demo app: SLI recording rules, multi-window burn-rate alerts, a Grafana SLO dashboard and an error budget policy, validated by injecting latency during a k6 load test.

phases.title: Incident Response & Postmortems

steps.what: Severity levels, incident commander and comms roles, runbooks, paging and escalation, status updates, game days and chaos drills
Blameless culture, timeline reconstruction, contributing factors, actionable follow-ups, sharing learnings across teams

phases.build: Three game-day drills on your cluster (pod kill, node drain, dependency latency via Chaos Mesh) with a runbook per alert, a mock on-call rotation and a published blameless postmortem for each.

phases.title: Distributed Systems & Capacity

steps.what: CAP and consistency models, replication, partitioning, consensus (Raft), timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, cascading failures
Load testing, saturation points, headroom, Little's Law, demand forecasting, autoscaling limits, cost vs reliability trade-offs

phases.build: A capacity and resilience report for the demo app: k6 tests finding saturation points, a headroom forecast for 3x traffic, and retries, timeouts and circuit breakers added and shown to stop a cascading failure.

platform-eng.summary: Learn Linux, containers and Go/Python, then cloud with Terraform, Kubernetes with GitOps, and finally package it all as a self-service internal developer platform.

phases.title: Engineering Foundations

steps.what: Processes, permissions, systemd, networking basics, SSH, shell scripting, reading logs
Branching, pull requests, rebasing, tags, monorepo vs polyrepo, branch protection
Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, layer caching, Compose, registries, image security basics
Go or Python fundamentals, CLIs (cobra or click), HTTP services, calling cloud and Kubernetes APIs, templating, testing

phases.build: A Go CLI that scaffolds a new service from a template (Dockerfile, Makefile, health endpoint, CI config) and builds it locally: the first piece of a golden path.

phases.title: Cloud & Infrastructure as Code

steps.what: IAM and least privilege, VPCs, compute, object storage, managed databases, managed Kubernetes (EKS/GKE), cost basics
HCL, providers, reusable modules, variables and validation, remote state and locking, workspaces, testing and linting IaC

phases.build: Reusable Terraform modules (network, Kubernetes cluster, Postgres, bucket) with remote state, input validation and examples, in a registry-style repo whose CI runs fmt, validate and tflint.

phases.title: Kubernetes, CI/CD & GitOps

steps.what: Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, RBAC, namespaces, resource quotas, Helm charts, operators and CRDs overview
Pipeline stages, reusable workflows, caching, secrets, building and pushing images, promoting between environments
Declarative config repos, Argo CD applications and sync policies, app-of-apps, Kustomize overlays, drift detection, rollbacks

phases.build: A GitOps setup where GitHub Actions builds images and bumps Helm values in a config repo, and Argo CD syncs dev and prod clusters, with one-commit rollback demonstrated.

phases.title: Building the Internal Platform

steps.what: Golden paths, self-service provisioning, platform-as-a-product, DORA and developer-experience metrics, abstractions with Crossplane or Helm templates
REST resource design, OpenAPI specs, versioning, idempotency, pagination, error formats, auth for internal APIs
catalog-info.yaml, ownership metadata, software templates, TechDocs, plugins, integrating CI and Kubernetes views

phases.build: A mini internal developer platform: a Backstage template that creates a repo, CI pipeline, Terraform-provisioned database and Argo CD app in one click, plus a documented OpenAPI service for environment requests.

build-release-eng.summary: Learn Linux, Git branching and how compilation works, then master build systems, CI/CD and artifact management, and automate signed, repeatable releases.

phases.title: Foundations: Linux, Git & Scripting

steps.what: Shell, filesystem, permissions, environment variables, processes, package managers, file archiving
Compile vs link steps, object files, static vs shared libraries, headers, compiler flags, Java classpath and JARs
Git internals, trunk-based vs GitFlow, release branches, rebasing, cherry-picks, tags, hooks, conventional commits, monorepo trade-offs
Bash variables, loops, exit codes, text processing; Python for file manipulation, subprocess, semver parsing and calling REST APIs

phases.build: A release-branch toolkit: scripts that cut release branches, generate changelogs from conventional commits and tag versions, demonstrated on a small C or Java project with a documented branching model.

phases.title: Build Systems & Dependencies

steps.what: Makefile dependency graphs, Gradle tasks and build cache, Bazel BUILD files and targets, hermetic and incremental builds, remote caching, reproducibility
Semantic versioning, lockfiles, transitive conflicts, Maven/Gradle resolution, pip and npm locks, automated updates, SBOM basics

phases.build: Migrate a multi-module open-source Java or C++ project to Bazel (or optimize its Gradle build), measuring clean, incremental and cached build times and documenting the speedup and reproducible outputs.

phases.title: CI/CD & Artifacts

steps.what: Pipeline stages, triggers, build matrices, caching, parallelism, secrets, required checks, nightly and release pipelines
Artifact repositories, immutable versioned artifacts, snapshot vs release repos, promotion between stages, retention policies, proxying public registries

phases.build: A CI pipeline for your build that runs tests, uses a remote build cache, publishes versioned artifacts to Nexus or Artifactory and promotes them from snapshot to release on approval.

phases.title: Release Automation & Supply Chain

steps.what: Automated version bumps and changelogs, release trains, approval gates, feature flags, rollbacks, generated release notes
Building .deb/.rpm packages, wheels, JARs and container images; GPG and Sigstore cosign signing, checksums, SLSA provenance

phases.build: A one-command release pipeline: on tag, CI builds, packages a .deb and Docker image, signs with cosign, attaches an SBOM and SLSA provenance, and publishes a GitHub Release with notes and a tested rollback.

cicd-eng.summary: Get comfortable with Linux, Git and scripting, then master CI platforms and Docker, pipeline-as-code with test integration, and secure Kubernetes deploys.

phases.title: Linux, Git & Scripting

steps.what: Shell, filesystem, permissions, processes, environment variables, package managers, SSH
Branches, pull requests, merge vs rebase, tags, webhooks, branch protection and required checks
Bash exit codes, traps, loops, text processing; Python for parsing test reports, calling REST APIs and YAML/JSON handling

phases.build: A repo of tested Bash and Python CI utilities (version stamping, JUnit failure summarizer, retry wrapper for flaky commands) with branch protection and PR-based reviews.

phases.title: Containers & CI Platforms

steps.what: Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, layer caching, BuildKit, Compose for test environments, registries, minimal base images
Runners and agents, triggers, jobs and stages, matrices, caching, secrets, environments, Jenkins controller/agent setup, self-hosted runners

phases.build: One containerized app with equivalent pipelines in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and a Dockerized Jenkins, plus a write-up comparing build times, caching and runner setup.

phases.title: Pipeline as Code & Testing

steps.what: Declarative Jenkinsfiles, shared libraries, reusable workflows and composite actions, GitLab includes and templates, linting and versioning pipelines
Unit, integration and e2e stages, parallel and sharded tests, JUnit reports, coverage gates, flaky-test detection and quarantine, Testcontainers
Versioned artifacts, snapshot vs release repos, container registries, retention and cleanup, promoting builds between environments

phases.build: A reusable pipeline library (GitHub reusable workflows or a Jenkins shared library) used by three sample repos: sharded tests, coverage gates, flaky-test quarantine and versioned artifacts published to Nexus.

phases.title: Secure Deployments

steps.what: Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps and Secrets, Helm charts, rolling and canary rollouts, deploying from CI
SAST, dependency (SCA) scanning, container image scanning, secrets detection, IaC scanning, severity thresholds that fail builds

phases.build: An end-to-end pipeline that blocks merges on Semgrep, Trivy or Gitleaks findings above a threshold and deploys passing builds to a kind cluster with a canary rollout and automatic rollback.

observability-eng.summary: Build a small system to observe, then instrument it with metrics, logs and traces, and finish with alerting, SLOs and commercial observability platforms.

phases.title: Foundations & a System to Observe

steps.what: Processes, systemd, filesystems, CPU/memory/disk tools, networking basics, reading system logs
Dockerfiles, Compose for multi-service stacks, container networking, volumes
Go or Python HTTP services, background workers, database access, concurrency basics, writing a simple load generator

phases.build: A 3-service order-processing app in Go or Python (API, queue worker, Postgres) on Docker Compose with a load generator: the system you instrument in later phases.

phases.title: Metrics & Dashboards

steps.what: Counters, gauges, histograms, labels and cardinality, RED and USE methods, golden signals, dashboard hierarchy, avoiding vanity panels
Prometheus architecture, client libraries, exporters, service discovery, scrape configs, recording rules, Grafana variables, dashboards as code
PromQL selectors, rate and irate, aggregations, histogram_quantile, vector matching, plus LogQL and TraceQL basics

phases.build: Instrument the app with Prometheus client libraries, add node and Postgres exporters, and ship provisioned Grafana dashboards (RED per service, USE per host) as code in the repo.

phases.title: Logs & Distributed Traces

steps.what: Structured JSON logs, log levels, shipping with Fluent Bit or Promtail, Loki labels, Elasticsearch indexing, Kibana queries, retention and cost
Spans and context propagation, OTel SDKs and auto-instrumentation, Collector pipelines, sampling, Jaeger or Tempo, correlating traces with logs

phases.build: Structured logs in Loki and OpenTelemetry traces in Tempo or Jaeger via an OTel Collector, with trace IDs in logs so one Grafana click goes from a latency spike to the slow span to its logs.

phases.title: Alerting, SLOs & Commercial Platforms

steps.what: Symptom vs cause alerts, Alertmanager routing, grouping and inhibition, severities, runbook links, reducing alert fatigue
Agents and integrations, APM, log pipelines, monitors, dashboards, OTel ingestion, cost and cardinality controls vs open-source stacks
SLIs from metrics, SLO targets, error budgets, multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts, SLO dashboards and reviews

phases.build: SLO burn-rate alerts routed through Alertmanager with runbooks, validated by fault injection, plus the same app sent to New Relic's free tier via OTel with a written comparison of cost, setup and query power.

infra-eng.summary: Start with Linux and networking, move into one cloud provider, then define everything as Terraform code, and finish with monitoring, Kubernetes, storage and hardening.

phases.title: Linux and network foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, merges, rebasing, pull requests, .gitignore, writing clear commit messages
Filesystem layout, permissions, processes and signals, systemd services, package managers, SSH keys, journald logs, disk and memory inspection
OSI/TCP-IP layers, IP addressing and CIDR subnetting, routing, DNS, HTTP/TLS, NAT, firewalls, load balancing basics, tcpdump and dig

phases.build: Two Linux VMs on a private network: Nginx reverse proxy in front of an app server, SSH key-only access, ufw rules, TLS via a self-signed CA, plus a Git repo holding configs and a troubleshooting runbook.

phases.title: Core cloud and scripting

steps.what: IAM users/roles/policies, VPCs and subnets, EC2, security groups, S3, RDS, load balancers, auto scaling, regions/AZs, free-tier billing alarms
Bash loops, conditionals and exit codes; Python with boto3 for listing, tagging and cleaning resources; argparse CLIs; JSON parsing with jq

phases.build: A three-tier app on AWS free tier (public/private subnets, ALB, EC2 auto scaling group, RDS) plus a boto3 script that reports untagged or idle resources and can stop them on a schedule.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code and visibility

steps.what: Providers, resources, variables and outputs, modules, remote state with locking, workspaces, plan/apply workflow, importing existing resources, drift
Metrics vs logs vs traces, CloudWatch metrics and alarms, Prometheus exporters, Grafana dashboards, alert thresholds, USE/RED methods

phases.build: Rebuild the phase-2 stack entirely in reusable Terraform modules with S3 remote state, dev/prod workspaces, and Terraform-managed CloudWatch alarms and a Grafana dashboard for CPU, latency and errors.

phases.title: Containers, data and hardening

steps.what: Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, resource requests/limits, probes, kubectl debugging, managed clusters (EKS)
Block vs object vs file storage, EBS snapshots, S3 lifecycle rules, RDS backups and read replicas, PostgreSQL basics, restore drills
Least-privilege IAM, CIS benchmarks, SSH hardening, patching, encryption at rest/in transit, security group audits, secrets handling

phases.build: An EKS cluster provisioned with Terraform running a containerized service backed by RDS with automated backups and a tested restore, plus a hardening report showing Lynis and Security Hub findings before and after fixes.

devex-eng.summary: Get fluent in a systems language and the command line, then build developer tooling, fast CI/CD and reproducible local environments, wrap them in golden paths and a portal, and learn to measure developer productivity.

phases.title: Language and command-line foundations

steps.what: Branching models, rebasing, hooks, submodules vs monorepos, bisect, resolving conflicts, pull request etiquette
Shell navigation, pipes and redirection, environment variables, PATH, processes, file permissions, editing in vim or nano
One language in depth (Go or Python) plus working TypeScript: modules, testing, error handling, packaging and publishing a CLI

phases.build: A repo-health CLI that scans a repository for missing README, CODEOWNERS, lint config and tests, prints a scorecard, has unit tests, and is published as a downloadable binary or pip package.

phases.title: Developer tooling and automation

steps.what: Linters and formatters, pre-commit hooks, build systems and caching, task runners, monorepo tools, code generators, editor integrations
Automating repetitive dev chores with Bash and Python, GitHub API scripting, cron and bot-driven workflows, idempotent scripts

phases.build: A monorepo starter kit with shared lint/format configs, pre-commit hooks, a task runner and a service scaffolding command, with measured build times before and after enabling remote caching.

phases.title: Fast pipelines and reproducible environments

steps.what: Pipeline stages, caching dependencies, matrix builds, reusable workflows, artifacts, flaky-test detection, preview deployments, pipeline speed tuning
Containerized dev setups, Dev Containers, Docker Compose for dependencies, environment parity, seeded data, one-command bootstrap scripts

phases.build: A sample multi-service project where a new contributor runs one command to get a working environment, and CI uses cached reusable workflows to cut pipeline time by a measured percentage.

phases.title: Golden paths and developer portals

steps.what: Paved-road templates, opinionated defaults, docs-as-code, onboarding guides, ADRs, how-to vs reference vs tutorial structure (Diataxis)
Software catalog and catalog-info.yaml, software templates, TechDocs, plugins, ownership metadata, integrating CI status into the portal

phases.build: A self-hosted Backstage portal with a software template that creates a new service repo with CI, docs and ownership pre-wired, plus TechDocs onboarding guides for that golden path.

phases.title: Measuring developer experience

steps.what: Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore; SPACE framework; collecting metrics from Git and CI data
Developer interviews, friction logs, surveys, journey mapping of onboarding, turning feedback into prioritized tooling work

phases.build: A DORA dashboard computed from a real open-source repo's GitHub data, paired with a friction-log study of five developers onboarding to your template and a prioritized list of fixes.

cloud-arch.summary: Build systems and networking fundamentals, go deep on one cloud's architecture patterns, then practise solution design in Terraform and finish with cost, migration and communicating tradeoffs.

phases.title: Systems and secure networking groundwork

steps.what: Shell, permissions, processes, systemd services, SSH, package management, logs and basic performance commands
Core syntax, functions, modules, working with JSON and REST APIs, virtual environments, small automation scripts
Commits, branches, pull requests, merge conflicts, repository structure for infrastructure code
CIDR subnetting, routing, DNS, TLS, VPC design, security groups vs NACLs, IAM least privilege, encryption, VPN/peering, zero-trust basics

phases.build: A documented network design for a two-tier app on AWS: CIDR plan, public/private subnets, bastion-free access via SSM, security group matrix and IAM roles, deployed by hand and verified with connectivity tests.

phases.title: Cloud architecture patterns

steps.what: Compute, storage and database choices, multi-AZ high availability, caching, queues and event-driven patterns, serverless, DR strategies, Azure/GCP equivalents
Six pillars (operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost, sustainability), lenses, running a workload review and a remediation plan

phases.build: A highly available image-processing service across two AZs (ALB, auto scaling, S3, SQS-driven Lambda workers, RDS Multi-AZ) reviewed with the Well-Architected Tool and a prioritized list of risks fixed.

phases.title: Solution design as code

steps.what: Gathering requirements and NFRs, C4 diagrams, architecture decision records, comparing options with tradeoff tables, sizing estimates, failure-mode thinking
Modules, variables and outputs, remote state, environments, reusable network and compute modules, plan reviews, tagging standards

phases.build: A full solution design for a food-delivery backend: requirements, C4 diagrams, five ADRs with alternatives considered, implemented as reusable Terraform modules with dev and prod environments.

phases.title: Cost, migration and communicating tradeoffs

steps.what: Pricing models, reserved vs spot vs on-demand, rightsizing, storage tiers, data transfer costs, budgets and alerts, unit economics, FinOps basics
The 7 Rs, discovery and dependency mapping, wave planning, database migration options, cutover and rollback plans, migration risk logs
Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, autoscaling, managed Kubernetes (EKS/AKS/GKE) vs serverless containers, when Kubernetes is the wrong choice
Explaining tradeoffs to non-engineers, one-page architecture briefs, cost and risk summaries, presenting options and recommendations

phases.build: A migration proposal for a VM-hosted monolith: 7R assessment, containerized target on EKS vs ECS comparison, Infracost before/after cost model, cutover plan, and a 10-minute recorded stakeholder presentation.

cloud-eng.summary: Build Linux and networking basics, get hands-on with a cloud provider and scripting, codify everything in Terraform with a pipeline, then run containers with monitoring and cost controls.

phases.title: Linux and networking basics

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, merge conflicts, tagging releases, keeping secrets out of repos
Filesystem, users and permissions, processes, systemd, package managers, SSH keys, logs, disk and network commands
IP addressing and CIDR, subnets, routing tables, DNS, HTTP/TLS, NAT, load balancers, firewalls, debugging with curl, dig and traceroute

phases.build: A Linux server running Nginx and a small API as systemd services behind a reverse proxy with TLS, firewall rules and log rotation, plus a written network diagram and troubleshooting notes.

phases.title: Hands-on cloud and scripting

steps.what: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS, ELB, auto scaling, Route 53, Lambda, CloudWatch logs, shared responsibility model, free-tier budgeting
Bash scripts with error handling, Python boto3 automation, parsing JSON with jq, scheduled jobs, writing small reusable CLIs

phases.build: A serverless file-ingestion pipeline (S3 upload triggers Lambda that validates and writes to RDS) behind a custom domain, with a boto3 script that snapshots volumes and deletes snapshots older than 7 days.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code and pipelines

steps.what: HCL, providers, resources, variables, outputs, modules, remote state with locking, workspaces, import, drift detection
Pipeline stages, terraform fmt/validate/plan on pull requests, gated apply on merge, OIDC auth to the cloud, artifact versioning

phases.build: The phase-2 pipeline rebuilt as Terraform modules with remote state, deployed through GitHub Actions that post plan output to pull requests and apply only after approval, using OIDC instead of stored keys.

phases.title: Containers, monitoring and cost

steps.what: Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, container registries, ECS vs EKS, Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps, probes, autoscaling
CloudWatch metrics, logs and alarms, dashboards, Prometheus and Grafana basics, alert routing, health checks
Cost allocation tags, budgets and alerts, Cost Explorer, rightsizing, spot instances, shutting down idle environments

phases.build: A containerized API on EKS provisioned by Terraform with CloudWatch/Grafana dashboards and alarms, cost tags on every resource, an AWS Budget alert, and an Infracost estimate posted on each pull request.

kubernetes-eng.summary: Learn Linux, networking and Docker, master core Kubernetes with Helm and Kustomize, go deep on CNI and service mesh, then add GitOps, Terraform, cluster security and Go operators.

phases.title: Linux, networking and containers

steps.what: Processes, namespaces and cgroups, systemd, filesystems, permissions, SSH, journald, iptables basics
Branches, pull requests, rebasing, tags, structuring repos for manifests and charts
IP and CIDR, routing, DNS, NAT, TCP/UDP, HTTP/TLS, load balancing, bridges and veth pairs
Images and layers, multi-stage Dockerfiles, volumes, container networking, Compose, registries, image size and security best practices

phases.build: A multi-service app (API, worker, PostgreSQL, Redis) containerized with multi-stage builds and Compose, with image sizes cut by a measured amount and images pushed to a registry with semantic tags.

phases.title: Core Kubernetes and packaging

steps.what: Control plane components, Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps, Secrets, probes, HPA, PDBs, RBAC, kubectl debugging
Chart structure, templates and values, dependencies, chart testing, Kustomize bases and overlays, per-environment configuration

phases.build: The phase-1 app deployed to a local multi-node kind cluster via a Helm chart and Kustomize overlays for dev and prod, with probes, HPA, PodDisruptionBudgets and zero-downtime rolling updates demonstrated.

phases.title: Cluster networking and service mesh

steps.what: Kubernetes network model, CNI plugins, kube-proxy and eBPF dataplanes, CoreDNS, NetworkPolicies, Ingress controllers, debugging pod-to-pod traffic
Sidecar vs ambient mesh, mTLS, traffic splitting, retries and timeouts, canary releases, mesh observability

phases.build: A kind cluster running Cilium with default-deny NetworkPolicies and Hubble flow visualisations, plus Linkerd providing mTLS and a 90/10 canary traffic split, documented with packet-path diagrams.

phases.title: GitOps and infrastructure as code

steps.what: Declarative desired state, ArgoCD Applications and app-of-apps, sync waves, drift detection, image update automation, promotion between environments
Providers, modules, remote state, provisioning managed clusters and node groups, bootstrapping ArgoCD via Terraform

phases.build: A managed cluster provisioned by Terraform that bootstraps ArgoCD, which then deploys the full app stack from Git across dev and prod with automatic drift correction.

phases.title: Securing and extending clusters

steps.what: RBAC least privilege, Pod Security Standards, admission policies, image scanning and signing, secrets encryption, CIS benchmark, runtime detection
Go syntax, structs and interfaces, error handling, client-go, controller-runtime, writing a CRD and reconcile loop

phases.build: A Kubernetes operator in Go (kubebuilder) that manages a custom resource for scheduled database backups, deployed into a cluster hardened with Kyverno policies, signed images and a clean kube-bench report.

devsecops-eng.summary: Build Linux, Git, Docker and web-security basics, wire SAST, DAST and SCA into CI/CD, secure containers, cloud and IaC with proper secrets handling, then cover Kubernetes security, compliance and threat modeling.

phases.title: Platform and web security basics

steps.what: Users and permissions, processes, systemd, SSH, logs, package management, file integrity basics
Branches, pull requests, protected branches, signed commits, git history and why leaked secrets persist
Images, layers, Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, volumes, networks, Compose, registries
OWASP Top 10, injection, XSS, CSRF, broken auth, SSRF, HTTP headers, CWE and CVSS scoring

phases.build: OWASP Juice Shop running in Docker with 10 vulnerabilities exploited and documented in a report that maps each to OWASP Top 10, CWE and CVSS and proposes a code-level fix.

phases.title: Security scanning in the pipeline

steps.what: Static analysis rules and false positives, dependency scanning and SBOMs, dynamic scanning against running apps, secret scanning, triaging findings
Shift-left gates, severity thresholds, SARIF uploads, branch protection, pipeline hardening, least-privilege tokens, OIDC, supply-chain attacks

phases.build: A GitHub Actions pipeline for a vulnerable Flask app running Semgrep, Trivy SCA, gitleaks and a ZAP baseline scan, failing on high severity, publishing SARIF to code scanning, and showing each fix commit.

phases.title: Containers, cloud, IaC and secrets

steps.what: Minimal and distroless images, non-root containers, image signing, IAM least privilege, CSPM, cloud logging, GuardDuty, misconfiguration audits
Scanning Terraform and Kubernetes manifests, common misconfigurations, custom policies, blocking risky plans in CI
Static vs dynamic secrets, Vault auth methods and policies, secret engines, injecting secrets into pipelines and apps, rotation

phases.build: A hardened, signed distroless image with SBOM deployed to AWS via Terraform that passes Checkov, pulling database credentials as dynamic Vault secrets, plus a Prowler report before and after remediation.

phases.title: Kubernetes security and compliance

steps.what: RBAC, Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicies, admission control, runtime detection, CIS benchmark, securing etcd and the API server
SOC 2 trust criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A controls, mapping technical controls to requirements, evidence collection, audit trails

phases.build: A kind cluster enforcing Kyverno policies with Falco runtime alerts and a kube-bench report, plus a control matrix mapping each pipeline and cluster control to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 with collected evidence.

phases.title: Automation and threat modeling

steps.what: Python for parsing scanner JSON/SARIF, deduplicating findings, calling GitHub and Jira APIs, Bash glue in pipelines
Data flow diagrams, trust boundaries, STRIDE, attack trees, ranking risks, turning threats into tests and backlog items

phases.build: A STRIDE threat model for the phase-2 app with data flow diagrams, plus a Python tool that merges findings from all scanners, deduplicates them and files prioritized issues automatically.

production-eng.summary: Get strong at coding and data structures, go deep on Linux internals and networking, learn distributed systems and debugging them, then practise on-call, automation and capacity planning.

phases.title: Coding foundations

steps.what: Branches, rebasing, bisect for finding regressions, code review workflow, reading large codebases
Arrays, hash maps, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting, BFS/DFS, complexity analysis, timed interview-style practice
Python fluency plus Go or C++: concurrency (goroutines/threads), memory model basics, profiling, testing, writing production-quality CLIs

phases.build: A concurrent log analyzer in Go that streams multi-GB access logs, computes per-endpoint p50/p99 latency and error rates, with unit tests, benchmarks and a profile showing where time is spent.

phases.title: Linux internals and networking

steps.what: Processes and scheduling, virtual memory, page cache, file descriptors, syscalls, signals, namespaces and cgroups, strace, perf, eBPF tools
TCP handshake, congestion control, TIME_WAIT, DNS, TLS, load balancers, socket options, packet capture and latency analysis

phases.build: A mini process supervisor in Go or C using fork/exec, signals, cgroup v2 limits and namespaces, plus a write-up diagnosing a deliberately slow service with strace, perf flame graphs and tcpdump.

phases.title: Distributed systems and debugging them

steps.what: Replication, partitioning, consensus (Raft), consistency models, CAP, idempotency, retries and backoff, queues, failure detection
Metrics, structured logs and distributed traces, correlation IDs, flame graphs, bisecting regressions, reading dashboards to localise faults

phases.build: A Raft-replicated key-value store in Go instrumented with OpenTelemetry traces and Prometheus metrics, with a fault-injection test suite (node kills, partitions) and a report of bugs found and fixed.

phases.title: Operating services in production

steps.what: SLIs/SLOs and error budgets, actionable alerts, runbooks, incident roles, mitigation before root cause, blameless postmortems
Auto-remediation scripts, safe rollouts and rollbacks, toil identification, config management basics, scheduled jobs
Load testing, saturation points, headroom, growth forecasting, queueing basics (Little's law), cost-aware scaling

phases.build: The KV store run as a service with SLO-based alerts and runbooks, three simulated incidents handled with written postmortems, an auto-remediation script, and a k6-driven capacity model with headroom targets.

sysadmin.summary: Learn operating systems and networking in a home lab, take on identity, access and scripting, add virtualization and backups, then keep it all monitored, patched and hardened.

phases.title: Servers and networks

steps.what: Processes, memory, storage, boot process, file systems, drivers, BIOS/UEFI, how Windows and Linux differ
Linux CLI, users, services, packages, logs; Windows Server roles and features, Server Manager, DHCP, DNS, file shares, Event Viewer
OSI model, IP addressing and subnetting, VLANs, routing, DHCP, DNS, NAT, firewalls, VPN basics, troubleshooting with ping, tracert, nslookup

phases.build: A home lab with a pfSense firewall, two VLANs, an Ubuntu file server and a Windows Server running DHCP and DNS, with a network diagram, IP plan and step-by-step rebuild documentation.

phases.title: Identity and scripting

steps.what: Active Directory domains, OUs, groups, Group Policy, least privilege, password policies, joining Linux to AD, onboarding and offboarding
PowerShell cmdlets, pipelines and AD module; Bash scripts, cron, error handling, logging; scheduled tasks

phases.build: An Active Directory domain with OUs, Group Policies and a joined Linux host, plus a PowerShell script that bulk-onboards users from CSV into the right groups and offboards them with an audit log.

phases.title: Virtualization and recovery

steps.what: Hypervisor types, ESXi install, vSphere concepts, VM templates, snapshots, virtual switches, resource pools, vMotion basics
3-2-1 rule, full vs incremental backups, RPO/RTO, image vs file backups, offsite copies, restore testing, DR runbooks

phases.build: A virtualized lab on ESXi with VM templates, plus scheduled Veeam and restic backups and a timed full-restore drill of the domain controller documented against target RPO and RTO.

phases.title: Monitoring and hardening

steps.what: Host and service checks, SNMP, thresholds and alerts, dashboards, log collection, capacity trends
Patch cycles, WSUS and unattended-upgrades, CIS benchmarks, disabling unused services, SSH and RDP hardening, audit logging

phases.build: Zabbix monitoring every lab host with email alerts, a documented monthly patch process, and CIS hardening applied with before/after Lynis and CIS-CAT scores.

linux-eng.summary: Get solid in shell scripting and C, go deep into Linux internals and storage, tune systemd, the kernel and networking, then automate and secure a fleet with Ansible and monitoring.

phases.title: Shell and systems programming basics

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, managing configs and scripts in version control
Pointers, memory allocation, structs, file I/O, compiling with gcc and make, reading man pages, debugging with gdb
Bash variables, arrays, conditionals, loops, functions, exit codes, traps, text processing with grep, sed, awk, safe scripting with set -euo pipefail

phases.build: A tested Bash toolkit (ShellCheck in CI, bats tests) that audits a host for open ports, failed services, disk pressure and stale users and emits a JSON report.

phases.title: Linux internals and storage

steps.what: Boot process, processes and scheduling, virtual memory, page cache, syscalls, /proc and /sys, namespaces, cgroups, signals
Partitions, LVM, ext4 vs XFS, mdadm RAID, mount options, inodes, fsck, NFS, I/O scheduling and benchmarking

phases.build: A minimal shell in C supporting pipes, redirection and job control, plus a storage lab with LVM on RAID 1, an online volume resize, a simulated disk failure and rebuild, and fio benchmarks.

phases.title: Tuning services, kernel and network

steps.what: Unit files, timers, dependencies, resource limits via cgroups, journald, sysctl parameters, ulimits, huge pages, I/O and CPU schedulers
ip and ss tools, routing, bonding and bridges, DNS, TCP tuning, nftables firewall rules, packet capture

phases.build: An Nginx web host tuned with custom systemd units and cgroup limits, sysctl TCP settings and nftables rules, with wrk benchmarks showing throughput and latency before and after each change.

phases.title: Fleet automation and security

steps.what: Inventories, playbooks, roles, variables, templates, handlers, idempotency, Ansible Vault, testing roles
Node metrics, log aggregation, alert rules, dashboards for CPU, memory, disk and network saturation
SSH hardening, SELinux/AppArmor, auditd, CIS benchmarks, minimal packages, sudo policy, automatic security updates

phases.build: Ansible roles, tested with Molecule, that configure a five-VM Vagrant fleet end to end: users, hardened SSH, SELinux enforcing, node_exporter, and a Prometheus/Grafana stack with disk and memory alerts.

release-manager.summary: Learn enough code and Git branching to reason about releases, build CI/CD and deployment automation, then practise release planning, change and risk management, and clear communication when things go wrong.
