phases.title: Code and version control

steps.what: Core syntax, functions, modules, reading and running test suites, small scripts for automating release chores
Shell navigation, environment variables, permissions, processes, reading logs, SSH
Trunk-based vs GitFlow, release branches, cherry-picks and hotfixes, tags, semantic versioning, Conventional Commits, merge strategies

phases.build: A sample multi-module repo run on trunk-based development with release branches, a hotfix cherry-pick flow, semantic version tags and changelogs generated automatically from Conventional Commits.

phases.title: Pipelines and deployment automation

steps.what: Build, test, package and promote stages, artifact versioning, environment promotion, approvals and quality gates, pipeline as code
Blue-green and canary deployments, rollbacks, feature flags, database migrations during deploys, Docker and Kubernetes deployment basics

phases.build: A pipeline that builds a containerized web service, promotes the same artifact through staging and production behind manual approval, ships via canary with automatic rollback, and toggles features with Unleash.

phases.title: Release planning and risk

steps.what: Release trains and cadences, release calendars, scope freeze, readiness checklists, go/no-go meetings, dependency tracking across teams
Change types (standard, normal, emergency), CAB process, risk registers, impact and blast-radius assessment, rollback criteria, ITIL change basics
Sprints, backlog, ceremonies, Kanban flow, how sprint output maps to release scope, velocity and its limits

phases.build: A release playbook for a mock three-team product: quarterly release calendar, go/no-go checklist, risk register, change request templates in Jira Service Management, and a scored dry-run of one release.

phases.title: Communication and incidents

steps.what: Release notes for different audiences, status updates, escalation paths, writing go/no-go summaries, running short release syncs
Incident roles, severity levels, comms cadence during an outage, coordinating rollback decisions, blameless postmortems

phases.build: A simulated failed production release run end to end: status page updates, stakeholder messages, rollback decision log, customer-facing release notes and a blameless postmortem with follow-up actions.

infra-automation-eng.summary: Learn Linux, Git and real scripting, provision cloud infrastructure with Terraform, configure it with Ansible through CI/CD, then enforce policy as code, test infrastructure code and extend to Kubernetes.

phases.title: Linux and scripting

steps.what: Filesystem, users and permissions, processes, systemd, package management, SSH keys, logs
Branches, pull requests, code review, tags, repository layout for infrastructure code, pre-commit hooks
Python CLIs, REST API clients, SSH automation, YAML/JSON handling, error handling and retries, unit tests; Go basics for compiled tooling

phases.build: A Python CLI that connects to a set of Linux VMs over SSH, detects package and config drift against a YAML baseline, outputs a report, and is covered by pytest tests.

phases.title: Cloud provisioning with Terraform

steps.what: IAM, VPC and subnets, EC2/VMs, S3/Blob storage, managed databases, load balancers, CLI usage, Azure equivalents
HCL, providers, modules, variables and outputs, remote state with locking, workspaces, import, drift detection, module versioning

phases.build: A versioned Terraform module library (network, compute, database) with remote state and locking that stands up identical dev and prod environments on AWS from one command.

phases.title: Configuration management and pipelines

steps.what: Inventories including dynamic cloud inventory, playbooks, roles, templates, handlers, idempotency, Ansible Vault, Galaxy
Plan on pull request, gated apply on merge, OIDC cloud auth, linting stages, artifact and state handling, pipeline secrets

phases.build: A pipeline where Terraform provisions hosts and Ansible roles configure them via dynamic inventory; pull requests show plan output and lint results, and merges apply changes with approval using OIDC.

phases.title: Policy, testing and Kubernetes

steps.what: Rego basics, evaluating Terraform plan JSON, tagging and security rules, Conftest in CI, Gatekeeper for Kubernetes admission
Static checks, terraform test, Terratest integration tests, Molecule for Ansible roles, ephemeral test environments, testing pyramid for infra
Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, Helm charts, managing clusters and workloads with Terraform providers

phases.build: Rego policies that block untagged or public resources in Terraform plans, Terratest and Molecule suites running in CI, and an EKS cluster plus Helm release provisioned through the same tested modules.

chaos-eng.summary: Learn Linux, containers and scripting, understand how distributed systems fail and inject faults by hand, add Kubernetes, observability and SRE practices, then run disciplined chaos experiments with real tooling.

phases.title: Linux, containers and scripting

steps.what: Processes, signals, systemd, networking commands, resource limits, logs, tc and iptables basics
Branches, pull requests, versioning experiment definitions and configs
Images, Dockerfiles, Compose, container networking, resource constraints, restart policies
Python and Bash for load generation, polling health endpoints, collecting latency/error stats, automating experiment steps

phases.build: A microservices demo (such as Online Boutique) running locally in Compose with a Python load generator that reports throughput, p95 latency and error rate per service.

phases.title: How distributed systems fail

steps.what: Partial failure, timeouts, retries and backoff, idempotency, circuit breakers, replication, consistency, cascading failures, thundering herds
Steady-state hypotheses, blast radius, latency and packet loss injection, killing processes, dependency outages, measuring impact and recovery

phases.build: A fault-injection report on the demo app: latency, packet loss and dependency outages injected with Toxiproxy and tc, cascading failures observed, and retries, timeouts and circuit breakers added with measured improvements.

phases.title: Kubernetes, observability and SRE

steps.what: Deployments, Services, probes, replicas, PodDisruptionBudgets, node failure behaviour, resource limits, rescheduling
Metrics, logs and traces, RED/USE methods, dashboards for steady state, distributed tracing to locate failing hops
SLIs, SLOs and error budgets, alerting on symptoms, toil, runbooks, game days, blameless culture

phases.build: The demo app on a kind cluster with Prometheus, Grafana and Jaeger, SLOs and error-budget alerts defined for checkout latency and availability, and runbooks for the top three alerts.

phases.title: Chaos experiments and learning from them

steps.what: Chaos experiment CRDs, pod-kill, network and stress faults, probes and abort conditions, scheduling experiments, running safely in CI
Timelines, contributing factors, five whys and its limits, writing blameless reports, tracking follow-up actions

phases.build: A game day run with LitmusChaos or Chaos Mesh: five hypothesis-driven experiments with abort conditions, SLO impact charts, resilience fixes, and a blameless write-up of the weaknesses found.

internal-tools-eng.summary: Learn web fundamentals and databases, become a capable full-stack developer, connect systems through APIs, automation and CI/CD, then design polished internal tools around what colleagues actually need.

phases.title: Web fundamentals

steps.what: Branches, pull requests, code review, resolving conflicts, semantic commit history
Semantic HTML, forms and validation, flexbox and grid, responsive layout, accessible tables and inputs
Types, functions, async/await, fetch, modules, DOM manipulation, error handling, TypeScript interfaces and generics

phases.build: A browser-based log viewer in plain TypeScript that loads JSON log files, filters by level, service and time range, highlights error spikes, and exports filtered results to CSV.

phases.title: Full-stack applications

steps.what: Relational modelling, SQL joins and aggregations, indexes, transactions, migrations, ORMs, audit tables
REST backends, authentication and roles, server and client rendering, forms, pagination, validation, deployment of a web app with a React frontend

phases.build: An equipment-checkout system for a college lab: PostgreSQL schema with history tables, Express or FastAPI backend with role-based login, a React UI for issue and return, and a full audit trail.

phases.title: Integrations and automation

steps.what: REST and GraphQL clients, OAuth 2.0, webhooks, rate limits and retries, pagination, syncing data between SaaS tools, idempotent sync jobs
Scheduled Python jobs, data cleanup scripts, CSV and spreadsheet automation, cron and serverless triggers, logging
Automated tests and linting on pull requests, preview deployments, environment variables and secrets, database migrations in pipelines

phases.build: A Slack bot connected to the checkout system that lets users request and return equipment, posts overdue reminders from a scheduled job, syncs a daily summary to Google Sheets, and deploys through CI.

phases.title: Designing internal tools people use

steps.what: Admin console patterns, bulk actions, permissions and approvals, audit logs, safe destructive actions, build vs low-code (Retool, Appsmith) tradeoffs
Data-heavy UIs: tables with sort and filter, server state with React Query, complex forms, component libraries, performance with large lists
Shadowing users, task analysis, usability tests, keyboard-first workflows, error messages, measuring time saved

phases.build: An admin console for the lab system with role-based approvals, bulk actions, an audit-log viewer and fast filterable tables, usability-tested with three real users and revised, with time-saved figures.

platform-architect.summary: Build programming, Linux and container basics, learn API design and Kubernetes on a cloud, then architect an internal platform in Terraform and finish with scalability, security and writing technical strategy.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: Syntax, structs and interfaces, error handling, goroutines and channels, HTTP servers, testing, modules
Branches, pull requests, code review, monorepo vs polyrepo tradeoffs
Processes, permissions, systemd, networking commands, logs, SSH
Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, image tagging, Compose, registries

phases.build: A Go HTTP service with structured logging, env-based config, graceful shutdown, health endpoints and unit tests, shipped as a small multi-stage Docker image.

phases.title: APIs, services and Kubernetes on a cloud

steps.what: REST resource modelling, OpenAPI, gRPC and protobuf, versioning, pagination, idempotency keys, error contracts, service boundaries
Managed Kubernetes, VPC and IAM integration, Deployments, Services, Ingress, autoscaling, namespaces and quotas, workload identity

phases.build: Two Go microservices with versioned OpenAPI and gRPC contracts deployed to managed Kubernetes with Ingress, autoscaling and per-team namespaces with quotas, plus a contract-change compatibility check in CI.

phases.title: Architecting the platform

steps.what: Internal developer platform layers, golden paths, multi-tenancy, C4 diagrams, ADRs, build vs buy, platform-as-product thinking
Modules, remote state, environment layout, provisioning clusters, namespaces-as-a-service modules, module versioning and registries

phases.build: A small internal platform design: C4 diagrams, six ADRs, and Terraform modules that provision a cluster and give each team a namespace with quotas, RBAC and a CI-ready service template.

phases.title: Scale, reliability and security

steps.what: Caching, queues, horizontal scaling, multi-AZ design, SLOs, backpressure, rate limiting, load testing, graceful degradation
Threat modeling, zero trust, mTLS, workload identity, secrets management, policy as code, network segmentation, supply-chain security

phases.build: The platform load-tested with k6 to find its limits, then improved with caching, a queue and rate limiting to meet defined SLOs, and secured with mTLS, Vault-issued secrets and Gatekeeper policies.

phases.title: Strategy and alignment

steps.what: Writing RFCs, 12-month roadmaps, build-vs-buy analysis, adoption metrics, sequencing migrations, deprecating legacy paths
Gathering requirements from product teams, presenting tradeoffs, handling disagreement, getting buy-in, communicating platform changes

phases.build: A platform RFC with a 12-month roadmap and a Backstage-vs-Port build-vs-buy analysis, reviewed by three peers acting as product teams, with their objections and your responses recorded in the doc.

cloudops-eng.summary: Learn Linux and networking, operate a real cloud environment with scripted automation, build monitoring and practise incident response, then manage cost, deployments and tickets like an ops team.

phases.title: Linux and networking basics

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, keeping scripts and runbooks in version control
IP addressing and CIDR, DNS, HTTP/TLS, ports, NAT, load balancers, troubleshooting with ping, curl, dig and traceroute
Filesystem, permissions, processes, systemd services, logs and journald, disk and memory checks, cron, SSH

phases.build: An Ubuntu server running Nginx and a Python app as systemd services with log rotation, a cron health check that restarts the app on failure, and a troubleshooting runbook for common faults.

phases.title: Operating a cloud environment

steps.what: IAM, VPC, EC2 and auto scaling, S3, RDS, Systems Manager for patching and run commands, backups, service quotas, health dashboards
Bash and Python boto3 scripts, Lambda with EventBridge schedules, automating snapshots, start/stop of dev instances, routine checks

phases.build: An AWS environment with an auto-scaled web tier and RDS, patched via Systems Manager, plus scheduled Lambda jobs that snapshot volumes nightly and stop untagged dev instances outside working hours.

phases.title: Monitoring and incident response

steps.what: CloudWatch metrics, logs and alarms, composite alarms, dashboards, Prometheus and Grafana, alert routing, reducing noisy alerts
Triage and severity levels, runbooks, escalation, communication during incidents, mitigation and rollback, blameless postmortems

phases.build: Dashboards and alarms for the phase-2 environment routed via SNS to Slack, then three injected failures (full disk, CPU spike, failing health checks) handled using runbooks and written up as postmortems.

phases.title: Cost, deployments and ops process

steps.what: Tagging policies, budgets and anomaly alerts, Cost Explorer, rightsizing, reserved and spot capacity, cleaning up orphaned resources
Pipeline stages, deploying to cloud with approvals, rollbacks, secrets in pipelines, OIDC authentication
Incident, request and change tickets, SLAs, ITIL basics, queues and prioritization, linking tickets to alerts

phases.build: A cost report with tagging policy, budgets and a rightsizing plan for the environment, a GitHub Actions deploy with approval and rollback, and a Jira Service Management project wired to receive alert-created incidents.

cloud-engineer.summary: Get comfortable on Linux and networks, go deep on one cloud (AWS), then codify it with Terraform, ship it through pipelines and run containers you can monitor.

phases.title: Operating-system and network foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, merges, pull requests, rebasing basics, .gitignore, resolving conflicts, writing useful commit messages
Filesystem layout, permissions, users/groups, processes, systemd services, package managers, SSH keys, logs in journalctl, disk and memory inspection
OSI/TCP-IP layers, IP addressing and CIDR subnetting, routing tables, DNS resolution, HTTP/TLS, ports, NAT, troubleshooting with dig, curl, traceroute

phases.build: A hardened Ubuntu VM serving a site over HTTPS behind Nginx, with SSH-key-only access, a UFW firewall, a systemd service, and a written runbook of the network path from browser to process.

phases.title: Core AWS and scripting

steps.what: IAM users/roles/policies, VPC with public/private subnets, EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, ALB, Route 53, CloudWatch, AWS CLI, shared responsibility model, free-tier hygiene
Python basics, functions, JSON/YAML parsing, boto3 for AWS automation, Bash scripting with loops and exit codes, cron jobs, argparse CLIs

phases.build: A two-tier app on AWS (ALB + EC2 Auto Scaling + RDS in private subnets) plus a boto3 script that finds untagged or idle resources and posts a nightly report to S3.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code and delivery

steps.what: HCL syntax, providers, resources, variables/outputs, remote state in S3 with locking, modules, workspaces, plan/apply workflow, importing existing resources
Pipeline stages, build/test/deploy jobs, secrets handling, OIDC to AWS, terraform plan on pull request and apply on merge, artifact versioning, rollbacks

phases.build: A reusable Terraform module set (VPC, compute, database) for dev and prod, deployed by a GitHub Actions pipeline that posts plans on PRs and applies on merge using OIDC instead of static keys.

phases.title: Containers and observability

steps.what: Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, image registries, Compose; Kubernetes pods, deployments, services, ingress, ConfigMaps/Secrets, EKS basics, kubectl debugging
Metrics vs logs vs traces, CloudWatch alarms and dashboards, Prometheus scraping, Grafana panels, alert thresholds, SLO basics

phases.build: A containerised API running on EKS (provisioned by your Terraform), with Prometheus/Grafana dashboards and CloudWatch alarms that page on error rate and latency.

solutions-architect.summary: Build enough engineering and cloud depth to design credible systems, then learn to scope, cost and pitch those designs to customers.

phases.title: Technical foundations

steps.what: Core syntax, functions, data structures, calling REST APIs with requests, reading JSON, writing small scripts for proofs of concept
Shell navigation, permissions, processes, package installs, SSH, environment variables, reading logs on a server
TCP/IP, CIDR subnetting, DNS, HTTP/TLS, load balancers, NAT, VPNs, private vs public connectivity, latency and bandwidth trade-offs

phases.build: A small Python service deployed on a Linux VM behind a reverse proxy with TLS, plus a one-page network diagram explaining every hop a request takes.

phases.title: Cloud platforms and security

steps.what: Compute, storage, databases, serverless, VPC/VNet, IAM and managed services on AWS, plus the equivalent Azure and GCP services and how they map across providers
Shared responsibility, IAM least privilege, encryption at rest/in transit, secrets management, network segmentation, OWASP Top 10, compliance basics (ISO 27001, SOC 2)

phases.build: The same three-tier web app deployed on AWS and on Azure, with a comparison doc mapping each service, its security controls and the trade-offs between the two platforms.

phases.title: Designing and costing solutions

steps.what: Requirements gathering, functional vs non-functional needs, reference architectures, scalability/HA patterns, architecture diagrams, ADRs, Well-Architected reviews
Pricing models (on-demand, reserved, spot), pricing calculators, TCO comparison vs on-prem, sizing assumptions, presenting cost ranges

phases.build: A full solution design for a fictional retailer's e-commerce platform: requirements, architecture diagrams, ADRs, HA/DR approach and a monthly cost estimate with three sizing scenarios.

phases.title: Customer-facing delivery

steps.what: Structuring technical narratives, whiteboarding, writing proposals and executive summaries, tailoring depth to audience, handling objections
Discovery calls, qualifying requirements, scoping a proof of concept, demo design, RFP responses, statements of work, success criteria
The 7 Rs of migration, application discovery, dependency mapping, wave planning, cutover and rollback plans

phases.build: A recorded 15-minute customer pitch and working proof of concept that answers a mock RFP, including a proposal document, a migration plan for their legacy app and defined POC success criteria.

systems-architect.summary: Master Linux, networks and the physical/virtual infrastructure stack, then learn to design platforms for availability and capacity and document them as standards.

phases.title: OS and network foundations

steps.what: Shell scripting, variables, loops, conditionals, pipes, text processing with grep/sed/awk, exit codes, scheduling with cron
Kernel vs user space, boot process, systemd, filesystems and LVM, process scheduling, memory management, performance tools, SELinux basics
TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs, routing and switching basics, DNS, DHCP, load balancing, firewalls, network troubleshooting

phases.build: A multi-VLAN lab network in Packet Tracer or GNS3 with Linux servers providing DNS and DHCP, plus a shell-script health checker that reports CPU, memory, disk and service status across the hosts.

phases.title: Infrastructure and virtualization

steps.what: Server hardware, CPU/RAM/NUMA basics, RAID, SAN/NAS and object storage, data-center power/cooling, on-prem vs cloud compute, IaaS building blocks
Type 1 vs Type 2 hypervisors, VM resource allocation, templates and snapshots, live migration, virtual switches, containers vs VMs

phases.build: A home-lab private cloud on Proxmox with shared NFS storage, VM templates, a virtual network, and documented live migration of a running VM between two nodes.

phases.title: Designing for reliability

steps.what: Requirements to architecture, layered designs, scalability (vertical/horizontal), caching, queues, consistency trade-offs, failure domains, architecture diagrams
Redundancy and failover, clustering (Pacemaker/keepalived), load-balanced pairs, RTO/RPO, health checks, eliminating single points of failure, chaos testing

phases.build: A highly available web platform in your lab: HAProxy pair with keepalived virtual IP, replicated database, and a failure-injection test report showing measured failover times against target RTO.

phases.title: Capacity and standards

steps.what: Utilisation baselines, growth forecasting, headroom policies, load testing, IOPS/throughput sizing, right-sizing VMs, reading performance metrics
Architecture design documents, standards and runbooks, decision records, diagrams-as-code, writing for reviewers and operators

phases.build: A capacity plan for your HA platform driven by k6 load tests and Grafana data, packaged with a full architecture design document, operational runbook and decision records.

infrastructure-architect.summary: Build hands-on fluency in networks, virtualization and cloud, then learn to set reference designs for security, disaster recovery and automated, code-driven builds.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Filesystems, permissions, systemd, networking commands, package management, storage and LVM, log inspection, SSH administration
Version control for configs and code: commits, branches, pull requests, code review flow, tagging releases
TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs, routing, DNS/DHCP, firewalls, load balancers, VPNs, data-center network topologies (spine-leaf)

phases.build: A segmented lab network with VLANs, a firewall and a site-to-site VPN between two simulated sites, with all router and server configs versioned in a Git repository.

phases.title: Compute platforms: virtual and cloud

steps.what: Hypervisors (ESXi, KVM, Hyper-V), clusters, resource pools, HA and live migration, virtual networking, storage for VMs
IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, VPC design, compute, block/object storage, managed databases, IAM, hybrid connectivity, landing zones, AWS/Azure core services

phases.build: A hybrid lab: an on-prem Proxmox cluster connected by VPN to an AWS landing zone, with a workload able to run in either location and a comparison of cost and performance.

phases.title: Reference architecture, security and DR

steps.what: Reference architectures, compute/storage/network sizing, standards and patterns, design reviews, HLD/LLD documents, trade-off analysis
Defense in depth, network segmentation, IAM, encryption, hardening baselines (CIS), patching strategy, logging and audit
RTO/RPO, backup vs replication, pilot light/warm standby/multi-site patterns, DR runbooks, failover testing

phases.build: A reference architecture pack for a mid-size company: HLD/LLD, segmentation and hardening standards, and a tested DR plan with documented failover of a workload to a second region.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code and automation

steps.what: Terraform providers, modules, remote state, environments, policy-as-code checks, codifying reference designs as reusable modules
Configuration management with Ansible playbooks and roles, Python/Bash scripting, idempotency, scheduled compliance checks

phases.build: Your reference architecture turned into Terraform modules plus Ansible roles that build a compliant environment from scratch, with Checkov policy checks enforcing your security standards.

finops-engineer.summary: Learn cloud and data basics, then master billing data and cost-optimisation levers, apply the FinOps Framework and turn spend into dashboards and forecasts.

phases.title: Cloud and data foundations

steps.what: Core compute, storage, database and networking services on AWS and Azure, pricing dimensions, regions, managed vs self-managed services
Pivot tables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, conditional formatting, charts, building simple cost models with scenarios
Syntax, functions, pandas DataFrames, groupby/pivot, reading CSV/Parquet, calling cloud SDKs (boto3, azure-mgmt) for cost data
SELECT, joins, GROUP BY, window functions, CTEs, date functions, querying large billing tables, cost allocation queries

phases.build: A pandas and SQL analysis of a public cloud billing sample (e.g. FOCUS sample data) that ranks spend by service, account and day and flags the top five cost spikes with explanations.

phases.title: Billing data and cost optimisation

steps.what: AWS Cost and Usage Report, Cost Explorer, Azure Cost Management exports, line-item types, blended vs unblended cost, credits, budgets and alerts
Rightsizing, idle resource cleanup, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans, spot usage, storage tiering, data-transfer costs, commitment coverage and utilisation

phases.build: A cost-optimisation report on your own AWS free-tier/sandbox account using CUR queried in Athena: identified waste, rightsizing and Savings Plan recommendations with estimated monthly savings.

phases.title: FinOps practice and governance

steps.what: Inform/Optimize/Operate phases, FinOps principles and personas, maturity model (crawl/walk/run), unit economics, showback vs chargeback, FOCUS spec
Tagging strategy and mandatory tags, tag policies, AWS Organizations SCPs, Azure Policy, budgets, cost allocation for untagged spend

phases.build: A FinOps playbook for a fictional startup: tagging standard enforced by Azure Policy or AWS tag policies, showback model by team, and a maturity assessment with a 90-day improvement plan.

phases.title: Reporting and forecasting

steps.what: Data modelling for cost data, KPIs (cost per unit, coverage, waste %), drill-downs by team/service, scheduled refresh, dashboard design for finance and engineers
Trend and seasonality, linear and exponential smoothing models, budget vs actual variance, scenario planning for growth and commitments

phases.build: A Power BI cloud-cost dashboard with team-level showback, unit-cost KPIs and a 6-month spend forecast (Prophet) compared against budget, refreshed from billing exports.

virtualization-engineer.summary: Start with server, OS and network basics, master ESXi and vSphere clusters, then add storage, automation, Hyper-V and backup/DR.

phases.title: Server, OS and network basics

steps.what: CPU sockets/cores, RAM, NICs, HBAs, RAID controllers, BIOS/UEFI, out-of-band management (iDRAC/iLO), hardware compatibility lists
Windows Server roles, Active Directory and DNS basics, Linux administration, services, permissions, patching, remote management
TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs and trunking, link aggregation, routing basics, DNS/NTP, how traffic leaves a hypervisor host

phases.build: A lab with a Windows Server domain controller (AD, DNS) and a Linux server on separate VLANs, documented with an IP plan and network diagram, ready to host hypervisors.

phases.title: ESXi and vSphere

steps.what: Installing ESXi (nested lab), host client, datastores, standard vSwitches and port groups, VM creation, VMware Tools, host patching, ESXi shell basics
vCenter deployment, clusters, HA and DRS, vMotion/Storage vMotion, resource pools, templates, distributed switches, permissions, lifecycle manager

phases.build: A nested vSphere lab: three ESXi hosts under vCenter with an HA/DRS cluster, distributed switch, VM templates, and documented vMotion and simulated host-failure tests.

phases.title: Storage and automation

steps.what: VMFS vs NFS datastores, iSCSI, thin/thick provisioning, RAID levels, IOPS and latency, multipathing, vSAN concepts, storage policies
PowerShell basics, PowerCLI cmdlets, bulk VM deployment, inventory and snapshot reports, scheduled tasks, error handling

phases.build: An iSCSI/NFS-backed vSphere cluster using TrueNAS, plus a PowerCLI toolkit that bulk-deploys VMs from CSV and emails a weekly report of old snapshots and over-provisioned VMs.

phases.title: Hyper-V and protection

steps.what: Hyper-V role installation, virtual switches, generation 1/2 VMs, checkpoints, failover clustering, live migration, SCVMM concepts, migrating VMs from VMware
Image-based backups, 3-2-1 rule, RPO/RTO, replication, restore testing, application-consistent snapshots, DR runbooks

phases.build: A Hyper-V failover cluster alongside your vSphere lab, with Veeam protecting both, a VM migrated from ESXi to Hyper-V, and a tested restore with measured RTO in a DR runbook.

storage-engineer.summary: Learn Linux and networking, then storage protocols and arrays, vendor platforms and backup, and finally cloud storage and automation.

phases.title: Systems foundations

steps.what: Block devices, partitions, filesystems (ext4/XFS), LVM, mount options, multipath, iostat/fio performance testing, NFS and iSCSI client setup
TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs, jumbo frames, link aggregation, storage network isolation, latency and throughput fundamentals

phases.build: A Linux storage benchmark lab: LVM volumes on different filesystems tested with fio across block sizes, with a report on IOPS, throughput and latency differences.

phases.title: Storage protocols and arrays

steps.what: Block vs file vs object, iSCSI targets/initiators, LUNs and masking, NFS and SMB shares, permissions, SAN vs NAS use cases
RAID levels and erasure coding, controllers and caching, thin provisioning, dedupe/compression, snapshots, tiering, all-flash vs hybrid, IOPS sizing
FC topology, HBAs, WWNs, zoning (single-initiator), fabric switches, FCoE basics, comparing FC with iSCSI and NVMe-oF

phases.build: A ZFS-based array in TrueNAS serving iSCSI LUNs to a Linux host and NFS/SMB shares to clients, with snapshots, compression stats and a written zoning plan for a hypothetical FC fabric.

phases.title: Enterprise platforms and data protection

steps.what: NetApp ONTAP SVMs, aggregates, volumes, SnapMirror; Dell PowerStore/Unity concepts; vendor management GUIs and CLIs via simulators
Full/incremental/differential backups, 3-2-1 rule, RPO/RTO, replication vs backup, immutable backups against ransomware, restore testing

phases.build: An ONTAP simulator pair with SnapMirror replication between two clusters, plus an immutable backup job with a documented restore test and measured RTO/RPO.

phases.title: Cloud storage and automation

steps.what: S3 buckets, storage classes, lifecycle rules, versioning, object lock, Azure Blob tiers, EBS/managed disks, hybrid gateways, cost per GB
Python and Bash for storage tasks, REST APIs of arrays, Ansible storage modules, capacity reporting and alerting scripts

phases.build: A tiered archive pipeline that pushes aged NAS data to S3 with lifecycle rules into Glacier, plus a Python script using the ONTAP REST API to produce a daily capacity and growth report.

aws-solutions-architect.summary: Build Linux, Python and networking basics, master core AWS services and security, then design Well-Architected solutions and codify them with infrastructure as code.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Shell commands, permissions, processes, package management, SSH, systemd services, reading logs
Syntax, functions, data structures, JSON handling, calling APIs, writing small Lambda-style handlers
TCP/IP, CIDR subnetting, routing, DNS, HTTP/TLS, NAT, load balancing, VPN concepts, private vs public addressing

phases.build: A Linux server running a Python API behind Nginx with TLS, plus a subnetting plan and network diagram for a three-tier app that you will later rebuild on AWS.

phases.title: Core AWS services

steps.what: Global infrastructure, regions/AZs, AWS CLI, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway, SQS/SNS, CloudFront, Route 53, CloudWatch; Cloud Practitioner/SAA scope
EC2 instance types, AMIs, Auto Scaling, EBS; S3 storage classes, policies, versioning; VPC subnets, route tables, IGW/NAT, security groups, NACLs, endpoints
IAM users/roles/policies, least privilege, STS and role assumption, KMS encryption, Secrets Manager, GuardDuty, CloudTrail, Security Hub

phases.build: A production-style VPC with public/private subnets across two AZs running an Auto Scaling web tier, private RDS, S3 static assets via CloudFront, least-privilege IAM roles and CloudTrail logging.

phases.title: Designing Well-Architected solutions

steps.what: Translating requirements into architectures, serverless vs container vs EC2 trade-offs, event-driven patterns, multi-AZ/multi-region, DR strategies, architecture diagrams
Six pillars (operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, cost, sustainability), lenses, running a WA review, prioritising high-risk issues

phases.build: A serverless event-driven order-processing design (API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, DynamoDB) with diagrams, DR strategy and a completed Well-Architected review listing risks and fixes.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code and cost

steps.what: CloudFormation templates, parameters, nested stacks, change sets; Terraform providers, modules, remote state; choosing between them
Pricing models, Savings Plans/RIs, spot, rightsizing, S3 lifecycle tiers, data transfer costs, budgets and Cost Explorer

phases.build: Your Phase 3 architecture fully deployed from Terraform or CloudFormation in one command, with a cost estimate, AWS Budgets alerts and a write-up of three cost optimisations you applied.

azure-cloud-engineer.summary: Learn scripting and admin basics, master core Azure services, identity and networking, then automate with Bicep and Terraform and run containers on AKS.

phases.title: Admin and scripting foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, merge conflicts, repository structure for infrastructure code
Shell navigation, permissions, services, package management, SSH keys, log inspection on Linux VMs
Cmdlets, pipeline and objects, variables, loops, functions, modules, error handling, Az PowerShell module for managing Azure resources

phases.build: A PowerShell module in a Git repo that audits a Windows/Linux host (services, disk, patches, open ports) and outputs an HTML report, with tests and a README.

phases.title: Core Azure, identity and networking

steps.what: Subscriptions, resource groups, VMs, App Service, Storage accounts, Azure SQL, Functions, Key Vault, Azure CLI, AZ-900/AZ-104 scope
Users, groups, app registrations, service principals, managed identities, Azure RBAC roles and scopes, Conditional Access, PIM basics
VNets, subnets, NSGs, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, Application Gateway, Load Balancer, VPN Gateway, Azure DNS

phases.build: A hub-and-spoke Azure network with Azure Firewall, an App Service web app reaching Azure SQL via private endpoint, secrets in Key Vault accessed through managed identity, and RBAC by team.

phases.title: Infrastructure as code

steps.what: ARM template structure, Bicep syntax, parameters, modules, loops/conditions, deployment scopes, what-if, deploying via Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions
AzureRM provider, state in Azure Storage, modules, workspaces, variables, plan/apply in pipelines, importing existing resources

phases.build: Your Phase 2 hub-and-spoke environment rebuilt as Bicep modules deployed by a pipeline with what-if previews, plus the same spoke in Terraform with a write-up comparing the two.

phases.title: Containers and operations

steps.what: Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, image tagging, Azure Container Registry, running and debugging containers locally
AKS cluster creation, node pools, kubectl, deployments, services, ingress, workload identity, ACR integration, autoscaling, upgrades
Azure Monitor metrics and alerts, Log Analytics and KQL queries, Application Insights, Container Insights, workbooks

phases.build: A containerised microservice on AKS (provisioned by Bicep) pulling from ACR with workload identity, Helm-deployed, with Container Insights and KQL-based alerts for pod restarts and latency.

gcp-cloud-architect.summary: Build Linux, Python and networking foundations, master GCP core services and IAM, add GKE and BigQuery, then design and codify complete GCP solutions.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Shell commands, permissions, processes, systemd, package management, SSH, log inspection on cloud VMs
Syntax, functions, data structures, HTTP APIs, JSON, writing small services and Cloud Functions-style handlers
TCP/IP, CIDR subnetting, routing, DNS, HTTP/TLS, NAT, load balancing, VPN and interconnect concepts

phases.build: A Flask API on a Linux VM behind a TLS reverse proxy, with a subnet plan and network diagram for a multi-tier app you will rebuild on GCP.

phases.title: Core Google Cloud

steps.what: Projects, folders, billing, Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Cloud Functions, gcloud CLI, Cloud Logging; ACE exam scope
Resource hierarchy and IAM roles, service accounts, workload identity federation, org policies, VPC Service Controls, Cloud KMS, Secret Manager

phases.build: A Cloud Run service backed by Cloud SQL and Pub/Sub in a properly structured project with least-privilege service accounts, secrets in Secret Manager and an org policy restricting regions.

phases.title: Kubernetes and data on GCP

steps.what: Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, Artifact Registry, local debugging, image security scanning
Autopilot vs Standard clusters, deployments, services, ingress, workload identity, node pools, autoscaling, upgrades, kubectl troubleshooting
SELECT, joins, GROUP BY, window functions, CTEs, date handling, query planning basics
Datasets, partitioning and clustering, loading and streaming data, slots vs on-demand pricing, scheduled queries, views and authorised datasets

phases.build: An analytics pipeline: a GKE-hosted ingestion service publishing events to Pub/Sub, landing in a partitioned BigQuery table, with scheduled queries feeding a Looker Studio dashboard.

phases.title: Architecting and codifying solutions

steps.what: Requirements to architecture, choosing Cloud Run vs GKE vs Compute Engine, HA and DR across regions, Google Cloud Architecture Framework, design docs and diagrams
Google provider, state in GCS, modules, project factory pattern, variables per environment, plan/apply in Cloud Build
Committed and sustained use discounts, rightsizing recommendations, BigQuery cost controls, budgets and billing export to BigQuery

phases.build: A Professional Cloud Architect-style case study answer: full design doc for a data-heavy SaaS on GCP, deployed via Terraform in Cloud Build, with a billing-export cost dashboard and budget alerts.

enterprise-architect.summary: Build a base in software delivery, data and cloud, then learn business strategy and EA modelling, the TOGAF method, solution design and governance.

phases.title: Technology foundations

steps.what: Relational modelling, keys and normalisation, SELECT with joins and aggregations, how business data flows through systems
Waterfall vs Agile/Scrum, requirements to release, environments, testing stages, DevOps basics, how IT projects are funded and delivered
IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, core AWS/Azure services, hybrid and multi-cloud, cloud operating models, landing zones, cloud cost drivers

phases.build: A system landscape map of a real organisation you know (college ERP, a family business): its applications, data flows and hosting, with a short note on which pieces should move to SaaS or cloud.

phases.title: Business strategy and EA modelling

steps.what: Business model canvas, value chains, competitive strategy, OKRs, business cases and ROI/NPV basics, digital transformation drivers
Business, data, application and technology layers, capability maps, value streams, application portfolio rationalisation, ArchiMate notation

phases.build: A capability map and ArchiMate model (in Archi) for a fictional bank, linking business capabilities to applications and infrastructure, with a heatmap highlighting redundant and at-risk systems.

phases.title: TOGAF and solution design

steps.what: ADM phases (Preliminary to H), architecture vision, baseline vs target, gap analysis, building blocks, architecture repository, TOGAF Foundation exam scope
Translating target architecture into solutions, integration patterns (APIs, events, ETL), non-functional requirements, architecture decision records

phases.build: A TOGAF ADM walk-through for the fictional bank's mobile-first initiative: architecture vision, baseline/target models, gap analysis and one detailed solution design with ADRs.

phases.title: Governance and roadmaps

steps.what: Architecture review boards, principles and standards, technology radar, compliance checks, exception handling, COBIT/ITIL awareness
Stakeholder mapping (power/interest), executive communication, facilitation, negotiating trade-offs, presenting to non-technical leaders
Transition architectures, sequencing initiatives by dependency and value, migration planning, portfolio prioritisation, roadmap visualisation

phases.build: A 3-year technology roadmap for the fictional bank with transition architectures, architecture principles, a tech radar, and a 10-slide board presentation backed by a stakeholder map.

cloud-infrastructure-engineer.summary: Build Linux, networking and Python automation skills, master one cloud and Terraform, then add Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines and monitoring for a self-service platform.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, pull requests, code review, merge conflicts, tagging, monorepo vs multi-repo for infrastructure code
Filesystem, permissions, processes, systemd, package management, SSH, networking commands, performance and log troubleshooting
TCP/IP, CIDR subnetting, routing, DNS, HTTP/TLS, NAT, load balancers, firewalls, VPN and peering concepts
Python syntax, functions, modules, file/JSON/YAML handling, subprocess, REST APIs, cloud SDKs, Bash scripting, writing small CLIs

phases.build: A Python CLI that provisions and configures Linux VMs over SSH (users, firewall, packages), versioned in Git with tests and documented networking setup.

phases.title: Cloud and infrastructure as code

steps.what: VPC/VNet design, compute, object/block storage, managed databases, IAM roles and policies, load balancers, DNS; deep on AWS with service mapping to Azure/GCP
HCL, providers, modules, remote state and locking, workspaces, module versioning, testing with terratest, policy checks, drift detection

phases.build: A versioned Terraform module library (network, compute, database, IAM) that lets a team self-serve a full environment by filling in one variables file, with Checkov scans and tests.

phases.title: Containers and Kubernetes

steps.what: Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, image registries, networking and volumes, Compose for local stacks, image scanning
Pods, deployments, services, ingress, ConfigMaps/Secrets, RBAC, namespaces, Helm charts, managed clusters (EKS/AKS/GKE), autoscaling

phases.build: A managed Kubernetes cluster provisioned by your Terraform modules, with namespaces per team, RBAC, an ingress controller and Helm charts for two sample services.

phases.title: Delivery pipelines and observability

steps.what: Pipeline design, plan-on-PR/apply-on-merge for Terraform, container build and deploy, OIDC federation to cloud, environments and approvals, GitOps with Argo CD
Metrics, logs and traces, Prometheus and exporters, Grafana dashboards, alert rules, cloud-native monitoring, SLIs and SLOs

phases.build: An end-to-end platform repo: GitHub Actions running Terraform plans on PRs, Argo CD syncing apps to your cluster, and Grafana dashboards with SLO-based alerts for the deployed services.

cloud-security-architect.summary: Start with Linux, networking and security fundamentals, learn cloud platforms with IAM and cloud security controls, then design zero-trust, encrypted, compliant architectures.

phases.title: Security foundations

steps.what: Permissions, users and sudo, processes, services, SSH hardening, logs and auditd, firewall rules with iptables/nftables
TCP/IP, subnetting, routing, DNS, HTTP/TLS handshakes, common ports, packet captures, NAT and VPN concepts
CIA triad, common attacks, authentication vs authorisation, hashing vs encryption, PKI and certificates, OWASP Top 10, logging and incident basics

phases.build: A hardened Linux web server (SSH keys only, nftables, auditd, TLS via your own CA) and a short report of nmap and Wireshark evidence showing exactly what is and is not exposed.

phases.title: Cloud platforms and identity

steps.what: Core AWS/Azure services, VPC/VNet, compute, storage, shared responsibility model, organisations and account structure, CLI usage
Users, roles, policies and conditions, least privilege, role assumption, permission boundaries, SCPs, federation and SSO (SAML/OIDC), access reviews
Guardrails, CSPM, logging with CloudTrail, threat detection, security posture scoring, misconfiguration remediation, container and serverless security basics

phases.build: A multi-account AWS organisation with SSO, SCP guardrails, centralised CloudTrail and Security Hub, plus a Prowler scan before and after remediation showing the posture score improvement.

phases.title: Network, data and zero-trust controls

steps.what: Security groups vs NACLs, cloud firewalls, WAF rules, private endpoints, segmentation, egress control, DDoS protection, flow log analysis
Symmetric vs asymmetric keys, envelope encryption, KMS key policies and rotation, customer-managed keys, TLS everywhere, secrets management
Never-trust principles, identity-aware proxies, device posture, microsegmentation, continuous verification, NIST SP 800-207 model

phases.build: A segmented three-tier app with WAF, private endpoints, egress filtering, KMS customer-managed keys and Vault-managed secrets, with admin access only through an identity-aware proxy (no VPN, no bastion).

phases.title: Architecture, compliance and threat modelling

steps.what: Reference security architectures, defense in depth, landing zone design, security patterns and guardrails-as-code, writing security design standards
ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, CIS Benchmarks, India DPDP Act basics, mapping controls to cloud services, evidence collection, automated compliance checks
STRIDE, data flow diagrams, attack trees, trust boundaries, prioritising mitigations, MITRE ATT&CK cloud matrix

phases.build: A secure landing-zone reference architecture codified in Terraform with OPA policies, a CIS/ISO 27001 control mapping backed by AWS Config rules, and a STRIDE threat model of a sample workload.

cloud-network-engineer.summary: Master classic networking first, then cloud VPC/VNet design and firewalls, followed by BGP-based hybrid connectivity and network infrastructure as code.

phases.title: Networking fundamentals

steps.what: OSI/TCP-IP models, IPv4/IPv6, CIDR subnetting, switching and VLANs, static routing, NAT, TCP vs UDP, packet analysis, CCNA-level topics
Networking commands (ip, ss, tcpdump, traceroute), interfaces and routes, iptables basics, SSH, troubleshooting connectivity from a host
Resolution process, record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV), TTLs, authoritative vs recursive, split-horizon DNS, private hosted zones, DNSSEC basics

phases.build: A multi-site Packet Tracer topology with VLANs, inter-VLAN routing and NAT, plus a BIND server providing split-horizon DNS, with Wireshark captures explaining each traffic flow.

phases.title: Cloud network design

steps.what: Cloud network constructs across AWS/Azure/GCP, regions and AZs, private connectivity, service endpoints, hub-and-spoke vs mesh, Transit Gateway and Virtual WAN
VPC/VNet CIDR planning, public/private subnets, route tables, internet and NAT gateways, peering, security groups, NACLs/NSGs, flow logs
Stateful vs stateless filtering, next-gen firewall features, cloud-native firewalls, centralised inspection VPC, rule design and logging

phases.build: A multi-VPC AWS hub-and-spoke design using Transit Gateway with a centralised inspection VPC running AWS Network Firewall, documented IP plan and flow-log evidence of blocked and allowed traffic.

phases.title: Routing and hybrid connectivity

steps.what: Dynamic routing, OSPF basics, BGP sessions, ASNs, path attributes (AS-path, local pref, MED), route filtering, route propagation in cloud route tables
IPsec site-to-site VPN, BGP over VPN, AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute concepts, redundancy designs, MTU and failover testing

phases.build: A simulated on-prem site (strongSwan + FRRouting on a Linux VM) connected to AWS by redundant IPsec tunnels with BGP, demonstrating automatic failover when one tunnel is cut.

phases.title: Automation and traffic distribution

steps.what: Network modules for VPCs, subnets, route tables, TGW attachments and firewalls; remote state, variables per environment, plan review
L4 vs L7 load balancers, ALB/NLB, health checks, TLS termination, sticky sessions, global load balancing and DNS-based failover

phases.build: Your entire hub-and-spoke and hybrid network rebuilt in Terraform modules, fronted by an ALB and NLB with Route 53 health-check failover across two regions.

cloud-migration-engineer.summary: Learn Linux, networking and databases, become fluent in a cloud platform and automation, then run assessments, plan migration waves and execute rehost/replatform cutovers.

phases.title: Source-estate foundations

steps.what: Server administration, services, filesystems, package management, SSH, log inspection, preparing servers for replication agents
TCP/IP, subnetting, DNS, firewalls, NAT, VPNs, latency and bandwidth planning for data transfer, hybrid connectivity concepts
SQL, MySQL/PostgreSQL administration, backups and restores, replication, schema and data migration, managed cloud databases (RDS, Azure SQL)

phases.build: A mock on-prem estate: a three-tier app (web, app, PostgreSQL) on local VMs with documented network flows, dependencies and a tested backup-and-restore of the database.

phases.title: Target cloud and automation

steps.what: AWS and Azure core services: VPC/VNet, EC2/VMs, storage, managed databases, IAM, landing zones, hybrid connectivity, service mapping between clouds
Python and Bash scripting, Terraform for target environments, Ansible for post-migration configuration, scripting repeatable migration steps

phases.build: A Terraform-built AWS landing zone (VPC, subnets, IAM, VPN to your mock on-prem estate) plus Ansible playbooks that configure migrated servers consistently.

phases.title: Assessment and wave planning

steps.what: Discovery agents and agentless scans, dependency mapping, right-sizing recommendations, TCO and cost reports, readiness assessments
The 7 Rs, portfolio analysis, dependency grouping, wave planning, risk registers, business case, success criteria, rollback strategy

phases.build: A migration assessment for your mock estate: Azure Migrate discovery output, dependency map, 7-Rs decision per workload, wave plan with risks and rollback, and a TCO comparison.

phases.title: Executing migrations

steps.what: Lift-and-shift with replication agents, test launches, replatforming databases to managed services, containerising an app, post-migration validation
Cutover runbooks, freeze windows, DNS switchover and TTL tuning, data sync validation, go/no-go criteria, hypercare and rollback execution

phases.build: A completed migration of your mock estate to AWS: web/app servers rehosted with MGN, PostgreSQL replatformed to RDS via DMS, and a timed cutover runbook with DNS switch and measured downtime.

cloud-consultant.summary: Build cloud fundamentals across two providers, learn to design and cost migrations, then package advisory thinking into client-ready deliverables.

phases.title: Cloud and client foundations

steps.what: Shell navigation, SSH, permissions, package managers, basic networking so you can reason about any cloud workload.
Cloud economics, shared responsibility, well-architected pillars, when cloud beats on-prem, and how to frame a client recommendation.
Running discovery interviews, translating tech into business value, writing crisp recommendation memos and slide narratives.

phases.build: A one-page cloud readiness assessment for a mock SME: current-state summary, three provider options with trade-offs, and a recommendation memo.

phases.title: Multi-cloud breadth

steps.what: Mapping equivalent compute, storage, networking and IAM services across AWS and Azure; portability, lock-in and landing-zone basics.
Identity, least privilege, encryption, network segmentation and compliance baselines clients always ask about.
Reference architectures, HA vs cost trade-offs, and drawing a target-state diagram from requirements.

phases.build: A side-by-side AWS vs Azure reference architecture for a web app with diagrams, a service-mapping table, and notes on where each provider wins.

phases.title: Migration and cost advisory

steps.what: The 6 Rs, dependency mapping, wave planning, pilot-light cutover, and building a realistic migration runbook.
Right-sizing, reserved vs spot, tagging strategy, budgets and alerts, and modelling TCO for a migration case.
Scoping statements of work, RACI, milestones, risk logs and status reporting on an engagement.

phases.build: A full migration proposal deck for a fictitious client: 6-R disposition per app, phased wave plan, TCO and savings model, risk log, and SoW.

datacenter-engineer.summary: Learn how servers, power, cooling and cabling physically fit together, then layer on networking, virtualization and the monitoring that keeps a floor healthy.

phases.title: The physical floor

steps.what: Rack layout and U-sizing, tier standards, change/ticket workflow, asset tracking, shift handover and floor safety.
Racking rails, CPUs/RAM/DIMM population, RAID, iDRAC/iLO, POST codes, FRU replacement and diagnosing hardware faults.

phases.build: A documented rack build for a 10-server lab (on paper or homelab): elevation diagram, asset inventory, cable schedule, and a fault-triage checklist.

phases.title: Power, cooling and cabling

steps.what: Single vs dual feed, PDUs, UPS/generator, redundancy (N+1), hot/cold aisle, airflow and reading rack power/thermal budgets.
Copper vs fiber, Cat6/OM4, patch panels, labelling standards, dressing and testing runs, and MDA/HDA topology.

phases.build: A power-and-cabling plan for one rack: redundant PDU feed diagram, per-device load budget, labelled patch schedule, and a cable-management standard.

phases.title: Network, compute and visibility

steps.what: VLANs, switching, top-of-rack vs core, IP addressing, out-of-band management and basic troubleshooting with show commands.
Hypervisor basics, provisioning VMs, resource pools, and how virtual hosts map onto the physical servers you rack.
Environmental and hardware telemetry, SNMP traps, alert thresholds and dashboards for power, temperature and node health.
Automating inventory pulls, bulk IPMI queries and report generation with small Python/Bash scripts.

phases.build: A monitored mini-datacenter on a hypervisor: ToR VLAN config, 2-3 VMs, a Grafana dashboard for host and environmental metrics, and a scripted inventory report.

hybrid-cloud-engineer.summary: Ground yourself in on-prem virtualization and one public cloud, then connect the two with networking, IaC and Kubernetes into a single hybrid operating model.

phases.title: Foundations both sides

steps.what: Shell, systemd, networking stack, SSH and package management underlying both VMs and cloud instances.
ESXi, vCenter, clusters, vMotion, datastores, templates and the lifecycle of an on-prem virtual estate.
Core compute, networking, storage, IAM and resource organisation in one public cloud to parity with on-prem.

phases.build: A small vSphere cluster plus a matching cloud VPC/VNet: same three-tier app deployed on both, with a comparison write-up of operations on each side.

phases.title: Connecting the estates

steps.what: Hybrid operating models, workload placement, identity federation, and platforms like Azure Arc / VMware Cloud that span both worlds.
Site-to-site VPN and ExpressRoute/Direct Connect, hybrid DNS, routing, and keeping address spaces from colliding.
On-prem SAN/NFS vs cloud block/object, replication, and tiering data between the two environments.

phases.build: A working hybrid link: VPN between your lab and cloud, federated identity, and one app whose front end runs in cloud while its database stays on-prem.

phases.title: Automation and portability

steps.what: Declarative provisioning across providers, modules, state management and reusing the same patterns on-prem and in cloud.
Pods, deployments, services, ingress, and running a cluster that spans or bursts between on-prem and cloud nodes.
Configuration management and pipelines that apply consistent state to both estates and handle drift.

phases.build: A Terraform + Ansible repo that stands up a Kubernetes workload on both your vSphere lab and the cloud from one pipeline, with drift detection documented.

cloudops-engineer.summary: Get fluent on Linux and one cloud, master observability and incident response, then automate the day-to-day run/operate work with IaC and pipelines.

phases.title: Operate the platform

steps.what: Processes, systemd, logs, networking, performance tools and the troubleshooting loop for a misbehaving host.
Running a cloud estate: resource lifecycle, patching, tagging, backups, quotas, health checks and operational runbooks.
Reading billing, budgets and alerts, spotting idle resources and basic right-sizing hygiene.

phases.build: A cloud environment you operate: tagged resources, an automated patch/backup schedule, a billing budget with alerts, and runbooks for three routine ops tasks.

phases.title: See and respond

steps.what: Metrics, logs and traces, SLIs/SLOs, dashboards, alert design and reducing noise so the signal is actionable.
On-call workflow, severity levels, triage, mitigation, comms and writing a blameless postmortem.

phases.build: An observability stack over a sample service: dashboards, SLO-based alerts, and a simulated incident you drive end-to-end with a written postmortem.

phases.title: Automate the toil

steps.what: Scripting routine ops, idempotent config and auto-remediation for common alerts.
Provisioning and changing cloud infra as code, modules, state, plan/apply review and drift.
Pipelines that lint, plan and deploy infra and app changes safely, with approvals and rollback.

phases.build: A GitOps pipeline that provisions the monitored service via Terraform, runs an auto-remediation script on a known alert, and deploys changes with a rollback path.

security.summary: Build systems and networking literacy, then learn to find weaknesses through threat modeling and network defense, and to run vulnerability management and response across cloud and app layers.

phases.title: Systems and scripting base

steps.what: Processes, permissions, syscalls, filesystems, auth logs and how attackers abuse each; the defender's mental model of a host.
Parsing logs, calling APIs, and automating repetitive security checks with small scripts.

phases.build: A Python toolkit that pulls auth logs from a Linux box, flags brute-force and privilege-escalation patterns, and outputs a summarized report.

phases.title: Find the weaknesses

steps.what: STRIDE, data-flow diagrams, trust boundaries, attack trees and turning a design into a ranked list of threats and mitigations.
TCP/IP, firewalls, segmentation, TLS, VPNs, IDS/IPS and reading traffic to tell normal from malicious.
Scanning, CVSS, prioritisation, tracking remediation and reporting risk over time rather than one-off scans.

phases.build: A threat model and hardening review of a small multi-tier app: DFD, ranked threats, a vuln-scan report of the deployed stack, and a prioritised remediation plan.

phases.title: Detect and respond

steps.what: Centralising logs, writing detection queries, correlation rules and dashboards to catch suspicious activity.
IAM least privilege, security groups, encryption, logging and common misconfigurations in AWS/Azure.
The IR lifecycle, scoping, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons-learned documentation.

phases.build: A mini SOC lab: ship logs from the app and a cloud account into a SIEM, build three detections, trigger one, and write the incident report end-to-end.

appsec-eng.summary: Start from solid coding and web fundamentals, learn to read code for flaws and reason about the OWASP Top 10, then wire security testing into the SDLC and the pipeline.

phases.title: Developer foundations

steps.what: Reading and writing code confidently, HTTP clients, parsing, and scripting small security checks.
Injection, broken auth, XSS, SSRF, access control, misconfig; how each works, is exploited and is fixed in real code.

phases.build: A vulnerable practice app (e.g. Juice Shop) fully exploited for each Top 10 category, with a write-up pairing each finding to a concrete code fix.

phases.title: Read code for flaws

steps.what: Reviewing diffs and modules for injection, authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization and crypto misuse; writing actionable findings.
Mapping attack surface, testing auth/session/access-control, and confirming review findings by exploiting them.
Proxy, repeater, intruder, scanner and extensions for intercepting and manipulating app traffic.

phases.build: A security code review of an open-source web app: documented findings with severity, proof-of-concept exploits via Burp, and suggested patches as a PR.

phases.title: Shift left into the SDLC

steps.what: STRIDE and data-flow diagrams on a feature, ranking threats and feeding mitigations into design before code.
Configuring static and dynamic scanners, tuning rules, and triaging findings to cut false positives.
Gating pipelines on SAST/DAST/dependency scans, secret detection, and failing builds on real risk.

phases.build: A CI/CD pipeline with SAST, DAST, dependency and secret scanning gates on a demo repo, plus a threat model for its newest feature and a tuned rule set.

product-security-eng.summary: Learn secure design and threat modeling for a product, hunt vulnerabilities in its code, and embed security through the SDLC with cloud and crypto fundamentals.

phases.title: Secure design thinking

steps.what: STRIDE, data-flow diagrams, trust boundaries and attack trees applied to a product feature, producing ranked threats and mitigations.
Symmetric/asymmetric crypto, hashing, signatures, TLS, key management and common misuse pitfalls.

phases.build: A threat model for a product's new auth/payments feature: DFD, trust boundaries, ranked threats, and a crypto design note covering key handling and TLS.

phases.title: Break the product

steps.what: Reading the product codebase for authz gaps, injection, unsafe deserialization and secret handling; writing clear findings.
Tracking discovered vulns, severity, SLAs, remediation ownership and verifying fixes.
Coverage-guided and mutation fuzzing of parsers/inputs, harness writing and triaging crashes.

phases.build: A vulnerability assessment of an open-source product: code-review findings, a fuzzing harness that surfaces a crash, and a tracked remediation plan with retests.

phases.title: Secure by default

steps.what: Security requirements, design review gates, secure defaults, dependency hygiene and release-time checks across the lifecycle.
IAM least privilege, secrets management, network controls and logging for the product's cloud footprint.

phases.build: A secure-SDLC blueprint for a product team: design-review checklist, pipeline security gates, cloud IAM baseline, and a secure-defaults guide developers can follow.

pentester.summary: Build attacker fundamentals on Linux and the web, master Burp and web/network exploitation, then chain findings and report them to a client standard.

phases.title: Attacker fundamentals

steps.what: Kali tooling, shell, networking, services and privilege concepts you lean on in every engagement.
Writing quick exploit and automation scripts, HTTP requests, sockets and parsing tool output.
Proxying traffic, repeater, intruder, decoder, scanner and extensions to manipulate and test web requests.

phases.build: A documented walkthrough of 10 web challenges owned with Burp (repeater/intruder), including the exact requests and a short methodology note per challenge.

phases.title: Exploit web and network

steps.what: Recon, enumeration, OWASP web attacks, service exploitation, pivoting and chaining findings into real impact.
Modules, payloads, Meterpreter, post-exploitation and when to use the framework vs manual exploitation.
Enumeration, Kerberoasting, lateral movement and common AD misconfig abuse in a lab domain.

phases.build: A full compromise of a vulnerable lab network (e.g. HTB/vulnhub boxes): initial access, privilege escalation, AD lateral movement, with a kill-chain diagram.

phases.title: Exploit craft and reporting

steps.what: Buffer overflows, debugging, fuzzing, bad-char handling and writing a working exploit from a crash.
Try-harder methodology, time-boxed enumeration discipline and the exam-style approach to owning a box.
Executive summary, risk ratings, reproducible steps, evidence and remediation advice at client quality.

phases.build: A professional pentest report for the lab engagement: scope, methodology, findings with CVSS and screenshots, a developed exploit, and remediation guidance.

red-team-operator.summary: Move from pentesting into long-haul adversary emulation: build C2 and tooling, attack Active Directory, evade EDR, and map everything to ATT&CK.

phases.title: Operator groundwork

steps.what: Tactics, techniques, procedures and using the matrix to plan, scope and document an emulation of a specific threat actor.
Objective-driven ops, kill-chain planning, infrastructure staging, OPSEC discipline and evidence collection over weeks.

phases.build: An emulation plan for a named APT: mapped ATT&CK techniques, objectives, infrastructure design, OPSEC rules, and success criteria written as a red-team ROE.

phases.title: C2 and lateral movement

steps.what: Listeners, beacons, malleable profiles, redirectors, domain fronting and running an engagement from a C2 console.
Kerberoasting, AS-REP, delegation abuse, ACL attacks, DCSync and lateral movement through a domain.
Pretext design, phishing infrastructure, payload delivery and tracking initial-access success safely.

phases.build: A C2 operation in an AD lab: phishing-style initial access, beacon with a custom profile and redirector, BloodHound-guided path to Domain Admin, logged per ATT&CK.

phases.title: Evasion and tooling

steps.what: AMSI/ETW bypass, in-memory execution, process injection, sleep masking and minimizing detectable footprint.
Writing loaders/shellcode runners in C/C# and understanding how defenders reverse them.

phases.build: A custom loader that executes a beacon in memory past a configured EDR/Sysmon lab, with a detection write-up showing what defenders would and would not see.

soc-analyst.summary: Learn how networks and logs behave, master a SIEM and detection logic, then triage and investigate alerts across EDR and traffic like a real blue-team shift.

phases.title: Know normal

steps.what: Common log sources (auth, DNS, proxy, Windows events), fields that matter, baselining normal and spotting anomalies.
Reading PCAPs, protocols, beaconing and exfil patterns, and pulling IOCs from captured traffic.

phases.build: An analysis notebook over provided logs and a PCAP: identify a simulated intrusion, extract IOCs, and build a timeline of what the attacker did.

phases.title: Run the SIEM

steps.what: Ingesting logs, SPL/KQL queries, correlation rules, dashboards and tuning alerts to cut false positives.
Mapping detections and observed activity to tactics and techniques to describe and hunt threats.

phases.build: A SIEM lab: ingest host and network logs, build five ATT&CK-mapped detections and a dashboard, then validate them against replayed attack data.

phases.title: Triage and investigate

steps.what: Alert severity, enrichment, true/false-positive decisions, escalation criteria and clear handoff notes.
Endpoint telemetry, process trees, isolating a host, and pivoting from an alert to root cause.
Following and writing response playbooks, documenting investigations and tracking cases to closure.

phases.build: A set of three worked investigations from alert to closure: enrichment, EDR process-tree analysis, verdict, and a reusable playbook written for each alert type.

grc-analyst.summary: Learn to assess risk and map controls to frameworks, run audits and write policy, and shepherd evidence toward certification like ISO 27001 and SOC 2.

phases.title: Risk and frameworks

steps.what: Asset and threat identification, likelihood/impact scoring, risk registers, treatment options and risk acceptance.
ISO 27001 Annex A and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, control objectives, and mapping controls to each.

phases.build: A risk register and ISO 27001/SOC 2 control mapping for a fictitious SaaS company: top risks scored, treatments assigned, and a Statement of Applicability draft.

phases.title: Policy and controls

steps.what: Structuring policies and standards, control language, ownership, review cycles and readable, auditable documents.
Using NIST CSF/800-53 and CIS Controls to benchmark a program and cross-walk to ISO/SOC 2.

phases.build: A policy pack for the SaaS company (access control, incident response, data handling) plus a NIST CSF maturity assessment with a cross-walk to its existing controls.

phases.title: Audit and evidence

steps.what: Audit planning, control testing, sampling, evidence requests, tracking findings and remediation to closure.
Vendor tiering, security questionnaires, reviewing SOC 2 reports and tracking remediation of vendor gaps.
Personal-data mapping, lawful basis, DPIAs, DSARs and core privacy obligations that intersect with controls.

phases.build: A SOC 2 readiness assessment: control-testing worksheet with evidence collected, a gap/finding log with owners, and a vendor-risk review of two key suppliers.

cloud-security-eng.summary: Build cloud and scripting fundamentals, master IAM and provider-native security, then enforce guardrails in Terraform, Kubernetes and CSPM at scale.

phases.title: Cloud and code base

steps.what: Automating cloud API calls, parsing config/findings and writing small remediation and audit scripts.
Principals, roles, policies, least privilege, trust and assume-role, federation and avoiding privilege escalation paths.

phases.build: A least-privilege IAM baseline for a cloud account: scoped roles, a Python script that flags over-permissive and unused policies, and a documented access model.

phases.title: Secure the estate

steps.what: Provider-native controls: network security, encryption, logging/audit, secrets, and the common misconfigs attackers hunt.
Continuous posture scanning, policy-as-code checks, prioritising misconfigurations and tracking drift.
Image scanning, minimal base images, registry controls and runtime protection for containers.

phases.build: A hardened multi-service cloud account scanned with Prowler/CSPM: top misconfigs remediated, logging and encryption enforced, and a before/after posture report.

phases.title: Guardrails as code

steps.what: Provisioning secure-by-default infra, modules, state, and policy-as-code gates that block risky resources.
RBAC, network policies, pod security standards, secrets and admission control to lock down a cluster.

phases.build: A Terraform baseline with policy-as-code that refuses insecure resources, plus a locked-down Kubernetes cluster (RBAC, network policy, admission control) and a test suite proving the guardrails fire.

dfir-analyst.summary: Learn evidence handling and host/log fundamentals, master forensic acquisition and memory analysis, then run the incident-response lifecycle from detection to recovery.

phases.title: Evidence fundamentals

steps.what: Windows/Linux event logs, timelines, artifacts of execution and persistence, and reconstructing attacker activity from logs.
Evidence integrity, hashing, acquisition documentation, handling procedures and keeping findings court-defensible.

phases.build: A forensic timeline from a provided disk/log image: reconstruct the intrusion story with artifact evidence, hashed and documented to a chain-of-custody standard.

phases.title: Dig into the host

steps.what: Disk imaging, filesystem and registry artifacts, browser/USB history, deleted-file recovery and anti-forensics awareness.
Capturing RAM, listing processes, injected code, network connections and credential artifacts from a memory image.
Static and dynamic triage, IOC extraction, sandboxing and classifying a suspicious binary safely.

phases.build: A full host investigation of a compromised VM: disk and memory analysis, the malware triaged and IOCs extracted, with a report on how the attacker gained and kept access.

phases.title: Run the incident

steps.what: The IR lifecycle: preparation, detection, scoping, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned under deadline.
Using endpoint telemetry to scope impact, isolate hosts, hunt for lateral movement and confirm eradication.

phases.build: A simulated breach run end-to-end: scope with EDR across hosts, contain and eradicate, then deliver an executive incident report with timeline, impact and recommendations.

security-architect.summary: Build threat-modeling and network/IAM fundamentals, learn to weigh risk against business needs, then design zero-trust, cloud-aware security blueprints for a whole organization.

phases.title: Weakness and risk lens

steps.what: STRIDE, data-flow diagrams, trust boundaries and attack trees to turn any system design into ranked threats and controls.
Risk registers, likelihood/impact, risk appetite and making defensible accept/mitigate decisions with the business.
How ISO 27001/SOC 2/NIST obligations shape architecture decisions and control selection.

phases.build: A threat model plus risk-ranked control set for a mid-size company's flagship system, with each control justified against risk appetite and a relevant framework.

phases.title: Core domains

steps.what: Segmentation, firewalls, TLS, VPNs and secure patterns for east-west and north-south traffic.
Identity lifecycle, authentication, authorization models, federation and privileged access design.
Reference architectures for IAM, networking, logging and encryption across major cloud providers.

phases.build: A reference security architecture for a cloud estate: network segmentation diagram, IAM model, logging/encryption standards, and the patterns teams must follow.

phases.title: The blueprint

steps.what: Enterprise security blueprints, control frameworks, defense-in-depth, standards-setting and reviewing major system designs.
Identity-centric access, microsegmentation, device trust, continuous verification and a staged migration from perimeter security.

phases.build: An organization-wide zero-trust target architecture: current-state assessment, target blueprint with standards, a phased roadmap, and a design-review checklist for new systems.

iam-eng.summary: Learn directories and scripting, master identity governance and federated SSO, then automate provisioning and lock down privileged access across the org.

phases.title: Identity foundations

steps.what: Users, groups, OUs, schema, LDAP queries and how directories back authentication and authorization.
Automating directory and identity tasks, API calls and bulk user operations with PowerShell/Python.

phases.build: A lab AD/LDAP directory with a scripted bulk onboarding/offboarding tool that creates, groups and disables accounts from a CSV with an audit log.

phases.title: Federated access

steps.what: SAML assertions, OAuth2/OIDC flows, tokens, claims, app integration and troubleshooting federated logins.
Configuring an IdP: app connections, authentication policies, MFA, conditional access and sign-on rules.

phases.build: A working SSO setup: an IdP federating two sample apps via SAML and OIDC, with MFA and a conditional-access policy, plus a troubleshooting guide for failed logins.

phases.title: Govern and provision

steps.what: Joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle, access reviews, role-based access, segregation of duties and certification campaigns.
Automating user provisioning/deprovisioning to downstream apps via SCIM and handling sync errors.
Vaulting credentials, just-in-time elevation, session recording and least privilege for admin accounts.

phases.build: An automated JML workflow: SCIM provisioning to apps on hire, an access-review campaign, and a PAM/just-in-time elevation policy for admin roles, all documented.

desktop-support.summary: From PC and Windows fundamentals to fixing hardware, imaging and deploying laptops, finishing with Active Directory and service-desk habits that make you useful on day one of an IT support internship.

phases.title: PC, Windows and network fundamentals

steps.what: CPU, RAM, storage, motherboards, PSUs, BIOS/UEFI settings, POST and boot sequence, peripherals and ESD safety at CompTIA A+ Core 1 depth
Windows 10/11 settings, local users and permissions, Event Viewer, Device Manager, Services, registry basics, Safe Mode and the recovery environment
IP addressing, DHCP, DNS, Wi-Fi vs Ethernet, mapped drives and network printers, diagnosing with ipconfig, ping, tracert and nslookup

phases.build: A documented Windows 11 lab (old PC or VMs) with a write-up of 10 deliberately broken faults - driver, DNS, boot, permissions, printer - showing how you diagnosed and fixed each one.

phases.title: Hardware and endpoint support

steps.what: Systematic fault isolation for no-POST, overheating, failing disks and RAM; swapping SSD, RAM, battery and keyboard; SMART and memory diagnostics, beep and LED codes
Driver and BIOS updates, printer and peripheral setup, Outlook/Office profile fixes, BitLocker recovery, standard vs admin users, remote assistance sessions

phases.build: Refurbish two or three second-hand or donated laptops end to end: diagnose faults, replace parts, update firmware, configure for a user, and publish a repair log with before/after diagnostics.
