phases.title: Imaging and software deployment

steps.what: Building a reference image, Sysprep, capturing and applying WIM images with DISM, PXE boot, driver injection, USB recovery media and keeping golden images patched
Silent installs with MSI/EXE switches, winget and Chocolatey, basic packaging, deploying apps via scripts or Group Policy, and verifying installs

phases.build: A PXE imaging server in a VM lab that boots a fresh client, applies a custom Windows 11 image with drivers and silently installs a standard app bundle, documented with timings per machine.

phases.title: Directory, service desk and mobile

steps.what: Domains, OUs, users and groups, password resets and unlocks, joining PCs to a domain, and basic Group Policy for drives, printers and desktop settings
Logging, categorising and prioritising tickets, SLAs, writing clear resolution notes, and turning a repeated fix into a knowledge-base article
Questioning non-technical users calmly, explaining fixes in plain language, setting expectations, handling frustrated users and following up after closure
Setting up Android and iOS for corporate email, Wi-Fi profiles and MFA apps, basic MDM enrollment, and troubleshooting sync and battery issues

phases.build: A mini service desk: a Windows Server domain with 20 test users, an osTicket instance and 15 resolved sample tickets (resets, mapped drives, printer, phone enrollment), each with a knowledge-base article.

endpoint-engineer.summary: Start with Windows, networking and Active Directory, add PowerShell and Group Policy, then manage a fleet with SCCM and Intune, finishing with Autopilot, Jamf and zero-trust device compliance.

phases.title: Windows and directory foundations

steps.what: Windows 10/11 for admins: services, registry, event logs, local policies, user profiles, Windows Update, BitLocker and Defender basics
TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, subnets, proxies and the firewall ports endpoint agents need; checking connectivity with Test-NetConnection and nslookup
Domains, OUs, users, groups, computer objects, domain join, DNS integration, and how Entra ID hybrid join relates to on-prem AD

phases.build: A Hyper-V or VirtualBox lab with a Windows Server domain controller, DNS and DHCP, plus three domain-joined Windows 11 clients organised into OUs - the base for every later phase.

phases.title: Scripting and on-prem management

steps.what: Cmdlets, pipeline and objects, scripts and functions, remoting, registry and WMI/CIM queries, error handling, and writing detection and remediation scripts
Creating and linking GPOs, inheritance and precedence, security filtering, ADMX templates, preferences, gpresult/RSoP troubleshooting and Intune equivalents
Site install, boundaries, discovery, client push, collections, application deployment, software update groups, OSD task sequences and compliance baselines

phases.build: A Configuration Manager lab that deploys 7-Zip and Chrome as applications, pushes monthly updates to a pilot collection and reimages a client via task sequence, with PowerShell scripts for health reports.

phases.title: Modern management with Intune

steps.what: Enrollment types, BYOD vs corporate-owned, configuration and compliance policies, app protection (MAM), remote wipe, and Apple/Android enrollment programs
Device enrollment, configuration profiles, compliance policies, Win32 app packaging, update rings, remediations, and co-management with SCCM
Hardware hash collection, deployment profiles, user-driven and self-deploying modes, Enrollment Status Page tuning, group tags and troubleshooting OOBE failures

phases.build: A Microsoft 365 trial tenant where a fresh VM goes through Autopilot and lands compliant in Intune with BitLocker, Defender and a Win32 app, and a phone enrolls with app protection - documented end to end.

phases.title: Mac fleet and zero-trust

steps.what: Apple Business Manager, Automated Device Enrollment, configuration profiles, Jamf policies and smart groups, Self Service, FileVault escrow and macOS patching
Device compliance as an access signal, Entra Conditional Access, least privilege, MFA, and how endpoint health feeds identity-based access decisions

phases.build: A cross-platform compliance report: a Jamf trial managing a Mac plus Intune Windows devices, Conditional Access blocking a non-compliant device, and a Graph API script exporting fleet compliance to CSV.

telecom-engineer.summary: Build networking and Linux basics, learn PSTN and SIP signalling, run your own PBX, then finish with the physical side - cabling, circuits and carriers - that telecom engineers handle daily.

phases.title: Networking and Linux foundations

steps.what: OSI and TCP/IP models, subnetting, VLANs, routing basics, UDP vs TCP, NAT and firewalls, and how voice traffic rides on IP networks
Shell navigation, package management, systemd services, logs, networking commands and editing config files needed to run open-source PBXs

phases.build: A routed lab in Packet Tracer or GNS3 with separate voice and data VLANs, DHCP options for IP phones and a Linux VM reachable across subnets, with a diagram and addressing plan.

phases.title: Telecom signalling and SIP

steps.what: PSTN structure, TDM, T1/E1 framing, ISDN PRI and Q.931, SS7 overview, DTMF, E.164 numbering plans, and analog FXS/FXO interfaces
SIP methods and response codes, registration, call flows, SDP offer/answer, proxies and registrars, NAT traversal issues and reading SIP traces

phases.build: Annotated Wireshark captures of a SIP registration, a successful call, a busy call and a failed call, each with a ladder diagram explaining every message and SDP field.

phases.title: PBX systems and troubleshooting

steps.what: Extensions, dial plans, inbound/outbound routes, trunks, IVRs, ring groups, voicemail, call recording, and how Avaya, Cisco and 3CX PBXs compare to Asterisk
Structured isolation of no audio, one-way audio, registration failures, echo and dropped calls using PBX logs, CDRs and packet traces

phases.build: A FreePBX system with 10 softphone extensions, an IVR, ring groups, voicemail-to-email and a SIP trunk to a second PBX acting as the carrier, plus a fault runbook for five common call failures.

phases.title: Physical plant and carriers

steps.what: Cat6 termination, punch-down and 110 blocks, patch panels, single vs multimode fiber, connectors, OTDR and cable testing, TIA-568 standards
Ordering and turning up PRI, SIP trunk, MPLS and DIA circuits; LOAs, demarc extension, test-and-turn-up checklists and number porting
Opening and escalating carrier tickets, SLAs, reading invoices and contracts, coordinating outages and tracking circuit IDs across providers
Circuit inventories, cable and port maps, dial-plan documents, network diagrams and change records another engineer can follow

phases.build: A telecom site pack for a fictional 50-person office: cable plan, patch-panel map, circuit inventory in NetBox, carrier escalation matrix and a turn-up checklist for a new SIP trunk.

voip-engineer.summary: Lay networking and Linux foundations, master SIP and RTP on an open-source PBX, move to Cisco CUCM and QoS, then finish with session border controllers and packet-level debugging of real call failures.

phases.title: Networking and Linux foundations

steps.what: CCNA-level TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs and voice VLANs, routing, NAT, DHCP option 150, and how latency, jitter and loss affect real-time traffic
Shell, package management, systemd services, log files, firewall basics and networking commands for running voice servers

phases.build: A GNS3 or Packet Tracer lab with separate voice and data VLANs, a router serving DHCP to IP phones and a Linux server VM, documented with an IP plan and topology diagram.

phases.title: Signalling, media and open-source PBX

steps.what: SIP methods and responses, registration and authentication, dialogs and transactions, SDP offer/answer, NAT traversal, SIP over TLS and reading call flows
RTP and RTCP, G.711, G.729 and Opus, packetization, bandwidth per call, jitter buffers, MOS, transcoding, and DTMF via RFC 2833 vs SIP INFO
Installing Asterisk/FreePBX, PJSIP endpoints, dialplan contexts, trunks, IVRs, queues, CDRs and debugging with the Asterisk CLI

phases.build: An Asterisk lab with softphones on two subnets, a trunk to a second PBX and codec negotiation tests (G.711 vs Opus), with a report on bandwidth and MOS measured for each codec.

phases.title: Enterprise voice: CUCM and QoS

steps.what: CUCM architecture, device pools, partitions and calling search spaces, route and translation patterns, gateways, phone registration and Unity Connection basics
DSCP and CoS marking, trust boundaries, classification, LLQ/CBWFQ queuing, policing vs shaping, and designing an end-to-end voice QoS policy

phases.build: A two-site CUCM dial plan in a lab or dCloud with partitions/CSS and a PSTN gateway route, plus a WAN QoS policy verified by saturating the link with iPerf while test calls stay clean.

phases.title: Edge security and deep troubleshooting

steps.what: SBC roles: topology hiding, NAT fix-ups, SIP normalization and security; Cisco CUBE and open-source SBCs, SIP trunk interop, TLS and SRTP
Isolating one-way audio, dropped calls and registration failures across firewalls, NAT and VLANs using traceroute, interface counters, MTU and ACL checks
Wireshark VoIP analysis: SIP flow graphs, RTP stream analysis, jitter and loss statistics, audio playback, and tcpdump on servers and SPAN ports

phases.build: A troubleshooting casebook: reproduce five failures in your lab (NAT one-way audio, codec mismatch, wrong CSS, SBC header problem, QoS drops) and publish the captures, root causes and fixes.

uc-engineer.summary: Learn networking and Microsoft 365 administration, master VoIP, SIP and QoS, then build Cisco UC and Teams Phone environments, finishing with video, contact center and PowerShell automation.

phases.title: Networking and Microsoft 365 foundations

steps.what: TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs, DNS, DHCP, NAT and firewalls, plus the ports and bandwidth that voice and video traffic need
Tenant setup, users and licences, Entra ID basics, Exchange Online and DNS records, admin center navigation and role-based admin access

phases.build: A Microsoft 365 trial tenant with a custom domain, 15 licensed test users in groups and verified DNS records, plus a written admin guide for onboarding and offboarding a user.

phases.title: Voice fundamentals

steps.what: Analog vs TDM vs IP telephony, IP phones and softphones, call setup, RTP media, codecs and bandwidth, E.164 numbering and emergency calling
SIP methods and responses, registration, call flows, SDP negotiation, SIP trunks, NAT traversal and reading SIP ladder diagrams
DSCP marking for voice and video, Teams media port ranges, LLQ basics, Wi-Fi WMM, and measuring jitter, latency and packet loss

phases.build: A two-site SIP lab (FreePBX plus softphones) with QoS markings applied on a router, and Wireshark captures proving correct DSCP values and clean RTP streams under load.

phases.title: Cisco UC and Microsoft Teams

steps.what: CUCM call control, partitions/CSS, route patterns, Unity Connection voicemail, Jabber and Webex, Expressway for remote access, and CUBE for SIP trunks
Teams admin center and policies, Teams Phone, Calling Plans vs Direct Routing vs Operator Connect, auto attendants, call queues and Teams Rooms basics

phases.build: A Teams Phone design for a fictional company: auto attendant, call queues and calling policies in a trial tenant, plus a Direct Routing design connecting it to a CUCM/CUBE environment in Cisco dCloud.

phases.title: Collaboration extras and automation

steps.what: Meeting room systems, Teams Rooms and Webex devices, SIP/H.323 video interop, cameras and audio DSPs, bandwidth planning and room troubleshooting
ACD, IVR, queues, skills-based routing, agent states, call recording and reporting with Webex Contact Center, Genesys Cloud or Teams-certified CCaaS
MicrosoftTeams module, bulk voice-enabling users, assigning numbers and policies, reporting on call queues and scripting repeatable tenant config

phases.build: A PowerShell toolkit that voice-enables 50 test users from a CSV, assigns calling policies and exports a call-queue and room-device report, alongside a small Amazon Connect contact flow with IVR and queues.

wireless-engineer.summary: Ground yourself in networking and RF physics, learn 802.11 and WLAN design, practise surveys with Ekahau and spectrum tools, then configure, secure and troubleshoot Cisco/Aruba wireless networks.

phases.title: Networking and RF basics

steps.what: TCP/IP, VLANs and trunking, DHCP, DNS, PoE budgets, and the switching and routing basics that access points and controllers depend on
Frequency and wavelength, dB/dBm/mW math, RSSI and SNR, free-space path loss, absorption and reflection, antenna gain and radiation patterns

phases.build: A Wi-Fi coverage study of your hostel or department floor: RSSI and SNR measured at 20+ points on 2.4 and 5 GHz, plotted against distance and walls and explained with path-loss math.

phases.title: 802.11 standards and WLAN design

steps.what: 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax/be, channel widths, MCS rates, OFDMA, MU-MIMO, beacons and association, 802.11k/v/r roaming and 6 GHz rules
Capacity vs coverage design, AP density, channel and power plans, co-channel interference, RSSI targets for voice and data, and high-density venues

phases.build: A predictive Wi-Fi design for a three-floor college building: AP placement, channel and power plan and capacity calculations for 600 devices, delivered as a design report.

phases.title: Site surveys and spectrum

steps.what: Predictive, passive, active and AP-on-a-stick surveys, survey walk methodology, validation surveys and post-install reporting
Floor plan scaling, wall attenuation, predictive models, heatmaps for signal, SNR and channel overlap, and generating survey reports
Reading waterfall and density views, identifying non-Wi-Fi interferers (microwaves, Bluetooth, wireless cameras), duty cycle and noise floor

phases.build: A passive site survey of a real building (library, hostel or lab) with heatmaps, a spectrum scan identifying interferers, and a remediation report recommending AP moves and channel changes.

phases.title: Controllers, security and troubleshooting

steps.what: Controller vs cloud-managed designs, Cisco Catalyst 9800 WLC and Aruba Central/Instant, SSIDs, RF profiles, AP groups, RRM/ARM tuning and guest portals
WPA2/WPA3 Personal and Enterprise, 802.1X/EAP, RADIUS, protected management frames, rogue AP detection, guest isolation and common Wi-Fi attacks
Diagnosing roaming problems, sticky clients, low data rates, DHCP and auth failures using client logs, controller debugs and over-the-air captures

phases.build: A wireless security lab: a WPA3-Enterprise SSID authenticating against FreeRADIUS, a separate guest SSID with isolation, and annotated captures of a failed and a successful 802.1X authentication.

rf-engineer.summary: Build the electromagnetics, signals and MATLAB base, learn propagation, antennas and link budgets, move into 5G/LTE and spectrum analysis, and finish with drive testing and spectrum regulation.

phases.title: EE and maths foundations

steps.what: Maxwell's equations in practice, transmission lines, impedance matching, the Smith chart, S-parameters, VSWR and return loss
Fourier transforms, sampling, filters, analog and digital modulation (AM/FM, QAM, OFDM), thermal noise and noise figure
Vectors and matrices, plotting, scripts and functions, Signal Processing and Communications Toolbox basics, simulating modulation and BER curves

phases.build: A MATLAB simulation of QPSK and 16-QAM links over AWGN and Rayleigh fading that plots BER vs SNR and compares results with theory, published with code on GitHub.

phases.title: Propagation, antennas and link budgets

steps.what: Free-space path loss, Okumura-Hata and COST-231 models, multipath, Rayleigh and Rician fading, shadowing, diffraction, indoor vs outdoor propagation
Dipoles, patches and arrays, gain, beamwidth, polarization, radiation patterns, MIMO and beamforming basics, and antenna simulation
Transmit power, antenna gains, cable losses, path loss, fade margin, receiver sensitivity and noise figure for cellular, microwave and satellite links

phases.build: A link-budget and coverage tool for a rural LTE cell or microwave hop comparing path-loss models in MATLAB, plus a simulated 3.5 GHz patch antenna with gain and return-loss plots.

phases.title: Cellular networks and spectrum

steps.what: LTE and 5G NR architecture, numerology, FR1/FR2 bands, physical channels, RSRP/RSRQ/SINR, handover, MIMO and beam management, and RAN planning basics
Analyzer settings (RBW, VBW, span), measuring channel power, ACLR and occupied bandwidth, interference hunting, and SDR-based captures

phases.build: An SDR survey of cellular bands in your city with an RTL-SDR or HackRF: identify carriers, measure channel power and occupancy, and write up findings as a short technical report.

phases.title: Field testing and regulation

steps.what: Drive-test planning, logging RSRP/SINR/throughput, post-processing, coverage plots, KPI analysis and spotting handover and interference problems
ITU and national spectrum allocation, licensing, EMF exposure limits, India's WPC, TRAI and TEC rules, and FCC/ETSI equivalents

phases.build: A drive-test study using a phone logging app: RSRP and SINR along a 10 km route, coverage mapped in QGIS, weak spots and handover failures flagged, and fixes argued with link-budget reasoning.

datacenter-tech.summary: Start with PC, Linux and networking basics, then learn server hardware, rack and stack and structured cabling, finishing with fault diagnosis, ticket discipline, DCIM and site security habits.

phases.title: Hardware, Linux and network basics

steps.what: CPU, memory, storage types, motherboards, PSUs, BIOS/UEFI, POST, ESD safety and basic component replacement
Shell basics, lsblk, dmesg, lshw, smartctl, ipmitool, reading logs, and booting rescue media to check hardware
Ethernet, IP addressing, VLANs, switch ports, SFP/QSFP optics, DAC vs AOC cables, link lights and testing connectivity

phases.build: An old PC turned into a Linux server with a hardware inventory script (lshw and smartctl output to CSV) and a labelled diagram of how it connects to your switch or router.

phases.title: Servers, racks and cabling

steps.what: Rack server anatomy, redundant PSUs, ECC DIMMs, RAID controllers, hot-swap drives, NICs, GPUs, BMCs (iDRAC/iLO) and firmware updates
Rack units, rails, weight distribution, hot/cold aisle airflow, PDUs and power redundancy, labelling, and safe lifting and install procedures
Copper and fiber types, patch panels, cable management, TIA-942 and TIA-568, termination, testing and certifying runs, labelling standards

phases.build: A rack elevation and cabling plan for a 42U rack of servers, switches and PDUs with power and airflow calculations, plus photos of patch cables you terminated and tested yourself.

phases.title: Fault diagnosis and tickets

steps.what: Reading BMC event logs, diagnosing failed DIMMs, drives, PSUs and fans, LED codes, swapping parts under RMA and verifying with vendor diagnostics
Smart-hands tickets, change windows, RMA tracking, updating tickets with serials and evidence photos, and escalation paths

phases.build: A troubleshooting runbook for eight common server failures (DIMM, disk, PSU, NIC, fan, BMC, boot, overheating), each with symptoms, sample BMC logs, swap procedure and a ticket update template.

phases.title: DCIM and site operations

steps.what: Asset tracking, rack and port mapping, power and cooling monitoring, capacity planning, and keeping records accurate after every change
Access control, mantraps, escort rules, CCTV, media destruction and chain of custody, and site safety procedures such as LOTO and ESD

phases.build: A NetBox instance modelling a small data hall - four racks, 20 devices, cabling and power feeds - with a change log recording a server decommission and a drive replacement correctly.

noc-engineer.summary: Learn networking and Linux, then monitoring and SNMP, then structured troubleshooting and incident handling, finishing with ITIL, ticketing and scripts that cut alert toil.

phases.title: Networking and Linux foundations

steps.what: CCNA-level OSI and TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs, STP, OSPF and BGP basics, NAT, DNS, DHCP, and reading show commands on Cisco IOS
Shell, SSH, file permissions, systemd services, log files in /var/log, and network tools like ip, ss, dig, mtr and tcpdump

phases.build: A GNS3 lab with two sites joined by OSPF and an eBGP link to a simulated ISP, plus a Linux jump host, documented with topology, IP plan and show-command verification.

phases.title: Monitoring and SNMP

steps.what: Uptime, latency, interface utilisation and error metrics, thresholds and alert tuning, dashboards, syslog, NetFlow basics and reducing alert noise
SNMP v2c vs v3, MIBs and OIDs, polling vs traps, snmpwalk and snmpget, adding devices to an NMS and interpreting interface counters

phases.build: A Zabbix or LibreNMS plus Grafana NOC dashboard monitoring your GNS3 routers via SNMPv3 and syslog, with alert rules for link down, high utilisation and BGP neighbour loss.

phases.title: Troubleshooting and incidents

steps.what: Layered isolation from physical to application, ping/traceroute/MTR, interface errors, routing table and BGP state checks, packet captures and confirming fixes
Incident lifecycle, severity levels, running a bridge call, status updates, timelines, workarounds vs fixes, and writing post-incident reports
When and how to escalate, on-call rotations, escalation matrices, carrier and vendor escalations, and handing over with clear context

phases.build: Three simulated outages in your lab (fiber cut, BGP flap, DHCP failure): trigger the alerts, work each to resolution, and publish incident timelines and post-incident reports.

phases.title: Process and automation

steps.what: ITIL 4 basics: service value chain, incident, problem, change and event management, SLAs and OLAs, at ITIL 4 Foundation level
Creating and updating incident tickets, linking alerts to tickets, recording carrier ticket references, shift handover notes and SLA timers
Python or Bash to ping-sweep, parse syslogs, pull interface stats over SNMP or SSH, and auto-create tickets or chat alerts through APIs

phases.build: A Python NOC helper that polls device health, de-duplicates alerts, opens tickets through the Jira Service Management API, posts summaries to Slack and generates a shift handover report.

network-automation-engineer.summary: Learn routing and switching alongside Python, drive devices through APIs and Netmiko/NAPALM, template configs with Ansible and Jinja2, and finish with Git-based CI/CD and Terraform.

phases.title: Networks and Python

steps.what: Shell, SSH keys, file editing, package managers, Python virtual environments and running scripts - the environment every automation tool runs in
CCNA-level subnetting, VLANs, STP, OSPF, BGP basics, ACLs, NAT, and reading running configs on Cisco IOS/NX-OS and Arista EOS
Data types, functions, files, exceptions, modules, virtualenvs, regex, JSON/CSV handling, and the ipaddress library

phases.build: A Containerlab or GNS3 multi-router OSPF/BGP lab plus a Python script that parses saved configs into an interface/IP inventory CSV and a subnet utilisation report.

phases.title: APIs and device libraries

steps.what: HTTP methods, status codes, auth tokens, JSON payloads, RESTCONF and NETCONF/YANG basics, and calling device and controller APIs from Python
SSH automation with Netmiko, multi-vendor getters and config merge/replace with NAPALM, parsing output with TextFSM or Genie, and concurrency with Nornir

phases.build: A Python tool that backs up every lab device's config via Netmiko, collects NAPALM facts and neighbours, diffs today's config against yesterday's, and pulls interface data via RESTCONF from a DevNet sandbox.

phases.title: Templating and Ansible

steps.what: YAML syntax and data models, Jinja2 templates with loops, conditionals and filters, and separating source-of-truth data from config templates
Inventory, playbooks, roles, variables, network modules, idempotency, check mode, Ansible Vault, and collections for Cisco, Arista and Juniper

phases.build: An Ansible project that renders and pushes VLAN, interface and OSPF config to six lab devices from YAML host vars via Jinja2 templates, with check-mode diffs and a post-change validation playbook.

phases.title: Git, CI/CD and infrastructure as code

steps.what: Branching, pull requests, code review, pre-commit linting, and GitHub Actions or GitLab CI pipelines that lint, test in a virtual lab and deploy approved changes
Providers, resources, state, plan and apply, modules, and managing cloud networking (VPCs, subnets, security groups) and NetBox objects as code

phases.build: A NetDevOps pipeline: a pull request changing a VLAN triggers GitHub Actions to lint, run Batfish/pyATS checks against a Containerlab topology and apply via Ansible on merge, plus Terraform for an AWS VPC.

field-service-tech.summary: Learn PC, Windows and networking basics, then hands-on hardware repair and cabling, finishing with on-site troubleshooting, customer handling and the paperwork that keeps field visits clean.

phases.title: PC, Windows and network basics

steps.what: CPU, RAM, storage, motherboards, PSUs, BIOS/UEFI, POST and boot sequence, printers and peripherals, and ESD safety
Windows install and recovery, drivers, Device Manager, Event Viewer, user accounts, BitLocker recovery and Safe Mode
IP addressing, DHCP, DNS, switches and routers, Wi-Fi setup, PoE, and testing with ping, ipconfig and a cable tester

phases.build: A portable diagnostic USB kit (Ventoy with Windows PE, MemTest86 and a Linux live image) plus a checklist mapping each tool to the faults it diagnoses, tested on at least three machines.

phases.title: Hardware repair and cabling

steps.what: Disassembling laptops, desktops and printers; replacing screens, keyboards, drives, RAM, PSUs and fans; ESD safety, parts identification and RMA handling
Cat5e/Cat6 termination (T568A/B), keystone jacks, patch panels, cable testing and labelling, basic fiber patching and tidy cable management

phases.build: Repair and document three real devices (laptop, desktop, printer) for friends or a local NGO, and wire a small office or lab room with terminated, tested and labelled Cat6 runs to a patch panel.

phases.title: On-site troubleshooting and customers

steps.what: Diagnosis under time pressure: reproduce the fault, isolate hardware vs software vs network, swap-test with spares and confirm the fix with the user
Professional arrival and introductions, explaining work to non-technical staff, managing expectations on parts and timelines, and handling unhappy customers
Dispatch and work orders, updating tickets from the field, logging parts used and time on site, closure notes and customer sign-off

phases.build: A field-visit simulation pack of six work orders (POS terminal, printer, Wi-Fi dropout, dead laptop, switch port, projector), each with diagnosis steps, parts list, customer summary and closure notes.

phases.title: Documentation and travel logistics

steps.what: Site surveys, before/after photos, asset tags and serials, network and cable maps, and clear handover notes for the next technician
Planning routes across multiple sites, carrying a parts and tools kit, site access and safety rules, and logging travel time and expenses

phases.build: A digital site binder template - site survey form, asset register, cable map, photo log and visit report - filled in completely for one real location you serviced.

it-ops-manager.summary: For students aiming at IT operations and service-management internships: IT and spreadsheet basics, then ITIL-based service and incident management, then leadership, vendors and budgets.

phases.title: IT and business foundations

steps.what: How end-user devices, networks, servers, cloud and SaaS fit together, common outage types, and CompTIA ITF+/A+ level vocabulary
Formulas, lookups, pivot tables, charts and simple dashboards for SLA, ticket-volume and cost reporting

phases.build: An IT operations dashboard in Excel from a public or synthetic ticket dataset: volume by category, SLA breach rate, mean time to resolve, monthly trends and three written recommendations.

phases.title: Service management and ITIL

steps.what: ITIL 4 guiding principles, service value chain, practices (incident, problem, change, service request, service level management) and ITIL 4 Foundation prep
Service catalogues, SLAs and OLAs, request fulfilment, knowledge management, CMDB basics, and configuring workflows in an ITSM tool
Major incident process, priority matrix, standard/normal/emergency changes, CAB, risk assessment, post-incident reviews and blameless RCA

phases.build: A ServiceNow developer instance or Jira Service Management project set up for a fictional 300-person company: service catalogue, SLA rules, incident priority matrix and a change approval workflow.

phases.title: Leading people and communicating

steps.what: Shift scheduling, delegation, 1:1s, giving feedback, coaching junior technicians, handling escalations within the team and basic performance metrics
Writing outage notifications, executive summaries and monthly service reviews, and translating technical risk into business impact

phases.build: A monthly service review deck for the fictional company: KPIs from your dashboard, two major-incident summaries written for executives, and a 90-day improvement plan with owners and dates.

phases.title: Vendors, budgets and infrastructure

steps.what: Comparing vendor proposals, SLAs and penalties in contracts, renewals, licence tracking and running vendor performance reviews
Capex vs opex, cost per user and per ticket, cloud and SaaS spend, building an annual IT budget and tracking actuals against forecast
IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, Microsoft 365 and Azure/AWS basics, backups and DR, monitoring, and how infrastructure choices affect cost and risk

phases.build: An annual IT budget for the fictional company covering licences, hardware refresh, cloud spend and support contracts, plus a scored RFP comparison of three helpdesk vendors.

network-security-engineer.summary: Learn Linux and routing and switching, then firewalls, VPNs and core network security, then detection with IDS/IPS and SIEM, finishing with zero-trust access and Python automation.

phases.title: Network and Linux foundations

steps.what: Shell, permissions, services, nftables/iptables basics, logs, SSH hardening, and networking commands such as ip, ss and tcpdump
CCNA-level subnetting, VLANs, STP, OSPF and BGP basics, ACLs, NAT, DHCP/DNS and port security on Cisco IOS

phases.build: A GNS3 or EVE-NG lab with a segmented campus (user, server and management VLANs), OSPF routing and ACLs between zones, documented with a topology and a traffic-flow matrix.

phases.title: Firewalls, VPNs and core security

steps.what: CIA triad, threat models, common attacks (spoofing, MITM, DoS, scanning), segmentation, defense in depth and hardening at Security+ depth
Stateful vs next-gen firewalls, zones, rule design and ordering, NAT policies, application control, logging, and Palo Alto/FortiGate/pfSense management
IPsec phase 1 and 2, IKEv2, site-to-site vs remote access, SSL VPN, WireGuard, certificates vs PSKs, and troubleshooting tunnel negotiation

phases.build: A pfSense/OPNsense firewall protecting your lab with zone rules and NAT, a site-to-site IPsec tunnel to a second firewall, WireGuard remote access, and an Nmap report proving only intended ports are open.

phases.title: Detection and monitoring

steps.what: Signature vs anomaly detection, Suricata and Snort rules, inline vs passive deployment, tuning false positives and checking alerts against packet captures
Firewall, IDS, Windows and Linux log sources, parsing and normalisation, correlation rules, dashboards, and triaging alerts into incidents

phases.build: Suricata on your firewall feeding Wazuh or Elastic: simulate a port scan, SSH brute force and beaconing from a Kali VM, then document the alerts, correlation rules and triage notes for each.

phases.title: Zero-trust and automation

steps.what: NIST SP 800-207 principles, identity-aware access, microsegmentation, device posture, ZTNA vs VPN and SASE concepts
Parsing firewall logs, auditing rules through vendor APIs, crafting packets with Scapy, and automating Nmap scans and reports

phases.build: ZTNA access to a lab web app via Cloudflare Zero Trust or Tailscale ACLs replacing the VPN, plus a Python firewall-rule auditor that flags shadowed, overly broad and unused rules in an exported ruleset.

qa.summary: Learn SDLC, web basics, Python and Git, then the core QA craft of test design, manual and exploratory testing and bug reporting, then SQL, API testing and automation in an agile CI workflow.

phases.title: Software and testing foundations

steps.what: SDLC models, STLC phases, verification vs validation, test levels (unit, integration, system, UAT), test types and ISTQB Foundation vocabulary
HTML, CSS and DOM basics, HTTP requests and status codes, cookies and sessions, and inspecting pages and network calls in browser DevTools
Variables, control flow, functions, lists and dicts, files, classes and modules - enough to read and write automation scripts confidently
Clone, commit, branch, merge, pull requests and resolving simple conflicts on GitHub

phases.build: A Python CLI that validates CSV invoices and flags malformed rows, with pytest unit tests, a test report in the README and a GitHub history showing branches and pull requests.

phases.title: Core QA craft

steps.what: Equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables, state transitions, pairwise testing, clear test case writing and traceability to requirements
Session-based exploratory testing, charters, heuristics like SFDPOT, cross-browser and responsive checks, and usability and accessibility spot checks
Reproducible bug reports, severity vs priority, bug lifecycle, attaching logs and screenshots, test runs and coverage reports in TestRail

phases.build: A full test pack for an open-source or demo web shop: 60+ designed test cases in TestRail, three exploratory session reports and 10+ reproducible bug reports logged in Jira.

phases.title: Data and API testing

steps.what: SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY and subqueries, using queries to verify data after UI or API actions and to set up test data
REST basics, requests and assertions, environments and variables, chaining requests, schema checks, negative tests and running collections with Newman

phases.build: A Postman collection of 40+ tests for a public REST API such as Restful-Booker covering positive, negative and auth cases, run via Newman, plus SQL checks verifying data a sample app writes.

phases.title: Automation and agile delivery

steps.what: Locators, waits, Page Object Model, assertions, test data, multi-browser runs, screenshots on failure and handling flaky tests with Selenium or Cypress
What CI/CD is, running tests on every push with GitHub Actions, publishing test reports as artifacts and gating merges on results
Sprints, user stories and acceptance criteria, definition of done, QA's role in refinement and stand-ups, and shift-left testing

phases.build: A Selenium or Cypress regression suite of 25+ Page Object Model tests for a demo web app, running in GitHub Actions on every push with an Allure report published as a build artifact.

sdet.summary: Learn Git, testing fundamentals and one language deeply, build UI and API automation frameworks, sharpen DSA for interviews, and finish with CI/CD, Docker and performance testing.

phases.title: Language and testing foundations

steps.what: Clone, commit, branch, rebase vs merge, pull requests, code review etiquette and resolving conflicts on GitHub
SDLC/STLC, test levels and types, the test pyramid, boundary value and equivalence class design, and writing good bug reports
One language deeply: OOP, collections, exceptions, generics or typing, file I/O, build tools (Maven or pip), and unit tests with JUnit/TestNG or pytest

phases.build: A small library in your chosen language, such as a date-range or currency parser, with 90%+ unit-test coverage via JUnit or pytest, coverage reports and a clean Git history on GitHub.

phases.title: UI automation and frameworks

steps.what: Locators, explicit waits, browser contexts, frames and pop-ups, Playwright auto-waiting and tracing, and mobile automation basics with Appium
Page Object Model, data-driven and BDD tests, config management, logging, reporting, parallel runs and retry strategies for flaky tests

phases.build: A reusable UI automation framework (Playwright or Selenium with TestNG/pytest) for a demo e-commerce site with POM, data-driven tests, parallel execution and Allure reports, documented for other engineers.

phases.title: API testing and problem solving

steps.what: HTTP and REST, status codes, OAuth and JWT auth, schema validation, contract tests, mocking with WireMock, and code-based tests with REST Assured or requests
Arrays, strings, hashing, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, sorting, binary search, recursion and complexity analysis for coding interviews

phases.build: A code-based API test suite for a public REST API with schema validation, auth flows and WireMock stubs, merged into your framework repo, alongside 100+ solved DSA problems tracked on GitHub.

phases.title: CI, containers and performance

steps.what: Pipelines as code, running tests on pull requests, parallel jobs and matrices, publishing reports, handling secrets and failing builds on quality gates
Images, Dockerfiles, containers, volumes and docker compose, running Selenium Grid and the app under test in containers for reproducible runs
Load, stress and soak tests, ramp-up and think time, p95/p99 latency, throughput and error rates, and scripting tests with k6 or JMeter

phases.build: A CI pipeline that starts the app and Selenium Grid with docker compose, runs UI and API suites in parallel on every PR, publishes Allure reports and runs a nightly k6 load test with p95 thresholds.

test-automation-eng.summary: Learn to code and test, master one browser automation tool, then design a reusable framework that runs in CI with clear reports.

phases.title: Code, Git and testing basics

steps.what: Variables, functions, OOP, modules, async/await, file I/O, exceptions, virtual envs or npm, reading stack traces
Commits, branching, pull requests, merge conflicts, rebasing, .gitignore, code review workflow
Test levels (unit/integration/E2E), test pyramid, equivalence partitioning, boundary values, assertions, fixtures
DOM structure, CSS selectors, XPath, browser DevTools, HTTP request/response, cookies and local storage

phases.build: A pytest or Jest unit-test suite for a small open-source utility library (e.g. a date or currency parser) with boundary-value cases, fixtures and a coverage report, developed through pull requests on GitHub.

phases.title: Browser automation

steps.what: Locators, auto-waits vs explicit waits, user actions, iframes, file uploads, multiple tabs, screenshots and traces, cross-browser and headless runs
HTTP methods, status codes, JSON schema validation, auth tokens, chaining requests, seeding test data through the API before UI tests

phases.build: An end-to-end suite of 25+ Playwright tests against a public demo shop (e.g. Sauce Demo) covering login, cart and checkout, plus API checks for its backend, running headless on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

phases.title: Framework design

steps.what: Page Object Model, fixtures, data-driven tests, per-environment config, test data factories, retries, parallelism, tagging, flaky-test triage
Gherkin syntax, feature files, step definitions, scenario outlines, keeping steps reusable, when BDD helps vs hurts

phases.build: A reusable hybrid UI+API test framework for a sample web app: page objects, API-based data seeding, dev/staging configs, parallel runs, Gherkin specs for 3 key flows, and a README on adding new tests.

phases.title: CI and reporting

steps.what: YAML workflows, running tests on every PR, matrix builds, dependency caching, browsers in Docker, artifacts, sharding, nightly regression schedules
Allure results, steps and attachments, screenshots and videos on failure, history trends, publishing reports

phases.build: Your framework wired into GitHub Actions: runs on every PR with sharded parallel jobs and a nightly regression schedule, publishing an Allure report with failure screenshots and trend history to GitHub Pages.

performance-test-eng.summary: Build scripting and systems basics, learn load tools and test design, then practise finding real bottlenecks with profilers, APM and database tuning.

phases.title: Systems and scripting foundations

steps.what: Python or JavaScript: functions, loops, JSON parsing, HTTP calls, reading CSV test data, regex for extracting dynamic values
HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2, keep-alive, headers, sessions, caching, load balancers, web/app/DB tiers, latency vs throughput
Shell navigation, processes, top/htop, vmstat, iostat, ss/netstat, log files, ulimits, SSH

phases.build: A Python script that sends concurrent requests to a self-hosted API, records per-call latency and prints p50/p95/p99 and error rate, with a short write-up comparing 1, 10 and 50 concurrent users.

phases.title: Load testing tools and test design

steps.what: Thread groups and VUs, ramp-up, think time, CSV parameterization, correlating dynamic tokens, assertions, thresholds, non-GUI and distributed runs
Workload modeling, load vs stress vs soak vs spike, SLAs and SLOs, percentiles, Little's Law, environment parity, baselines and pass/fail criteria

phases.build: A k6 and JMeter test pack for a self-hosted demo app (e.g. Spring PetClinic) with load, stress, spike and 4-hour soak profiles, CSV-driven users, thresholds and a results report against defined SLOs.

phases.title: Finding bottlenecks

steps.what: CPU, memory, GC and thread-pool saturation, flame graphs, heap dumps, connection-pool exhaustion, USE and RED methods, correlating load with resource graphs
Indexes, EXPLAIN plans, slow query log, N+1 queries, connection pooling, locking and contention, caching hot reads
Distributed traces, service maps, transaction breakdowns, error analytics, dashboards and alerts, tying load-test runs to APM data

phases.build: A bottleneck investigation on an intentionally slow app: drive load with k6, find an N+1 query and a thread-pool limit using traces and flame graphs, fix both, and publish before/after p95 and throughput charts.

phases.title: Scaling load in the cloud

steps.what: Distributed load generation, load agents on cloud VMs, generator saturation and network limits, cost control, provisioning with infrastructure-as-code
Pods, deployments, services, resource requests and limits, HPA autoscaling, running load generators as Jobs, watching pods under load

phases.build: Deploy a microservice demo (e.g. Google Online Boutique) on minikube, run distributed k6 tests via the k6 Operator, and document how HPA autoscaling and resource limits change latency and error rates under ramping load.

manual-qa.summary: Learn testing fundamentals and disciplined test execution, get sharp at exploratory testing and bug reports, then add planning, regression and basic SQL.

phases.title: Testing fundamentals and execution

steps.what: SDLC and STLC, verification vs validation, test levels and types, severity vs priority, defect life cycle, ISTQB Foundation syllabus
Client/server, HTTP status codes, cookies and sessions, DevTools console and network tab, responsive layouts
Reading test cases, preconditions, steps vs expected results, recording pass/fail/blocked, capturing evidence, test runs and cycles

phases.build: Execute a 40-case test cycle on a public demo app (e.g. OrangeHRM demo), recording pass/fail/blocked with evidence screenshots and a cycle summary of coverage and blockers.

phases.title: Finding and reporting bugs

steps.what: Session-based test charters, heuristics (SFDIPOT, tours), boundary and negative inputs, time-boxing, session notes, test oracles
Clear titles, minimal repro steps, expected vs actual, environment details, severity and priority, screen recordings, console and network logs
Jira issues, workflows, JQL filters and dashboards; TestRail suites, sections, runs, milestones and requirement traceability

phases.build: Run five time-boxed exploratory sessions on a self-hosted open-source app (e.g. Mattermost or WordPress), log 10+ well-written bugs in Jira with recordings and logs, and publish the charters and session notes.

phases.title: Planning, regression and data checks

steps.what: Scope, objectives, entry/exit criteria, test approach, environments, risks, schedule and deliverables in an IEEE 829-style outline
Selecting regression suites, smoke vs sanity, impact analysis after a change, prioritizing cases, maintaining a regression pack
Scrum ceremonies, user stories, acceptance criteria, definition of done, the tester's role in a sprint, shift-left testing
SELECT, WHERE, JOIN and GROUP BY to verify data behind the UI, checking records after form submissions

phases.build: A test plan and 60-case regression pack for a sample e-commerce app, with acceptance-criteria-driven cases for 3 user stories, SQL queries verifying orders in the database, and a sprint test summary report.

qa-lead.summary: Get solid in testing and basic automation, then learn to set test strategy, oversee automation health and lead a small team through releases.

phases.title: Testing and coding foundations

steps.what: Test levels and types, equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables, defect life cycle, ISTQB Foundation concepts
Functions, classes, modules, pytest basics, assertions, fixtures, reading other people's test code
Branches, pull requests, reviewing diffs, resolving conflicts

phases.build: A pytest suite for a small open-source library with cases derived from equivalence partitioning and boundary values, developed and reviewed through pull requests on GitHub.

phases.title: Test strategy and release gates

steps.what: Test pyramid, what to automate vs explore, test levels per component, environments and data, non-functional coverage, writing a one-page strategy
Risk identification, likelihood x impact scoring, risk matrices, mapping risk to test depth, risk-based regression prioritization
Entry/exit criteria, go/no-go checklists, defect thresholds, coverage gates in CI, post-deploy smoke tests, release sign-off

phases.build: A test strategy and risk register for an open-source app (e.g. Saleor): risk-scored features, test depth per risk, and a CI quality gate (tests plus a SonarQube coverage threshold) that blocks merges.

phases.title: Automation oversight and metrics

steps.what: Reviewing test code, page objects and fixtures, flaky-test triage, automation ROI, coverage gaps, keeping a suite fast and healthy
Defect density, escape rate, pass-rate trends, flaky rate, cycle time, dashboards that drive decisions rather than vanity numbers

phases.build: A Playwright suite for a demo app plus a test-health dashboard tracking pass rate, flaky tests and escaped defects over 20 CI runs, with a written review of three flaky tests and how you fixed them.

phases.title: Leading people

steps.what: Planning sprint test work, delegating, running stand-ups and bug triage, giving feedback, handling conflict, leading a student project team
Test summary reports, explaining risk to PMs and developers, presenting go/no-go recommendations, pushing back with data
Pairing sessions, onboarding guides, constructive test-review feedback, teaching test design to juniors

phases.build: Lead a 3-4 person QA effort on a hackathon or open-source release: assign test areas, run triage, write the onboarding guide, and present a go/no-go release report backed by your metrics.

qa-manager.summary: Learn how testing and automation work, then build the management toolkit: QA process, quality strategy, people management and resourcing.

phases.title: Testing and automation literacy

steps.what: SDLC and STLC, test levels and types, test design techniques, defect life cycle, ISTQB Foundation concepts
Python and pytest basics, what a Playwright UI test and an API test look like, how a CI pipeline runs tests

phases.build: A small test repository for a demo web app with 15 manual cases, 10 automated Playwright/API checks and a GitHub Actions run, plus a note on which cases you chose to automate and why.

phases.title: QA process and quality strategy

steps.what: Designing the QA workflow: defect life cycle, triage cadence, test-case standards, definition of done, release process, SOPs
Quality goals, shift-left, test pyramid across teams, quality metrics (escape rate, DORA), quality OKRs, balancing speed vs risk

phases.build: A QA playbook for a fictional 3-team startup: defect workflow configured in Jira, test-case standards, definition of done, release checklist, and a quality strategy with OKRs and target metrics.

phases.title: Managing people and stakeholders

steps.what: 1:1s, goal setting, SBI feedback, interviewing testers, performance reviews, career ladders, managing workload and burnout
Stakeholder mapping, quality reporting to leadership, negotiating release dates, escalation paths, explaining risk to non-technical audiences

phases.build: A QA team-building kit: tester career ladder, interview loop with a practical exercise, 1:1 template, and a quarterly quality review deck, piloted while leading a college project or club team.

phases.title: Tooling, budget and governance

steps.what: What to automate, tool evaluation (Playwright vs Cypress vs Selenium), automation ROI, rollout plan, CI integration, ownership model
Estimating test effort, capacity planning, headcount vs automation trade-offs, tool licensing costs, cost of quality
Audit trails, traceability matrices, ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 25010 basics, SOC 2 and regulated-industry test evidence
Evaluating outsourced and crowdtesting vendors, statements of work, SLAs, vendor scorecards

phases.build: An automation adoption proposal for an open-source project: scored tool comparison, a two-quarter rollout plan, effort and cost estimate, audit-ready traceability matrix, and a vendor-vs-hire comparison.

game-qa.summary: Learn to break games methodically and report bugs developers can act on, then add test plans, regression, platform coverage and light scripting.

phases.title: Playing to break

steps.what: Test types, severity vs priority, defect life cycle, smoke vs sanity, test case anatomy, game bug categories (crash, collision, progression)
Mechanics, controls, progression, collision, AI behavior, balance, edge cases like input spamming, save/load abuse and out-of-bounds exploits
Narrowing repro steps, repro rate, build and platform info, video capture, crash dumps, A/B/C severity classes, concise bug titles

phases.build: Test 3 open-source or free itch.io games and publish 15+ bug reports with repro rates, captured video and severity, plus a short summary of each game's weakest systems.

phases.title: Plans, regression and the bug database

steps.what: Feature and level test plans, checklists, platform and settings test matrices, new-build smoke tests, entry/exit criteria
Build-over-build regression, verifying fixes, regression checklists, closing and reopening bugs, tracking reopen rates
Filing and updating bugs, fields and workflows, JQL filters, attaching logs and video, finding duplicates and linking issues

phases.build: A test plan and 80-item checklist for an open-source game (e.g. SuperTuxKart), run across 3 nightly builds with regression verification logged in Jira and a fix/reopen-rate summary.

phases.title: Platforms, cert and scripting

steps.what: PC specs and graphics settings, controller vs keyboard, Android/iOS devices, resolutions and aspect ratios, FPS checks, install and update flows
What platform certification checks: suspend/resume, save data, user accounts, network loss, achievements/trophies, naming and rating rules
Python basics for parsing logs and crash reports, automating repetitive input, simple Unity Test Framework checks

phases.build: A compatibility report for an open-source Unity or Godot game on PC and Android: settings and resolution matrix, FPS captures, a mock cert checklist (suspend, save loss, network drop) and a Python crash-log parser.

qa-analyst.summary: Learn to turn requirements into well-designed test cases, run functional testing with proper defect tracking, then add SQL, UAT and basic automation.

phases.title: From requirements to test cases

steps.what: SDLC and STLC, test levels and types, verification vs validation, defect life cycle, ISTQB Foundation concepts
Reading BRDs, SRS and user stories, acceptance criteria, spotting ambiguity, traceability matrices, clarifying questions, domain flows such as payments
Equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables, state transitions, pairwise testing, positive and negative cases

phases.build: For a sample fund-transfer spec, produce a requirements review with 10+ clarifying questions, a traceability matrix and 50 test cases derived with EP, BVA, decision tables and state transitions.

phases.title: Functional testing and defects

steps.what: Executing functional, integration, smoke and regression tests on web flows, validating business rules, cross-browser checks, test evidence
Defect life cycle, severity vs priority, triage meetings, root-cause tagging, defect metrics, retest and closure
Test repositories, plans and runs, linking cases to requirements and defects, coverage and progress reports
SELECT, JOINs, GROUP BY and subqueries to validate backend data, integrity checks, before/after state of transactions

phases.build: Test a self-hosted open-source business app (e.g. Odoo): run your cases in TestRail linked to requirements, log defects in Jira, and verify transactions with SQL queries against its database.

phases.title: UAT and first automation

steps.what: UAT planning, business-user scenarios, environment readiness, sign-off criteria, collecting feedback, triaging UAT defects
Python and Playwright basics: locators, simple scripted checks, assertions, deciding when automating a regression case pays off

phases.build: A UAT pack for the same app (business scenarios, sign-off form, feedback log) plus 10 Playwright scripts automating its most frequently run regression cases.

mobile-qa.summary: Learn how mobile apps fail across devices and OS versions, then automate them with Appium and run everything in CI with proxy and performance debugging.

phases.title: Mobile testing fundamentals

steps.what: Test levels and types, test design techniques, severity vs priority, defect life cycle
Install/upgrade flows, permissions, interruptions, orientation, background/foreground, deep links, push, offline mode, store guidelines
Device, OS and build details, repro steps, screen recordings, adb logcat and Xcode console logs, crash reports

phases.build: A 60+ case mobile test checklist for an open-source Android app from F-Droid, executed with 10+ bug reports that include logcat output and screen recordings.

phases.title: Devices, emulators and code

steps.what: Android emulators and iOS simulators, AVD configs, fragmentation matrices, network throttling, real-device clouds, adb commands
Classes, collections, exceptions, interfaces, Maven or Gradle builds, JUnit/TestNG test structure
Commits, branches, pull requests, resolving merge conflicts

phases.build: A device coverage matrix (OS versions, screen sizes, manufacturers) justified with market-share data, plus a test pass of one app on 6 emulator/cloud configs including throttled 3G and offline runs.

phases.title: Mobile automation

steps.what: Appium server and capabilities, Appium Inspector, locators, gestures, waits, Espresso view matchers, XCUITest basics, page objects
REST endpoints behind the app, status codes, JSON assertions, auth tokens, validating app data through the API

phases.build: An Appium + TestNG framework in Java with page objects automating login, search and checkout on an open-source Android app, plus RestAssured checks for the APIs those screens call.

phases.title: CI and deep debugging

steps.what: Building APK/IPA in CI, running emulators in GitHub Actions, Firebase Test Lab, parallel device runs, test artifacts
Intercepting HTTPS traffic, SSL proxying setup, rewriting responses, simulating errors and slow networks
App launch time, frame drops, memory leaks, CPU and battery drain profiling, Android Vitals

phases.build: Run your Appium suite on every push via GitHub Actions and Firebase Test Lab, plus a debugging report: 3 API failures forced through Charles and launch-time and memory profiles of a heavy flow.

api-test-eng.summary: Learn HTTP and a scripting language, master REST and GraphQL testing in Postman and RestAssured, then add contracts, database checks, CI, mocks and load.

phases.title: HTTP and scripting foundations

steps.what: Client/server, HTTP methods, status codes, headers, cookies, JSON and XML, REST principles, auth with API keys, OAuth2 and JWT
Commits, branches, pull requests, resolving merge conflicts
Java or Python: OOP, collections, JSON parsing, HTTP clients, test runners (TestNG/pytest), data-driven tests, logging

phases.build: A small CLI checker in Python or Java that calls the GitHub REST API, validates status codes and response fields for 10 endpoints, and exits non-zero on failure, developed through pull requests.

phases.title: API testing core

steps.what: CRUD flows, positive and negative cases, schema validation, pagination, auth, idempotency, rate limits, GraphQL queries, mutations and errors
Postman collections, environments, pre-request scripts, JS tests, Newman CLI; RestAssured given/when/then, request specs, POJO serialization

phases.build: A RestAssured + TestNG suite and a Postman collection for Restful-Booker and the GitHub GraphQL API with 50+ tests covering auth, CRUD, schema validation and negative cases.

phases.title: Integration, data and CI

steps.what: Consumer-driven contracts, Pact broker, OpenAPI schema checks, multi-service flows, environment and test data setup
SELECT, JOINs and aggregates to validate API writes in the database, test data setup and cleanup scripts
Running API suites in GitHub Actions or Jenkins, secrets per environment, Newman in CI, test reports, gating merges on failures

phases.build: Two Dockerized microservices with Pact consumer contracts and an integration suite that verifies database state via SQL, all running in GitHub Actions with published reports and merge gating.

phases.title: Mocks and performance

steps.what: Stubbing third-party APIs, simulating timeouts and error codes, request matching, record and playback
Basic API load scripts, virtual users, thresholds, p95 latency and error rates under load

phases.build: Extend the microservice suite with WireMock stubs for a payment provider (timeouts, 500s, slow responses) and a k6 script with p95 thresholds that runs nightly in CI.

test-architect.summary: Become a strong multi-language engineer first, then design scalable automation frameworks, CI pipelines and environments, and add performance and security testing.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: One typed language (Java or TypeScript) and Python: OOP, design patterns, async, package managers, idioms each test stack relies on
Branching strategies, pull requests, code review, monorepo basics
Shell, processes, environment variables, SSH, file permissions, reading logs

phases.build: The same API smoke-test suite implemented in Python (pytest) and TypeScript (Jest) against the GitHub REST API, with a write-up comparing structure, tooling and readability.

phases.title: Framework and automation architecture

steps.what: Test pyramid vs trophy, layered framework design, page objects vs screenplay, fixtures, config, data builders, reporting hooks
Driver abstraction layers, shared libraries across teams, parallel and distributed runs, flaky-test quarantine, test selection, design patterns

phases.build: A UI+API automation framework published as a reusable package: pluggable drivers, environment config, data builders, parallel runs, flaky-test quarantine tags, and onboarding docs for a new team.

phases.title: CI, cloud and test data

steps.what: Pipeline design, test stages per environment, sharding, caching, test impact analysis, quality gates, containerized runners, reporting
Docker images and Compose, Kubernetes basics, ephemeral test environments, Selenium Grid on Kubernetes, cloud browser and device farms
Synthetic data generation, database seeding and reset, data masking, isolated data per parallel worker

phases.build: A CI pipeline that spins up an ephemeral Docker Compose environment per PR with Testcontainers-seeded data, runs your framework sharded across 4 jobs, enforces SonarQube gates and publishes Allure trends.

phases.title: Non-functional testing and mentoring

steps.what: Load test design and CI thresholds with k6; OWASP Top 10, DAST baseline scans, dependency scanning, writing security test cases
Framework docs and contribution guides, reviewing others' tests, running a short workshop on test design

phases.build: Add k6 performance thresholds and an OWASP ZAP baseline scan to the pipeline, then publish a contributor guide and run a workshop where classmates add tests to your framework through reviewed PRs.

accessibility-tester.summary: Learn semantic web basics and WCAG, test hands-on with screen readers and other assistive tech, then run full audits with automated and manual checks.

phases.title: Web basics and WCAG

steps.what: Document structure, forms and labels, headings, lists, tables, CSS display and visibility, focus styles, the DevTools accessibility pane
POUR principles, A/AA/AAA levels, key criteria (1.1.1, 1.4.3, 2.1.1, 2.4.7, 4.1.2), WCAG 2.2 additions, Understanding docs and techniques

phases.build: An accessible signup form and data-table page built from scratch, checked against a WCAG 2.2 AA checklist you wrote in plain language, with each design choice mapped to a success criterion.

phases.title: Assistive technology in practice

steps.what: Browse vs focus mode, headings and landmarks navigation, rotor, forms mode, name/role/state announcements, live regions, TalkBack and VoiceOver gestures
Keyboard-only flows, focus order and traps, 400% zoom and reflow, forced colors and high contrast, voice control, switch access
Native elements first, roles/states/properties, accessible names, aria-live, aria-expanded, APG patterns (dialog, tabs, combobox), common ARIA misuse

phases.build: Test 5 complex widgets (modal, tabs, combobox, carousel, data grid) from an open-source UI library with NVDA, VoiceOver and keyboard only; document defects and ship ARIA-correct fixed versions in a public repo.

phases.title: Audits, compliance and remediation

steps.what: axe DevTools, WAVE and Lighthouse scans, axe-core in Playwright tests, what automation cannot catch and how to report it
Audit scoping, page sampling, contrast checks, alt text and headings review, forms and error handling, logging findings per success criterion
Revised Section 508, EN 301 549 clauses, European Accessibility Act, ADA basics, VPAT/ACR structure
Severity rating, user-impact descriptions, code-level fix recommendations, writing an ACR, retesting fixes

phases.build: A full WCAG 2.2 AA audit of an open-source web app: axe-core checks in CI, manual and screen-reader findings per success criterion, a prioritized remediation report, and a draft VPAT/ACR.

game-qa-lead.summary: Get solid at hands-on game testing, then learn to plan coverage, triage the bug database, handle cert and cross-platform passes, and lead a testing team to ship.

phases.title: Game testing and test planning

steps.what: Gameplay, progression, collision, AI and balance testing; repro steps and repro rate, video capture, build smoke tests, A/B/C bug classes
Feature and level test plans, test matrices (platform x settings x mode), smoke vs full passes, milestone plans (alpha, beta, gold), effort estimates

phases.build: A milestone test plan for an open-source game (e.g. SuperTuxKart) with a feature/platform matrix and effort estimates, executed on one build with 15+ logged bugs.

phases.title: Triage, platforms and certification

steps.what: Severity vs priority for games, duplicate hunting, repro verification, ship-blocker calls, triage meetings, bug database hygiene and JQL
PC hardware and graphics configs, controllers, Android/iOS devices, console differences, performance captures, input and resolution matrices
Platform requirement checklists, suspend/resume, save data, user switching, network loss, achievements/trophies, rating and naming rules

phases.build: A triaged bug database for a game-jam title: 30+ bugs with severity, priority and ship-blocker calls, a PC + Android cross-platform pass, and a mock certification checklist run with results.

phases.title: Leading the QA team to ship

steps.what: Assigning test areas, stand-ups and handovers, onboarding testers, reviewing bug quality, managing crunch and morale, escalation
Daily quality reports, ship-risk summaries, negotiating fix priorities, writing for producers vs developers, milestone sign-off
Bug find/fix rates, open blocker trends, test-pass completion, burndown to milestone, dashboards
Where automation fits in games: smoke tests, Unity Test Framework, automated playthroughs, reviewing test scripts, flaky-test triage

phases.build: Lead 3-5 testers through a student game's final week: daily triage, quality reports to the dev lead, a bug burndown dashboard, a Unity Test Framework smoke suite, and a gold sign-off memo.

localization-qa.summary: Learn i18n basics and linguistic review in your strongest languages, then run in-context LQA passes across locales and add CAT tools and simple check scripts.

phases.title: Localization basics and linguistic review

steps.what: Test types, severity vs priority, defect life cycle, test case anatomy, smoke vs regression
i18n vs l10n, locale codes, string resources, Unicode and UTF-8, pluralization, date/number/currency formats, RTL, pseudo-localization
Mistranslations, terminology consistency, grammar and spelling, tone and register, glossary and style-guide compliance, untranslated strings, placeholders
Target-language grammar references, register for UI vs marketing text, tech and gaming terminology, critically reading localized products

phases.build: A linguistic review of your native-language localization of an open-source app on Weblate: 30+ issues categorized as accuracy, terminology, grammar or style, with suggested fixes submitted upstream.

phases.title: Multi-language, in-context QA

steps.what: LQA passes across several locales, truncation and overlap, font and glyph rendering, RTL mirroring, locale formats, switching device languages
LQA bug fields: locale, string ID, screenshot with expected text, category and severity, repro steps, batching repeated issues
Checking strings on their real screens, context mismatches, gender and plural agreement, button length limits, layout breaks across resolutions

phases.build: An LQA pass of an open-source app in 3 locales (e.g. Hindi, Tamil and Arabic RTL): 25+ screenshot-backed bugs for truncation, encoding, RTL and formatting issues logged in Jira with string IDs.

phases.title: Culture, CAT tools and automation

steps.what: Culturally sensitive imagery and color, name/address/phone formats, legal and rating differences, regional variants (pt-BR vs pt-PT), idioms and humor
Translation memories, termbases, built-in QA checks, XLIFF files, reviewing in CAT tools, MQM error scoring
Python scripts that check placeholders, string-length limits and missing keys in JSON, XLIFF or .strings files; automated screenshot capture

phases.build: A Python LQA checker that flags missing keys, broken placeholders and over-length strings across an open-source project's locale files, plus an MQM-scored review and regional notes for 2 markets.

pm.summary: Learn how software gets built and how to understand users, then practise strategy, data-driven prioritization, roadmapping and leading a team through a launch.

phases.title: Users and product strategy

steps.what: How web and mobile apps work (client, server, API, database), the development life cycle, tech debt, release processes, reading a PRD
User interviews, survey design, usability tests, affinity mapping, personas, Jobs-to-be-Done, avoiding leading questions
Vision, target segments, problem framing, competitive analysis, positioning, business models, north-star metric, strategic bets

phases.build: A strategy memo for an Indian consumer app (e.g. Zepto or CRED) built on 6 user interviews: personas, JTBD, competitive map, north-star metric and three strategic bets with risks.

phases.title: Data for product decisions

steps.what: SELECT, JOINs, GROUP BY, CTEs and window functions for funnels and cohorts on event tables
Funnels, cohorts, retention curves, A/B test basics and significance, product metrics (activation, DAU/MAU, churn), dashboards

phases.build: A funnel and retention analysis of the public Google Merchandise Store dataset in BigQuery: SQL queries, a Metabase dashboard, and three product recommendations backed by the numbers.

phases.title: Prioritization and roadmaps

steps.what: RICE and ICE scoring, impact vs effort, Kano model, opportunity sizing, cutting scope, documenting trade-offs
Outcome vs feature roadmaps, now/next/later, themes and OKRs, sequencing dependencies, communicating uncertainty, PRDs and user stories

phases.build: A RICE-scored backlog of 20 ideas and a now/next/later roadmap with OKRs for the phase-1 app, plus one full PRD with user stories, acceptance criteria and success metrics.

phases.title: Execution and launch

steps.what: Stakeholder mapping, aligning engineering, design and sales, running reviews, written updates, handling disagreement, influence without authority
Sprints, backlog grooming, story points, stand-ups, reviews and retros, Kanban, the PM vs product owner role
Launch plans, positioning and messaging, pricing basics, launch channels, enabling sales and support, launch metrics

phases.build: Run a 4-week product sprint for a college club or hackathon team: Jira backlog, sprint ceremonies, weekly stakeholder updates, a launch plan with messaging and metrics, and a post-launch review.

associate-pm.summary: Build product sense through research and teardowns, add data analysis and prototyping, then practise shipping a small feature with a team in sprints.

phases.title: Product sense and user research

steps.what: How web and mobile apps work (client, server, API, database), the development life cycle, what engineers need in a spec
Product teardowns, identifying user problems, judging UX, defining success metrics, product design and estimation frameworks (CIRCLES)
User interviews, survey design, usability tests, affinity mapping, personas, Jobs-to-be-Done, avoiding leading questions

phases.build: A research-backed teardown of a popular Indian app: 6 user interviews, an affinity-mapped synthesis, 3 prioritized problems, and a proposed feature with success metrics.

phases.title: Data and metrics

steps.what: SELECT, JOINs, GROUP BY and simple window functions on product event tables
Funnels, cohorts, retention, A/B test basics, product metrics (activation, DAU/MAU, churn), charts that answer a question

phases.build: A funnel and cohort analysis of a public product dataset (e.g. Google Merchandise Store in BigQuery) with a one-page memo recommending one change and how you would measure it.

phases.title: Prototyping and planning

steps.what: User flows, low-fi wireframes, Figma components and auto layout, clickable prototypes, usability testing a prototype
Now/next/later roadmaps, slicing a feature into increments, OKRs, writing a PRD with user stories and acceptance criteria

phases.build: A clickable Figma prototype of your proposed feature tested with 5 users, plus a PRD and a now/next/later roadmap shipping it in three increments.

phases.title: Shipping with a team

steps.what: Sprints, backlog grooming, story points, stand-ups, reviews and retros, Kanban boards
Crisp specs and status updates, pyramid-principle structure, presenting to leadership, running meetings, async writing

phases.build: Ship your feature with a student dev team (or no-code in Bubble) across 2 sprints: Jira backlog, sprint ceremonies, weekly written updates, and a launch retro with usage metrics.

senior-pm.summary: Senior PM is not an entry role, so this path builds APM-internship readiness the senior way: product basics and numbers first, then strategy, roadmaps and stakeholder craft, then data, experiments and launches.

phases.title: Product foundations

steps.what: Product lifecycle, PM vs project manager, problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, RICE prioritization basics
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, cohort tables, simple revenue and unit-economics models, scenario toggles

phases.build: A teardown of an Indian consumer app (e.g., Swiggy or CRED) written as a PRD-style doc: target users, top three problems, RICE-scored fixes and a spreadsheet model sizing the impact of the top fix.

phases.title: Strategy and roadmaps

steps.what: Market sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM), competitive analysis, positioning, North Star metric, strategy kernel (diagnosis, policy, actions), writing strategy memos
Outcome vs feature roadmaps, Now/Next/Later format, RICE and Kano prioritization, dependency mapping, communicating trade-offs and what is not on the roadmap

phases.build: A one-year strategy memo and Now/Next/Later outcome roadmap for a real product area (e.g., UPI payments inside a shopping app), with a North Star metric, sizing model and explicitly rejected options.

phases.title: Users and stakeholders

steps.what: Stakeholder mapping, RACI, status updates, running review meetings, negotiating scope, handling disagreement, saying no with evidence
Interview scripts, usability tests, survey design, affinity mapping, synthesizing insights into problem statements, avoiding leading questions

phases.build: Run 8-10 user interviews and a survey for a campus product, synthesize findings into an insights deck, and present a recommendation to a mock stakeholder panel with a RACI and decision log.

phases.title: Data and experimentation

steps.what: Metric trees, leading vs lagging indicators, funnel and cohort reads, dashboards, writing decision memos that state the data and the call
Hypothesis design, sample size and power, statistical significance, guardrail metrics, novelty effects, reading and reporting test results
SELECT, joins, GROUP BY, CTEs, window functions; querying event tables for funnels, retention and experiment readouts

phases.build: Analyze a public e-commerce event dataset with SQL, build funnel and retention dashboards, design an A/B test for the biggest drop-off with a sample-size calculation, and write a decision memo.

phases.title: Launch and lead

steps.what: Launch tiers, positioning and messaging, pricing basics, launch checklists, sales and support enablement, adoption metrics after launch
Running 1:1s, SBI feedback model, coaching instead of telling, writing onboarding guides for juniors

phases.build: A full launch plan for a feature you prototyped: positioning doc, pricing hypothesis, launch checklist and success metrics, plus an onboarding guide you used to mentor a junior club member through the launch.

technical-pm.summary: Starts with real coding, Git and web fundamentals, then API design and system architecture, then technical strategy, data and engineering collaboration, so a student can hold their own with engineers in a TPM internship.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: Variables, functions, data structures, OOP basics, reading JSON, calling REST APIs with requests, error handling, small scripts
Commits, branches, pull requests, code review etiquette, merge conflicts, reading a repo's history
Client-server model, HTTP methods and status codes, headers, DNS, cookies vs tokens, how a request flows through a web app

phases.build: A Python CLI that pulls data from a public API (e.g., GitHub or data.gov.in), handles pagination, rate limits and errors, with a clean README and a reviewed pull-request history on GitHub.

phases.title: APIs and systems

steps.what: REST resource modelling, versioning, pagination, idempotency, error schemas, OpenAPI specs, OAuth and API keys, REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC
Monolith vs microservices, SQL vs NoSQL, caching, queues, load balancers, CAP trade-offs, latency budgets, reading architecture diagrams

phases.build: An OpenAPI spec and FastAPI implementation of a ticket-booking API with versioning and rate limits, plus an architecture diagram and a one-page doc defending your caching and queue choices.

phases.title: Technical product strategy

steps.what: Platform vs product bets, build/buy/partner, tech debt as roadmap work, developer personas, competitive analysis of dev tools, strategy narratives
Outcome roadmaps, Now/Next/Later, sequencing around technical dependencies and migrations, RICE prioritization

phases.build: A strategy memo and 12-month roadmap for a developer tool (e.g., an open-source logging library), covering build vs buy, tech-debt sequencing, migration milestones and adoption metrics.

phases.title: Data for decisions

steps.what: Joins, aggregations, CTEs, window functions; querying API logs and product events for adoption, errors and latency
Metric definitions, funnel and cohort analysis, latency percentiles, basic statistics, exploration in pandas, building dashboards

phases.build: An API usage dashboard built from synthetic request logs: SQL for adoption, error rates and p95 latency per endpoint, with a written analysis recommending which endpoints to deprecate.

phases.title: Shipping with engineers

steps.what: Writing PRDs and technical specs, estimation conversations, design reviews, scope vs quality trade-offs, bug triage, incident follow-ups
Sprints, backlog grooming, story points, standups, retrospectives, Kanban vs Scrum

phases.build: Act as PM for a 3-sprint student project: PRD, technical spec reviewed by engineer peers, groomed backlog, sprint retros and a shipped feature with release notes.

group-pm.summary: Group PM is a leadership rung, so this path builds APM-internship readiness with an eye on it: product basics, then strategy and stakeholder craft, then leading people, portfolio coordination and business cases.

phases.title: Product foundations

steps.what: Product lifecycle, problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, prioritization basics
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, cohort tables, revenue and cost models with scenarios

phases.build: A product teardown of an Indian app (e.g., Zomato or Groww) with a prioritized list of problems and a spreadsheet model estimating the business impact of fixing the top one.

phases.title: Strategy and stakeholders

steps.what: Market sizing, competitive analysis, positioning, North Star metric, domain-level strategy, strategy memos with explicit trade-offs
Stakeholder mapping, RACI, pre-wiring decisions, review meetings, negotiating scope, managing disagreement across functions
