phases.build: A domain strategy memo (e.g., the restaurant-partner side of a food-delivery app) with sizing, competitor map, North Star metric, and a stakeholder map and alignment plan for getting it approved.

phases.title: Leading people

steps.what: Team vision and charters, delegation, team rituals, psychological safety, conflict resolution, DACI decision-making
1:1 structure, SBI feedback, GROW coaching model, career ladders, giving and receiving feedback

phases.build: Lead a 4-6 person team (fest tech team, hackathon or club product) through a full cycle: team charter, DACI decision log, GROW-based 1:1 notes and a written retrospective on your leadership.

phases.title: Portfolio and coordination

steps.what: Running multiple roadmaps, capacity allocation, core/adjacent/new balance, cross-team dependency maps, quarterly planning
Working with design, engineering, marketing, sales and legal; launch reviews, operating cadences, async status updates

phases.build: A portfolio roadmap for three related product teams (e.g., a fintech app's onboarding, payments and rewards) with capacity split, dependency map and a cross-team launch review plan.

phases.title: Business cases and metrics

steps.what: Revenue and cost modelling, unit economics, payback and NPV basics, sensitivity analysis, writing investment proposals
Writing and grading OKRs, North Star and input metrics, metric trees, team dashboards

phases.build: A business case for a new product bet with a 3-year spreadsheet model and sensitivity scenarios, team OKRs tied to a metric tree, pitched as a 10-slide deck.

principal-pm.summary: Principal PM is a senior IC track, so this path builds APM-internship readiness its way: sharp writing and product basics, then vision, systems thinking and influence, then market and technical depth.

phases.title: Foundations of product thinking

steps.what: Product lifecycle, problem framing, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, prioritization basics
Pyramid principle, one-page memos, Amazon-style narrative docs, editing for clarity, writing for skeptical readers

phases.build: Two narrative docs: a teardown of a complex marketplace (e.g., Ola or Urban Company) and a one-page problem-framing memo, each revised after written peer review.

phases.title: Vision and systems

steps.what: Vision narratives, North Star, strategy kernel (diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent actions), long-term bets, flywheels
Feedback loops, second-order effects, marketplace dynamics, network effects, causal loop diagrams, unintended consequences

phases.build: A vision narrative for a two-sided marketplace with a causal loop diagram of its supply-demand flywheel, identifying second-order risks of three proposed features.

phases.title: Influence and alignment

steps.what: Stakeholder mapping, pre-wiring decisions, persuasive narratives, negotiation, credibility through data, disagree-and-commit
Reconciling conflicting team goals, shared OKRs, decision forums, escalation paths, writing alignment docs

phases.build: Drive one decision across two student orgs with conflicting goals (e.g., a shared event platform): stakeholder map, pre-read doc, decision meeting and a written record of the agreed path.

phases.title: Market and technical depth

steps.what: TAM/SAM/SOM, competitive landscape, pricing benchmarks, customer segmentation, reading industry reports, trend analysis
System design basics, APIs, databases, scalability, ML basics, reading engineering design docs and asking sharp questions
Coaching juniors, feedback frameworks, sharing product craft through write-ups and workshops

phases.build: A market analysis of an Indian SaaS segment with sizing and competitor map, plus a technical review of a leader's architecture inferred from its API docs and blog, taught to juniors as a workshop.

director-product.summary: Director is an executive role, so this path builds APM-internship readiness pointed toward it: product basics and numbers, then vision and portfolio prioritization, then people leadership and business ownership.

phases.title: Product foundations

steps.what: Product lifecycle, problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, prioritization basics
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, revenue and cost models, scenario analysis

phases.build: A teardown of a multi-product Indian company (e.g., Paytm) mapping its product lines, users and revenue streams, with a spreadsheet estimating which line drives most value.

phases.title: Vision and portfolio

steps.what: Vision narratives, North Star, strategy kernel, translating company goals into product bets, strategy memos
Core/adjacent/transformational balance, WSJF and RICE at portfolio level, capacity allocation, kill/continue decisions, opportunity cost

phases.build: A product-line vision and portfolio review for a real company's suite (e.g., Zoho), ranking 8-10 initiatives with WSJF, a capacity allocation and two explicit kill decisions with reasoning.

phases.title: Leading and building teams

steps.what: 1:1s, feedback, performance conversations, career ladders, delegation, handling underperformance, team health checks
Role scoping, structured interviews, scorecards, PM case interviews, onboarding plans, team composition

phases.build: A PM hiring kit (job description, interview loop, scorecards, case question) used to run mock interviews for peers, plus a 30-60-90 onboarding plan and the 1:1 template you used leading a club team.

phases.title: Business and executive fluency

steps.what: P&L structure, revenue, COGS, gross margin, CAC/LTV, unit economics, budgeting, reading an annual report
Exec summaries, BLUF writing, board-style decks, pyramid principle, handling tough questions, concise status reports
Writing and grading OKRs, North Star and input metrics, metric trees, quarterly business reviews

phases.build: A quarterly business review for a listed Indian tech company built from its annual report: P&L breakdown, unit economics, proposed OKRs and a 5-slide exec deck with a one-page BLUF summary.

vp-product.summary: VP of Product is years away, so this path builds APM-internship readiness with executive range: product basics and numbers, then vision and business strategy, then org leadership, P&L and go-to-market.

phases.title: Product foundations

steps.what: Product lifecycle, problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, prioritization basics
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, revenue and cost models, scenario analysis

phases.build: A teardown of an Indian startup's core product (e.g., Zepto) with user problems, prioritized fixes and a spreadsheet model linking the top fix to revenue.

phases.title: Vision and business strategy

steps.what: Multi-year vision narratives, North Star, product principles, long-term bets, connecting vision to near-term roadmaps
Porter's Five Forces, business models, moats, platform economics, competitive strategy, case studies of Indian startups

phases.build: A 3-year product vision and business strategy for a startup in a crowded market (e.g., quick commerce), with a business model canvas, moat analysis and three strategic bets.

phases.title: Leading the org

steps.what: Product org structures, team topologies, operating principles, culture, change management, decision rights, leading through leaders
Exec summaries, BLUF writing, all-hands narratives, board-style decks, handling tough questions

phases.build: A product org design for a 50-person startup scaling to 200: team topology, operating principles, decision-rights doc and an all-hands style presentation explaining the change.

phases.title: Money and markets

steps.what: P&L structure, gross margin, CAC/LTV, unit economics, budgeting, forecasting, reading company financials
Segmentation, ideal customer profile, positioning, pricing and packaging, channels, launch sequencing, sales and marketing alignment
Funding stages, pitch decks, cap table basics, board updates, investor metrics (ARR, burn, runway)

phases.build: A GTM plan and P&L model for a new product line, plus a mock board update and investor memo reporting ARR, burn and runway against plan.

cpo.summary: The CPO seat is the end of a long road, so this path builds APM-internship readiness with C-suite range: product basics and numbers, then company vision and strategy, then leadership, org scaling, P&L and positioning.

phases.title: Product foundations

steps.what: Product lifecycle, problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, prioritization basics
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, revenue and cost models, scenario analysis

phases.build: A teardown of a mid-size Indian SaaS product (e.g., Freshworks) covering users, pricing tiers and top problems, with a spreadsheet estimating revenue per tier.

phases.title: Company-level vision and strategy

steps.what: Multi-year vision narratives, product principles, North Star, long-term bets, linking vision to company mission
Porter's Five Forces, business models, moats, platform economics, build/buy/partner, competitive response, strategy case studies

phases.build: A company-level product vision and strategy for a mid-size SaaS company expanding globally, with a business model canvas, moat analysis and a build/buy/partner decision for one bet.

phases.title: Executive leadership and scaling

steps.what: Setting direction, leading leadership teams, decisions under uncertainty, crisis communication, culture building, partnering with the CEO
Team topologies, spans and layers, product trios, hiring plans, scaling a PM team from 5 to 50, career ladders

phases.build: An org-scaling plan for a product team growing from 5 to 50 PMs: team topology at each stage, hiring plan, career ladder and a leadership memo explaining the operating model.

phases.title: Business, market and board

steps.what: P&L structure, gross margin, CAC/LTV, unit economics, budgeting, forecasting, reading company financials
Category design, positioning statements, competitive differentiation, messaging hierarchy, analyst and customer perception
Funding stages, board decks, investor metrics (ARR, NRR, burn, runway), handling board questions, investor updates

phases.build: A positioning doc and board pack for a SaaS company: P&L model, ARR/NRR/burn metrics, competitive positioning map and a 10-slide board presentation with a Q&A prep sheet.

product-owner.summary: Starts with how software is actually built, then Scrum, backlogs and user stories, then sprint mechanics and tooling, then stakeholder and domain depth, ready for a PO or business-analyst internship in an agile team.

phases.title: How software gets built

steps.what: Waterfall vs iterative delivery, requirements to release, dev/test/prod environments, QA, release and rollback basics
Problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRDs vs backlogs, product vs project thinking

phases.build: A process map of how a feature moves from idea to production at a real company (from engineering blogs or alumni interviews), documenting roles, environments and handoffs.

phases.title: Scrum, stories and backlogs

steps.what: Scrum Guide roles, events and artifacts, Kanban, velocity, definition of done, SAFe overview for enterprises
INVEST stories, story splitting, Given-When-Then acceptance criteria, story mapping, edge cases and non-functional requirements
Backlog refinement, ordering, epic/feature/story hierarchy, definition of ready, backlog hygiene, tech-debt items

phases.build: A story map and refined backlog of 40+ INVEST user stories with Given-When-Then acceptance criteria for a campus canteen pre-order system, organized into epics and a release plan.

phases.title: Running sprints

steps.what: Capacity planning, sprint goals, story-point estimation, planning poker, forecast vs commitment, burndown charts
Jira boards, workflows, JQL, dashboards, Confluence pages, Azure DevOps boards basics
MoSCoW, WSJF, RICE, Kano, value vs effort, cost of delay

phases.build: Act as PO for a student dev team over three 1-week sprints: sprint goals, planning-poker estimates, JQL dashboards, burndown charts and a WSJF-ordered backlog, ending in a sprint review demo.

phases.title: Customer voice and domain

steps.what: Stakeholder mapping, sprint reviews, managing expectations, saying no, communicating trade-offs and release dates
One domain in depth (banking, insurance, retail or healthcare): core workflows, regulations, terminology and key systems

phases.build: A domain primer for one industry (e.g., retail bank loan origination) with process flows and a glossary, plus a stakeholder communication plan and backlog for a feature in that domain.

growth-pm.summary: Builds the data base first (spreadsheets, statistics, SQL), then funnels, retention and rigorous A/B testing, then acquisition and behavioral levers, ready for a growth or product-analytics internship.

phases.title: Data foundations

steps.what: Pivot tables, lookups, charts, cohort tables, simple funnel models
Descriptive stats, distributions, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, p-values, correlation vs causation
Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs, window functions, date handling; writing funnel, cohort and retention queries on event tables

phases.build: A SQL and spreadsheet analysis of a public e-commerce dataset (e.g., Olist on Kaggle) answering five growth questions: order trends, repeat-purchase rate, top categories and drop-offs.

phases.title: Funnels and retention

steps.what: Tracking plans, AARRR funnels, conversion rates, cohort retention curves, DAU/MAU, churn, LTV, finding the activation moment
pandas exploration, segmentation, time series, visualizations, turning findings into a clear recommendation

phases.build: Instrument a small web app with PostHog, write its tracking plan, and build funnel and cohort-retention dashboards that identify the activation moment and the biggest drop-off.

phases.title: Experimentation

steps.what: Randomization, sample size and power, significance, confidence intervals, guardrail metrics, peeking, sample ratio mismatch, novelty effects
Growth loops, ICE scoring, experiment backlogs, test velocity, experiment docs, learning repositories, iterating on losers

phases.build: Design and analyze 3 experiments on a real or simulated dataset: experiment docs with ICE scores, power calculations, a Python readout with confidence intervals and SRM check, and ship/kill calls.

phases.title: Acquisition and behavior

steps.what: Channels (SEO, paid, referral, content, partnerships), CAC, attribution, UTM tracking, referral loops, app store optimization
Hooked model, Fogg behavior model, nudges, loss aversion, social proof, anchoring, avoiding dark patterns
STP, positioning, 4Ps, messaging, lifecycle email and push campaigns

phases.build: Grow a real asset (club newsletter, Discord or side project) with a referral loop and UTM-tracked channels, apply 3 behavioral nudges, and report CAC, conversion and 4-week retention.

platform-pm.summary: Starts with coding and technical fluency, then platform strategy and API/SDK product craft, then developer experience and architecture, then cross-team planning, ready for a platform or technical PM internship.

phases.title: Coding and technical fluency

steps.what: Functions, data structures, modules, reading JSON, calling APIs, writing small services and scripts
Commits, branches, pull requests, code review, merge conflicts
HTTP and REST, JSON, databases, cloud basics (compute, storage), containers, CI/CD, reading code and logs, auth

phases.build: A small REST service in FastAPI with a database, Dockerfile and GitHub Actions CI, documented well enough that a classmate can run it in under 10 minutes.

phases.title: Platforms and APIs as products

steps.what: Internal vs external platforms, platform-as-product, paved roads, network effects, leverage and adoption metrics, build vs buy
API lifecycle, versioning and deprecation, SDK design across languages, rate limits, changelogs, breaking changes, API metrics

phases.build: A platform strategy doc for an internal notifications platform, with an OpenAPI spec, a Python SDK wrapper, a versioning and deprecation policy and adoption metrics.

phases.title: Developers and architecture

steps.what: Time-to-first-call, onboarding flows, docs, error messages, sandboxes, developer surveys, friction logs
Service boundaries, microservices, queues, caching, multi-tenancy, scalability, SLOs and reliability, reading design docs

phases.build: A DX friction log from integrating 3 public developer APIs (e.g., Razorpay, Twilio, GitHub) with time-to-first-call measurements, plus an architecture diagram of a multi-tenant platform you propose.

phases.title: Planning across teams

steps.what: Dependency mapping, internal customer intake, service-level agreements, negotiating priorities, running migration programs
Platform roadmaps, sequencing migrations, Now/Next/Later, communicating timelines to consuming teams

phases.build: A 2-quarter platform roadmap with a dependency map across 4 consuming teams, an internal intake process and a migration plan for deprecating an old API version.

data-pm.summary: Starts with Python, spreadsheets and strong SQL, then metrics and data-product strategy, then pipelines and governance, then stakeholders and ML basics, ready for a data product or analytics-PM internship.

phases.title: Data foundations

steps.what: Functions, data structures, pandas DataFrames, reading CSV and JSON, notebooks, basic plotting
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, cohort tables
Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs, window functions, date logic, query performance basics, writing metric queries others can trust

phases.build: A SQL and pandas analysis of a large public dataset (e.g., NYC taxi trips or Indian Railways data) with documented, reusable metric queries and a short findings report.

phases.title: Metrics and data products

steps.what: Metric definitions, North Star and metric trees, semantic layers, dashboard design, data storytelling, avoiding vanity metrics
Data as a product, internal customers, data mesh basics, build vs buy for data tools, success metrics and SLAs for data products

phases.build: A metrics layer and Metabase dashboard for a sample SaaS dataset, plus a data-product one-pager defining users, metric definitions, freshness SLAs and adoption goals.

phases.title: Pipelines and governance

steps.what: ETL vs ELT, batch vs streaming, warehouses vs lakes, orchestration, dbt models, data freshness, cost trade-offs
Data quality tests, lineage, catalogs, access control, PII handling, India's DPDP Act and GDPR basics, data contracts

phases.build: An ELT pipeline loading public data into DuckDB or BigQuery with dbt models, data-quality tests, lineage docs and a PII handling note aligned to India's DPDP Act.

phases.title: Stakeholders and ML

steps.what: Requirements from analysts, finance and ops; prioritizing data requests; SLAs; communicating data incidents
Supervised vs unsupervised learning, features, train/test splits, evaluation metrics, LLM basics, when ML is the wrong tool

phases.build: A data-request intake process and prioritized roadmap for a mock analytics team, plus a scikit-learn churn model prototype with a memo on whether it should become a data product.

ai-pm.summary: Starts with Python and ML basics, then what LLMs can do and how to evaluate them, then AI product strategy and prompt iteration, then shipping responsibly, ready for an AI product internship.

phases.title: Code and ML foundations

steps.what: Functions, data structures, pandas, notebooks, calling REST APIs, handling JSON
Supervised learning, train/test splits, overfitting, precision/recall, embeddings intuition, neural networks at a high level

phases.build: A notebook comparing two scikit-learn classifiers on a public dataset (e.g., spam or loan default) that explains the precision/recall trade-off in product terms, such as cost of a false approval.

phases.title: Model capabilities and evaluation

steps.what: Tokens, context windows, temperature, hallucination, RAG, tool use, fine-tuning vs prompting, latency and cost trade-offs, multimodal models
Golden datasets, labeling guidelines, LLM-as-judge, precision/recall, offline vs online evals, error analysis and failure taxonomies

phases.build: A RAG chatbot over your college handbook or syllabus with a 100-question golden eval set, labeling guidelines and an error analysis of where and why it hallucinates.

phases.title: AI product strategy

steps.what: Spotting AI-suitable problems, build vs buy vs fine-tune, data moats, cost per query, human-in-the-loop design, AI UX patterns, success metrics
Prompt patterns, few-shot examples, structured outputs, prompt versioning, regression testing, comparing models on an eval set

phases.build: A PRD and strategy memo for an AI feature (e.g., resume feedback for students) with model cost analysis, prompt versions compared on your eval set, and a human-fallback UX mocked in Figma.

phases.title: Shipping responsibly

steps.what: APIs, latency and caching, vector databases, system design for AI apps, reading model cards and API docs
A/B tests for AI features, online quality metrics, user feedback signals, sample size, guardrail metrics
Bias and fairness, red-teaming, privacy and PII, transparency, India's DPDP Act and EU AI Act basics
Model deployment, monitoring and drift, model registries, CI for models, feedback loops into retraining

phases.build: Ship your AI feature as a FastAPI app with a vector database, run a small user test with feedback logging, publish a red-team report on bias and safety failures, and an MLflow monitoring plan.

product-ops.summary: Starts with product basics, spreadsheets and SQL, then process design and analytics tooling, then coordination and planning cadences, then reporting and communication, ready for a product operations internship.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Product lifecycle, PRDs, launches, how PM, design and engineering work together
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, data cleaning, simple automations
SELECT, joins, GROUP BY, CTEs, date filters; pulling adoption and support data for reports

phases.build: A feature-adoption and support-ticket analysis of a public SaaS dataset using SQL and spreadsheets, with a one-page summary of what the product team should fix first.

phases.title: Process and tooling

steps.what: Current-state mapping, swimlanes, bottleneck analysis, intake processes, PRD and launch templates, lean basics, writing SOPs
Event taxonomies, tracking plans, analytics tool setup, feedback tools, tool-stack audits, integrations and automations

phases.build: A product-org operating kit for a student startup or club: swimlane map of idea-to-launch, PRD and launch templates, a tracking plan and a PostHog dashboard wired to the product.

phases.title: Coordination and cadence

steps.what: Launch readiness reviews, RACI, cross-team rituals, async updates, dependency tracking, meeting design
Quarterly planning cycles, writing and grading OKRs, capacity planning, planning calendars, retros on the process itself
Jira projects, workflows, JQL, roadmap views, Productboard insights and roadmaps, keeping tools in sync

phases.build: Design and run a quarterly planning cycle for 2-3 student teams: OKR templates, a planning calendar, Jira and Productboard set up with linked roadmaps, and a launch readiness checklist.

phases.title: Reporting and communication

steps.what: KPI dashboards, automated reports, weekly business reviews, data storytelling, dashboard hygiene
Product newsletters, release notes, exec updates, feedback loops to sales and support, writing for different audiences

phases.build: An automated weekly product report (Looker Studio dashboard plus newsletter-style release notes) for a real or simulated product, run for 4 weeks with reader feedback incorporated.

api-pm.summary: Starts with coding and hands-on REST/GraphQL fluency, then API strategy and developer experience, then docs and ecosystem, then usage analytics and roadmaps, ready for an API or developer-platform PM internship.

steps.what: Functions, data structures, modules, reading JSON, calling APIs, writing small web services
Commits, branches, pull requests, code review, merge conflicts
HTTP, REST constraints, status codes, OAuth 2.0 and API keys, pagination, webhooks, GraphQL schemas, queries and mutations

steps.what: Docs structure (quickstarts, guides, reference), OpenAPI-generated reference, code samples, changelogs, docs-as-code

phases.build: A Docusaurus docs site for your API (quickstart, guides, OpenAPI reference, changelog), plus a partner-program one-pager and a developer community launch post.

phases.title: Measure and plan

API roadmaps, versioning timelines, deprecation communication, Now/Next/Later, balancing partner requests

phases.build: A usage dashboard built from your API's request logs (calls, errors, p95 latency, active keys) that feeds a 2-quarter roadmap with a v2 migration and deprecation timeline.

payments-pm.summary: Starts with product and spreadsheet basics, then the payments domain and Indian regulation, then strategy and gateway integrations, then fraud, data and stakeholders, ready for a fintech or payments PM internship.

steps.what: Product lifecycle, problem statements, personas, jobs-to-be-done, PRD structure, prioritization basics
Pivot tables, lookups, charts, fee and margin models, scenario analysis

RBI payment aggregator rules, KYC/AML, card tokenization, data localization, PCI DSS, DPDP Act basics, cross-border rules
