Gateway APIs, checkout SDKs, webhooks, idempotency keys, retries, sandbox testing, settlement and reconciliation reports

phases.build: A working checkout using Razorpay or Stripe test mode with webhooks, idempotent retries and a reconciliation script, plus a strategy memo on raising payment success rate.

phases.title: Risk, data and stakeholders

steps.what: Card-not-present fraud, account takeover, friendly fraud, chargebacks, rules engines, velocity checks, risk scoring, 3DS, false declines
SQL on transaction data, success-rate breakdowns by bank and method, cohort analysis, anomaly detection basics, dashboards
Working with banks, compliance, legal, finance, ops and engineering; partner escalations; incident communication

phases.build: Analyze a public card-fraud dataset: SQL fraud and success-rate breakdowns, a rules engine plus a scikit-learn risk score, and a memo for finance and compliance trading fraud loss against false declines.

security-pm.summary: Build networking and PM basics, learn security and compliance deeply enough to talk to engineers, then practise turning threats and enterprise buyer demands into a security product roadmap.

phases.title: Technical and product groundwork

steps.what: TCP/IP and OSI layers, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS and TLS handshakes, ports, firewalls, VPNs, NAT, reading packet captures
Problem discovery, user stories, PRDs, prioritisation frameworks (RICE, MoSCoW), success metrics, release planning

phases.build: A written PRD for a password-reset improvement in an existing app, with problem statement, user stories, success metrics, and an annotated packet capture showing what actually travels over the network during login.

phases.title: Security and technical depth

steps.what: CIA triad, IAM, OAuth 2.0/OIDC, SAML SSO, MFA, encryption at rest/in transit, SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, India DPDP Act, shared responsibility model
REST APIs, client-server and microservice architecture, cloud IAM and VPCs, logging and SIEM concepts, reading architecture diagrams, asking engineers good trade-off questions

phases.build: A threat model and compliance-gap report for an open-source app (e.g. a self-hosted Nextcloud): architecture diagram, data-flow trust boundaries, STRIDE findings, and a SOC 2 control mapping with prioritised fixes.

phases.title: Security product strategy

steps.what: Security market segments (IAM, SIEM, EDR, CNAPP), competitive positioning, build vs. partner, packaging security as paid tiers, security as a feature vs. as a product
MITRE ATT&CK tactics, OWASP Top 10, phishing, ransomware, supply-chain and credential-stuffing attacks, reading CVEs and public breach postmortems

phases.build: A competitive teardown of three identity products (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra, Auth0) mapped against five recent real breaches, ending in a one-page strategy memo recommending where a new entrant should play.

phases.title: Enterprise readiness and execution

steps.what: CISO and IT-admin personas, security questionnaires, SSO/SCIM/audit-log/RBAC requirements, data residency, procurement and RFP cycles, trust centers
Outcome-based roadmaps, now/next/later framing, sequencing by dependency and risk, balancing compliance deadlines with customer asks, communicating trade-offs
Working with security engineering and AppSec on reviews, writing security acceptance criteria, triaging vulnerability reports, incident comms with legal and support

phases.build: A two-quarter enterprise-readiness roadmap for a mock B2B SaaS (SSO, SCIM, audit logs, granular RBAC), with a full PRD for one feature including security acceptance criteria and a filled vendor security questionnaire.

product-designer.summary: Learn design fundamentals and Figma, then flows, prototyping and product thinking, layer in research, UI craft and systems, and finish by testing and understanding how designs become code.

phases.title: Foundations and Figma

steps.what: Gestalt principles, visual hierarchy, contrast, alignment, Nielsen's 10 heuristics, the double-diamond design process
Frames, auto layout, constraints, components and variants, styles, variables basics, collaborative files, Dev Mode handoff

phases.build: A pixel-accurate rebuild of four screens from a real Indian app (e.g. CRED or Zepto) in Figma using auto layout and components, plus a short write-up of the heuristics each screen follows or breaks.

phases.title: Product thinking and flows

steps.what: Problem framing, jobs-to-be-done, user vs. business goals, defining success metrics, scoping an MVP, reading funnel data, trade-offs with engineering effort
Task flows and user flows, happy and edge paths, low-fidelity sketches, mid-fi wireframes, content-first layouts, empty and error states

phases.build: A problem brief and complete flow set for a campus service (e.g. placement-cell drive registration): metrics to move, user flow with edge cases, and annotated mid-fi wireframes for every step.

phases.title: Prototyping and interaction

steps.what: Click-through and high-fidelity prototypes, smart animate, interactive components, variables and conditional logic, prototyping for testing vs. for stakeholders
Affordances and signifiers, feedback and system states, transitions, gestures on mobile, form design, platform patterns from Material and Apple HIG

phases.build: An interactive Figma prototype of the campus-service flow with realistic states (loading, errors, confirmation) and micro-transitions, shareable as a link and recorded as a 60-second walkthrough.

phases.title: Research, UI craft and systems

steps.what: Research plans, recruiting, semi-structured interviews, contextual inquiry, affinity mapping, turning insights into design opportunities
Type scales, 8-pt spacing, grids, colour and contrast, iconography, density, dark mode, polishing screens to production quality
Atomic design, reusable components with variants, design tokens and Figma variables, documenting usage, studying Material and Polaris

phases.build: A redesign of a real student pain point backed by six user interviews, delivered as polished hi-fi screens built entirely from your own mini design system (tokens, 15+ components, usage notes).

phases.title: Validation and handoff

steps.what: Task-based test scripts, moderated and unmoderated tests, think-aloud, success rate and time-on-task, SUS, severity ratings, iterating on findings
Semantic HTML, box model, flexbox and grid, responsive breakpoints, how components and tokens map to CSS, reading what engineers ship

phases.build: A portfolio case study showing the full arc: problem, research, flows, two rounds of usability testing with before/after metrics, and one key screen hand-coded in HTML/CSS to prove handoff fluency.

ux.summary: Start with design fundamentals and user-centred thinking, learn Figma and wireframing, then information architecture and research, and finish by prototyping, testing and designing accessibly.

phases.title: Thinking like a UX designer

steps.what: Gestalt principles, visual hierarchy, Nielsen's 10 heuristics, Norman's design principles, the double-diamond process
ISO 9241-210 HCD cycle, personas, empathy maps, jobs-to-be-done, mental models, cognitive load, designing for context of use

phases.build: A heuristic evaluation of an Indian public-service portal (e.g. IRCTC or DigiLocker): 15+ issues ranked by severity, each with a screenshot, violated heuristic, and a user-centred fix.

phases.title: Figma and wireframing

steps.what: Frames, auto layout, components and variants, styles, FigJam for flows, sharing and commenting, Dev Mode basics
Sketching, low- vs. mid-fidelity wireframes, layout grids, content priority, annotating behaviour, wireframing empty, error and loading states

phases.build: An annotated wireframe set (20+ screens) for a hostel-mess feedback and menu-voting app, covering every state and edge case, with notes engineers could build from.

phases.title: Structure and research

steps.what: Content inventories, card sorting, tree testing, sitemaps, navigation patterns, labelling and taxonomy, search vs. browse
Research questions, recruiting, interview guides, contextual inquiry, surveys, affinity mapping, insight statements

phases.build: An IA overhaul of your college website: content inventory, an open card sort with 15 students, a tree test comparing old vs. new navigation, and the resulting sitemap with success-rate evidence.

phases.title: Prototype, test and include

steps.what: Click-through and interactive prototypes, smart animate, interactive components, choosing fidelity to match the question being tested
Affordances, feedback, system status, form design and validation, gestures, transitions, Material and Apple HIG patterns
Test plans and task scenarios, moderated and remote tests, think-aloud, success rate, SUS scores, severity ratings, synthesising into fixes
WCAG 2.2 AA, colour contrast, focus order, touch target size, screen-reader labels, designing for low literacy and regional languages

phases.build: A tested prototype of the mess-feedback app: two rounds of usability tests with 5 users each, SUS before/after, WCAG AA audit fixes, and a case study documenting what changed and why.

ui-designer.summary: Learn design fundamentals and Figma, then go deep on visual craft, typography, colour and layout, build systematic responsive UI, and add prototyping, icons and motion polish.

phases.title: Foundations and Figma

steps.what: Gestalt principles, proximity and alignment, contrast, repetition, visual weight, how UI differs from print design
Frames, auto layout, constraints, components and variants, styles and variables, plugins, organising pages for handoff

phases.build: Pixel-perfect rebuilds of five screens from apps you admire (e.g. Linear, Swiggy, CRED), fully auto-layouted and componentised, with a side-by-side overlay proving accuracy.

phases.title: Visual craft

steps.what: Visual hierarchy, emphasis, balance, depth and elevation, imagery and illustration use, UI styles, critiquing screens with precise vocabulary
Type anatomy, pairing, modular type scales, line height and measure, weight for hierarchy, Indic script support, variable fonts
Colour models, palettes and semantic colours, contrast ratios, dark mode, 8-pt spacing, column grids, whitespace and density

phases.build: A full visual redesign of a dated Indian utility app (e.g. a state transport booking app): 8 hi-fi screens with a defined type scale, colour palette with contrast checks, and a before/after rationale.

phases.title: Systems and responsive UI

steps.what: Atomic design, design tokens with Figma variables, component variants and properties, light/dark modes, documentation pages
Breakpoints, fluid grids, auto layout resizing, mobile-first layouts, adapting navigation and tables across phone, tablet and desktop
Icon grids and keylines, stroke consistency, optical sizing, building an icon set as components, exporting SVG

phases.build: A themeable UI kit (light and dark) with tokens, 25+ responsive components and a custom 20-icon set, demonstrated by one dashboard laid out at mobile, tablet and desktop breakpoints.

phases.title: Bringing UI to life

steps.what: Interactive components, smart animate, overlays, scroll behaviours, variables for stateful prototypes, presenting to stakeholders
Easing curves, duration, transitions between states, micro-interactions on buttons and toggles, exporting motion with Lottie

phases.build: An interactive, motion-polished prototype of the redesigned app with animated state changes and micro-interactions, published as a Dribbble/Behance case study with a screen-recorded demo.

ux-researcher.summary: Learn UX basics and qualitative methods, master interviews and usability tests, then synthesis and journey maps, and round out with surveys, quant analysis and stakeholder storytelling.

phases.title: Research foundations

steps.what: What UX research is for, the design process, Nielsen's heuristics, where research fits in product cycles, generative vs. evaluative research
Framing research questions, choosing methods, contextual inquiry, diary studies, sampling and recruiting, informed consent and research ethics

phases.build: A complete research plan for understanding how first-year students choose electives: objectives, research questions, method rationale, screener, recruitment plan and consent form.

phases.title: Talking to users

steps.what: Interview guides, open and non-leading questions, probing and laddering, active listening, note-taking, remote interviewing, avoiding bias
Task scenarios, moderated and unmoderated tests, think-aloud protocol, success rate, time-on-task, SUS, severity ratings

phases.build: Eight recorded interviews on elective selection plus a 5-user usability test of your college's course registration portal, with transcripts, task metrics and a severity-ranked issue log.

phases.title: Making sense of data

steps.what: Coding transcripts, affinity mapping, thematic analysis, insight statements, personas and JTBD from evidence, prioritising findings
Current-state journey maps, stages, actions, thoughts and emotions, touchpoints, pain points and opportunity areas

phases.build: A synthesis report from your interviews: coded themes, five evidence-backed insights, two personas and an end-to-end journey map of elective selection with prioritised opportunities.

phases.title: Quant methods and influence

steps.what: Question types, Likert scales, avoiding leading and double-barrelled questions, sampling, piloting, response rates, survey logic
Descriptive statistics, confidence intervals, t-tests and chi-square, sample size, A/B test basics, triangulating quant with qual
Cleaning survey data, pivot tables, cross-tabs, basic charts, analysing open-text responses, intro to Python pandas
Research readouts, executive summaries, storytelling with clips and quotes, recommendations tied to decisions, managing pushback

phases.build: A mixed-methods study: a 100+ response survey sizing the problems found in interviews, statistical analysis in Sheets, and a 15-minute readout deck with video clips presented to your department.

design-systems-designer.summary: Get solid in UI fundamentals and Figma, build component libraries with variables and tokens, learn governance and versioning, then connect to code, accessibility and adoption across teams.

phases.title: UI and Figma foundations

steps.what: Type scales, spacing systems, grids, colour and contrast, visual consistency, auditing an interface for inconsistencies
Frames, auto layout, constraints, styles, team libraries, plugins, organising files and pages for many contributors

phases.build: An interface inventory of a real product (e.g. your college ERP): screenshots of every button, input and colour in use, grouped to show inconsistencies, with a proposal for consolidation.

phases.title: Components and variables

steps.what: Atomic design, component architecture, variants and properties, instance swap and slots, nested auto layout, naming conventions, base vs. composite components
Variable collections, modes for light/dark and density, aliasing primitives to semantics, scoping, binding variables to component properties

phases.build: A Figma library of 30+ components (buttons, inputs, selects, tabs, modals, tables) wired to variables, switching between light/dark and compact/comfortable modes without detaching anything.

phases.title: Tokens and governance

steps.what: Token taxonomy (primitive, semantic, component), W3C DTCG format, Style Dictionary transforms to CSS/iOS/Android, syncing tokens to GitHub
Semantic versioning, changelogs, contribution and request process, deprecation policy, Figma branching and library publishing, RFCs

phases.build: A token pipeline: tokens exported from Tokens Studio to a GitHub repo, transformed by Style Dictionary into CSS variables, with a versioned v1.0 to v1.1 release, changelog and contribution guide.

phases.title: Code and accessibility

steps.what: Semantic HTML, box model, flexbox and grid, CSS custom properties, component states in CSS, basic React component props
WCAG 2.2 AA, contrast tokens, focus states, keyboard patterns from WAI-ARIA APG, accessible names, touch targets
Writing stories, args and controls, docs pages, accessibility addon, visual regression basics, linking Storybook to Figma

phases.build: Ten of your library's components coded in HTML/CSS (or React) consuming the generated tokens, published in Storybook with accessibility checks passing and docs linking each story to its Figma component.

phases.title: Documentation and adoption

steps.what: Usage guidelines, do/don't examples, anatomy diagrams, content guidelines, writing for designers and developers, docs site structure
Office hours, adoption metrics, gathering requests from product teams, running a design-system council, negotiating one-off vs. system components

phases.build: A public docs site for your system with guidelines for every component, plus an adoption pilot where two student project teams use it, with their feedback logged as tracked requests.

interaction-designer.summary: Learn visual basics, Figma and core design principles, then model flows and behaviour, prototype motion and micro-interactions, and validate them with users and a little front-end code.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Gestalt principles, hierarchy, contrast, spacing, type and colour basics needed to make interactive screens readable
Frames, auto layout, components and variants, interactive components, styles and variables, FigJam for flows
Norman's affordances, signifiers, mapping, feedback, constraints; Fitts's and Hick's laws; Nielsen heuristics; consistency and error prevention

phases.build: An interaction teardown of three apps (e.g. Google Pay, Instagram, Swiggy): annotated Figma frames mapping each key interaction to the principles it uses or violates.

phases.title: Flows and behaviour

steps.what: Task and user flows, decision points, happy and edge paths, system states, mapping flows to screens
State machines for UI, feedback and system status, input modalities, gestures, form behaviour, undo and error recovery, Material and HIG interaction patterns

phases.build: A behaviour spec for a UPI payment flow: user flow with failure paths (timeout, wrong PIN, bank down), a state diagram for each screen, and annotated designs for every state.

phases.title: Prototyping and motion

steps.what: Smart animate, interactive components, variables and conditionals, multi-step stateful prototypes, sensor and gesture prototypes in ProtoPie
Triggers, rules, feedback, loops and modes; easing curves, duration, choreography, spatial continuity; motion specs for engineers

phases.build: A high-fidelity ProtoPie prototype of the UPI flow with gesture input, animated success/failure feedback and a motion spec sheet (durations, easings, choreography) engineers could implement.

phases.title: Validate and implement

steps.what: Task scenarios, think-aloud, observing hesitation and mis-taps, measuring task success and errors, iterating interactions from findings
HTML/CSS layout, CSS transitions and keyframes, JavaScript events and DOM updates, intro to Framer Motion in React

phases.build: A usability-tested and coded interaction: run tests with 5 users on the prototype, fix the top issues, then implement the payment-confirmation micro-interaction in HTML/CSS/JS and publish it on CodePen.

service-designer.summary: Learn design thinking and systems thinking, research real users to build journey maps, blueprint and prototype whole services, then facilitate workshops and connect the work to business strategy.

phases.title: Seeing the whole system

steps.what: Human-centred design, double diamond, divergent and convergent thinking, problem reframing, how-might-we statements
Stocks and flows, feedback loops, causal loop diagrams, leverage points (Meadows), ecosystem and actor mapping, unintended consequences

phases.build: An ecosystem and causal-loop map of a public service you have used (e.g. getting a passport or a scholarship disbursement), identifying actors, feedback loops and three leverage points.

phases.title: Research and journeys

steps.what: Contextual inquiry, shadowing, interviews with users and frontline staff, field notes, diary studies, affinity mapping
Current- and future-state journeys across channels, stages, actions, emotions, touchpoints, moments of truth, pain-point evidence

phases.build: A cross-channel journey map of a hospital OPD visit (booking, queue, consultation, pharmacy, follow-up) built from interviews with 6 patients and 2 staff, with evidence-backed pain points.

phases.title: Blueprinting and prototyping

steps.what: Frontstage and backstage actions, lines of interaction, visibility and internal interaction, support processes, physical evidence, fail points and wait times
Service prototyping: desktop walkthroughs, role-play, Wizard of Oz, paper props, low-cost pilots, measuring a pilot

phases.build: Current- and future-state service blueprints for the OPD visit, plus a role-played prototype of the redesigned check-in tested with 5 people, with measured wait-time and confusion points.

phases.title: Co-creation and business case

steps.what: Agenda design, warm-ups, divergent/convergent activities, managing group dynamics, remote facilitation, capturing outputs
Stakeholder mapping, co-design sessions, aligning departments with conflicting goals, prioritisation exercises, turning workshop output into decisions
Business model canvas, value proposition canvas, cost-to-serve, service KPIs, building a business case for a service change

phases.build: A co-design workshop you plan and run with 8+ participants (students, staff, administrators) for a campus service, ending in a prioritised roadmap and a one-page business case with KPIs.

content-designer.summary: Sharpen writing fundamentals and editing, learn to write interface copy with a consistent voice in Figma, then build content strategy and IA, and validate words with research, localisation and SEO.

phases.title: Writing foundations

steps.what: Grammar and punctuation, plain language, active voice, sentence length, reading level, writing for scanning
Self-editing and line editing, cutting word count, headlines and microcopy, persuasive vs. instructional copy, style guides (Mailchimp, GOV.UK)

phases.build: A before/after rewrite portfolio of 20 real pieces of confusing copy (college notices, bank SMS alerts, app error messages), each with word count, reading level and the editing principle applied.

phases.title: Words in the interface

steps.what: Buttons and labels, error messages, empty states, onboarding, confirmation dialogs, notifications, form hints, writing to content-first wireframes
Defining voice attributes, tone shifts by context (error, success, legal), voice charts, consistency audits
Working in design files, editing text layers, components, commenting, content variants, copy-review plugins

phases.build: A full copy pass in Figma on an existing app flow (e.g. a UPI app's failed-payment journey): every string rewritten, a voice-and-tone chart, and a string table ready for engineering.

phases.title: Content strategy and structure

steps.what: Content audits, content models, governance and ownership, style guides, terminology lists, content lifecycle, measuring content performance
Card sorting, tree testing, navigation labels, taxonomy, sitemaps, help-centre structure, findability

phases.build: A content audit and strategy for your college's website or a student club's help pages: inventory spreadsheet, content model, terminology list, new sitemap validated by a 10-person tree test.

phases.title: Evidence and reach

steps.what: Comprehension testing, cloze tests, highlighter tests, A/B testing copy, interview basics, reading analytics for drop-off
Writing for translation, string length expansion, avoiding idioms, Hindi and regional-language considerations, ICU message format basics
Search intent, keyword research, titles and meta descriptions, headings structure, help-article SEO, Search Console basics

phases.build: An evidence-backed content case study: comprehension tests on your rewritten flow with 8 users, a localisation-ready string table with Hindi adaptations, and two SEO-optimised help articles.

design-manager.summary: Build a product-design craft base first, then learn people management, mentoring and critique, and finish with the strategy, roadmapping, stakeholder and hiring skills that design managers lean on.

phases.title: Design craft base

steps.what: Design process, user flows, wireframing, visual hierarchy, usability heuristics, presenting design rationale
Auto layout, components, libraries, prototyping, commenting and review workflows, organising team files

phases.build: A product-design case study for a campus problem (flows, wireframes, hi-fi prototype) that demonstrates enough craft to credibly review other designers' work.

phases.title: Leading people

steps.what: Running 1:1s, SBI feedback, goal setting, delegation, psychological safety, handling conflict and low performance, team rituals
GROW coaching model, design career ladders and competency matrices, growth plans, giving portfolio feedback, sponsorship vs. mentorship

phases.build: A six-week mentorship programme for 4 juniors in your college design club: 1:1 notes, individual growth plans against a competency matrix, and a retrospective showing each mentee's progress.

phases.title: Leading design quality

steps.what: Setting a quality bar, team design principles, review cadences, balancing craft with deadlines, design ops basics, communicating a team vision
Critique formats, separating feedback from preference, framing goals before feedback, facilitating group crits, documenting decisions

phases.build: A critique system for a student design team: written team design principles, a weekly crit format you facilitate for a month, and logged decisions showing how designs changed as a result.

phases.title: Business partnership

steps.what: Vision and strategy, market and competitor analysis, north-star metrics, jobs-to-be-done, how design bets connect to business outcomes
Outcome-based roadmaps, now/next/later, sequencing design work against engineering, capacity planning for a design team
Stakeholder mapping, aligning PM/engineering/design, negotiating scope, status updates, saying no with alternatives
Writing design job descriptions, portfolio review rubrics, structured interviews, design exercises, reducing bias, closing candidates

phases.build: A design-team operating plan for a real student product (e.g. a fest app): strategy one-pager, quarterly design roadmap, stakeholder map, and a hiring rubric you use to recruit two designers.

motion-designer.summary: Learn storyboarding and animation principles, master After Effects and visual design, build motion-design craft, then learn product motion handoff with Lottie before adding 3D and video editing.

phases.title: Animation foundations

steps.what: Thumbnails, shot framing, sequencing, animatics, timing notes, translating a brief into a storyboard
Disney's 12 principles, timing and spacing, easing, anticipation, follow-through, arcs, squash and stretch, bouncing-ball and pendulum drills

phases.build: A principles reel: 12 short loops, each demonstrating one of Disney's principles (bouncing ball, pendulum, character jump), with storyboard frames shown beside each.

phases.title: After Effects and visual craft

steps.what: Keyframes, graph editor, shape layers, masks and track mattes, precomps, parenting and nulls, expressions (wiggle, loopOut), render queue
Composition, typography, colour and contrast for motion, styleframes, consistent visual language across a sequence

phases.build: A 20-second animated logo reveal for a college fest or club, built from your own styleframes in After Effects using shape layers, mattes and graph-editor easing.

phases.title: Motion design craft

steps.what: Kinetic typography, transitions, explainer pacing, sound sync, brief to styleframes to animatic to final, UI motion vs. brand motion
Frames, components, auto layout, preparing layered files for After Effects import, smart animate basics

phases.build: A 45-60 second explainer for a real product feature (e.g. how UPI AutoPay works), from script and storyboard through styleframes and animatic to a sound-synced final render.

phases.title: Product motion and handoff

steps.what: Smart animate, interactive components, ProtoPie interactions, motion specs with durations and easing curves, motion tokens
Bodymovin export, LottieFiles and dotLottie, supported vs. unsupported AE features, file-size optimisation, MP4/WebM/GIF export, Rive basics

phases.build: A set of five product micro-animations (loader, success tick, pull-to-refresh, empty state, onboarding) shipped as optimised Lottie files under 50 KB each, embedded in a working demo web page.

phases.title: Extending the toolkit

steps.what: Modelling basics, materials, lighting, cameras, keyframe animation, rendering with Eevee/Cycles, compositing 3D renders in AE
Cutting to music, pacing, colour correction, audio mixing, exporting for Instagram, YouTube and product pages

phases.build: A 60-90 second motion showreel combining your 2D, UI and 3D work, edited to music with colour-matched cuts, published on Behance and Vimeo.

visual-designer.summary: Start with sketching and visual design, master typography and layout, get fluent in colour, Figma and Adobe tools, and finish with brand identity, illustration and production work.

phases.title: Seeing and sketching

steps.what: Thumbnail sketches, quick idea generation, basic perspective and form, sketching layouts before going digital
Gestalt principles, hierarchy, contrast, balance, rhythm, scale, use of imagery, critique vocabulary, studying design history movements

phases.build: A visual study journal: 30 analysed designs (posters, apps, packaging) annotated for hierarchy and balance, plus 10 of your own poster thumbnails exploring the same principles.

phases.title: Typography and layout

steps.what: Type anatomy and classification, pairing, type scales, kerning and tracking, leading and measure, Devanagari and Latin pairing, expressive type
Modular and Swiss grids, whitespace, alignment, focal points, editorial layout, multi-format adaptation from poster to social to web

phases.build: A typographic poster series of 3 posters for a college event plus an 8-page editorial magazine spread, all on a documented grid, with bilingual (English/Hindi) typesetting on at least one piece.

phases.title: Colour and tools

steps.what: Colour wheel and harmonies, value and saturation, colour psychology and cultural meaning, palettes for brand and UI, RGB vs. CMYK, accessible contrast
Frames, auto layout, components, styles, plugins, building social and web templates, sharing for review
Photoshop compositing and retouching, Illustrator vector work and pen tool, InDesign multi-page documents, linked assets and libraries

phases.build: A campaign key visual for a real student product or startup: hero image composited in Photoshop, vector assets in Illustrator, and a Figma template set adapting it to 6 social and web formats.

phases.title: Brand and production

steps.what: Brand strategy basics, logo design, visual identity systems, brand guidelines, applying identity across touchpoints
Vector illustration, spot and hero illustrations, consistent illustration style, brushes and texture
Bleed, trim and safe zones, CMYK and spot colours, resolution, preflight, export presets for print, web and social

phases.build: A complete identity for a local business or campus club: logo, colour and type system, custom illustration set, 20-page brand guidelines, and print-ready files actually produced (cards, banners).

ux-engineer.summary: Master HTML/CSS and JavaScript, learn UI and interaction design in Figma, build in React with code prototypes, then specialise in design systems and accessibility with TypeScript and tooling.

phases.title: Web foundations

steps.what: Commits, branches, merges, pull requests, resolving conflicts, GitHub Pages deploys
Semantic HTML, box model, flexbox and grid, responsive design and media queries, custom properties, transitions and keyframes, cascade and specificity
ES6+ syntax, DOM manipulation, events, closures, promises and async/await, fetch API, modules, array methods

phases.build: A responsive, framework-free web page that recreates a complex real UI (e.g. a Razorpay checkout) with working tabs, form validation and transitions, deployed on GitHub Pages.

phases.title: Design craft

steps.what: Visual hierarchy, type scales, spacing, colour, component states, feedback and affordances, motion principles, Material and HIG patterns
Auto layout, components and variants, variables, Dev Mode, inspecting specs, exporting assets, reading designers' files

phases.build: A small Figma design of a settings or onboarding flow you design yourself, with all states (hover, focus, error, loading) specified, ready to be built in code in the next phase.

phases.title: React and code prototyping

steps.what: Components, props, state and hooks, effects, controlled forms, composition patterns, context, rendering lists, React Router basics
High-fidelity code prototypes, animation with Framer Motion, faking data, rapid iteration, deciding when to prototype in code vs. Figma

phases.build: Your Figma flow built as a live React prototype with Framer Motion transitions and mocked data, deployed on Vercel, with a write-up comparing the coded result to the design.

phases.title: Design systems and accessibility

steps.what: Tokens as CSS variables, component APIs, variants, composition, theming, documentation, syncing Figma components with code
WCAG 2.2 AA, semantic markup, ARIA roles and WAI-ARIA APG patterns, keyboard navigation, focus management, screen-reader testing

phases.build: A themeable React component library of 12 components (button, input, select, modal, tabs, toast) driven by tokens, keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible, documented in Storybook.

phases.title: Production tooling

steps.what: Types and interfaces, generics, typing props and hooks, discriminated unions for component variants, strict mode
Vite builds, npm packages, ESLint and Prettier, unit tests with Vitest and Testing Library, visual regression, CI with GitHub Actions

phases.build: Your component library migrated to TypeScript and published as an npm package, with typed props, linting, unit tests, Chromatic visual regression and a CI pipeline on every pull request.

design-lead.summary: Build strong product-design craft in Figma with research and prototyping, then practise leading design across teams, setting strategy and mentoring others from a student-team context.

phases.title: Craft foundations

steps.what: Gestalt principles, hierarchy, typography and colour basics, Nielsen's heuristics, the double-diamond process
Auto layout, components and variants, variables, libraries, prototyping, FigJam, Dev Mode handoff

phases.build: A Figma rebuild of a complex real product area (e.g. a stock-trading app's order screen) with componentised, auto-layouted screens and annotated design decisions.

phases.title: End-to-end product design

steps.what: Problem framing, success metrics, user flows, wireframes, hi-fi UI, edge and error states, designing within technical constraints, shipping and measuring
Interviews, contextual inquiry, usability testing, affinity mapping, insight statements, triangulating with analytics
Interactive prototypes, variables and conditionals, choosing fidelity for the question, prototypes for stakeholder buy-in

phases.build: A shipped-quality case study for a real student-facing product: research with 8 users, flows, hi-fi prototype, two test rounds, and measured outcomes after a teammate builds and launches it.

phases.title: Leading across teams

steps.what: Working rituals with PMs and engineers, design reviews, writing design specs, negotiating scope, handling disagreement, shared success metrics
Setting design principles and a quality bar, running crits, aligning teams on a vision, making and explaining hard trade-offs, leading without authority

phases.build: Lead design for a hackathon or club project with 2+ designers and 3+ engineers: written design principles, a weekly crit you run, a spec engineers built from, and a retro on what you would change.

phases.title: Direction and mentoring

steps.what: North-star visions, connecting design bets to business goals, competitive analysis, opportunity sizing, multi-quarter design roadmaps
Portfolio and craft feedback, pairing on design problems, growth plans, coaching questions, creating learning resources for juniors
Mapping product ecosystems, feedback loops, second-order effects of design decisions, designing coherent experiences across surfaces

phases.build: A north-star vision deck for a multi-surface product (app, web, notifications) with a system map of how surfaces connect, plus a documented mentorship of two junior designers through their first case studies.

design-director.summary: Ground yourself in product-design craft and Figma, then learn design leadership and people management, design and product strategy, and the executive communication and team-building skills directors rely on.

phases.title: Craft base

steps.what: Design process, user research basics, flows, wireframes, visual hierarchy, usability heuristics, presenting rationale
Auto layout, components, libraries, prototyping, commenting and review workflows

phases.build: An end-to-end product-design case study for a real campus or community problem, strong enough to show you understand the craft you will later lead others in.

phases.title: Leading designers

steps.what: Setting quality bars and design principles, running reviews and crits, balancing craft with delivery, communicating a design vision to a team
1:1s, SBI feedback, goal setting, delegation, career ladders, psychological safety, managing conflict and performance

phases.build: Run a semester-long student design team (5+ members) as its lead: documented design principles, 1:1 notes, individual growth goals, and a retro with outcomes for each member.

phases.title: Strategy and vision

steps.what: Linking design to business goals, design maturity models, opportunity mapping, multi-quarter design roadmaps, measuring design impact
Market and competitor analysis, positioning, north-star metrics, jobs-to-be-done, bets and trade-offs across a product line
North-star vision prototypes, vision storytelling, managing a portfolio of design initiatives, balancing short-term fixes with long bets

phases.build: A design strategy for a real Indian product line (e.g. an edtech or fintech app family): competitive analysis, maturity assessment, a north-star vision prototype, and a prioritised portfolio of initiatives.

phases.title: Executive influence and organisation

steps.what: Pyramid principle, one-page memos, exec-ready decks, framing design in revenue and risk terms, concise updates, handling tough questions
Team structures (centralised, embedded, hybrid), role definitions, hiring plans, onboarding, team culture and rituals
DesignOps basics, tooling and file standards, research ops, critique and review cadences, measuring team throughput and quality

phases.build: A design-org proposal pitched to a real audience (club faculty advisor or startup founder): exec memo and 10-slide deck covering team structure, hiring plan, ops standards and expected impact.

eng-fellow.summary: Build deep engineering and research foundations, learn to reproduce and extend published work, then practise the writing, architecture and public influence that research-track internships look for.

phases.title: Engineering foundations

steps.what: Idiomatic Python, typing, packaging, virtual environments, unit testing with pytest, NumPy arrays and vectorised computation
Asymptotic analysis, hashing, trees, heaps, graphs, dynamic programming, amortised analysis and proving correctness of algorithms
Branching, rebasing, pull requests, code review etiquette, semantic versioning and contributing to an open-source repository

phases.build: A tested, documented Python graph-algorithms package on PyPI with CI, plus a benchmark notebook comparing measured runtimes to the theoretical complexity of each algorithm.

phases.title: Research craft

steps.what: Reading papers critically, forming hypotheses, experiment design, baselines and ablations, statistical significance, reproducing published results
Paper structure, related-work surveys, LaTeX writing, figures, peer review process, prior-art search and how patent claims are drafted

phases.build: Reproduce the key result of a recent systems or ML paper, extend it with one new ablation, and write it up as a 6-page LaTeX workshop-style paper with released code.

phases.title: Architecture and long-range thinking

steps.what: Distributed-systems basics: replication, partitioning, consistency models, caching, queues, failure modes, and writing design docs with trade-off tables
Writing RFCs, framing multi-year technical bets, evaluating emerging technology, technology radars and arguing for a direction with evidence
How tech strategy is set: build-vs-buy, platform bets, deprecation plans, technical debt portfolios and case studies from well-known engineering orgs

phases.build: An RFC proposing a new architecture for a real open-source project's bottleneck, backed by a working prototype and benchmarks, submitted to the project for discussion.

phases.title: Influence and communication

steps.what: Technical blogging, giving talks, open-source maintainership, building a public body of work and engaging constructively with a research community
One-page memos, executive summaries, translating technical risk into business impact and answering decision-maker questions concisely

phases.build: A three-part technical blog series on your research reproduction, a 20-minute talk delivered at a college or city tech meetup, and a one-page memo summarising its business implications.

head-of-platform.summary: Start with Linux, scripting and networking, build real CI/CD and cloud infrastructure, add SRE practice and platform-as-product thinking, then lead a small team running it.

phases.title: Systems foundations

steps.what: Shell, file permissions, processes, systemd, package management, logs, SSH and Bash scripting for automation
Scripting, CLI tools with argparse/Typer, calling REST APIs, file and JSON handling, and testing small automation scripts
TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, TLS, load balancers, subnets and CIDR, firewalls, and debugging with curl, dig and tcpdump
Branching strategies, pull requests, trunk-based development, tags and release workflows

phases.build: A Python CLI that provisions a fresh Ubuntu VM into a ready developer machine (users, SSH keys, toolchain, dotfiles) idempotently, with tests and a README.

phases.title: Infrastructure and developer experience

steps.what: Docker images, CI/CD pipelines, build caching, Terraform modules, dev containers, golden-path service templates and measuring developer friction
AWS VPC, IAM, EC2, S3, RDS, load balancing, autoscaling, Kubernetes basics (pods, deployments, services) and the Well-Architected pillars

phases.build: A golden-path template: one command scaffolds a containerised service with CI tests, Terraform-provisioned AWS infra and a Helm deploy to a Kubernetes cluster, documented end to end.

phases.title: Reliability and platform as a product

steps.what: SLIs, SLOs and error budgets, metrics and logs, alerting on symptoms, load testing, incident response and blameless postmortems
Platform-as-a-product, paved roads vs guardrails, internal developer portals, DORA metrics, adoption measurement and deciding what to centralise

phases.build: A Backstage developer portal cataloguing your services, with SLO dashboards in Grafana, DORA metrics computed from GitHub data, and a written postmortem of a simulated outage.

phases.title: Leading and enabling teams

steps.what: Running standups and planning, delegating ownership, code-review culture, giving feedback, 1:1s and keeping a small team unblocked
Writing onboarding guides and runbooks, internal workshops, office hours, migration playbooks and collecting feedback from platform users
Now-next-later roadmaps, RICE prioritisation, balancing reliability work against feature requests and communicating trade-offs
Cloud cost breakdowns, FinOps basics, rightsizing, reserved vs spot capacity, and comparing managed services against self-hosting

phases.build: Lead a 3-4 person college team adopting your platform for their project: publish onboarding docs, a quarterly platform roadmap and a cost report showing a measured cloud-spend reduction.

head-of-eng.summary: Become a strong builder first, then learn to ship reliably with a team, lead and grow people, and connect engineering work to roadmaps, OKRs and budgets.

phases.title: Builder foundations

steps.what: Modern JavaScript and TypeScript, async/await, modules, Node.js APIs, and testing with Jest or Vitest
Arrays, hash maps, trees, graphs, sorting, recursion, complexity analysis and common interview patterns
REST API design, relational schemas, authentication, a React frontend, deployment and basic observability
Feature branches, pull requests, code review, merge conflicts, tags and release notes

phases.build: A deployed full-stack app (for example a college club event and ticketing system) with auth, PostgreSQL, tests and CI, used by real students.

phases.title: Shipping with a team

steps.what: Breaking work into tickets, estimation, sprint planning, CI/CD and release trains, tracking cycle time, retrospectives and cutting scope to hit dates
Architecture decision records, build vs buy, managing technical debt, choosing a stack and writing a lightweight design doc

phases.build: Ship a multi-person project over four two-week sprints with a public board, ADRs for key decisions, a release changelog and retro notes showing measured improvement in cycle time.

phases.title: Leading and growing people

steps.what: Mentoring, code-review standards, running 1:1s, giving feedback, psychological safety, and making technical calls under uncertainty
Team roles and topologies, onboarding docs, engineering rituals, splitting teams as they grow and defining an engineering ladder
Writing job descriptions, structured interviews, work-sample tasks, scoring rubrics, reducing bias and running debriefs

phases.build: Lead a 5-8 person college tech club or open-source team for a semester: design its onboarding guide, recruit members with a written rubric, and publish a team handbook.

phases.title: Business alignment

steps.what: Mapping stakeholders, status updates, managing expectations, negotiating scope and saying no with alternatives
Writing objectives and measurable key results, quarterly planning, roadmap formats and grading OKRs at quarter end
Headcount and tooling costs, cloud spend forecasting, and making a business case for an engineering investment

phases.build: A quarterly engineering plan for your club or startup idea: OKRs with metrics, a roadmap, a headcount and tooling budget, and a stakeholder update deck reviewed by a faculty mentor.

tpm.summary: Build enough technical depth to talk credibly with engineers, learn agile delivery and program mechanics, then practise coordinating multi-team work with risks, roadmaps and metrics.

phases.title: Technical grounding

steps.what: Variables, functions, data structures, reading and modifying existing code, calling REST APIs and simple automation scripts
SELECT, joins, GROUP BY, window functions and answering delivery or product questions directly from a database
SDLC, client-server and APIs, databases, cloud basics, microservices, CI/CD, system design trade-offs and reading architecture diagrams

phases.build: A small REST API with a database, deployed to the cloud, plus a one-page architecture doc that explains its components, failure points and the trade-offs you chose.

phases.title: Agile delivery and program mechanics

steps.what: Scrum roles and events, backlog refinement, user stories and acceptance criteria, Kanban flow, WIP limits and running retrospectives
Scope and charters, work breakdown structures, milestones, critical path, RACI, status reporting and change control

phases.build: Run a college hackathon or fest tech track as a program: charter, WBS, milestone plan, RACI and weekly status reports, with a post-event retrospective.

phases.title: Coordinating across teams

steps.what: Running syncs with clear agendas, decision logs, interface agreements between teams, escalation paths and unblocking without authority
RAID logs, dependency mapping, probability-impact scoring, mitigation plans and early-warning signals for slipping work
Quarterly planning, capacity estimates, sequencing work across teams, roadmap formats and replanning when scope changes

phases.build: Coordinate a cross-team open-source or college project with 3+ sub-teams: publish the dependency map, RAID log and quarterly roadmap, and show how one flagged risk was mitigated.

phases.title: Communication and metrics

steps.what: Executive status updates, red-amber-green reporting, launch announcements, writing for different audiences and presenting trade-offs
Velocity, burndown, cycle and lead time, DORA metrics, defining program KPIs and building delivery dashboards

phases.build: A live delivery dashboard pulling Jira or GitHub data into Looker Studio (cycle time, burndown, open risks), plus a monthly stakeholder update written from it.

chief-architect.summary: Master programming and data fundamentals, go deep on system design and cloud architecture, then learn enterprise architecture frameworks, governance and how to align many teams behind one design.

phases.title: Software foundations

steps.what: OOP, collections, generics, exceptions, concurrency basics, build tools and unit testing; Spring Boot for a first REST service
Complexity analysis, hashing, trees, graphs, sorting and searching, and choosing structures for performance
Relational modelling, normalisation, indexes, transactions and isolation levels, query plans
Branching, pull requests, code review and monorepo vs polyrepo conventions

phases.build: A Spring Boot REST service with a normalised PostgreSQL schema, indexed queries justified by EXPLAIN plans, integration tests and CI.

phases.title: System design at scale

steps.what: Load balancing, caching, sharding, replication, message queues, CAP and consistency models, rate limiting, capacity estimation
AWS core services, microservices vs modular monolith, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, multi-region and the Well-Architected framework

phases.build: A URL-shortener or ticket-booking system split into services with Redis caching and Kafka events, deployed via Terraform to Kubernetes, with a load-test report and capacity estimate.

phases.title: Enterprise architecture and governance

steps.what: TOGAF ADM basics, business capability maps, C4 model, ArchiMate views, integration patterns and current-to-target state roadmaps
Architecture decision records, technology radars, architecture review boards, API and security standards, and fitness functions

phases.build: An enterprise architecture pack for a fictional mid-size bank or e-commerce firm: capability map, C4 diagrams, target-state roadmap, a tech radar and five ADRs.

phases.title: Vision and alignment

steps.what: Writing a multi-year technical vision, evaluating emerging technology, migration and modernisation strategies, and quantifying trade-offs
Running architecture forums, RFC review processes, reconciling conflicting team designs and building consensus on shared standards
Explaining architecture in business terms, cost and risk framing, concise decision memos and presenting to non-technical leaders
Reviewing designs constructively, teaching trade-off thinking, pairing on design docs and running design-review sessions

phases.build: A modernisation proposal moving a legacy monolith to a target architecture: vision doc, phased migration plan, cost-risk analysis and a 10-slide executive deck presented to a faculty panel.

embedded-eng.summary: Learn C and the electronics underneath, program ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers on real boards, master serial protocols and lab instruments, then move to RTOS-based firmware and modern tooling.

phases.title: C and electronics foundations

steps.what: Pointers, arrays, structs, memory layout, bitwise operations, volatile and const, the build process, linker basics and debugging with GDB
Ohm's law, logic levels, pull-up/pull-down resistors, GPIO, ADC/DAC, PWM, reading schematics and basic soldering
Version control for firmware projects, branching, tags for releases and .gitignore for build artifacts

phases.build: A C library of fixed-size ring buffers, CRC and bit-manipulation utilities with unit tests running on the host, plus a breadboard LED/button circuit documented with a KiCad schematic.

phases.title: Microcontroller programming

steps.what: GPIO, clocks, timers, interrupts and the NVIC, DMA, startup code, memory map and register-level vs HAL programming
Reading datasheets and reference manuals, pin muxing, power-up sequences, clock trees and bringing up a new board peripheral by peripheral

phases.build: An STM32 board running an interrupt-driven stopwatch with timer-based PWM display dimming and debounced buttons, written against registers with a bring-up checklist in the README.

phases.title: Peripherals and lab debugging

steps.what: Framing, clocking and addressing, baud rates, clock polarity and phase, ACK/NACK, writing interrupt and DMA-driven drivers for real sensors
Triggering, timebase, probing safely, decoding I2C/SPI/UART traffic, measuring timing and jitter, and finding signal-integrity issues

phases.build: A battery-powered environmental sensor node reading I2C and SPI sensors and streaming over UART, with logic-analyzer captures proving correct bus timing in the documentation.

phases.title: RTOS-based firmware

steps.what: Tasks, schedulers and priorities, queues, semaphores and mutexes, priority inversion, stack sizing, timing analysis and watchdogs
Classes, RAII, references, templates, constexpr, and embedded C++ constraints: no exceptions, no heap, static allocation

phases.build: A FreeRTOS data logger with separate sensor, storage (SD card over SPI) and comms tasks, a watchdog, and a measured worst-case task latency report.

phases.title: Tooling and modern languages

steps.what: pyserial host tools, automated hardware-in-the-loop tests, log parsing and plotting sensor data
Ownership and borrowing, no_std, embedded-hal traits, peripheral access crates, RTIC and flashing with probe-rs

phases.build: A Python hardware-in-the-loop test rig that flashes your logger, drives inputs and checks outputs over UART, plus a port of one driver to Rust with embedded-hal.

firmware-eng.summary: Learn C and computer architecture, write bare-metal code against registers, build your own drivers and bootloader, then add safe OTA updates, low-power design and debugging depth.

phases.title: C and hardware foundations

steps.what: Pointers, structs and unions, memory layout, bitwise operations, volatile, fixed-width types, the compile-link process and undefined behaviour
CPU pipeline, memory hierarchy, memory-mapped I/O, interrupts, flash vs RAM, digital logic and reading schematics
Branching, tagging firmware releases, and reproducible builds

phases.build: A host-tested C module set (ring buffer, CRC32, fixed-point math) with unit tests and a static-analysis-clean build in CI.

phases.title: Bare-metal programming

steps.what: Bit masks and shifts, read-modify-write, set/clear registers, bit-banding, and safe access to peripheral registers
Startup code, vector table, linker scripts, clock configuration, SysTick, interrupts and building firmware with no vendor HAL
Debug probes, breakpoints and watchpoints, inspecting registers and memory, HardFault analysis and semihosting

phases.build: A from-scratch bare-metal STM32 project (own linker script and startup file, no HAL) that blinks, reads a button via interrupt and prints over UART, with a HardFault handler that dumps registers.

phases.title: Drivers and bootloaders

steps.what: Driver layering, interrupt and DMA-driven UART/SPI/I2C drivers, flash programming, vector table relocation and jumping to an application image
ARM Thumb-2 instructions, calling conventions, stack frames, reading compiler output and writing startup routines in assembly

phases.build: A custom UART bootloader that receives a new application image, verifies its CRC, writes it to flash and jumps to it, plus a reusable interrupt-driven SPI flash driver.

phases.title: Field-ready firmware

steps.what: A/B partitions, image headers and versioning, signing and verification, rollback on failed boot, and secure update flows
Sleep and stop modes, clock gating, wake-up sources, peripheral power-down and measuring current to estimate battery life
Ownership, no_std, peripheral access crates, embedded-hal drivers and flashing with probe-rs

phases.build: A coin-cell BLE sensor on nRF52 or ESP32 with signed A/B OTA updates and automatic rollback, plus a measured current profile proving a target battery life above one year.

robotics-eng.summary: Get fluent in Python, C++, Linux and the math, learn ROS 2 in simulation, then build up kinematics, motion planning and control, and finally perception with sensor fusion and SLAM.

phases.title: Programming and math foundations

steps.what: Shell, processes, file system, package management, environment variables and building code with CMake
Vectors, matrices, rotations, eigenvalues, derivatives and Jacobians, and basic probability for robotics
Functions, classes, NumPy, Matplotlib, writing small simulations and scripts to analyse sensor logs
Modern C++17: classes, RAII, smart pointers, STL containers, templates, lambdas, and Eigen for linear algebra

phases.build: A 2D differential-drive robot simulator in Python with keyboard control and plotted trajectories, re-implemented in C++ with Eigen and benchmarked against the Python version.

phases.title: ROS 2 and simulation

steps.what: Nodes, topics, services, actions, launch files, parameters, TF2 transforms, URDF, rosbag recording and RViz visualisation
Spawning robots from URDF, simulated sensors (lidar, camera, IMU), world files, and bridging simulation to ROS 2

phases.build: A ROS 2 package for a simulated TurtleBot-style robot in Gazebo with teleop, a lidar-based obstacle-stop node and recorded rosbags visualised in RViz.

phases.title: Kinematics, planning and control

steps.what: Homogeneous transforms, DH parameters, forward and inverse kinematics, Jacobians, and rigid-body dynamics basics
A*, RRT and PRM planners, trajectory generation, PID control, pure pursuit, MPC basics and the ROS 2 Nav2 stack

phases.build: A 6-DOF arm in simulation doing pick-and-place with MoveIt 2 and your own IK solver, plus a mobile robot following an A*-planned path with a tuned pure-pursuit controller.

phases.title: Perception and localisation

steps.what: Kalman and extended Kalman filters, IMU and wheel-odometry fusion, sensor noise models and time synchronisation
Occupancy grids, scan matching, particle filters, graph-based SLAM, loop closure and map evaluation
Camera models and calibration, feature detection, ArUco markers, depth images and object detection for robot perception

phases.build: An autonomous navigation demo: a robot (simulated or a low-cost real one) builds a SLAM map, localises with an EKF fusing IMU and odometry, and drives to ArUco-marked goals.

controls-eng.summary: Build the math and signals background, learn MATLAB/Simulink modelling and classical plus state-space control, then implement controllers in real-time C/C++ on real motors.

phases.title: Math and modelling tools

steps.what: ODEs, Laplace transforms, matrices, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and linearisation around an operating point
Transfer functions, impulse and step response, frequency response, Bode plots, sampling and the z-transform
MATLAB scripting, Control System Toolbox, Simulink block diagrams, solvers, parameter sweeps and generating code from models

phases.build: A Simulink model of a mass-spring-damper and a DC motor with scripted parameter sweeps, step and Bode responses, and a short report validating it against analytical solutions.

phases.title: Control design

steps.what: First-principles electrical and mechanical models, system identification from step data, model validation and uncertainty
PID tuning, root locus, gain and phase margins, state-space models, controllability, pole placement, LQR and observers

phases.build: An inverted-pendulum-on-cart controller designed twice (PID and LQR with an observer) in Simulink, compared on settling time, robustness to model error and disturbance rejection.

phases.title: Real-time implementation

steps.what: Pointers, structs, fixed-point and floating-point arithmetic, classes, and writing discrete-time controllers and filters in code
Control-loop timing, interrupts and timers, jitter and latency, RTOS scheduling, deadline analysis and anti-windup in discrete loops

phases.build: A 1 kHz discrete PID speed controller for a DC motor on an STM32 with encoder feedback, with measured loop jitter and step responses matching your Simulink model.

phases.title: Motion hardware and industrial control

steps.what: DC, stepper and BLDC motors, H-bridges and PWM, encoders, current loops, field-oriented control basics and cascaded position-velocity loops
Complementary and Kalman filters for IMU orientation, encoder-IMU fusion and noise characterisation
Industrial fieldbus basics: EtherCAT, CANopen, Modbus, distributed clocks and servo drive profiles (CiA 402)

phases.build: A self-balancing robot or 2-axis gimbal with cascaded BLDC control and IMU fusion, with tuning plots and a write-up comparing simulated and measured performance.

game-engine-eng.summary: Get very strong at C++, data structures and 3D math, learn how engines are architected by building one, then specialise in performance, memory and multithreading, finishing with commercial engines.

phases.title: C++ and math foundations

steps.what: Modern C++17/20: RAII, move semantics, smart pointers, templates, STL internals, undefined behaviour and debugging with Visual Studio
Arrays vs linked structures, hash maps, trees, spatial partitioning (grids, quadtrees, BVH), sorting and complexity
Vectors, matrices, transforms, quaternions, projections, intersection tests and numerical stability

phases.build: A header-only C++ math library (vectors, matrices, quaternions, ray-AABB and ray-triangle tests) with unit tests and benchmarks against GLM.

phases.title: Engine architecture

steps.what: Stack vs heap, custom allocators (linear, pool, stack), alignment, fragmentation, object lifetimes and memory tracking
Game loop and fixed timestep, entity-component-system, scene graphs, resource management, event systems and a basic OpenGL renderer

phases.build: A small 2D/3D engine in C++ with an ECS, custom allocators, asset loading, an ImGui editor panel and a playable demo level built on top of it.

phases.title: Performance and concurrency

steps.what: Profiling, cache-friendly data-oriented design, SIMD basics, branch prediction, frame budgets and reducing draw calls
Threads, atomics, mutexes, lock-free queues, job systems, false sharing and data races

phases.build: Add a job system to your engine and refactor it to data-oriented layouts, with Tracy captures showing frame time cut by a measured amount while simulating 100k entities.

phases.title: Commercial engines and gameplay

steps.what: Unreal C++ gameplay framework, Blueprints interop, engine source navigation, Unity C# scripting and how both engines structure subsystems
Character controllers, state machines, input handling, collision response, cameras and data-driven gameplay configuration

phases.build: A custom Unreal Engine 5 C++ plugin (for example a spatial-hash crowd system) with a profiled demo map, plus a short write-up comparing its design to your own engine.

graphics-eng.summary: Learn C++ and the linear algebra of 3D, understand pipelines by writing a rasterizer and OpenGL shaders, then move to Vulkan or DirectX 12, profiling, lighting and ray tracing.

phases.title: C++ and 3D math

steps.what: Modern C++17: RAII, smart pointers, move semantics, templates, STL, memory layout and debugging native code
Vectors, matrices, homogeneous coordinates, model-view-projection transforms, quaternions, barycentric coordinates

phases.build: A CPU software rasterizer in C++ that loads OBJ models and renders them with perspective-correct texturing, depth buffering and flat/Gouraud shading to an image file.

phases.title: Pipelines and shaders

steps.what: Vertex processing, rasterisation, depth and stencil, blending, forward vs deferred rendering, render targets and post-processing
Vertex and fragment shaders, uniforms, texture sampling, normal mapping, Phong/Blinn-Phong, and porting GLSL to HLSL

phases.build: An OpenGL deferred renderer with a G-buffer, normal mapping, many point lights, bloom and tone-mapping post-processing, and an ImGui panel to toggle passes.

phases.title: Modern GPU APIs and profiling

steps.what: Instances, devices, command buffers, pipelines, descriptor sets, synchronisation and barriers, memory allocation and swapchains
Frame captures, GPU timings, occupancy, bandwidth and overdraw analysis, and finding pipeline bottlenecks

phases.build: Port your deferred renderer to Vulkan or DirectX 12 with proper synchronisation, then publish RenderDoc and Nsight captures documenting two bottlenecks you found and fixed.

phases.title: Lighting and advanced techniques

steps.what: Physically based rendering, image-based lighting, shadow maps and cascades, SSAO, HDR and tone mapping
Workgroups, shared memory, GPU particle systems, tiled/clustered light culling and compute-based post-processing
Ray-scene intersection, BVH construction, path tracing basics, denoising and hardware ray tracing pipelines

phases.build: A PBR renderer loading glTF scenes with cascaded shadows, clustered lighting via compute shaders and a hardware ray-traced reflections toggle, with a performance comparison write-up.

blockchain-eng.summary: Start with JavaScript and cryptography, understand how blockchains and the EVM work, write and test smart contracts with dApp frontends, then move to protocol languages and node infrastructure.

phases.title: Programming and cryptography foundations

steps.what: Modern JavaScript and TypeScript, async/await, Node.js, npm packages and testing with Mocha or Vitest
Branching, pull requests, code review and contributing to open-source repositories
Hash functions, Merkle trees, public-key crypto, ECDSA and secp256k1, digital signatures, and commitment schemes

phases.build: A TypeScript library implementing Merkle trees with inclusion proofs and ECDSA transaction signing and verification, with tests against known vectors.

phases.title: How blockchains work

steps.what: Blocks, transactions, accounts, gas, the EVM stack machine, storage, logs, the mempool and how Ethereum clients execute blocks
Proof of work, proof of stake, finality, fork choice rules, BFT protocols, and the economic security behind validators

phases.build: A toy proof-of-stake blockchain in TypeScript with signed transactions, Merkle-rooted blocks, validator selection and a fork-choice rule, running as a 3-node local network.

phases.title: Smart contracts and dApps

steps.what: Types, storage vs memory, mappings, events, modifiers, inheritance, interfaces, errors and upgradeable proxy patterns
ERC-20 and ERC-721 standards, access control, testing and fuzzing, deployment to testnets, verification and common vulnerabilities
Providers and signers, contract ABIs, sending transactions, listening to events, wallet connection and indexing on-chain data

phases.build: A fully tested escrow or crowdfunding dApp deployed and verified on the Sepolia testnet, with a React frontend using Ethers.js and a subgraph indexing its events.

phases.title: Protocol languages and infrastructure

steps.what: Ownership, borrowing, traits, error handling, async with Tokio, and reading Rust blockchain codebases such as Reth or Solana
Goroutines, channels, interfaces, testing, and navigating the go-ethereum codebase
Running execution and consensus clients, RPC endpoints, syncing modes, monitoring and load-balancing node fleets

phases.build: A Rust service that indexes a testnet via JSON-RPC from your own Docker-hosted Geth and Lighthouse node, exposing an API and Grafana dashboard of block and gas metrics.

smart-contract-eng.summary: Learn JavaScript and Ethereum basics, write and test Solidity with Foundry and Hardhat, then focus on security, gas, DeFi mechanics and auditing, adding Rust chains last.

phases.title: Foundations

steps.what: Modern JavaScript and TypeScript, async/await, Node.js scripting and npm tooling
Accounts, transactions, gas, blocks, wallets, testnets, and reading transactions and contracts on a block explorer
Hash functions, keccak256, ECDSA signatures, signature recovery, EIP-712 typed data and Merkle proofs

phases.build: A TypeScript script set that creates wallets, signs EIP-712 messages, builds a Merkle allowlist and sends and decodes transactions on the Sepolia testnet.

phases.title: Solidity and testing

steps.what: Types, storage layout, mappings, events, modifiers, inheritance, custom errors, libraries, ERC-20/721/1155 and proxy upgrade patterns
Unit tests, fuzz and invariant tests, mainnet forking, cheatcodes, deployment scripts, gas reports and contract verification

phases.build: A staking vault with ERC-20 rewards and a Merkle-allowlist NFT, with Foundry unit, fuzz and invariant tests at over 95% coverage, deployed and verified on Sepolia.

phases.title: Security and gas

steps.what: Reentrancy, access control bugs, oracle manipulation, flash-loan attacks, front-running, signature replay and the SWC registry
Opcodes, stack/memory/storage costs, storage packing, calldata vs memory, inline Yul, and reading bytecode and traces

phases.build: Solve all Ethernaut and Damn Vulnerable DeFi levels with written exploit tests in Foundry, then gas-optimise your vault and document the before/after gas snapshot.

phases.title: DeFi, auditing and other chains

steps.what: AMMs and constant-product math, lending and liquidations, oracles, stablecoins, vaults (ERC-4626) and governance
Audit methodology, threat modelling, writing findings with severity, invariant testing, symbolic execution and formal specs
Rust ownership and traits, Solana account model and Anchor programs, CosmWasm contracts and their security pitfalls

phases.build: A minimal AMM with an ERC-4626 vault, plus a public audit report on a past Code4rena or Sherlock contest codebase with at least two valid findings and proof-of-concept tests.

arvr-eng.summary: Learn C# or C++ with 3D math, build in Unity or Unreal with real-time rendering knowledge, add XR SDKs and natural input, then optimise for frame-rate, shaders and computer vision.

phases.title: Programming and 3D math

steps.what: Version control for game projects, Git LFS for large assets, branching and pull requests
C# classes, generics, delegates, async and LINQ; C++ memory, pointers and RAII for engine-level or native plugin work
Vectors, matrices, quaternions, coordinate spaces, raycasting, anchors, poses and world-scale tracking concepts

phases.build: A C# 3D math toolkit (transforms, quaternion interpolation, ray-plane and ray-sphere tests) with unit tests, used in a small interactive scene visualising coordinate frames.

phases.title: Real-time engines

steps.what: Scenes, prefabs, components, physics, input systems, UI, animation and building to Android or PC; Unreal Blueprints basics
Render pipelines (URP/HDRP), lighting and baking, materials, LOD, occlusion culling and stereo rendering basics

phases.build: A polished 3D interactive scene in Unity (for example a physics puzzle room) with baked lighting, LODs and a stable frame-rate on a mid-range Android phone.

phases.title: XR development

steps.what: OpenXR runtimes, XR Interaction Toolkit, plane detection, anchors, image tracking, passthrough and building for Quest and phones
Hand skeletons and gestures, pinch and poke interactions, gaze-based selection, foveation and comfortable interaction design

phases.build: A mixed-reality app on Meta Quest or an ARCore phone, for example an AR lab-equipment trainer with anchored 3D models and hand-gesture interaction, published as a public build or demo video.

phases.title: Performance and visuals

steps.what: Profiling CPU and GPU, draw-call batching, single-pass instanced rendering, fixed foveated rendering and hitting 72-90 fps budgets
Shader Graph, HLSL basics, mobile-friendly shaders, stereo-correct effects and avoiding expensive transparency
Camera models, feature tracking, marker detection, depth estimation and how SLAM powers XR tracking

phases.build: Optimise your XR app to a steady 72+ fps on Quest with a profiling report, add custom shaders, and integrate a MediaPipe or OpenCV feature such as marker-triggered content.

quantum-eng.summary: Build Python, linear algebra and quantum mechanics foundations, learn the circuit model, implement core algorithms in Qiskit, Cirq and PennyLane, then tackle noise and error correction.

phases.title: Math and programming foundations

steps.what: Functions, classes, NumPy arrays, Matplotlib, Jupyter notebooks and writing tested scientific code
Complex vector spaces, inner products, unitary and Hermitian matrices, eigen-decomposition, tensor products and Dirac notation
Random variables, distributions, expectation, sampling and estimating quantities from repeated measurements

phases.build: A NumPy state-vector simulator for up to 10 qubits supporting single- and two-qubit gates and measurement sampling, validated against analytical results for Bell and GHZ states.

phases.title: Quantum foundations

steps.what: Postulates, superposition, measurement, spin-1/2 systems, entanglement, density matrices and decoherence
Qubits, Bloch sphere, gates and circuits, universality, entanglement, no-cloning, teleportation and superdense coding

phases.build: An interactive notebook series demonstrating teleportation, superdense coding and Bell-inequality violation, run both on your simulator and on real IBM Quantum hardware with results compared.

phases.title: Algorithms and frameworks

steps.what: Building and transpiling circuits, simulators and noise models, running on cloud hardware, parameterised circuits and autodiff
Deutsch-Jozsa, Bernstein-Vazirani, Grover, QFT and phase estimation, Shor's outline, VQE and QAOA

phases.build: An open-source repo implementing Grover, QPE and a VQE for the H2 molecule plus QAOA for Max-Cut, each benchmarked on simulators with noise and on real hardware.

phases.title: Noise, error correction and performance

steps.what: Noise channels, bit-flip and phase-flip codes, stabiliser formalism, surface codes, decoders, and error mitigation like zero-noise extrapolation
Modern C++ basics, performance-minded code, and Python bindings for fast simulation kernels

phases.build: A surface-code memory experiment in Stim with a PyMatching decoder plotting logical error rate versus physical error rate, plus a C++ gate kernel bound to Python via pybind11.

technical-recruiter.summary: Build enough tech literacy to read engineering profiles credibly, then learn to source, screen and track candidates in an ATS before moving on to search strings, interview logistics, employer brand and offer negotiation.

phases.title: Tech literacy and recruiter toolkit

steps.what: Frontend vs backend vs data vs DevOps roles, common stacks (MERN, Java/Spring, Python/Django), cloud basics, what SDE-1/2/3 and staff levels mean, reading a GitHub profile
Pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, conditional formatting, funnel conversion rates, time-to-fill and source-of-hire calculations, simple dashboards
Concise outreach emails, job description structure, candidate-facing tone, writing feedback summaries for hiring managers, LinkedIn InMail etiquette

phases.build: A tech-role glossary and leveling guide for 8 engineering roles (stack, typical interview loop, SDE-1 to staff expectations) plus a spreadsheet model computing funnel conversion and time-to-fill from sample pipeline data.

phases.title: Core recruiting: source, screen, track

steps.what: Building talent maps, sourcing on LinkedIn, GitHub, Stack Overflow and Naukri, X-ray search basics, personalized multi-touch outreach sequences, tracking response rates
Intake meetings with hiring managers, must-have vs nice-to-have criteria, structured phone screens, probing project depth, notice period and CTC checks, writing scorecards
Job setup, pipeline stages, candidate profiles and tags, scorecards, email templates, rejection reasons, compliance hygiene, pipeline and source reports

phases.build: An end-to-end mock search for a backend SDE-1 role: written intake notes, a 40-profile talent map, outreach sequence with tracked reply rates, 5 structured screen scorecards, and the whole pipeline run in a free ATS trial.

phases.title: Scaling the pipeline and closing offers

steps.what: AND/OR/NOT, quotes and parentheses, site: and inurl: X-ray strings for GitHub and LinkedIn, synonym banks for skills and titles, iterating strings by result quality
Panel scheduling across time zones, interview loop design, interviewer briefing packs, candidate prep emails, feedback chasing, debrief facilitation
EVP definition, engineering blog and tech-talk content, Glassdoor/AmbitionBox review response, campus hiring outreach, careers page copy, measuring applicant quality
Fixed vs variable vs ESOPs, CTC breakdown, market benchmarking, pre-closing expectations early, handling counteroffers and buyouts, reducing offer dropouts

phases.build: A hiring playbook for a 10-engineer startup team: a library of tested Boolean strings per role, a 4-round interview loop with scheduling templates, an employer-brand campaign draft, and an offer-closing guide with CTC benchmarks.
